exercises.name: Ab Scissors
exercises.description: Lying on your back with legs lifted, crossing them over each other like scissors.
setup: Lie on your back with hands under your hips and straight legs lifted.
steps: Open your legs apart, then cross one over the other.
Open again and cross the other way.
cues: Lower back stays down
Small, controlled crosses
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily throughout.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel
exercises.description: Rolling an ab wheel forward from your knees and pulling it back, keeping the core braced.
setup: Kneel on a pad holding the ab wheel on the floor under your shoulders.
steps: Roll the wheel forward as far as you can without your lower back arching.
Pull it back to the start using your abs.
cues: Ribs down, slight round in the upper back
Only go as far as you can control
mistakes: Leading with the hips on the way back
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you roll out, breathe out as you pull back.
safety: Start with short rollouts and increase the range gradually.

exercises.name: Barbell Ab Rollout
exercises.description: Barbell Ab Rollout is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the lower back. A variation of the ab wheel: a loaded barbell with round plates replaces the wheel.
setup: For this exercise you will need to get into a pushup position, but instead of having your hands of the floor, you will be grabbing on to an Olympic barbell (loaded with 5-10 lbs on each side) instead. This will be your starting position.
steps: While keeping a slight arch on your back, lift your hips and roll the barbell towards your feet as you exhale. Tip: As you perform the movement, your glutes should be coming up, you should be keeping the abs tight and should maintain your back posture at all times. Also your arms should be staying perpendicular to the floor throughout the movement. If you don't, you will work out your shoulders and back more than the abs.
After a second contraction at the top, start to roll the barbell back forward to the starting position slowly as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Ribs down, slight round in the upper back
Only go as far as you can control
mistakes: Leading with the hips on the way back
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you roll out, breathe out as you pull back.
safety: Start with short rollouts and increase the range gradually.
variation_notes: A loaded barbell with round plates replaces the wheel.

exercises.name: Barbell Ab Rollout - On Knees
exercises.description: Barbell Ab Rollout - On Knees is an advanced-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the lower back. A variation of the ab wheel: barbell rollout from the knees, the easier version.
setup: Hold an Olympic barbell loaded with 5-10lbs on each side and kneel on the floor.
steps: Now place the barbell on the floor in front of you so that you are on all your hands and knees (as in a kneeling push up position). This will be your starting position.

Slowly roll the barbell straight forward, stretching your body into a straight position. Tip: Go down as far as you can without touching the floor with your body. Breathe in during this portion of the movement.
After a second pause at the stretched position, start pulling yourself back to the starting position as you breathe out. Tip: Go slowly and keep your abs tight at all times.
cues: Ribs down, slight round in the upper back
Only go as far as you can control
mistakes: Leading with the hips on the way back
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you roll out, breathe out as you pull back.
safety: Start with short rollouts and increase the range gradually.
variation_notes: Barbell rollout from the knees, the easier version.

exercises.name: Barbell Rollout from Bench
exercises.description: Barbell Rollout from Bench is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the glutes, hamstrings and lats. A variation of the ab wheel: kneeling on a bench gives a longer range below the hands.
setup: Place a loaded barbell on the ground, near the end of a bench. Kneel with both legs on the bench, and take a medium to narrow grip on the barbell. This will be your starting position.
steps: To begin, extend through the hips to slowly roll the bar forward. As you roll out, flex the shoulder to roll the bar above your head. Ensure that your arms remain extended throughout the movement.
When the bar has been moved as far forward as possible, return to the starting position.
cues: Ribs down, slight round in the upper back
Only go as far as you can control
mistakes: Leading with the hips on the way back
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you roll out, breathe out as you pull back.
safety: Start with short rollouts and increase the range gradually.
variation_notes: Kneeling on a bench gives a longer range below the hands.

exercises.name: Suspended Fallout
exercises.description: Suspended Fallout is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the chest and lower back. A variation of the ab wheel: hands in suspension straps; lean forward with arms extending overhead.
setup: Adjust the straps so the handles are at an appropriate height, below waist level.
steps: Begin standing and grasping the handles. Lean into the straps, moving to an incline push-up position. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your arms straight, lean further into the suspension straps, bringing your body closer to the ground, allowing your shoulders to extend, raising your arms up and over your head.
Maintain a neutral spine and keep the rest of your body straight, your shoulders being the only joints allowed to move.
Pause during the peak contraction, and then return to the starting position.
cues: Ribs down, slight round in the upper back
Only go as far as you can control
mistakes: Leading with the hips on the way back
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you roll out, breathe out as you pull back.
safety: Start with short rollouts and increase the range gradually.
variation_notes: Hands in suspension straps; lean forward with arms extending overhead.

exercises.name: Lower Back Curl
exercises.description: Lower Back Curl is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the abs & core.
steps: Lie on your stomach with your arms out to your sides. This will be your starting position.
Using your lower back muscles, extend your spine lifting your chest off of the ground. Do not use your arms to push yourself up. Keep your head up during the movement. Repeat for 10-20 repetitions.
cues: Move slowly through the spine, one segment at a time
Stay in a comfortable range; this should feel easy
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.
safety: Stop if you feel pain shooting down a leg, and see a professional.

exercises.name: Torso Rotation
exercises.description: Torso Rotation is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the abs & core.
steps: Stand upright holding an exercise ball with both hands. Extend your arms so the ball is straight out in front of you. This will be your starting position.
Rotate your torso to one side, keeping your eyes on the ball as you move. Now, rotate back to the opposite direction. Repeat for 10-20 repetitions.
cues: Move slowly through the spine, one segment at a time
Stay in a comfortable range; this should feel easy
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.
safety: Stop if you feel pain shooting down a leg, and see a professional.

exercises.name: One-Arm Medicine Ball Slam
exercises.description: One-Arm Medicine Ball Slam is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the lats. A variation of the ball slams: one hand, slamming across the body.
setup: Start in a standing position with a staggered, athletic stance. Hold a medicine ball in one hand, on the same side as your back leg. This will be your starting position.
steps: Begin by winding the arm, raising the medicine ball above your head. As you do so, extend through the hips, knees, and ankles to load up for the slam.
At peak extension, flex the shoulders, spine, and hips to throw the ball hard into the ground directly in front of you.
Catch the ball on the bounce and continue for the desired number of repetitions.
cues: Use the whole body
Hinge to pick it up
mistakes: Rounding the back to pick up the ball
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lift, breathe out hard as you slam.
safety: Use a dead-bounce slam ball.
variation_notes: One hand, slamming across the body.

exercises.name: Spider Crawl
exercises.description: Spider Crawl is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the chest and triceps. A variation of the bear crawl: low crawl, bringing each knee toward the elbow.
setup: Begin in a prone position on the floor. Support your weight on your hands and toes, with your feet together and your body straight. Your arms should be bent to 90 degrees. This will be your starting position.
steps: Initiate the movement by raising one foot off of the ground. Externally rotate the leg and bring the knee toward your elbow, as far forward as possible.
Return this leg to the starting position and repeat on the opposite side.
cues: Back flat, hips low
Small steps
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily through the nose and mouth; do not hold your breath.
variation_notes: Low crawl, bringing each knee toward the elbow.

exercises.name: Bent Press
exercises.description: Bent Press is an advanced-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the glutes, hamstrings, lower back, quadriceps and triceps.
setup: Clean a kettlebell to your shoulder. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you raise the kettlebell towards your shoulder. The wrist should rotate as you do so. This will be your starting position.
steps: Begin my leaning to the side opposite the kettlebell, continuing until you are able to touch the ground with your free hand, keeping your eyes on the kettlebell. As you do so, press the weight vertically be extending through the elbow, keeping your arm perpendicular to the ground.
Return to an upright position, with the kettlebell above your head. Return the kettlebell to the shoulder and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
cues: Kettlebell locked out above the shoulder
Lean away and under the bell rather than pressing it
Watch the bell the whole time
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Bicycle Crunch
exercises.description: Alternating elbow-to-opposite-knee crunches while pedalling the legs, working the abs and obliques.
setup: Lie on your back with hands lightly behind your head and legs raised, knees bent 90°.
steps: Bring one knee in while rotating the opposite shoulder toward it.
Straighten that leg as you switch sides.
Continue alternating smoothly.
cues: Rotate from the ribs, not the elbows
Slow and controlled
exercises.breathing: Breathe out each time you rotate.

exercises.name: Bicycle Crunch Raised Legs
exercises.description: Alternating elbow-to-opposite-knee crunches while pedalling the legs, working the abs and obliques.
setup: Lie on your back with hands lightly behind your head and legs raised, knees bent 90°.
steps: Bring one knee in while rotating the opposite shoulder toward it.
Straighten that leg as you switch sides.
Continue alternating smoothly.
cues: Rotate from the ribs, not the elbows
Slow and controlled
exercises.breathing: Breathe out each time you rotate.
variation_notes: Keep both legs raised the whole time instead of extending them toward the floor.

exercises.name: Bosu Ball Cable Crunch With Side Bends
exercises.family_name: Bosu Ball Cable Crunch With Side Bends
exercises.description: Bosu Ball Cable Crunch With Side Bends is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core.
setup: Connect a standard handle to each arm of a cable machine, and position them in the most downward position.
steps: Grab a Bosu Ball and position it in front and center of the cable machine.
Lie down on the Bosu Ball with the small of your back arched around the ball. Your rear end should be close to the floor without touching it.
With both hands, reach back and grab the handle of each cable.
With your feet positioned in a wide stance, extend your arms straight out in front of you and in between your knees. Your hands should be at knee level.
Keep your arms straight and in-line with the upward angle of the cable. Elevate your torso in a crunching motion without dropping or bending your arms.
Maintain the rigid position with your arms. Slowly descend back to the starting position with your back arched around the Bosu Ball and your abdominals elongated.
Repeat the same series of movements to failure.
Once you reach failure, keep your abs tight and raise your torso into plank position so your back is elevated off the Bosu Ball.
Lower your arms down to your side; keep them straight. Start doing alternating side bends; reach for your heels! This finishing movement will focus on your obliques.
cues: Brace on the ball before each rep
Crunch down, then bend to each side
Slow and controlled
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Butt-Ups
exercises.description: Butt-Ups is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core.
setup: Begin a pushup position but with your elbows on the ground and resting on your forearms. Your arms should be bent at a 90 degree angle.
steps: Arch your back slightly out rather than keeping your back completely straight.

Raise your glutes toward the ceiling, squeezing your abs tightly to close the distance between your ribcage and hips. The end result will be that you'll end up in a high bridge position. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Lower back down slowly to your starting position as you breathe in. Tip: Don't let your back sag downwards.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Start in a forearm plank
Lift the hips straight up into a pike
Lower back to a flat plank
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Cable Core Pallof Press
exercises.description: Standing side-on to a cable and pressing the handle straight out from your chest while resisting the twist.
setup: Set a pulley at chest height and stand side-on to it.
Hold the handle at your chest with both hands, feet shoulder-width.
steps: Press the handle straight out in front of your chest.
Hold for 1–2 seconds without letting your body rotate.
Bring it back to your chest.
cues: Hips and shoulders stay square
The hands stay in the middle of your body
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you press out, breathe in as you return.

exercises.name: Cable Crunch
exercises.description: Kneeling below a high cable and curling your torso down. Lets you load the abs progressively.
setup: Attach a rope to a high pulley and kneel facing the stack.
Hold the rope beside your head.
steps: Curl your torso down, bringing your elbows toward your thighs.
Squeeze the abs.
Return slowly to upright.
cues: Round the spine; hips stay still
Elbows to knees
mistakes: Sitting back on the heels and pulling with the arms
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Cable Seated Crunch
exercises.description: Cable Seated Crunch is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the cable crunch: seated facing away from a high pulley, rope behind the head.
setup: Seat on a flat bench with your back facing a high pulley.
steps: Grasp the cable rope attachment with both hands (with the palms of the hands facing each other) and place your hands securely over both shoulders. Tip: Allow the weight to hyperextend the lower back slightly. This will be your starting position.
With the hips stationary, flex the waist so the elbows travel toward the hips. Breathe out as you perform this step.
As you inhale, go back to the initial position slowly.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Round the spine; hips stay still
Elbows to knees
mistakes: Sitting back on the heels and pulling with the arms
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Seated facing away from a high pulley, rope behind the head.

exercises.name: Kneeling Cable Crunch With Alternating Oblique Twists
exercises.description: Kneeling Cable Crunch With Alternating Oblique Twists is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the cable crunch: alternate bringing each elbow toward the opposite knee to add the obliques.
setup: Connect a rope attachment to a high pulley cable and position a mat on the floor in front of it.
steps: Grab the rope with both hands and kneel approximately two feet back from the tower.
Position the rope behind your head with your hands by your ears.
Keep your hands in the same place, contract your abs and pull downward on the rope in a crunching movement until your elbows reach your knees.
Pause briefly at the bottom and rise up in a slow and controlled manner until you reach the starting position.
Repeat the same downward movement until you're halfway down, at which time you'll begin rotating one of your elbows to the opposite knee.
Again, pause briefly at the bottom and rise up in a slow and controlled manner until you reach the starting position.
Repeat the same movement as before, but alternate the other elbow to the opposite knee.
Continue this series of movements to failure.
cues: Round the spine; hips stay still
Elbows to knees
mistakes: Sitting back on the heels and pulling with the arms
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Alternate bringing each elbow toward the opposite knee to add the obliques.

exercises.name: Rope Crunch
exercises.description: Rope Crunch is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the cable crunch: rope attachment held at the sides of the head.
setup: Kneel 1-2 feet in front of a cable system with a rope attached.
steps: After selecting an appropriate weight, grasp the rope with both hands reaching overhead. Your torso should be upright in the starting position.
To begin, flex at the spine, attempting to bring your rib cage to your legs as you pull the cable down.
Pause at the bottom of the motion, and then slowly return to the starting position.
These can be done with twists or to the side to hit the obliques.
cues: Round the spine; hips stay still
Elbows to knees
mistakes: Sitting back on the heels and pulling with the arms
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Rope attachment held at the sides of the head.

exercises.name: Standing Rope Crunch
exercises.description: Standing Rope Crunch is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the cable crunch: standing facing away from a high pulley; crunch the ribs toward the hips without bending at the hips.
setup: Attach a rope to a high pulley and select an appropriate weight.
steps: Stand with your back to the cable tower. Take the rope with both hands over your shoulders, holding it to your upper chest. This will be your starting position.
Perform the movement by flexing the spine, crunching the weight down as far as you can.
Hold the peak contraction for a moment before returning to the starting position.
cues: Round the spine; hips stay still
Elbows to knees
mistakes: Sitting back on the heels and pulling with the arms
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Standing facing away from a high pulley; crunch the ribs toward the hips without bending at the hips.

exercises.name: Cable Judo Flip
exercises.description: Cable Judo Flip is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core.
setup: Connect a rope attachment to a tower, and move the cable to the lowest pulley position. Stand with your side to the cable with a wide stance, and grab the rope with both hands.
steps: Twist your body away from the pulley as you bring the rope over your shoulder like you're performing a judo flip.
Shift your weight between your feet as you twist and crunch forward, pulling the cable downward.
Return to the starting position and repeat until failure.
Then, reposition and repeat the same series of movements on the opposite side.
cues: Feet planted, hips turning with the pull
Pull diagonally across the body from high to low
Control the return
mistakes: Rounding the back at the bottom
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Cable Twist (Down to up)
exercises.description: Rotating a cable handle diagonally across your body, like chopping wood, to work the obliques.
setup: Set the pulley high or low depending on the direction and stand side-on.
Hold the handle with both hands, arms almost straight.
steps: Pull the handle diagonally across your body by rotating the torso.
Let the hips and back foot pivot naturally.
Return slowly; finish all reps, then switch sides.
cues: Power comes from the torso
Arms stay long
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you rotate, breathe in as you return.
variation_notes: Pulley set low; chop up and across the body.

exercises.name: Cable Twist (Up to down)
exercises.description: Rotating a cable handle diagonally across your body, like chopping wood, to work the obliques.
setup: Set the pulley high or low depending on the direction and stand side-on.
Hold the handle with both hands, arms almost straight.
steps: Pull the handle diagonally across your body by rotating the torso.
Let the hips and back foot pivot naturally.
Return slowly; finish all reps, then switch sides.
cues: Power comes from the torso
Arms stay long
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you rotate, breathe in as you return.
variation_notes: Pulley set high; chop down and across the body.

exercises.name: Overhead Stretch
exercises.description: Overhead Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the chest, forearms, lats and triceps.
steps: Standing straight up, lace your fingers together and open your palms to the ceiling. Keep your shoulders down as you extend your arms up.
To create a full torso stretch, pull your tailbone down and stabilize your torso as you do this. Stretch the muscles on both the front and the back of the torso.
cues: Keep the shoulders down away from the ears
Keep the ribs down; do not arch the back to fake the range
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Seated Overhead Stretch
exercises.description: Seated Overhead Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the abs & core.
setup: Sit up straight on an exercise mat.
steps: Touch the soles of your feet together with your feet six to eight inches in front of your hips.
Place one hand on the floor beside you and your other hand behind your head.
Lift your elbow to the ceiling as you incline your torso to the other side. Hold for 10 to 20 seconds, then switch sides.
cues: Keep the shoulders down away from the ears
Keep the ribs down; do not arch the back to fake the range
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Standing Lateral Stretch
exercises.description: Standing Lateral Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the abs & core.
setup: Take a slightly wider than hip distance stance with your knees slightly bent.
steps: Place your right hand on your right hip to support the spine.
Raise your left arm in a vertical line and place your left hand behind your head. Keep it there as you incline your torso to the right.
Keep your weight evenly distributed between both legs (don't lean into your left hip). Switch sides.
cues: Keep the shoulders down away from the ears
Keep the ribs down; do not arch the back to fake the range
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Cocoons
exercises.description: Cocoons is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core.
setup: Begin by lying on your back on the ground. Your legs should be straight and your arms extended behind your head. This will be your starting position.
steps: To perform the movement, tuck the knees toward your chest, rotating your pelvis to lift your glutes from the floor. As you do so, flex the spine, bringing your arms back over your head to perform a simultaneous crunch motion.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
cues: Arms reach overhead and legs out long
Bring knees and chest together in one motion
Lower with control
mistakes: Letting the lower back arch when the legs go out
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Crunch
exercises.description: Cross-Body Crunch is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the crunch: bring one elbow toward the opposite knee to add the obliques.
setup: Lie flat on your back and bend your knees about 60 degrees.
steps: Keep your feet flat on the floor and place your hands loosely behind your head. This will be your starting position.

Now curl up and bring your right elbow and shoulder across your body while bring your left knee in toward your left shoulder at the same time. Reach with your elbow and try to touch your knee. Exhale as you perform this movement. Tip: Try to bring your shoulder up towards your knee rather than just your elbow and remember that the key is to contract the abs as you perform the movement; not just to move the elbow.
Now go back down to the starting position as you inhale and repeat with the left elbow and the right knee.
Continue alternating in this manner until all prescribed repetitions are done.
cues: Ribs toward hips
Lower back stays on the floor
Look at the ceiling; keep space under the chin
mistakes: Pulling on the neck with the hands
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Bring one elbow toward the opposite knee to add the obliques.

exercises.name: Crunch
exercises.description: Curling the upper back off the floor by contracting the abs, while the lower back stays down.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Place your hands lightly beside your head or across your chest.
steps: Curl your head, shoulders and upper back off the floor by bringing your ribs toward your pelvis.
Pause and squeeze the abs.
Lower slowly.
cues: Ribs toward hips
Lower back stays on the floor
Look at the ceiling; keep space under the chin
mistakes: Pulling on the neck with the hands
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Crunch (Machine)
exercises.description: A seated ab crunch against a weight stack, which lets you add load to the abs in small steps.
setup: Adjust the seat so the chest pad or handles sit at chest height.
Hook your feet under the pads if there are any.
steps: Curl your torso forward and down against the resistance, bringing your ribs toward your hips.
Squeeze the abs.
Return slowly without letting the weights touch.
cues: Ribs toward hips
Move by curling the spine, not by bending at the hips
Slow on the way back
mistakes: Letting the stack rest between reps
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Crunch (Weighted)
exercises.description: Curling the upper back off the floor by contracting the abs, while the lower back stays down.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Place your hands lightly beside your head or across your chest.
steps: Curl your head, shoulders and upper back off the floor by bringing your ribs toward your pelvis.
Pause and squeeze the abs.
Lower slowly.
cues: Ribs toward hips
Lower back stays on the floor
Look at the ceiling; keep space under the chin
mistakes: Pulling on the neck with the hands
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Crunch - Hands Overhead
exercises.description: Crunch - Hands Overhead is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the crunch: arms overhead make the lever longer, so the same crunch is harder.
setup: Lie on the floor with your back flat and knees bent with around a 60-degree angle between the hamstrings and the calves.
steps: Keep your feet flat on the floor and stretch your arms overhead with your palms crossed. This will be your starting position.

Curl your upper body forward and bring your shoulder blades just off the floor. At all times, keep your arms aligned with your head, neck and shoulder. Don't move them forward from that position. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement and hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly lower down to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Ribs toward hips
Lower back stays on the floor
Look at the ceiling; keep space under the chin
mistakes: Pulling on the neck with the hands
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Arms overhead make the lever longer, so the same crunch is harder.

exercises.name: Crunch - Legs On Exercise Ball
exercises.description: Crunch - Legs On Exercise Ball is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the crunch: calves rest on a ball, which keeps the hips and knees at 90 degrees.
setup: Lie flat on your back with your feet resting on an exercise ball and your knees bent at a 90 degree angle.
steps: Place your feet three to four inches apart and point your toes inward so they touch.
Place your hands lightly on either side of your head keeping your elbows in. Tip: Don't lock your fingers behind your head.
Push the small of your back down in the floor in order to better isolate your abdominal muscles. This will be your starting position.

Begin to roll your shoulders off the floor and continue to push down as hard as you can with your lower back. Your shoulders should come up off the floor only about four inches, and your lower back should remain on the floor. Breathe out as you execute this portion of the movement. Squeeze your abdominals hard at the top of the contraction and hold for a second. Tip: Focus on a slow, controlled movement. Refrain from using momentum at any time.
Slowly go back down to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Ribs toward hips
Lower back stays on the floor
Look at the ceiling; keep space under the chin
mistakes: Pulling on the neck with the hands
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Calves rest on a ball, which keeps the hips and knees at 90 degrees.

exercises.name: Decline Crunch
exercises.description: Curling the upper back off the floor by contracting the abs, while the lower back stays down.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Place your hands lightly beside your head or across your chest.
steps: Curl your head, shoulders and upper back off the floor by bringing your ribs toward your pelvis.
Pause and squeeze the abs.
Lower slowly.
cues: Ribs toward hips
Lower back stays on the floor
Look at the ceiling; keep space under the chin
mistakes: Pulling on the neck with the hands
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Done on a decline bench with feet hooked; the angle makes it harder.

exercises.name: Decline Crunch (Weighted)
exercises.description: Curling the upper back off the floor by contracting the abs, while the lower back stays down.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Place your hands lightly beside your head or across your chest.
steps: Curl your head, shoulders and upper back off the floor by bringing your ribs toward your pelvis.
Pause and squeeze the abs.
Lower slowly.

Lower back stays on the floor
Look at the ceiling; keep space under the chin
mistakes: Pulling on the neck with the hands
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Decline Oblique Crunch
exercises.description: Decline Oblique Crunch is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the crunch: on a decline bench, twisting one shoulder toward the opposite hip.
setup: Secure your legs at the end of the decline bench and slowly lay down on the bench.
steps: Raise your upper body off the bench until your torso is about 35-45 degrees if measured from the floor.
Put one hand beside your head and the other on your thigh. This will be your starting position.

Raise your upper body slowly from the starting position while turning your torso to the left. Continue crunching up as you exhale until your right elbow touches your left knee. Hold this contracted position for a second. Tip: Focus on keeping your abs tight and keeping the movement slow and controlled.
Lower your body back down slowly to the starting position as you inhale.

After completing one set on the right for the recommended amount of repetitions, switch to your left side. Tip: Focus on really twisting your torso and feeling the contraction when you are in the up position.
cues: Ribs toward hips
Lower back stays on the floor
Look at the ceiling; keep space under the chin
mistakes: Pulling on the neck with the hands
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: On a decline bench, twisting one shoulder toward the opposite hip.

exercises.name: Exercise Ball Crunch
exercises.description: Exercise Ball Crunch is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the crunch: lying on a ball lets the spine extend over it first, giving a longer range.
setup: Lie on an exercise ball with your lower back curvature pressed against the spherical surface of the ball. Your feet should be bent at the knee and pressed firmly against the floor. The upper torso should be hanging off the top of the ball. The arms should either be kept alongside the body or crossed on top of your chest as these positions avoid neck strains (as opposed to the hands behind the back of the head position).
steps: Lower your torso into a stretch position keeping the neck stationary at all times. This will be your starting position.

With the hips stationary, flex the waist by contracting the abdominals and curl the shoulders and trunk upward until you feel a nice contraction on your abdominals. The arms should simply slide up the side of your legs if you have them at the side or just stay on top of your chest if you have them crossed. The lower back should always stay in contact with the ball. Exhale as you perform this movement and hold the contraction for a second.
As you inhale, go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Ribs toward hips
Lower back stays on the floor
Look at the ceiling; keep space under the chin
mistakes: Pulling on the neck with the hands
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Lying on a ball lets the spine extend over it first, giving a longer range.

exercises.name: Oblique Crunch
exercises.description: Curling the upper back off the floor by contracting the abs, while the lower back stays down.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Place your hands lightly beside your head or across your chest.
steps: Curl your head, shoulders and upper back off the floor by bringing your ribs toward your pelvis.
Pause and squeeze the abs.
Lower slowly.
cues: Ribs toward hips
Lower back stays on the floor
Look at the ceiling; keep space under the chin
mistakes: Pulling on the neck with the hands
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Curl up and rotate one shoulder toward the opposite knee, or lie on your side and crunch sideways.

exercises.name: Oblique Crunches
exercises.description: Oblique Crunches is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the crunch: knees drop to one side so the crunch works the obliques.
setup: Lie flat on the floor with your lower back pressed to the ground. For this exercise, you will need to put one hand beside your head and the other to the side against the floor.
steps: Make sure your feet are elevated and resting on a flat surface.
Now lift the shoulder in which your hand is touching your head.

Simply elevate your shoulder and body upward until you touch your knee. For example, if you have your right hand besides your head, then you want to elevate your body upwards until your right elbow touches your left knee. The same variation can be applied doing the inverse and using your left elbow to touch your right knee.
After your knee touches your elbow, lower your body until you have reached the starting position.
Remember to breathe in during the eccentric (lowering) part of the exercise and to breathe out during the concentric (upward) part of the exercise.
Continue alternating in this manner until all of the recommended repetitions for each side have been completed.
cues: Ribs toward hips
Lower back stays on the floor
Look at the ceiling; keep space under the chin
mistakes: Pulling on the neck with the hands
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Knees drop to one side so the crunch works the obliques.

exercises.name: Tuck Crunch
exercises.description: Tuck Crunch is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the crunch: knees pulled in toward the chest, which shortens the range and makes it easier.
setup: To begin, lie down on the floor or an exercise mat with your back pressed against the floor. Your arms should be lying across your sides with the palms facing down.
steps: Your legs should be crossed by wrapping one ankle around the other. Slowly elevate your legs up in the air until your thighs are perpendicular to the floor with a slight bend at the knees. Note: Your knees and toes should be parallel to the floor as opposed to the thighs.
Move your arms from the floor and cross them so they are resting on your chest. This is the starting position.
While keeping your lower back pressed against the floor, slowly lift your torso. Remember to exhale while perform this part of the exercise.
Slowly begin to lower your torso back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Ribs toward hips
Lower back stays on the floor
Look at the ceiling; keep space under the chin
mistakes: Pulling on the neck with the hands
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Knees pulled in toward the chest, which shortens the range and makes it easier.

exercises.name: Weighted Crunches
exercises.description: Weighted Crunches is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the crunch: hold a medicine ball at the chest or overhead for extra load.
setup: Lie flat on your back with your feet flat on the ground or resting on a bench with your knees bent at a 90 degree angle.
steps: Hold a weight to your chest, or you may hold it extended above your torso. This will be your starting position.
Now, exhale and slowly begin to roll your shoulders off the floor. Your shoulders should come up off the floor about 4 inches while your lower back remains on the floor.
At the top of the movement, flex your abdominals and hold for a brief pause.
Then inhale and slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position.
cues: Ribs toward hips
Lower back stays on the floor
Look at the ceiling; keep space under the chin
mistakes: Pulling on the neck with the hands
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Hold a medicine ball at the chest or overhead for extra load.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.description: Lying on your back with arms and legs up, slowly extending the opposite arm and leg while the back stays flat.
setup: Lie on your back with arms pointing up and knees bent 90° above the hips.
Press your lower back into the floor.
steps: Slowly lower one arm overhead and the opposite leg toward the floor.
Return and switch sides.
cues: Lower back never lifts
Move slowly
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you extend the arm and leg, breathe in as you return.

exercises.name: Dragon Flag
exercises.description: Lying on a bench holding behind your head, you raise your whole body up straight from the shoulders and lower it slowly.
setup: Lie on a bench and grip the bench behind your head.
steps: Lift your hips and legs until your body is nearly vertical, balanced on your upper back.
Lower your body as one straight line, as slowly as you can.
Stop before your hips touch, then raise again.
cues: Body stays straight from shoulders to toes
exercises.breathing: Breathe out slowly as you lower.
safety: Very demanding; build up with reverse crunches and leg raises.

exercises.name: Dragonfly
exercises.description: A partial dragon flag: lying on a bench gripping behind your head, you lower your hips and legs with bent knees or a shorter range.
setup: Lie on a bench and grip it behind your head.
steps: Raise your hips and legs up toward the ceiling.
Lower them slowly with knees bent, keeping the movement controlled.
cues: Control the lowering
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you lower.

exercises.name: Toe Touchers
exercises.description: Toe Touchers is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the abs & core.
setup: To begin, lie down on the floor or an exercise mat with your back pressed against the floor. Your arms should be lying across your sides with the palms facing down.
steps: Your legs should be touching each other. Slowly elevate your legs up in the air until they are almost perpendicular to the floor with a slight bend at the knees. Your feet should be parallel to the floor.
Move your arms so that they are fully extended at a 45 degree angle from the floor. This is the starting position.
While keeping your lower back pressed against the floor, slowly lift your torso and use your hands to try and touch your toes. Remember to exhale while perform this part of the exercise.
Slowly begin to lower your torso and arms back down to the starting position while inhaling. Remember to keep your arms straight out pointing towards your toes.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Start small and slow, then grow the range
Smooth, controlled movement, no flinging
About 8–12 reps per side as a warm-up
mistakes: Swinging into end range with momentum
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Elbow to Knee
exercises.description: Bringing one elbow to the opposite knee, standing or lying, to work the obliques.
setup: Stand tall with hands behind your head, or lie on your back as for a crunch.
steps: Lift one knee and rotate to bring the opposite elbow toward it.
Return and switch sides.
cues: Crunch the side of the torso
Stay tall when standing
mistakes: Pulling the head with the hands
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as elbow and knee meet.

exercises.name: Flutter Kicks
exercises.description: Lying on your back with legs lifted, kicking them up and down in small, quick alternating movements.
setup: Lie on your back with hands under your hips and legs straight, lifted a few centimetres.
steps: Kick the legs up and down alternately in small movements.
Continue for the set count.
cues: Lower back stays down
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily throughout.

exercises.name: Gorilla Chin/Crunch
exercises.description: Gorilla Chin/Crunch is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the biceps and lats.
setup: Hang from a chin-up bar using an underhand grip (palms facing you) that is slightly wider than shoulder width.
steps: Now bend your knees at a 90 degree angle so that the calves are parallel to the floor while the thighs remain perpendicular to it. This will be your starting position.

As you exhale, pull yourself up while crunching your knees up at the same time until your knees are at chest level. You will stop going up as soon as your nose is at the same level as the bar. Tip: When you get to this point you should also be finishing the crunch at the same time.
Slowly start to inhale as you return to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Knees bent at 90 degrees under the bar
Pull up and crunch the knees to the elbows together
Lower slowly to a full hang
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Hanging Knee Raise
exercises.description: Hanging from a bar and pulling your knees up toward your chest.
setup: Hang from a bar with straight arms, shoulders engaged.
steps: Raise your knees toward your chest, curling the pelvis up.
Lower slowly without swinging.
cues: Curl the hips up at the top
Stop the swing between reps
mistakes: Only lifting the knees to hip height
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as the knees rise, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.description: Hanging from a bar and raising straight legs to at least hip height.
setup: Hang from a bar with straight arms.
steps: Raise your straight legs to hip height or higher.
Lower slowly.
cues: Legs straight
No swinging
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the legs.

exercises.name: Hanging Pike
exercises.description: Hanging Pike is an advanced-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the hanging leg raise: straight legs all the way up toward the bar.
setup: Hang from a chin-up bar with your legs and feet together using an overhand grip (palms facing away from you) that is slightly wider than shoulder width. Tip: You may use wrist wraps in order to facilitate holding on to the bar.
steps: Now bend your knees at a 90 degree angle and bring the upper legs forward so that the calves are perpendicular to the floor while the thighs remain parallel to it. This will be your starting position.
Pull your legs up as you exhale until you almost touch your shins with the bar above you. Tip: Try to straighten your legs as much as possible while at the top.
Lower your legs as slowly as possible until you reach the starting position. Tip: Avoid swinging and using momentum at all times.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Legs straight
No swinging
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the legs.
variation_notes: Straight legs all the way up toward the bar.

exercises.name: Heel Taps
exercises.description: Lying with shoulders slightly lifted, you reach side to side to tap each heel.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat and a little wider than hips.
Lift your shoulders slightly off the floor.
steps: Reach one hand toward the same-side heel by bending sideways.
Return to the middle and reach to the other side.
cues: Shoulders stay lifted throughout
mistakes: Dropping the head to the floor between reps
exercises.breathing: Breathe out with each reach.

exercises.name: High Knee Skips
exercises.description: Running on the spot while driving the knees up to hip height.
setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width.
steps: Drive one knee up to hip height while pumping the opposite arm.
Switch quickly and keep going.
cues: Stay on the balls of the feet
Tall posture
exercises.breathing: Breathe rhythmically.
variation_notes: A skipping version that travels forward with a hop on each step.

exercises.name: High Knees
exercises.description: Running on the spot while driving the knees up to hip height.
setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width.
steps: Drive one knee up to hip height while pumping the opposite arm.
Switch quickly and keep going.
cues: Stay on the balls of the feet
Tall posture
exercises.breathing: Breathe rhythmically.

exercises.name: Hollow Rock
exercises.description: Holding a "banana" position on your back with arms and legs lifted, rocking gently back and forth.
setup: Lie on your back, press your lower back into the floor.
Lift your arms overhead and legs straight a little off the floor.
steps: Hold the hollow shape.
Rock gently from shoulders to hips without losing the shape.
cues: Lower back glued down
Arms by the ears
mistakes: Bending at the hips to rock
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and steadily through the hold; do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Exercise Ball Pull-In
exercises.description: Exercise Ball Pull-In is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the jack knife (suspension): shins on a ball in a push-up position; roll the ball in with the knees.
setup: Place an exercise ball nearby and lay on the floor in front of it with your hands on the floor shoulder width apart in a push-up position.
steps: Now place your lower shins on top of an exercise ball. Tip: At this point your legs should be fully extended with the shins on top of the ball and the upper body should be in a push-up type of position being supported by your two extended arms in front of you. This will be your starting position.

While keeping your back completely straight and the upper body stationary, pull your knees in towards your chest as you exhale, allowing the ball to roll forward under your ankles. Squeeze your abs and hold that position for a second.
Now slowly straighten your legs, rolling the ball back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Hips stay level at the plank
Pull with the abs
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as the knees come in.
variation_notes: Shins on a ball in a push-up position; roll the ball in with the knees.

exercises.name: Jack Knife (Suspension)
exercises.description: In a high plank with your feet in suspension straps, pulling your knees toward your chest.
setup: Place your feet in the straps and get into a high plank, hands under shoulders.
steps: Pull your knees toward your chest.
Extend the legs back to the plank.
cues: Hips stay level at the plank
Pull with the abs
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as the knees come in.

exercises.name: Jackknife Sit Up
exercises.description: Lying flat, you lift arms and legs at the same time to meet above your hips, folding like a jackknife.
setup: Lie flat with arms extended overhead and legs straight.
steps: Lift your legs and upper body together, reaching your hands toward your feet.
Lower both back down with control.
cues: Move arms and legs together
Lower slowly
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Around the World
exercises.description: Passing a kettlebell around your body from hand to hand while keeping the torso still.
setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand in front of you.
steps: Pass the kettlebell behind your back to the other hand.
Bring it around the front and keep circling.
Switch direction halfway through the set.
cues: Hips and shoulders stay facing forward
Brace the core
mistakes: Dropping the bell during the hand-off
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily; do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Figure 8
exercises.description: Kettlebell Figure 8 is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the hamstrings.
steps: Place one kettlebell between your legs and take a wider than shoulder width stance. Bend over by pushing your butt out and keeping your back flat.
Pick up a kettlebell and pass it to your other hand between your legs. The receiving hand should reach from behind the legs. Go back and forth for several repetitions.
cues: Hinge with a flat back, knees soft
Pass the kettlebell hand to hand between the legs
Keep the chest up and the movement controlled
mistakes: Dropping the kettlebell during the hand-off
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Pass Between The Legs
exercises.description: Kettlebell Pass Between The Legs is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the glutes and hamstrings.
steps: Place one kettlebell between your legs and take a comfortable stance. Bend over by pushing your butt out and keeping your back flat.
Pick up a kettlebell and pass it to your other hand between your legs, in the fashion of a "W". Go back and forth for several repetitions.
cues: Hinge with a flat back, knees soft
Pass the kettlebell hand to hand between the legs
Keep the chest up and the movement controlled
mistakes: Dropping the kettlebell during the hand-off
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Advanced Kettlebell Windmill
exercises.description: Advanced Kettlebell Windmill is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the glutes and hamstrings.
setup: Clean and press a kettlebell overhead with one arm.
steps: Keeping the kettlebell locked out at all times, push your butt out in the direction of the locked out kettlebell. Keep the non-working arm behind your back and turn your feet out at a forty-five degree angle from the arm with the kettlebell.
Lower yourself as far as possible.
Pause for a second and reverse the motion back to the starting position.
cues: Keep the weighted arm locked and vertical; watch the kettlebell
Push the hips out to the side of the weighted arm
Slide the free hand down the inside of the front leg
Back stays long; the hinge comes from the hip
mistakes: Bending the elbow of the weighted arm
Rounding the back to reach lower
exercises.breathing: Inhale at the top, exhale slowly as you lower, inhale at the bottom and exhale as you come back up.
safety: Learn it with no weight first; it needs good shoulder stability.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Windmill
exercises.description: Double Kettlebell Windmill is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the glutes, hamstrings and triceps.
setup: Place a kettlebell in front of your front foot and clean and press a kettlebell overhead with your opposite arm. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrist as you do so, so that the palm faces forward.
steps: Keeping the kettlebell locked out at all times, push your butt out in the direction of the locked out kettlebell. Turn your feet out at a forty-five degree angle from the arm with the locked out kettlebell.
Bending at the hip to one side, sticking your butt out, slowly lean until you can retrieve the kettlebell from the floor. Keep your eyes on the kettlebell that you hold over your head at all times.
Pause for a second after retrieving the kettlebell from the ground and reverse the motion back to the starting position.
cues: Keep the weighted arm locked and vertical; watch the kettlebell
Push the hips out to the side of the weighted arm
Slide the free hand down the inside of the front leg
Back stays long; the hinge comes from the hip
mistakes: Bending the elbow of the weighted arm
Rounding the back to reach lower
exercises.breathing: Inhale at the top, exhale slowly as you lower, inhale at the bottom and exhale as you come back up.
safety: Learn it with no weight first; it needs good shoulder stability.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Windmill
exercises.description: Kettlebell Windmill is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the glutes, hamstrings and triceps.
setup: Place a kettlebell in front of your lead foot and clean and press it overhead with your opposite arm. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrist as you do so, so that the palm faces forward. Press it overhead by extending the elbow.
steps: Keeping the kettlebell locked out at all times, push your butt out in the direction of the locked out kettlebell. Turn your feet out at a forty-five degree angle from the arm with the locked out kettlebell. Bending at the hip to one side, sticking your butt out, slowly lean until you can touch the floor with your free hand. Keep your eyes on the kettlebell that you hold over your head at all times.
Pause for a second after reaching the ground and reverse the motion back to the starting position.
cues: Keep the weighted arm locked and vertical; watch the kettlebell
Push the hips out to the side of the weighted arm
Slide the free hand down the inside of the front leg
Back stays long; the hinge comes from the hip
mistakes: Bending the elbow of the weighted arm
Rounding the back to reach lower
exercises.breathing: Inhale at the top, exhale slowly as you lower, inhale at the bottom and exhale as you come back up.
safety: Learn it with no weight first; it needs good shoulder stability.

exercises.name: Knee Raise Parallel Bars
exercises.description: Supporting yourself on your forearms on a captain's chair or parallel bars and raising your knees.
setup: Support yourself on the forearm pads with back against the pad and legs hanging.
steps: Raise your knees toward your chest, curling the pelvis.
Lower slowly.
cues: Back stays against the pad
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as the knees rise.

exercises.name: L-Sit Hold
exercises.description: Supporting yourself on straight arms with legs held straight out in front, forming an L.
setup: Support yourself on parallel bars, parallettes or the floor with straight arms.
steps: Lift your straight legs until they are parallel to the floor.
Hold.
cues: Push the shoulders down
Point the toes
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and steadily through the hold; do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Landmine 180
exercises.description: Holding the end of a landmine bar overhead with straight arms and swinging it in an arc from one hip to the other.
setup: Stand facing the end of a landmine bar holding it with both hands at arm's length above your head.
steps: Rotate the bar down to one hip in an arc, pivoting the feet.
Bring it back up through the middle and down to the other hip.
cues: Arms stay straight
Control the arc
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you rotate to each side.
safety: Start with an empty bar.

exercises.name: Leg Raise Parallel Bars
exercises.description: The straight-leg version of the parallel bar raise, lifting the legs to hip height or above.
setup: Support yourself on the forearm pads with back against the pad.
steps: Raise your straight legs to hip height or above.
Lower slowly.
cues: Keep the legs straight
Back against the pad
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as the legs rise.

exercises.name: Bent-Knee Hip Raise
aliases: Lying Knee Raise (Bent Knee Hip Raise)
exercises.description: Bent-Knee Hip Raise is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the lying knee raise: knees bent; curl the hips off the floor at the top.
setup: Lay flat on the floor with your arms next to your sides.
steps: Now bend your knees at around a 75 degree angle and lift your feet off the floor by around 2 inches.

Using your lower abs, bring your knees in towards you as you maintain the 75 degree angle bend in your legs. Continue this movement until you raise your hips off of the floor by rolling your pelvis backward. Breathe out as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: At the end of the movement your knees will be over your chest.
Squeeze your abs at the top of the movement for a second and then return to the starting position slowly as you breathe in. Tip: Maintain a controlled motion at all times.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Lower back stays down
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as the knees come in.
variation_notes: Knees bent; curl the hips off the floor at the top.
search_terms: lying knee raise (bent knee hip raise)

exercises.name: Flat Bench Leg Pull-In
exercises.description: Flat Bench Leg Pull-In is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the lying knee raise: on the end of a bench, legs straighten out and pull back in.
setup: Lie on an exercise mat or a flat bench with your legs off the end.
steps: Place your hands either under your glutes with your palms down or by the sides holding on to the bench (or with palms down by the side on an exercise mat). Also extend your legs straight out. This will be your starting position.
Bend your knees and pull your upper thighs into your midsection as you breathe out. Continue this movement until your knees are near your chest. Hold the contracted position for a second.
As you breathe in, slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Lower back stays down
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as the knees come in.
variation_notes: On the end of a bench, legs straighten out and pull back in.

exercises.name: Leg Pull-In
exercises.description: Leg Pull-In is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the lying knee raise: on the floor, legs straighten out and pull back in.
setup: Lie on an exercise mat with your legs extended and your hands either palms facing down next to you or under your glutes. Tip: My preference is with the hands next to me. This will be your starting position.
steps: Bend your knees and pull your upper thighs into your midsection as you breathe out. Continue the motion until your knees are around chest level. Contract your abs as you execute this movement and hold for a second at the top. Tip: As you perform the motion, the lower legs (calves) should always remain parallel to the floor.
Return to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Lower back stays down
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as the knees come in.
variation_notes: On the floor, legs straighten out and pull back in.

exercises.name: Lying Knee Raise
exercises.description: Lying on your back and pulling bent knees toward your chest. An easier version of the leg raise.
setup: Lie on your back with legs straight and slightly lifted.
steps: Bend your knees and pull them toward your chest.
Extend the legs back out without touching the floor.
cues: Lower back stays down
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as the knees come in.

exercises.name: Seated Flat Bench Leg Pull-In
exercises.description: Seated Flat Bench Leg Pull-In is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the lying knee raise: seated on the edge of a bench, leaning back.
setup: Sit on a bench with the legs stretched out in front of you slightly below parallel and your arms holding on to the sides of the bench. Your torso should be leaning backwards around a 45-degree angle from the bench. This will be your starting position.
steps: Bring the knees in toward you as you move your torso closer to them at the same time. Breathe out as you perform this movement.
After a second pause, go back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Lower back stays down
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as the knees come in.
variation_notes: Seated on the edge of a bench, leaning back.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Tucks
exercises.description: Seated Leg Tucks is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the lying knee raise: seated, lean back and tuck the knees toward the chest.
setup: Sit on a bench with the legs stretched out in front of you slightly below parallel and your arms holding on to the sides of the bench. Your torso should be leaning backwards around a 45-degree angle from the bench. This will be your starting position.
steps: Bring the knees in toward you as you move your torso closer to them at the same time. Breathe out as you perform this movement.
After a second pause, go back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Lower back stays down
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as the knees come in.
variation_notes: Seated, lean back and tuck the knees toward the chest.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Raise
exercises.description: Lying on your back and raising straight legs up to vertical while the lower back stays on the floor.
setup: Lie flat on your back with legs straight, hands under your hips or beside you.
steps: Raise your straight legs until they point at the ceiling.
Lower them slowly, stopping before your lower back lifts off the floor.
cues: Lower back stays pressed down
Slow on the way down
mistakes: Arching the back as the legs lower
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the legs, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Full Twist
exercises.description: Medicine Ball Full Twist is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the abs & core.
setup: For this exercise you will need a medicine ball and a partner. Stand back to back with your partner, spaced 2-3 feet apart. This will be your starting position.
steps: Hold the ball in front of the trunk. Open the hips and turn the shoulders at the same time as your partner.
For full rotation, you and your partner should twist in the same direction, i.e. counter-clockwise.
Pass the ball to your partner, and both of you can now twist in the opposite direction to repeat the procedure.
cues: Use the legs and hips first, the arms last
Throw as hard as you can; every rep is maximal
Use a light ball (2–5 kg) you can move fast
Reset fully between throws
mistakes: Using a ball too heavy to move quickly
Rounding the back when picking up or catching
exercises.breathing: Inhale as you load, exhale forcefully as you release the ball.
safety: Throw against a solid wall or into open space, never toward people.

exercises.name: Supine One-Arm Overhead Throw
exercises.description: Supine One-Arm Overhead Throw is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the chest and lats.
setup: Lay on the ground on your back with your knees bent. Hold the ball with one hand, extending the arm fully behind your head. This will be your starting position.
steps: Initiate the movement at the shoulder, throwing the ball directly forward of you as you sit up, attempting to go for maximum distance.
The ball can be thrown to a partner or bounced off of a wall.
cues: Use the legs and hips first, the arms last
Throw as hard as you can; every rep is maximal
Use a light ball (2–5 kg) you can move fast
Reset fully between throws
mistakes: Using a ball too heavy to move quickly
Rounding the back when picking up or catching
exercises.breathing: Inhale as you load, exhale forcefully as you release the ball.
safety: Throw against a solid wall or into open space, never toward people.

exercises.name: Supine Two-Arm Overhead Throw
exercises.description: Supine Two-Arm Overhead Throw is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the chest and lats.
setup: Lay on the ground on your back with your knees bent.
steps: Hold the ball with both hands, extending the arms fully behind your head. This will be your starting position.
Initiate the movement at the shoulder, throwing the ball directly forward of you as you sit up, attempting to go for maximum distance.
The ball can be thrown to a partner or bounced off of a wall.
cues: Use the legs and hips first, the arms last
Throw as hard as you can; every rep is maximal
Use a light ball (2–5 kg) you can move fast
Reset fully between throws
mistakes: Using a ball too heavy to move quickly
Rounding the back when picking up or catching
exercises.breathing: Inhale as you load, exhale forcefully as you release the ball.
safety: Throw against a solid wall or into open space, never toward people.

exercises.name: Mountain Climber
exercises.description: From a high plank, driving the knees toward the chest one after the other at a fast pace.
setup: Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders.
steps: Drive one knee toward your chest.
Switch legs quickly, as if running in place.
cues: Hips stay low and level
Shoulders over the hands
exercises.breathing: Breathe rhythmically; do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Pallof Press With Rotation
exercises.description: Pallof Press With Rotation is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the chest and triceps.
setup: Connect a standard handle to a tower, and position the cable to shoulder height.
steps: With your side to the cable, grab the handle with one hand and step away from the tower. You should be approximately arm's length away from the pulley, with the tension of the weight on the cable. Align outstretched arm with cable.
With your feet positioned hip-width apart, pull the cable into your chest and grab the handle with your other hand. Both hands should be on the handle at this time.
Facing forward, press the cable away from your chest. You core should be tight and engaged.
Keeping your hips straight, twist your torso away from the pulley until you get a full quarter rotation.
Maintain your rigid stance and straight arms. Return to the neutral position in a slow and controlled manner. Your arms should be extended in front of you.
With the side tension still engaging your core, bring your hands to your chest and immediately press outward to a fully extended position. This constitutes one rep.
Repeat to failure.
Then, reposition and repeat the same series of movements on the opposite side.
cues: Press the handle out, then rotate away from the cable with control
Hips stay square
Return slowly
mistakes: Bending the arms during the turn
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.description: Holding a straight body position on your forearms and toes. Builds core stability.
setup: Place your forearms on the floor, elbows under the shoulders.
Step your feet back so your body forms a straight line.
steps: Brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes.
Hold the position for the target time.
cues: Tuck the pelvis slightly; ribs down
Push the floor away with the forearms
Straight line head to heels
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and steadily through the hold; do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Intermediate Hip Flexor and Quad Stretch
exercises.variation: Intermediate Hip Flexor and Quad Stretch
exercises.description: Intermediate Hip Flexor and Quad Stretch is an intermediate-level stretch that mainly targets the abs & core.
steps: Lie face down on the floor, with a rope, belt, or band looped around one foot.

Flex the knee and extend the hip of the leg to be stretched, using both hands to pull on the belt. Your knee and your hip should come off of the floor, creating tension in the hip flexors and quadriceps. Hold the stretch for 10-20 seconds, and repeat on the other leg.
cues: Tuck the pelvis under and squeeze the glute on the stretching side
Keep the knees close together for the quad stretch
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Arching the lower back instead of tucking the pelvis
Pulling the knee out to the side
Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.
