exercises.name: Kneeling Hip Flexor
exercises.description: Kneeling Hip Flexor is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the quadriceps.
steps: Kneel on a mat and bring your right knee up so the bottom of your foot is on the floor and extend your left leg out behind you so the top of your foot is on the floor.
Shift your weight forward until you feel a stretch in your hip. Hold for 15 seconds, then repeat for your other side.
cues: Tuck the pelvis under and squeeze the glute on the stretching side
Keep the knees close together for the quad stretch
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Arching the lower back instead of tucking the pelvis
Pulling the knee out to the side
Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Flexors
exercises.description: Standing Hip Flexors is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the abs & core.
steps: Stand up straight with the spine vertical, the left foot slightly in front of the right.

Bend both knees and lift the back heel off the floor as you press the right hip forward. You can't get a thorough, deep stretch in this position, however, because it's hard to relax the hip flexor and stand on it at the same time. Switch sides.
cues: Tuck the pelvis under and squeeze the glute on the stretching side
Keep the knees close together for the quad stretch
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Arching the lower back instead of tucking the pelvis
Pulling the knee out to the side
Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Bottoms Up
exercises.description: Bottoms Up is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the reverse crunch: legs start straight up; lift the hips off the floor toward the ceiling.
setup: Begin by lying on your back on the ground. Your legs should be straight and your arms at your side. This will be your starting position.
steps: To perform the movement, tuck the knees toward your chest by flexing the hips and knees. Following this, extend your legs directly above you so that they are perpendicular to the ground. Rotate and elevate your pelvis to raise your glutes from the floor.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
cues: Curl the pelvis, do not just swing the legs
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Legs start straight up; lift the hips off the floor toward the ceiling.

exercises.name: Cable Reverse Crunch
exercises.description: Cable Reverse Crunch is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the reverse crunch: a low cable attached to the ankles adds resistance.
setup: Connect an ankle strap attachment to a low pulley cable and position a mat on the floor in front of it.
steps: Sit down with your feet toward the pulley and attach the cable to your ankles.
Lie down, elevate your legs and bend your knees at a 90-degree angle. Your legs and the cable should be aligned. If not, adjust the pulley up or down until they are.
With your hands behind your head, bring your knees inward to your torso and elevate your hips off the floor.
Pause for a moment and in a slow and controlled manner drop your hips and bring your legs back to the starting 90-degree angle. You should still have tension on your abs in the resting position.
Repeat the same movement to failure.
cues: Curl the pelvis, do not just swing the legs
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: A low cable attached to the ankles adds resistance.

exercises.name: Decline Reverse Crunch
exercises.description: Decline Reverse Crunch is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the reverse crunch: a decline bench makes the hips lift against more gravity.
setup: Lie on your back on a decline bench and hold on to the top of the bench with both hands. Don't let your body slip down from this position.
steps: Hold your legs parallel to the floor using your abs to hold them there while keeping your knees and feet together. Tip: Your legs should be fully extended with a slight bend on the knee. This will be your starting position.
While exhaling, move your legs towards the torso as you roll your pelvis backwards and you raise your hips off the bench. At the end of this movement your knees will be touching your chest.
Hold the contraction for a second and move your legs back to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Curl the pelvis, do not just swing the legs
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: A decline bench makes the hips lift against more gravity.

exercises.name: Reverse Crunch
exercises.description: Lying on your back and curling the hips up off the floor, bringing your knees toward your chest.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent 90° and lifted, arms by your sides.
steps: Curl your hips off the floor, bringing your knees toward your chest.
Lower the hips slowly.
cues: Curl the pelvis, do not just swing the legs
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Suspended Reverse Crunch
exercises.description: Suspended Reverse Crunch is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the reverse crunch: feet in suspension straps from a plank position; pull the knees to the chest.
setup: Secure a set of suspension straps with the handles hanging about a foot off of the ground. Move yourself into a pushup plank position facing away from the rack.
steps: Place your feet into the handles. You should maintain a straight posture, not allowing the hips to sag. This will be your starting position.
Begin the movement by flexing the knees and hips, drawing the knees to your torso. As you do so, anteriorly tilt your pelvis, allowing your spine to flex.
At the top of the controlled motion, return to the starting position.
cues: Curl the pelvis, do not just swing the legs
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Feet in suspension straps from a plank position; pull the knees to the chest.

exercises.name: Cable Russian Twists
exercises.description: Cable Russian Twists is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the russian twist: seated beside a cable at chest height; rotate away from the stack.
setup: Connect a standard handle attachment, and position the cable to a middle pulley position.
steps: Lie on a stability ball perpendicular to the cable and grab the handle with one hand. You should be approximately arm's length away from the pulley, with the tension of the weight on the cable.
Grab the handle with both hands and fully extend your arms above your chest. You hands should be directly in-line with the pulley. If not, adjust the pulley up or down until they are.
Keep your hips elevated and abs engaged. Rotate your torso away from the pulley for a full-quarter rotation. Your body should be flat from head to knees.
Pause for a moment and in a slow and controlled manner reset to the starting position. You should still have side tension on the cable in the resting position.
Repeat the same movement to failure.
Then, reposition and repeat the same series of movements on the opposite side.
cues: Rotate the ribcage, not just the arms
Chest up
exercises.breathing: Breathe out with each rotation.
safety: Avoid if rotation under load bothers your lower back.
variation_notes: Seated beside a cable at chest height; rotate away from the stack.

exercises.name: Russian Twist (Bodyweight)
exercises.description: Sitting leaned back with feet lifted or on the floor, rotating the torso from side to side.
setup: Sit with knees bent and lean back to about 45°, back straight.
Lift your feet if you can keep the position.
steps: Rotate your torso to bring your hands beside one hip.
Rotate to the other side.
cues: Rotate the ribcage, not just the arms
Chest up
exercises.breathing: Breathe out with each rotation.
safety: Avoid if rotation under load bothers your lower back.

exercises.name: Russian Twist (Weighted)
exercises.description: Sitting leaned back with feet lifted or on the floor, rotating the torso from side to side.
setup: Sit with knees bent and lean back to about 45°, back straight.
Lift your feet if you can keep the position.
steps: Rotate your torso to bring your hands beside one hip.
Rotate to the other side.
cues: Rotate the ribcage, not just the arms
Chest up
exercises.breathing: Breathe out with each rotation.
safety: Avoid if rotation under load bothers your lower back.
variation_notes: Hold a plate, dumbbell or medicine ball at your chest.

exercises.name: Seated Barbell Twist
exercises.description: Seated Barbell Twist is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core.
setup: Start out by sitting at the end of a flat bench with a barbell placed on top of your thighs. Your feet should be shoulder width apart from each other.
steps: Grip the bar with your palms facing down and make sure your hands are wider than shoulder width apart from each other. Begin to lift the barbell up over your head until your arms are fully extended.
Now lower the barbell behind your head until it is resting along the base of your neck. This is the starting position.

While keeping your feet and head stationary, move your waist from side to side so that your oblique muscles feel the contraction. Only move from side to side as far as your waist will allow you to go. Stretching or moving too far can cause an injury to occur. Tip: Use a slow and controlled motion.
Remember to breathe out while twisting your body to the side and in when moving back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Sit tall with the bar across the shoulders
Rotate side to side from the ribs
Use a light bar and a smooth pace
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Shoulder Taps
exercises.description: Tapping each shoulder in turn from a high plank while keeping the hips still.
setup: Get into a high plank with hands under your shoulders and feet slightly wider than hips.
steps: Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder.
Return it to the floor and repeat with the other hand.
cues: Hips stay level; imagine a glass of water on your back
Squeeze the glutes
mistakes: Rocking the hips side to side
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily, out with each tap.

exercises.name: Barbell Side Bend
exercises.description: Barbell Side Bend is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the lower back. A variation of the side bend: bar on the back; bend straight to the side without leaning forward.
setup: Stand up straight while holding a barbell placed on the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck). Your feet should be shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.
steps: While keeping your back straight and your head up, bend only at the waist to the right as far as possible. Breathe in as you bend to the side. Then hold for a second and come back up to the starting position as you exhale. Tip: Keep the rest of the body stationary.
Now repeat the movement but bending to the left instead. Hold for a second and come back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Bend sideways, not forward
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you return to upright.
variation_notes: Bar on the back; bend straight to the side without leaning forward.

exercises.name: One-Arm High-Pulley Cable Side Bends
exercises.description: One-Arm High-Pulley Cable Side Bends is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the side bend: pulls down against a high pulley, working the side nearest the cable.
setup: Connect a standard handle to a tower. Move cable to highest pulley position.
steps: Stand with side to cable. With one hand, reach up and grab handle with underhand grip.
Pull down cable until elbow touches your side and the handle is by your shoulder.
Position feet hip-width apart. Place free hand on hip to help gauge pivot point.
Keep arm in static position. Contract oblique to bring the weight down in a side crunch.
Once you reach maximum contraction, slowly release the weight to the starting position. The weight stack should never be unloaded in a resting position. The aim is constant tension during the set.
Repeat to failure.
Then, reposition and repeat the same series of movements on the opposite side.
cues: Bend sideways, not forward
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you return to upright.
variation_notes: Pulls down against a high pulley, working the side nearest the cable.

exercises.name: Side Bend
exercises.description: Standing and bending sideways at the waist to work the obliques.
setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
steps: Bend directly to one side, sliding your hand down your leg.
Return to upright using the opposite side of your waist.
cues: Bend sideways, not forward
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you return to upright.

exercises.name: Side Bend (Dumbbell)
exercises.description: Standing and bending sideways at the waist to work the obliques.
setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
steps: Bend directly to one side, sliding your hand down your leg.
Return to upright using the opposite side of your waist.
cues: Bend sideways, not forward
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you return to upright.
variation_notes: Hold one dumbbell; bend toward it and return using the opposite obliques.

exercises.name: Weighted Ball Side Bend
exercises.description: Weighted Ball Side Bend is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the side bend: lying sideways over a ball, holding a weight.
setup: To begin, lie down on an exercise ball with your left side of the torso (waist, hips and shoulder) pressed against the ball.
steps: Your feet should be on the floor while your legs are crossed and hanging from the ball. Hold a weighted plate with your right hand directly to the right side of your head. Tip: Make sure the smooth side of the plate is resting against your head.
Place your left arm across your torso so that your palm is on your obliques. There should be a right angle between your left forearm and upper arm. This is the starting position.
Raise the side of your torso up by laterally flexing at the waist while exhaling.
Hold the contraction for a second and slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Switch sides and repeat the exercise.
cues: Bend sideways, not forward
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you return to upright.
variation_notes: Lying sideways over a ball, holding a weight.

exercises.name: Side Jackknife
exercises.description: Side Jackknife is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core.
setup: Lie on your side with legs straight and stacked. Place the lower arm on the floor in front of you for balance and the top hand behind your head.
steps: Squeeze the side of your waist to lift your legs and upper body off the floor at the same time, bringing the top elbow towards the hip.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower slowly back to the start.
Complete the set, then switch sides.
cues: Legs and upper body lift together
Lead with the side of the ribs, not the elbow
Lower slowly
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.description: Holding your body straight on one forearm and the side of your foot, working the sides of the core.
setup: Lie on your side with your elbow under your shoulder and legs stacked.
steps: Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line.
Hold, then switch sides.
cues: Hips high and forward
Shoulder over elbow
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and steadily through the hold; do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: 3/4 Sit-Up
exercises.description: 3/4 Sit-Up is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the sit up: stop when the torso is about 45 degrees up so the abs never get a rest at the top.
setup: Lie down on the floor and secure your feet. Your legs should be bent at the knees.
steps: Place your hands behind or to the side of your head. You will begin with your back on the ground. This will be your starting position.
Flex your hips and spine to raise your torso toward your knees.
At the top of the contraction your torso should be perpendicular to the ground. Reverse the motion, going only ¾ of the way down.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Curl up, do not jerk
Control the way down
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Stop when the torso is about 45 degrees up so the abs never get a rest at the top.

exercises.name: Frog Sit-Ups
exercises.description: Frog Sit-Ups is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the sit up: soles of the feet together and knees out, which takes the hip flexors out of the movement.
setup: Lie with your back flat on the floor (or exercise mat) and your legs extended in front of you.
steps: Now bend at the knees and place your outer thighs by the floor (or mat) as you make the soles of your feet touch each other.

Now try pushing both soles and bringing them up as near you as possible while you keep the outer thighs on the floor (or at least almost touching it). Tip: In this position your legs should create a diamond shape.
Now, cross your arms in front of you by touching the opposite shoulders. This will be your starting position.
As you exhale flatten your lower back to the floor while curling the torso upwards. Tip: This will be like performing the first 1/4 movement of a sit up. Hold at the top position for a second.
As you inhale, slowly lower back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Curl up, do not jerk
Control the way down
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Soles of the feet together and knees out, which takes the hip flexors out of the movement.

exercises.name: Janda Sit-Up
exercises.description: Janda Sit-Up is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the sit up: press the heels down into the floor to switch off the hip flexors, so the abs do the work. Small range.
setup: Position your body on the floor in the basic sit-up position; knees to a ninety degree angle with feet flat on the floor and arms either crossed over your chest or to the sides. This will be your starting position.
steps: As you strongly tighten your glutes and hamstrings, fill your lungs with air and in a slow (three to six second count) ascent, slowly exhale. Tip: It is important to tighten the glutes and hamstrings as this will cause the hip flexors to be inactivated in a process called reciprocal inhibition, which basically means that opposite muscles to the contracted ones will relax.
As you inhale, slowly go back in a controlled manner to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Curl up, do not jerk
Control the way down
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Press the heels down into the floor to switch off the hip flexors, so the abs do the work. Small range.

exercises.name: Otis-Up
exercises.description: Otis-Up is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the chest and triceps. A variation of the sit up: holds a weight plate at the chest on the way up and presses it overhead at the top.
setup: Secure your feet and lay back on the floor. Your knees should be bent. Hold a weight with both hands to your chest. This will be your starting position.
steps: Initiate the movement by flexing the hips and spine to raise your torso up from the ground.
As you move up, press the weight up so that it is above your head at the top of the movement.
Return the weight to your chest as you reverse the sit-up motion, ensuring not to go all the way down to the floor.
cues: Curl up, do not jerk
Control the way down
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Holds a weight plate at the chest on the way up and presses it overhead at the top.

exercises.name: Press Sit-Up
exercises.description: Press Sit-Up is an advanced-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the chest and triceps. A variation of the sit up: holds a light barbell at the chest on the way up and presses it at the top.
setup: To begin, lie down on a bench with a barbell resting on your chest. Position your legs so they are secure on the extension of the abdominal bench. This is the starting position.
steps: While inhaling, tighten your abdominals and glutes. Simultaneously curl your torso as you do when performing a sit-up and press the barbell to an overhead position while exhaling. Tip: Use your arms to push the barbell out as you perform this exercise while still focusing on the abdominal muscles.
Lower your upper body back down to the starting position while bringing the barbell back down to your torso. Remember to breathe in while lowering the body.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Curl up, do not jerk
Control the way down
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Holds a light barbell at the chest on the way up and presses it at the top.

exercises.name: Sit Up
exercises.description: Curling all the way up from lying on your back to sitting upright.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat (anchored if needed).
steps: Curl up one vertebra at a time until you are sitting upright.
Lower back down slowly.
cues: Curl up, do not jerk
Control the way down
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Sit Up (Weighted)
exercises.description: Curling all the way up from lying on your back to sitting upright.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat (anchored if needed).
steps: Curl up one vertebra at a time until you are sitting upright.
Lower back down slowly.
cues: Curl up, do not jerk
Control the way down
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Hold a plate on your chest or above your head.

exercises.name: Weighted Sit-Ups - With Bands
exercises.description: Weighted Sit-Ups - With Bands is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the sit up: a band anchored behind you adds resistance at the top.
setup: Start out by strapping the bands around the base of the decline bench. Place the handles towards the inside of the decline bench so that when lying down, you can reach for both of them.
steps: Position your legs through the decline machine until they are secured. Now reach for the exercise bands with both hands. Use a pronated (palms forward) grip to grasp the handles. Position them near your collar bone and rotate your wrist to a neutral grip (palms facing the torso). Note: Your arms should remain stationary throughout the exercise. This is the starting position.

Move your torso upward until your upper body is perpendicular to the floor while exhaling. Hold the contraction for a second and lower your upper body back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Curl up, do not jerk
Control the way down
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: A band anchored behind you adds resistance at the top.

exercises.name: Sledgehammer Swings
exercises.description: Sledgehammer Swings is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the calves, forearms, lats and upper back.
setup: You will need a tire and a sledgehammer for this exercise. Stand in front of the tire about two feet away from it with a staggered stance. Grip the sledgehammer.
steps: If you are right handed, your left hand should be at the bottom of the handle, and your right hand should be choking up closer to the head.

As you bring the sledge up, your right hand slides toward the head; as you swing down, your right hand will slide down to join your left hand. Slam it down as hard as you can against the tire. Control the bounce of the hammer off of the tire.
Repeat on the other side.
cues: Slide the top hand down the handle as you swing
Use the hips and legs to drive the hammer
Alternate sides
exercises.breathing: Inhale and brace before you start the movement, keep the brace through the hardest part, then exhale at the top.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Hip Raise
exercises.description: Smith Machine Hip Raise is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core.
setup: Position a bench in the rack and load the bar to an appropriate weight. Lie down on the bench, placing the bottom of your feet against the bar. Unlock the bar and extend your legs. You may need to use your hands to assist you. For added stability grasp the sides of the Smith Machine. This will be your starting position.
steps: Initiate the movement by rotating your pelvis, flexing your spine to raise your hips off of the bench. Maintain a slight bend in the knees throughout the motion.
After a brief pause, return the hips to the bench.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
cues: Feet press the bar up overhead
Curl the hips off the bench to raise the bar
Lower slowly
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Spell Caster
exercises.description: Spell Caster is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core, with help from the glutes.
setup: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated grip. Your feet should be wide with your hips and knees extended. This will be your starting position.
steps: Begin the movement by pulling both of the dumbbells to one side next to your hip, rotating your torso.
Keeping your arms straight and the dumbbells parallel to the ground, rotate your torso to swing the weights to your opposite side.
Continue alternating, rotating from one side to the other until the set is complete.
cues: Hips and legs stay still
Swing the dumbbells across the body with control
Rotate from the ribs
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Spiderman
exercises.description: From a plank, bringing one knee out to the side toward the elbow on the same side.
setup: Start in a high or forearm plank.
steps: Bring one knee out to the side toward the same-side elbow.
Return and switch sides.
cues: Keep the hips low
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as the knee comes forward.

exercises.name: Wind Sprints
exercises.description: Wind Sprints is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abs & core. A variation of the sprints: short sprints with walking recovery.
setup: Hang from a pull-up bar using a pronated grip. Your arms and legs should be extended. This will be your starting position.
steps: Begin by quickly raising one knee as high as you can. Do not swing your body or your legs. 3
Immediately reverse the motion, returning that leg to the starting position. Simultaneously raise the opposite knee as high as possible.
Continue alternating between legs until the set is complete.
cues: Drive the knees and arms
Run tall
exercises.breathing: Match your breathing to the effort. At an easy pace you should be able to talk in full sentences; at hard efforts breathe deeply and rhythmically through the mouth.
safety: Hamstring strains are common in sprinting; warm up well and build up the number of sprints slowly.
variation_notes: Short sprints with walking recovery.

exercises.name: Stomach Vacuum
exercises.description: Stomach Vacuum is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the abs & core.
setup: To begin, stand straight with your feet shoulder width apart from each other. Place your hands on your hips. This is the starting position.
steps: Now slowly inhale as much air as possible and then start to exhale as much as possible while bringing your stomach in as much as possible and hold this position. Try to visualize your navel touching your backbone.
One isometric contraction is around 20 seconds. During the 20 second hold, try to breathe normally. Then inhale and bring your stomach back to the starting position.
Once you have practiced this exercise, try to perform this exercise for longer than 20 seconds. Tip: You can work your way up to 40-60 seconds.
Repeat for the recommended amount of sets.
cues: Exhale completely
Pull the belly button in toward the spine and hold
Hold 10–20 seconds, then breathe
mistakes: Sucking the chest up instead of the belly in
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry (Dumbbell)
exercises.description: Walking with a heavy weight in one hand, resisting the pull to lean to that side.
setup: Pick up one heavy dumbbell or kettlebell at your side like a suitcase.
steps: Stand tall with shoulders level.
Walk the set distance.
Switch hands and repeat.
cues: Shoulders and hips stay level
mistakes: Leaning away from or toward the weight
exercises.breathing: Breathe in short, controlled breaths while staying braced.

exercises.name: Toe Touch
exercises.description: Lying with legs straight up in the air, you crunch up to reach your hands toward your toes.
setup: Lie on your back with legs pointing straight up.
steps: Crunch up and reach your hands toward your toes.
Lower your shoulders back down.
cues: Legs stay vertical
Reach up, not forward
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Toes to Bar
exercises.description: Hanging from a bar and raising your feet all the way up to touch the bar.
setup: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip.
steps: Press the bar down slightly with straight arms and raise your feet to touch the bar.
Lower with control.
cues: Push the bar away to help lift the hips
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as your feet rise.

exercises.name: Torso Rotation
exercises.description: A seated machine where you rotate your torso against resistance.
setup: Sit in the machine and set the starting angle.
Hold the handles or pads in front of your chest.
steps: Rotate your torso to the side against the resistance.
Return slowly; finish all reps, then switch sides.
cues: Rotate from the ribs, hips stay put
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you rotate.

exercises.name: V Up
exercises.description: Lifting straight legs and torso at the same time to touch your toes, forming a V shape.
setup: Lie flat with arms overhead and legs straight together.
steps: Raise your straight legs and torso at the same time.
Reach for your toes at the top, balancing on your hips.
Lower slowly.
cues: Keep the legs straight
Control the lowering
mistakes: Arching the lower back on the way down
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and squeeze the abs, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Windmills
exercises.description: Windmills is an intermediate-level stretch that mainly targets the abductors, with help from the glutes, hamstrings and lower back.
setup: Lie on your back with your arms extended out to the sides and your legs straight. This will be your starting position.
steps: Lift one leg and quickly cross it over your body, attempting to touch the ground near the opposite hand.
Return to the starting position, and repeat with the opposite leg. Continue to alternate for 10-20 repetitions.
cues: Keep the shoulders down away from the ears
Keep the ribs down; do not arch the back to fake the range
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Clamshell
exercises.description: Lying on your side with knees bent, you open the top knee like a clam shell.
setup: Lie on your side, hips and knees bent about 45°, feet together.
Place a band above the knees if you want more resistance.
steps: Keeping the feet together, lift the top knee as high as you can without rolling the hips.
Lower slowly.
cues: Hips stacked; do not roll back
mistakes: Rolling the pelvis to lift higher
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you open, breathe in as you close.

exercises.name: Hip Circles (prone)
exercises.description: Hip Circles (prone) is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the abductors, with help from the adductors.
setup: Position yourself on your hands and knees on the ground. Maintaining good posture, raise one bent knee off of the ground. This will be your starting position.
steps: Keeping the knee in a bent position, rotate the femur in an arc, attempting to make a big circle with your knee.
Perform this slowly for a number of repetitions, and repeat on the other side.
cues: Start small and slow, then grow the range
Smooth, controlled movement, no flinging
About 8–12 reps per side as a warm-up
mistakes: Swinging into end range with momentum
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Circles
exercises.description: Standing Hip Circles is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the abductors, with help from the adductors.
setup: Begin standing on one leg, holding to a vertical support.
steps: Raise the unsupported knee to 90 degrees. This will be your starting position.
Open the hip as far as possible, attempting to make a big circle with your knee.
Perform this movement slowly for a number of repetitions, and repeat on the other side.
cues: Start small and slow, then grow the range
Smooth, controlled movement, no flinging
About 8–12 reps per side as a warm-up
mistakes: Swinging into end range with momentum
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Fire Hydrants
exercises.description: On hands and knees, you lift one bent leg out to the side.
setup: Start on hands and knees, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
steps: Lift one knee out to the side, keeping it bent 90°.
Lower slowly.
cues: Keep the torso still
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you lift, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Iliotibial Tract-SMR
exercises.description: Iliotibial Tract-SMR is an intermediate-level self-massage (foam rolling) exercise that mainly targets the abductors.
setup: Lay on your side, with the bottom leg placed onto a foam roller between the hip and the knee. The other leg can be crossed in front of you.
steps: Place as much of your weight as is tolerable onto your bottom leg; there is no need to keep your bottom leg in contact with the ground. Be sure to relax the muscles of the leg you are stretching.
Roll your leg over the foam from you hip to your knee, pausing for 10-30 seconds at points of tension. Repeat with the opposite leg.
cues: Roll slowly, about 2–3 cm per second
Pause 20–30 seconds on tender spots
Support your weight with hands and feet to control the pressure
30–90 seconds per area
mistakes: Rolling directly over joints or bones
Pressing so hard you tense up
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and stay relaxed. On a tender spot, pause and take a few long exhales to let the muscle release.
safety: Avoid rolling the lower back and neck with full body weight; use a softer tool there.

exercises.name: IT Band and Glute Stretch
exercises.description: IT Band and Glute Stretch is an intermediate-level stretch that mainly targets the abductors.
steps: Loop a belt, rope, or band around one of your feet, and swing that leg across your body to the opposite side, keeping the leg extended as you lay on the ground. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your foot off of the floor, pull on the belt, using the tension to pull the toes up. Hold for 10-20 seconds, and repeat on the other side.
cues: Keep the hips square and the lower back flat on the floor where lying
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Twisting the pelvis to fake the range
Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Lying Crossover
exercises.description: Lying Crossover is an advanced-level stretch that mainly targets the abductors.
setup: Lie on your back with your legs extended.
steps: Cross one leg over your body with the knee bent, attempting to touch the knee to the ground. Your partner should kneel beside you, holding your shoulder down with one hand and controlling the crossed leg with the other. this will be your starting position.
Attempt to raise the bent knee off of the ground as your partner prevents any actual movement.
After 10-20 seconds, relax the leg as your partner gently presses the knee towards the floor. Repeat with the other side.
cues: Keep the hips square and the lower back flat on the floor where lying
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Twisting the pelvis to fake the range
Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Hip Abduction (Cable)
exercises.description: Pushing the legs apart against resistance. Trains the side glutes that stabilise the hips and knees.
setup: Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley and stand side-on with the far leg strapped.
steps: Lift the strapped leg out to the side.
Return slowly across the front of the other leg.
cues: Slow on the way back
Lean slightly forward for more glute work
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you push out, breathe in as you return.

exercises.name: Hip Abduction (Machine)
exercises.description: Pushing the legs apart against resistance. Trains the side glutes that stabilise the hips and knees.
setup: Sit in the machine with the pads on the outside of your knees.
steps: Push your knees apart as far as is comfortable.
Pause, then return slowly.
cues: Slow on the way back
Lean slightly forward for more glute work
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you push out, breathe in as you return.

exercises.name: Lateral Band Walks
exercises.description: Stepping sideways with a band around the legs to work the side glutes.
setup: Place a mini band around your ankles or just above your knees.
Stand in a quarter squat with feet hip-width.
steps: Step sideways with one foot, keeping tension in the band.
Follow with the other foot without letting the feet touch.
Walk the set number of steps, then go back.
cues: Stay low
Toes forward
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily throughout.

exercises.name: Monster Walk
exercises.description: Monster Walk is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the abductors. A variation of the lateral band walks: walk forward and backward on diagonals instead of sideways.
setup: Place a band around both ankles and another around both knees. There should be enough tension that they are tight when your feet are shoulder width apart.
steps: To begin, take short steps forward alternating your left and right foot.
After several steps, do just the opposite and walk backward to where you started.
cues: Stay low
Toes forward
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily throughout.
variation_notes: Walk forward and backward on diagonals instead of sideways.

exercises.name: Lateral Leg Raises
exercises.description: Lying on your side and lifting the top leg straight up.
setup: Lie on your side with legs straight and stacked.
steps: Lift the top leg up with the toes pointing forward.
Lower slowly.
cues: Lead with the heel
Do not roll backward
mistakes: Turning the toes to the ceiling
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you lift, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Lateral Bound
exercises.description: Lateral Bound is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the adductors, with help from the abductors, calves, glutes, hamstrings and quadriceps.
setup: Assume a half squat position facing 90 degrees from your direction of travel. This will be your starting position.
steps: Allow your lead leg to do a countermovement inward as you shift your weight to the outside leg.
Immediately push off and extend, attempting to bound to the side as far as possible.
Upon landing, immediately push off in the opposite direction, returning to your original start position.
Continue back and forth for several repetitions.
cues: Load the hips and swing the arms back before each jump
Drive through the whole foot and extend the hips fully
Stick the landing with bent knees before the next rep
exercises.breathing: Take a quick breath before each effort and exhale sharply as you take off. Reset your breathing between reps.

exercises.name: Groiners
exercises.description: Groiners is an intermediate-level stretch that mainly targets the adductors.
setup: Begin in a pushup position on the floor. This will be your starting position.
steps: Using both legs, jump forward landing with your feet next to your hands. Keep your head up as you do so.
Return to the starting position and immediately repeat the movement, continuing for 10-20 repetitions.
cues: Start small and slow, then grow the range
Smooth, controlled movement, no flinging
About 8–12 reps per side as a warm-up
mistakes: Swinging into end range with momentum
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Side Leg Raises
exercises.description: Side Leg Raises is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the adductors.
setup: Stand next to a chair, which you may hold onto as a support. Stand on one leg. This will be your starting position.
steps: Keeping your leg straight, raise it as far out to the side as possible, and swing it back down, allowing it to cross the opposite leg.
Repeat this swinging motion 5-10 times, increasing the range of motion as you do so.
cues: Start small and slow, then grow the range
Smooth, controlled movement, no flinging
About 8–12 reps per side as a warm-up
mistakes: Swinging into end range with momentum
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Adductor
exercises.description: Adductor is an intermediate-level stretch that mainly targets the adductors.
setup: Lie face down with one leg on a foam roll.
steps: Rotate the leg so that the foam roll contacts against your inner thigh. Shift as much weight onto the foam roll as can be tolerated.
While trying to relax the muscles if the inner thigh, roll over the foam between your hip and knee, holding points of tension for 10-30 seconds. Repeat with the other leg.
cues: Roll slowly, about 2–3 cm per second
Pause 20–30 seconds on tender spots
Support your weight with hands and feet to control the pressure
30–90 seconds per area
mistakes: Rolling directly over joints or bones
Pressing so hard you tense up
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and stay relaxed. On a tender spot, pause and take a few long exhales to let the muscle release.
safety: Avoid rolling the lower back and neck with full body weight; use a softer tool there.

exercises.name: Adductor/Groin
exercises.description: Adductor/Groin is an intermediate-level stretch that mainly targets the adductors.
setup: Lie on your back with your feet raised towards the ceiling.
steps: Have your partner hold your feet or ankles. Abduct your legs as far as you can. This will be your starting position.
Attempt to squeeze your legs together for 10 or more seconds, while your partner prevents you from doing so.

Now, relax the muscles in your legs as your partner pushes your feet apart, stretching as far as is comfortable for you. Be sure to let your partner know when the stretch is adequate to prevent overstretching or injury.
cues: Let the knees fall out under their own weight before pressing gently
Sit tall with a long spine
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Groin and Back Stretch
exercises.description: Groin and Back Stretch is an intermediate-level stretch that mainly targets the adductors.
setup: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet together.
steps: Interlock your fingers behind your head. This will be your starting position.
Curl downwards, bringing your elbows to the inside of your thighs. After a brief pause, return to the starting position with your head up and your back straight. Repeat for 10-20 repetitions.
cues: Let the knees fall out under their own weight before pressing gently
Sit tall with a long spine
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Lying Bent Leg Groin
exercises.description: Lying Bent Leg Groin is an advanced-level stretch that mainly targets the adductors.
setup: Lie on your back with your knees bent and the soles of the feet pressed together. Have your partner hold your knees. This will be your starting position.
steps: Attempt to squeeze your knees together, while your partner prevents any movement from occurring.
After 10-20 seconds, relax your muscles as your partner gently pushes your knees towards the floor. Be sure to inform your helper when the stretch is adequate to prevent injury or overstretching.
cues: Let the knees fall out under their own weight before pressing gently
Sit tall with a long spine
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Side Lying Groin Stretch
exercises.description: Side Lying Groin Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the adductors, with help from the hamstrings.
setup: Start off by lying on your right side and bend your right knee in front of you to stabilize the torso.
steps: Rest your head on your right hand or shoulder. Lift your left leg upward and hold it by the back of the knee (easier) or the foot (harder).
Pull your left knee in toward your left shoulder and simultaneously press your foot or knee down to the floor. To intensify this stretch, straighten your left leg. Switch sides.
cues: Let the knees fall out under their own weight before pressing gently
Sit tall with a long spine
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Band Hip Adductions
exercises.description: Band Hip Adductions is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the adductors. A variation of the hip adduction: standing, a band at the ankle pulls the leg out; bring it in across the body.
setup: Anchor a band around a solid post or other object.
steps: Stand with your left side to the post, and put your right foot through the band, getting it around the ankle.
Stand up straight and hold onto the post if needed. This will be your starting position.
Keeping the knee straight, raise your right legs out to the side as far as you can.
Return to the starting position and repeat for the desired rep count.
Switch sides.
cues: Control the stretch on the way out
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you squeeze, breathe in as you open.
variation_notes: Standing, a band at the ankle pulls the leg out; bring it in across the body.

exercises.name: Hip Adduction (Cable)
exercises.description: Squeezing the legs together against resistance to train the inner thighs.
setup: Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley and stand side-on with the near leg strapped.
steps: Pull the strapped leg across in front of the other leg.
Return slowly.
cues: Control the stretch on the way out
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you squeeze, breathe in as you open.

exercises.name: Hip Adduction (Machine)
exercises.description: Squeezing the legs together against resistance to train the inner thighs.
setup: Sit in the machine with the pads on the inside of your knees.
steps: Squeeze your knees together.
Pause, then let them open slowly.
cues: Control the stretch on the way out
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you squeeze, breathe in as you open.

exercises.name: Lateral Cone Hops
exercises.description: Lateral Cone Hops is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the adductors, with help from the abductors, calves, glutes, hamstrings and quadriceps.
setup: Position a number of cones in a row several feet apart.
steps: Stand next to the end of the cones, facing 90 degrees to the direction of travel. This will be your starting position.
Begin the jump by dipping with the knees to initiate a stretch reflex, and immediately reverse direction to push off the ground, jumping up and sideways over the cone.
Use your legs to absorb impact upon landing, and rebound into the next jump, continuing down the row of cones.
cues: Land softly on the balls of the feet
Spend as little time on the ground as possible
Knees track over the toes
Arms drive each jump
mistakes: Landing on the heels or stiff-legged
Doing too many reps when tired
exercises.breathing: Take a quick breath before each effort and exhale sharply as you take off. Reset your breathing between reps.
safety: Use a forgiving surface and stop the set when landings get sloppy.

exercises.name: Carioca Quick Step
exercises.description: Carioca Quick Step is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the adductors, with help from the abs & core, abductors, calves, glutes, hamstrings and quadriceps.
setup: Begin with your feet a few inches apart and your left arm up in a relaxed, athletic position.
steps: With your right foot, quick step behind and pull the knee up.
Fire your arms back up when you pull the right knee, being sure that your knee goes straight up and down. Avoid turning your feet as you move and continue to look forward as you move to the side.

exercises.name: Standing One-Arm Dumbbell Curl Over Incline Bench
exercises.description: Standing One-Arm Dumbbell Curl Over Incline Bench is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the biceps. A variation of the preacher curl: standing, upper arm resting over the top of an incline bench.
setup: Stand on the back side of an incline bench as if you were going to be a spotter for someone. Have a dumbbell in one hand and rest it across the incline bench with a supinated (palms up) grip.
steps: Position your non lifting hand at the corner or side of the incline bench. The chest should be pressed against the top part of the incline and your feet should be pressed against the floor at a wide stance. This is the starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the dumbbell upward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Only the forearms should move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to starting position as your breathe in.

exercises.name: Zottman Preacher Curl
exercises.description: Zottman Preacher Curl is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the biceps, with help from the forearms. A variation of the preacher curl: curl palms up, turn palms down at the top, lower slowly.
setup: Grab a dumbbell in each hand and place your upper arms on top of the preacher bench or the incline bench. The dumbbells should be held at shoulder height and the elbows should be flexed. Hold the dumbbells with the palms of your hands facing down. This will be your starting position.
steps: As you breathe in, slowly lower the dumbbells keeping the palms down until your upper arm is extended and your biceps are fully stretched.
Now rotate your wrists once you are at the bottom of the movement so that the palms of the hands are facing up.

As you exhale, use your biceps to curl the weights up until they are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder height. Again, remember that to ensure full contraction you need to bring that small finger higher than the thumb.
Squeeze the biceps hard for a second at the contracted position and rotate your wrists so that the palms are facing down again.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Upper arms stay flat on the pad
Slow at the bottom
mistakes: Dropping fast into a locked elbow
Lifting the elbows off the pad
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl the weight up, breathe in as you lower it.
safety: Do not drop into the bottom with heavy weight; the stretched elbow is vulnerable.
variation_notes: Curl palms up, turn palms down at the top, lower slowly.

setup: Grab an EZ-bar using a shoulder width and palms down (pronated) grip.
steps: Now place the upper part of both arms on top of the preacher bench and have your arms extended. This will be your starting position.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps are fully contracted and the barbell is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard for a second at the contracted position.

exercises.name: Reverse Plate Curls
exercises.description: Reverse Plate Curls is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the biceps, with help from the forearms. A variation of the reverse curl: a weight plate held overhand by the rim.
setup: Start by standing straight with a weighted plate held by both hands and arms fully extended. Use a pronated grip (palms facing down) and make sure your fingers grab the rough side of the plate while your thumb grabs the smooth side. Note: For the best results, grab the weighted plate at an 11:00 and 1:00 o'clock position.
steps: Your feet should be shoulder width apart from each other and the weighted plate should be near the groin area. This is the starting position.

Slowly lift the plate up while keeping the elbows in and the upper arms stationary until your biceps and forearms touch while exhaling. The plate should be evenly aligned with your torso at this point.
Feel the contraction for a second and begin to lower the weight back down to the starting position while inhaling
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

exercises.name: Flexor Incline Dumbbell Curls
exercises.description: Flexor Incline Dumbbell Curls is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the biceps. A variation of the seated incline curl: wrists curled in at the top to also work the forearm flexors.
setup: Hold the dumbbell towards the side farther from you so that you have more weight on the side closest to you. (This can be done for a good effect on all bicep dumbbell exercises). Now do a normal incline dumbbell curl, but keep your wrists as far back as possible so as to neutralize any stress that is placed on them.
steps: Sit on an incline bench that is angled at 45-degrees while holding a dumbbell on each hand.

Let your arms hang down on your sides, with the elbows in, and turn the palms of your hands forward with the thumbs pointing away from the body. Tip: You will keep this hand position throughout the movement as there should not be any twisting of the hands as they come up. This will be your starting position.

Curl up the two dumbbells at the same time until your biceps are fully contracted and exhale. Tip: Do not swing the arms or use momentum. Keep a controlled motion at all times. Hold the contracted position for a second at the top.
As you inhale, slowly go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Shoulders stay back against the bench
Feel the stretch at the bottom
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl the weight up, breathe in as you lower it.
variation_notes: Wrists curled in at the top to also work the forearm flexors.

exercises.name: Incline Inner Biceps Curl
exercises.description: Incline Inner Biceps Curl is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the biceps. A variation of the seated incline curl: dumbbells curled outward to the sides.
setup: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lie back on an incline bench.
steps: The dumbbells should be at arm's length hanging at your sides and your palms should be facing out. This will be your starting position.

Now as you exhale curl the weight outward and up while keeping your forearms in line with your side deltoids. Continue the curl until the dumbbells are at shoulder height and to the sides of your deltoids. Tip: The end of the movement should look similar to a double biceps pose.
After a second contraction at the top of the movement, start to inhale and slowly lower the weights back to the starting position using the same path used to bring them up.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Prone Incline Curl
exercises.description: Dumbbell Prone Incline Curl is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the biceps. A variation of the spider curl: lying face down on an incline bench.
setup: Grab a dumbbell on each hand and lie face down on an incline bench with your shoulders near top of the incline. Your knees can rest on the seat or your legs can be straddled to the sides (my preferred way).
steps: Let your arms extend and hang naturally in front of you so that they are perpendicular to the floor.
Now keep your elbows in by your side and face the palms forward. This will be your starting position.

Raise the dumbbells by contracting the biceps until your arms are fully flexed. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement and ensure that only the forearms move. The upper arms should remain stationary at all times.

exercises.name: Lying High Bench Barbell Curl
exercises.description: Lying High Bench Barbell Curl is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the biceps. A variation of the spider curl: lying face down on a high bench.
setup: Lie face forward on a tall flat bench while holding a barbell with a supinated grip (palms facing up). Tip: If you are holding a barbell grab it using a shoulder-width grip and if you are using an E-Z Bar grab it on the inner handles. Your upper body should be positioned in a way that the upper chest is over the end of the bench and the barbell is hanging in front of you with the arms extended and perpendicular to the floor. steps: While keeping the elbows in and the upper arms stationary, curl the weight up in a semi-circular motion as you contract the biceps and exhale. Hold at the top of the movement for a second.
As you inhale, slowly go back to the starting position. Tip: Maintain full control of the weight at all times and avoid any swinging. Remember, only the forearms should move throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Spider Curl
exercises.description: Spider Curl is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the biceps. A variation of the spider curl: eZ bar.
setup: Start out by setting the bar on the part of the preacher bench that you would normally sit on. Make sure to align the barbell properly so that it is balanced and will not fall off.
steps: Move to the front side of the preacher bench (the part where the arms usually lay) and position yourself to lay at a 45 degree slant with your torso and stomach pressed against the front side of the preacher bench.
Make sure that your feet (especially the toes) are well positioned on the floor and place your upper arms on top of the pad located on the inside part of the preacher bench.
Use your arms to grab the barbell with a supinated grip (palms facing up) at about shoulder width apart or slightly closer from each other.
Slowly begin to lift the barbell upwards and exhale. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps.
Slowly begin to bring the barbell back to the starting position as your breathe in. .

exercises.name: Calf Press On The Leg Press Machine
exercises.description: Calf Press On The Leg Press Machine is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the calves. A variation of the calf press: on a leg press machine, balls of the feet at the bottom edge.
setup: Using a leg press machine, sit down on the machine and place your legs on the platform directly in front of you at a medium (shoulder width) foot stance.
steps: Lower the safety bars holding the weighted platform in place and press the platform all the way up until your legs are fully extended in front of you without locking your knees. (Note: In some leg press units you can leave the safety bars on for increased safety. If your leg press unit allows for this, then this is the preferred method of performing the exercise.) Your torso and the legs should make perfect 90-degree angle. Now carefully place your toes and balls of your feet on the lower portion of the platform with the heels extending off. Toes should be facing forward, outwards or inwards as described at the beginning of the chapter. This will be your starting position.

Press on the platform by raising your heels as you breathe out by extending your ankles as high as possible and flexing your calf. Ensure that the knee is kept stationary at all times. There should be no bending at any time. Hold the contracted position by a second before you start to go back down.
Go back slowly to the starting position as you breathe in by lowering your heels as you bend the ankles until calves are stretched.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Knees stay straight
Full range
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you press, breathe in as you return.
safety: Keep the safety stops engaged where possible; your feet are only half on the platform.

Using a band, towel, or your hand if you can reach, pull the toes toward you. Hold for 10 to 20 seconds, then switch sides.

Straight knee targets the calf; bent knee targets the soleus and Achilles
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Standing Gastrocnemius Calf Stretch
exercises.description: Standing Gastrocnemius Calf Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the calves, with help from the hamstrings.
setup: Place your right heel on a step with your knee extended and lean forward to grab your right toe with your right hand. Your left knee should be slightly bent and your back should be straight.
steps: Support your weight on your left leg and place your left hand on your left thigh.
Pull your right toes toward your knee until you feel a stretch in your calf.
cues: Keep the heel on the floor
Straight knee targets the calf; bent knee targets the soleus and Achilles

exercises.name: Standing Soleus And Achilles Stretch
exercises.description: Standing Soleus And Achilles Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the calves.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-distance apart, one foot slightly in front of the other.
Bend both knees, keeping your back heel on the floor. Switch sides.
cues: Keep the heel on the floor
Straight knee targets the calf; bent knee targets the soleus and Achilles

exercises.name: Ankle Circles
exercises.description: Ankle Circles is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the calves.
setup: Use a sturdy object like a squat rack to hold yourself.
steps: Lift the right leg in the air (just around 2 inches from the floor) and perform a circular motion with the big toe. Pretend that you are drawing a big circle with it. Tip: One circle equals 1 repetition. Breathe normally as you perform the movement.
When you are done with the right foot, then repeat with the left leg.
cues: Start small and slow, then grow the range
Smooth, controlled movement, no flinging
About 8–12 reps per side as a warm-up
mistakes: Swinging into end range with momentum
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

setup: Stand with your legs together and hands by your waist.
steps: Now move your knees in a circular motion as you breathe normally.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

exercises.name: Anterior Tibialis-SMR
exercises.description: Anterior Tibialis-SMR is an intermediate-level self-massage (foam rolling) exercise that mainly targets the calves.
steps: Begin seated on the ground with your legs bent and your feet on the floor.

Using a Muscle Roller or a rolling pin, apply pressure to the muscles on the outside of your shins. Work from just below the knee to above the ankle, pausing at points of tension for 10-30 seconds. Repeat on the other leg.
cues: Roll slowly, about 2–3 cm per second
Pause 20–30 seconds on tender spots
Support your weight with hands and feet to control the pressure
30–90 seconds per area
mistakes: Rolling directly over joints or bones
Pressing so hard you tense up
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and stay relaxed. On a tender spot, pause and take a few long exhales to let the muscle release.
safety: Avoid rolling the lower back and neck with full body weight; use a softer tool there.

exercises.name: Calves-SMR
exercises.description: Calves-SMR is an intermediate-level self-massage (foam rolling) exercise that mainly targets the calves.
steps: Begin seated on the floor. Place a foam roller underneath your lower leg. Your other leg can either be crossed over the opposite or be placed on the floor, supporting some of your weight. This will be your starting position.

Place your hands to your side or just behind you, and press down to raise your hips off of the floor, placing much of your weight against your calf muscle. Roll from below the knee to above the ankle, pausing at points of tension for 10-30 seconds. Repeat for the other leg.
cues: Roll slowly, about 2–3 cm per second
Pause 20–30 seconds on tender spots
Support your weight with hands and feet to control the pressure
30–90 seconds per area

exercises.name: Foot-SMR
exercises.description: Foot-SMR is an intermediate-level self-massage (foam rolling) exercise that mainly targets the calves.
steps: This exercise stretches the fascia of the muscles in the feet. Start off seated with your shoes removed. Using a foot roller or a similar object, such as a small section of pvc pipe, place your foot against the roller across the arch of your foot. This will be your starting position.
Press down firmly, rolling across the arch of your foot. Hold for 10-30 seconds, and then switch feet.
cues: Roll slowly, about 2–3 cm per second
Pause 20–30 seconds on tender spots
Support your weight with hands and feet to control the pressure

exercises.name: Peroneals-SMR

steps: Lay on your side, supporting your weight on your forearm and on a foam roller placed on the outside of your lower leg. Your upper leg can either be on top of your lower leg, or you can cross it in front of you. This will be your starting position.
Raise your hips off of the ground and begin to roll from below the knee to above the ankle on the side of your leg, pausing at points of tension for 10-30 seconds. Repeat on the other leg.

exercises.name: Barbell Seated Calf Raise
exercises.description: Barbell Seated Calf Raise is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the calves. A variation of the seated calf raise: bar resting on the thighs near the knees, on a pad.
setup: Place a block about 12 inches in front of a flat bench.
steps: Sit on the bench and place the ball of your feet on the block.
Have someone place a barbell over your upper thighs about 3 inches above your knees and hold it there. This will be your starting position.
Raise up on your toes as high as possible as you squeeze the calves and as you breathe out.
After a second contraction, slowly go back to the starting position. Tip: To get maximum benefit stretch your calves as far as you can.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Full stretch and full squeeze
Slow tempo
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you rise, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Bar resting on the thighs near the knees, on a pad.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Seated One-Leg Calf Raise
exercises.description: Dumbbell Seated One-Leg Calf Raise is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the calves. A variation of the seated calf raise: one dumbbell on one knee.
setup: Place a block on the floor about 12 inches from a flat bench.
steps: Sit on a flat bench and place a dumbbell on your upper left thigh about 3 inches above your knee.
Now place the ball of your left foot on the block. This will be your starting position.
Raise your toes up as high as possible as you exhale and you contract your calf muscle. Hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly return to the starting position, stretching as far down as possible.
Repeat for your prescribed number of repetitions and then repeat with the right leg.
cues: Full stretch and full squeeze
Slow tempo
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you rise, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: One dumbbell on one knee.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.description: A calf raise with bent knees. Bending the knee shifts the work to the soleus, the deeper calf muscle.
setup: Sit with the pad on your lower thighs and the balls of your feet on the platform.
steps: Release the stop and lower your heels for a full stretch.
Push up onto your toes as high as you can.
Pause, then lower slowly.
cues: Full stretch and full squeeze
Slow tempo
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you rise, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Reverse Calf Raises
exercises.description: Smith Machine Reverse Calf Raises is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the calves.
setup: Adjust the barbell on the smith machine to fit your height and align a raised platform right under the bar.
steps: Stand on the platform with the heels of your feet secured on top of it with the balls of your feet extending off it. Position your toes facing forward with a shoulder width stance.

Now, place your shoulders under the barbell while maintaining the foot positioning described and push the barbell up by extending your hips and knees until your torso is standing erect. The knees should be kept with a slight bend; never locked. This will be your starting position. Tip: The barbell on your back is only for balance purposes.

Raise the balls of your feet as you breathe out by extending your toes as high as possible and flexing your calf. Ensure that the knee is kept stationary at all times. There should be no bending at any time. Hold the contracted position for a second before you start to go back down.
Slowly go back down to the starting position as you breathe in by lowering the balls of your feet and toes.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Heels on a platform, toes off
Lift the toes as high as possible
Lower slowly
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Calf Raise On A Dumbbell
exercises.description: Calf Raise On A Dumbbell is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the calves. A variation of the standing calf raise: balls of the feet on a dumbbell handle for balance work.
setup: Hang on to a sturdy object for balance and stand on a dumbbell handle, preferably one with round plates so that it rolls as in this manner you have to work harder to stabilize yourself; thus increasing the effectiveness of the exercise.
steps: Now roll your foot slightly forward so that you can get a nice stretch of the calf. This will be your starting position.

Lift the calf as you roll your foot over the top of the handle so that you get a full extension. Exhale during the execution of this movement. Contract the calf hard at the top and hold for a second. Tip: As you come up, roll the dumbbell slightly backward.
Now inhale as you roll the dumbbell slightly forward as you come down to get a better stretch.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Pause at the bottom stretch
Straight knees
Push through the big toe
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you rise, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Balls of the feet on a dumbbell handle for balance work.

exercises.name: Calf Raises - With Bands
exercises.description: Calf Raises - With Bands is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the calves. A variation of the standing calf raise: standing on a band.
setup: Grab an exercise band and stand on it with your toes making sure that the length of the band between the foot and the arms is the same for both sides.
steps: While holding the handles of the band, raise the arms to the side of your head as if you were getting ready to perform a shoulder press. The palms should be facing forward with the elbows bent and to the sides. This movement will create tension on the band. This will be your starting position.
Keeping the hands by your shoulder, stand up on your toes as you exhale and contract the calves hard at the top of the movement.
After a one second contraction, slowly go back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Pause at the bottom stretch
Straight knees
Push through the big toe
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you rise, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Standing on a band.

exercises.name: Donkey Calf Raises
exercises.description: Donkey Calf Raises is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the calves. A variation of the standing calf raise: bent forward at the hips, which stretches the calves more.
setup: For this exercise you will need access to a donkey calf raise machine. Start by positioning your lower back and hips under the padded lever provided. The tailbone area should be the one making contact with the pad.
steps: Place both of your arms on the side handles and place the balls of your feet on the calf block with the heels extending off. Align the toes forward, inward or outward, depending on the area you wish to target, and straighten the knees without locking them. This will be your starting position.

Raise your heels as you breathe out by extending your ankles as high as possible and flexing your calf. Ensure that the knee is kept stationary at all times. There should be no bending at any time. Hold the contracted position by a second before you start to go back down.
Go back slowly to the starting position as you breathe in by lowering your heels as you bend the ankles until calves are stretched.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Pause at the bottom stretch
Straight knees
Push through the big toe
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you rise, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Bent forward at the hips, which stretches the calves more.

exercises.name: Rocking Standing Calf Raise
exercises.description: Rocking Standing Calf Raise is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the calves. A variation of the standing calf raise: alternate toes up and heels up.
setup: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place it on the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck).
steps: Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times as looking down will get you off balance. Also maintain a straight back and keep the knees with a slight bend; never locked. This will be your starting position.

Raise your heels as you breathe out by extending your ankles as high as possible and flexing your calf. Ensure that the knee is kept stationary at all times. There should be no bending (other than the slight initial bend we created during positioning) at any time. Hold the contracted position by a second before you start to go back down.
Go back slowly to the starting position as you breathe in by lowering your heels as you bend the ankles until calves are stretched.
Now lift your toes by contracting the tibia muscles in the front of the calves as you breathe out.
Hold for a second and bring them back down as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Pause at the bottom stretch
Straight knees
Push through the big toe
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you rise, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Alternate toes up and heels up.

setup: Position two equally loaded EZ bars on the ground next to each other. Ensure they are able to roll.
