Using a slow and controlled motion, move your hands away from the midline of your body, rolling the bars apart. Inhale during this portion of the motion.
After moving the bars as far apart as you can, return to the starting position by pulling them back together. Exhale as you perform this movement.

exercises.name: Flat Bench Cable Flyes
exercises.description: Flat Bench Cable Flyes is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the chest. A variation of the cable fly: lying on a flat bench between low pulleys.
setup: Position a flat bench between two low pulleys so that when you are laying on it, your chest will be lined up with the cable pulleys.
steps: Lay flat on the bench and keep your feet on the ground.
Have someone hand you the handles on each hand. You will grab each single handle attachment with a palms up grip.

Extend your arms by your side with a slight bend on your elbows. Tip: You will keep this bend constant through the whole movement. Your arms should be parallel to the floor. This is your starting position.

Now start lifting the arms in a semi-circle motion directly in front of you by pulling the cables together until both hands meet at the top of the movement. Squeeze your chest as you perform this motion and breathe out during this movement. Also, hold the contraction for a second at the top. setup: Set a decline bench to about 15–30° and lock your legs under the pads.
Lie back with your shoulder blades pulled together.
Grip slightly wider than shoulder width.
steps: Start with arms straight above your lower chest.
Lower the weight to your lower chest.
Press back up to straight arms.
cues: Elbows about 45° from your body
Control the descent
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath and brace before lowering. Hold it on the way down, then breathe out through pursed lips as you push past the hardest part of the press.
safety: Your head is below your hips, so have a spotter for heavy barbell sets and sit up slowly afterwards.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Decline Barbell Bench Press
exercises.description: Wide-Grip Decline Barbell Bench Press is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the chest, with help from the triceps. A variation of the decline bench press: a wider grip puts more load on the chest.
setup: Lie back on a decline bench with the feet securely locked at the front of the bench. Using a wide, pronated (palms forward) grip that is around 3 inches away from shoulder width (for each hand), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked. The bar will be perpendicular to the torso and the floor. This will be your starting position.
steps: As you breathe in, come down slowly until you feel the bar on your lower chest.

After a second pause, bring the bar back to the starting position as you breathe out and push the bar using your chest muscles. Lock your arms and squeeze your chest in the contracted position, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly again. Tip: It should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
cues: Elbows about 45° from your body
Control the descent
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath and brace before lowering. Hold it on the way down, then breathe out through pursed lips as you push past the hardest part of the press.
safety: Your head is below your hips, so have a spotter for heavy barbell sets and sit up slowly afterwards.
variation_notes: A wider grip puts more load on the chest.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Squeeze Press
exercises.description: A dumbbell press where you squeeze the dumbbells together the whole time, which keeps the chest working hard.
setup: Lie on a flat bench holding two dumbbells together above your chest, palms facing each other.
Pull your shoulder blades back.
steps: Squeeze the dumbbells together firmly.
Lower them to your chest while keeping them pressed together.
Press back up, still squeezing.
cues: Squeeze as if crushing something between the dumbbells
Elbows close to your sides
mistakes: Using weight too heavy to keep the squeeze
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath and brace before lowering. Hold it on the way down, then breathe out through pursed lips as you push past the hardest part of the press.

exercises.name: Dynamic Chest Stretch
exercises.description: Dynamic Chest Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the chest, with help from the upper back.
steps: Stand with your hands together, arms extended directly in front of you. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your arms straight, quickly move your arms back as far as possible and back in again, similar to an exaggerated clapping motion. Repeat 5-10 times, increasing speed as you do so.
cues: Start small and slow, then grow the range
Smooth, controlled movement, no flinging
About 8–12 reps per side as a warm-up
mistakes: Swinging into end range with momentum
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Alternating Floor Press
exercises.description: Alternating Floor Press is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the chest, with help from the abs & core and triceps. A variation of the floor press: two kettlebells pressed one at a time.
setup: Lie on the floor with two kettlebells next to your shoulders.
steps: Position one in place on your chest and then the other, gripping the kettlebells on the handle with the palms facing forward.
Extend both arms, so that the kettlebells are being held above your chest. Lower one kettlebell, bringing it to your chest and turn the wrist in the direction of the locked out kettlebell.
Raise the kettlebell and repeat on the opposite side.
cues: Elbows about 45° from your body
Pause on the floor, do not bounce
mistakes: Slamming the elbows into the floor
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath and brace before lowering. Hold it on the way down, then breathe out through pursed lips as you push past the hardest part of the press.
variation_notes: Two kettlebells pressed one at a time.

exercises.name: Extended Range One-Arm Kettlebell Floor Press
exercises.description: Extended Range One-Arm Kettlebell Floor Press is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the chest, with help from the triceps. A variation of the floor press: single kettlebell; reach past the shoulder at the top.
steps: Lie on the floor and position a kettlebell for one arm to press. The kettlebell should be held by the handle. The leg on the same side that you are pressing should be bent, with the knee crossing over the midline of the body.
Press the kettlebell by extending the elbow and adducting the arm, pressing it above your body. Return to the starting position.
cues: Elbows about 45° from your body
Pause on the floor, do not bounce
mistakes: Slamming the elbows into the floor
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath and brace before lowering. Hold it on the way down, then breathe out through pursed lips as you push past the hardest part of the press.
variation_notes: Single kettlebell; reach past the shoulder at the top.

exercises.name: Floor Press (Barbell)
exercises.description: A press lying on the floor. The floor stops your elbows partway, so it trains the top half of the press and is easy on the shoulders.
setup: Lie on your back on the floor, knees bent or legs straight.
Position the weight over your chest with arms straight.
Pull your shoulder blades together.
steps: Lower the weight until the backs of your upper arms gently touch the floor.
Pause briefly without relaxing.
Press back up to straight arms.
cues: Elbows about 45° from your body
Pause on the floor, do not bounce
mistakes: Slamming the elbows into the floor
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath and brace before lowering. Hold it on the way down, then breathe out through pursed lips as you push past the hardest part of the press.
safety: With a barbell, set it up in a rack at the right height or use pins; getting a heavy bar into position from the floor is hard.

exercises.name: Leg-Over Floor Press
exercises.description: Leg-Over Floor Press is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the chest, with help from the triceps. A variation of the floor press: leg on the working side crossed over for a stable base.
setup: Lie on the floor with one kettlebell in place on your chest, holding it by the handle. Extend leg on working side over leg on non-working side. Your free arm can be extended out to your side for support.
steps: Press the kettlebll into a locked out position.
Lower the weight until the elbow touches the ground, keeping the kettlebell above the elbow. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
cues: Elbows about 45° from your body
Pause on the floor, do not bounce
mistakes: Slamming the elbows into the floor
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath and brace before lowering. Hold it on the way down, then breathe out through pursed lips as you push past the hardest part of the press.
variation_notes: Leg on the working side crossed over for a stable base.

exercises.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Floor Press
exercises.description: One-Arm Kettlebell Floor Press is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the chest, with help from the triceps. A variation of the floor press: one kettlebell from the floor.
setup: Lie on the floor holding a kettlebell with one hand, with your upper arm supported by the floor. The palm should be facing in.
steps: Press the kettlebell straight up toward the ceiling, rotating your wrist.
Lower the kettlebell back to the starting position and repeat.
cues: Elbows about 45° from your body
Pause on the floor, do not bounce
mistakes: Slamming the elbows into the floor
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath and brace before lowering. Hold it on the way down, then breathe out through pursed lips as you push past the hardest part of the press.

exercises.name: Hammer Grip Incline DB Bench Press
exercises.description: Hammer Grip Incline DB Bench Press is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the chest, with help from the triceps. A variation of the incline bench press: palms face each other.
setup: Lie back on an incline bench with a dumbbell on each hand on top of your thighs. The palms of your hand will be facing each other.
steps: By using your thighs to help you get the dumbbells up, clean the dumbbells one arm at a time so that you can hold them at shoulder width.

Once at shoulder width, keep the palms of your hands with a neutral grip (palms facing each other). Keep your elbows flared out with the upper arms in line with the shoulders (perpendicular to the torso) and the elbows bent creating a 90-degree angle between the upper arm and the forearm. This will be your starting position.
Now bring down the weights slowly to your side as you breathe in. Keep full control of the dumbbells at all times.

As you breathe out, push the dumbbells up using your pectoral muscles. Lock your arms in the contracted position, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly. Tip: It should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the dumbbells back in your thighs and then on the floor. This is the safest manner to dispose of the dumbbells.
cues: Elbows slightly tucked, not flared
Chest stays up toward the weight
Wrists stacked over elbows
mistakes: Lowering to the lower chest or stomach
Arching so much the incline is lost
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath and brace before lowering. Hold it on the way down, then breathe out through pursed lips as you push past the hardest part of the press.
safety: Use safety bars or a spotter for heavy barbell sets.
variation_notes: Palms face each other.

exercises.name: Incline Chest Press (Machine)
exercises.description: A machine version of the incline press. The fixed path makes it easy to learn and safe to push close to failure.
setup: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with your upper chest.
Sit with your back against the pad and feet flat.
Pull your shoulder blades back.
steps: Press the handles forward and up until your arms are almost straight.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch in the chest.
cues: Keep your back on the pad
Control the way back
mistakes: Seat too low, which turns it into a shoulder press
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you press, breathe in as the handles come back.

exercises.name: Isometric Chest Squeezes
exercises.description: Isometric Chest Squeezes is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the chest, with help from the triceps.
setup: While either seating or standing, bend your arms at a 90-degree angle and place the palms of your hands together in front of your chest. Tip: Your hands should be open with the palms together and fingers facing forward (perpendicular to your torso).
steps: Push both hands against each other as you contract your chest. Start with slow tension and increase slowly. Keep breathing normally as you execute this contraction.
Hold for the recommended number of seconds.
Now release the tension slowly.
Rest for the recommended amount of time and repeat.
cues: Press the palms together in front of the chest
Squeeze hard for 5–10 seconds
Keep the shoulders down
exercises.breathing: Keep the core braced and breathe in short, steady breaths behind the brace. Do not hold your breath for the whole set.

exercises.name: Isometric Wipers
exercises.description: Isometric Wipers is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the chest, with help from the abs & core and triceps.
setup: Assume a push-up position, supporting your weight on your hands and toes while keeping your body straight. Your hands should be just outside of shoulder width. This will be your starting position.
steps: Begin by shifting your body weight as far to one side as possible, allowing the elbow on that side to flex as you lower your body.
Reverse the motion by extending the flexed arm, pushing yourself up and then dropping to the other side.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
cues: Push-up position with a wide base
Shift the weight to one arm, then the other
Body stays in a straight line
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Chest Push (multiple response)
exercises.description: Chest Push (multiple response) is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the chest, with help from the abs & core and triceps.
setup: Begin in a kneeling position facing a wall or utilize a partner. Hold the ball with both hands tight into the chest.
steps: Execute the pass by exploding forward and outward with the hips while pushing the ball as hard as possible.
Follow through by falling forward, catching yourself with your hands.
Immediately return to an upright position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
cues: Use the legs and hips first, the arms last
Throw as hard as you can; every rep is maximal
Use a light ball (2–5 kg) you can move fast
Reset fully between throws
mistakes: Using a ball too heavy to move quickly
Rounding the back when picking up or catching
exercises.breathing: Inhale as you load, exhale forcefully as you release the ball.
safety: Throw against a solid wall or into open space, never toward people.

setup: Begin in a three point stance, squatted down with your back flat and one hand on the ground. Place the medicine ball directly in front of you.
steps: To begin, take your first step as you pull the ball to your chest, positioning both hands to prepare for the throw.
As you execute the second step, explosively release the ball forward as hard as possible.

exercises.description: Chest Push with Run Release is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the chest, with help from the abs & core and triceps.
setup: Begin in an athletic stance with the knees bent, hips back, and back flat. Hold the medicine ball near your legs. This will be your starting position.
steps: While taking your first step draw the medicine ball into your chest.

exercises.name: Heavy Bag Thrust
exercises.description: Heavy Bag Thrust is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the chest, with help from the abs & core and triceps.
setup: Utilize a heavy bag for this exercise. Assume an upright stance next to the bag, with your feet staggered, fairly wide apart. Place your hand on the bag at about chest height. This will be your starting position.
steps: Begin by twisting at the waist, pushing the bag forward as hard as possible. Perform this move quickly, pushing the bag away from your body.
Receive the bag as it swings back by reversing these steps.

steps: Begin facing your partner holding the medicine ball at your torso with both hands.
Pull the ball to your chest, and reverse the motion by extending through the elbows. For sports applications, you can take a step as you throw.
Your partner should catch the ball, and throw it back to you.
Receive the throw with both hands at chest height.

exercises.name: Plate Press
exercises.description: Standing press with a weight plate held between the palms, pushed straight out from the chest.
setup: Stand tall holding a plate at chest height between your flat palms.
Squeeze the plate hard.
steps: Press the plate straight out until your arms are straight.
Bring it back to your chest under control.
cues: Keep squeezing the plate the whole time

mistakes: Letting the plate drop below chest height
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you push the plate away, breathe in as it returns.

steps: Press the plate straight out until your arms are straight.

exercises.name: Front Raise And Pullover
exercises.description: Front Raise And Pullover is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the chest, with help from the lats and triceps. A variation of the pullover: barbell raised from the thighs to overhead while lying on a bench.
setup: Lie on a flat bench while holding a barbell using a palms down grip that is about 15 inches apart.
steps: Place the bar on your upper thighs, extend your arms and lock them while keeping a slight bend on the elbows. This will be your starting position.

Now raise the weight using a semicircular motion and keeping your arms straight as you inhale. Continue the same movement until the bar is on the other side above your head . (Tip: the bar will travel approximately 180-degrees). At this point your arms should be parallel to the floor with the palms of your hands facing the ceiling.
Now return the barbell to the starting position by reversing the motion as you exhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Ribs down; do not arch to get more range
Elbows stay slightly bent
mistakes: Going deeper than your shoulders allow
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as the weight goes back, breathe out as you pull it over.
safety: Skip or shorten the range if you have shoulder pain overhead.
variation_notes: Barbell raised from the thighs to overhead while lying on a bench.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Decline Barbell Pullover
exercises.description: Wide-Grip Decline Barbell Pullover is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the chest, with help from the triceps. A variation of the pullover: decline bench, wide grip.
setup: Lie down on a decline bench with both legs securely locked in position. Reach for the barbell behind the head using a pronated grip (palms facing out). Make sure to grab the barbell wider than shoulder width apart for this exercise. Slowly lift the barbell up from the floor by using your arms.
steps: When positioned properly, your arms should be fully extended and perpendicular to the floor. This is the starting position.

Begin by moving the barbell back down in a semicircular motion as if you were going to place it on the floor, but instead, stop when the arms are parallel to the floor. Tip: Keep the arms fully extended at all times. The movement should only happen at the shoulder joint. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Now bring the barbell up while exhaling until you are back at the starting position. Remember to keep full control of the barbell at all times.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions of your training program.
When finished with your set, slowly lower the barbell back down until it is level with your head and release it.
cues: Ribs down; do not arch to get more range
Elbows stay slightly bent
mistakes: Going deeper than your shoulders allow
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as the weight goes back, breathe out as you pull it over.
safety: Skip or shorten the range if you have shoulder pain overhead.
variation_notes: Decline bench, wide grip.

exercises.name: Clap Push Ups
exercises.description: The classic bodyweight press. It trains the chest, shoulders and triceps while the core holds the body straight.
setup: Place your hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulder width, under or just outside your shoulders.
Step your feet back so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your core.
steps: Lower your body as one unit until your chest is a few centimetres from the floor.
Keep your elbows about 45° from your body.
Push the floor away until your arms are straight.

Elbows point back, not out
Push the floor away at the top

exercises.name: Clock Push-Up
exercises.description: Clock Push-Up is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the chest, with help from the triceps. A variation of the push up: hands walk around in a circle between reps.
setup: Move into a prone position on the floor, supporting your weight on your hands and toes.
steps: Your arms should be fully extended with the hands around shoulder width. Keep your body straight throughout the movement. This will be your starting position.
Descend by flexing at the elbow, lowering your chest toward the ground.
At the bottom, reverse the motion by pushing yourself up through elbow extension as quickly as possible until you are air borne. Aim to "jump" 12-18 inches to one side.
As you accelerate up, move your outside foot away from your direction of travel. Leaving the ground, shift your body about 30 degrees for the next repetition.
Return to the starting position and repeat the exercise, working all the way around until you are back where you started.
cues: Body stays one straight plank
Elbows point back, not out
Push the floor away at the top
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push up.
safety: If your wrists hurt, use push-up handles or dumbbells to keep the wrists straight.
variation_notes: Hands walk around in a circle between reps.

exercises.name: Incline Push-Up Depth Jump

exercises.name: Plank Pushup
exercises.description: Moving between a forearm plank and a high plank, one arm at a time.
setup: Place your hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulder width, under or just outside your shoulders.

Squeeze your glutes and brace your core.
steps: Start in a forearm plank.
Place one hand under your shoulder and push up, then the other, to reach a high plank.
Lower back down to your forearms one arm at a time.
Alternate the leading arm each rep.

exercises.name: Plyo Kettlebell Pushups
exercises.description: Plyo Kettlebell Pushups is an advanced-level strength exercise that mainly targets the chest, with help from the triceps. A variation of the push up: push up explosively, moving the hands between the floor and a kettlebell.
setup: Place a kettlebell on the floor. Place yourself in a pushup position, on your toes with one hand on the ground and one hand holding the kettlebell, with your elbows extended. This will be your starting position.
steps: Begin by lowering yourself as low as you can, keeping your back straight.

Quickly and forcefully reverse direction, pushing yourself up to the other side of the kettlebell, switching hands as you do so. Continue the movement by descending and repeating the movement back and forth.

setup: With your hands wide apart, support your body on your toes and hands in a plank position. Your elbows should be extended and your body straight. Do not allow your hips to sag. This will be your starting position.
steps: To begin, allow the elbows to flex, lowering your chest to the floor as you inhale.
Using your pectoral muscles, press your upper body back up to the starting position by extending the elbows. Exhale as you perform this step.
After pausing at the contracted position, repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

variation_notes: Hands wider than the shoulders puts more on the chest.

exercises.name: Push-Ups With Feet On An Exercise Ball
exercises.description: Push-Ups With Feet On An Exercise Ball is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the chest, with help from the triceps. A variation of the push up: feet on a ball; harder for the core.
setup: Lie on the floor face down and place your hands about 36 inches apart from each other holding your torso up at arms length.
steps: Place your toes on top of an exercise ball. This will allow your body to be elevated.
Lower yourself until your chest almost touches the floor as you inhale.
Using your pectoral muscles, press your upper body back up to the starting position and squeeze your chest. Breathe out as you perform this step.
After a second pause at the contracted position, repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
cues: Body stays one straight plank

Push the floor away at the top

exercises.name: Suspended Push-Up
exercises.description: Suspended Push-Up is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the chest, with help from the triceps. A variation of the push up: hands in suspension straps; the instability works the chest and shoulders harder.
setup: Anchor your suspension straps securely to the top of a rack or other object.
steps: Leaning into the straps, take a handle in each hand and move into a push-up plank position. You should be as close to parallel to the ground as you can manage with your arms fully extended, maintaining good posture.
Maintaining a straight, rigid torso, descend slowly by allowing the elbows to flex.
Continue until your elbows break 90 degrees, pausing before you extend to return to the starting position.
cues: Body stays one straight plank
Elbows point back, not out
Push the floor away at the top

exercises.name: Push Up to Side Plank
exercises.description: Push Up to Side Plank is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the chest, with help from the abs & core and triceps.
setup: Get into pushup position on the toes with your hands just outside of shoulder width.
steps: Perform a pushup by allowing the elbows to flex. As you descend, keep your body straight.
Do one pushup and as you come up, shift your weight on the left side of the body, twist to the side while bringing the right arm up towards the ceiling in a side plank.
Lower the arm back to the floor for another pushup and then twist to the other side.
Repeat the series, alternating each side, for 10 or more reps.
cues: Do a full push-up
Rotate onto one hand into a side plank
Return and alternate sides
mistakes: Hips sagging in the side plank
exercises.breathing: Keep the core braced and breathe in short, steady breaths behind the brace. Do not hold your breath for the whole set.

exercises.name: Forward Drag with Press
exercises.description: Forward Drag with Press is an intermediate-level strongman exercise that mainly targets the chest, with help from the calves, glutes, hamstrings, quadriceps and triceps. A variation of the sled pull: walking forward, pressing the straps out in front on each step.
steps: Attach a dual handled chain or rope attachment to the sled. You should be facing away from the sled, holding a handle in each hand.

Begin the movement by moving forward for one step. Leaning forward, extend through the legs and hips to move, pausing with each step to extend through the elbows, pressing your hands forward. Step forward until you return to the start position prepared to press.
cues: Stay low and drive through the legs
exercises.breathing: Breathe hard and rhythmically.
variation_notes: Walking forward, pressing the straps out in front on each step.

exercises.name: Kneeling Forearm Stretch
exercises.description: Kneeling Forearm Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the forearms.
steps: Start by kneeling on a mat with your palms flat and your fingers pointing back toward your knees.
Slowly lean back keeping your palms flat on the floor until you feel a stretch in your wrists and forearms. Hold for 20-30 seconds.
cues: Keep the shoulder relaxed and down
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Reverse Grip Concentration Curl
exercises.description: A seated one-arm curl with the elbow braced against the inner thigh, which removes any swinging.
setup: Sit on a bench with legs apart.
Hold a dumbbell and rest the back of that upper arm against your inner thigh.
steps: Curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder.
Squeeze at the top.
Lower until the arm is straight.
cues: Upper arm stays pressed into the thigh
Turn the little finger up at the top
mistakes: Lifting the elbow off the thigh
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl the weight up, breathe in as you lower it.
variation_notes: Palms face down, shifting work to the forearm and brachialis.

exercises.name: Dead Hang
exercises.description: Simply hanging from a bar for time. It builds grip strength and decompresses the shoulders.
setup: Grip a pull-up bar overhand, about shoulder-width apart.
steps: Lift your feet and hang with straight arms.
Keep a light tension in the shoulders rather than fully collapsing.
Hold for the target time, then step down.
cues: Relax the legs
Breathe steadily
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and steadily throughout the hold.
safety: Use a box to step down safely.

exercises.name: Wrist Circles
exercises.description: Wrist Circles is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the forearms.
setup: Start by standing straight with your feet being shoulder width apart from each other. Elevate your arms to the side of you until they are fully extended and parallel to the floor at a height that is evenly aligned with your shoulders. Tip: Your torso and arms should form the letter "T: Your palms should be facing down. This is the starting position.
steps: Keeping your entire body stationary except for the wrists, begin to rotate both wrists forward in a circular motion. Tip: Pretend that you are trying to draw circles by using your hands as the brush. Breathe normally as you perform this exercise.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Start small and slow, then grow the range
Smooth, controlled movement, no flinging
About 8–12 reps per side as a warm-up
mistakes: Swinging into end range with momentum
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Farmers Walk
exercises.description: Walking while holding heavy weights at your sides. Builds grip, traps and a strong core.
setup: Stand between two heavy dumbbells, kettlebells or farmer handles.
Squat or hinge down with a flat back and pick them up.
steps: Stand tall with shoulders back and down.
Walk with short, quick steps for the set distance.
Set the weights down with a flat back.
cues: Tall posture; do not lean
Squeeze the handles hard
exercises.breathing: Breathe in short, controlled breaths while staying braced.
safety: Pick up and set down the weights like a deadlift.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lying Pronation
exercises.description: Dumbbell Lying Pronation is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the forearms.
setup: Lie on a flat bench face down with one arm holding a dumbbell and the other hand on top of the bench folded so that you can rest your head on it.
steps: Bend the elbows of the arm holding the dumbbell so that it creates a 90-degree angle between the upper arm and the forearm.

Now raise the upper arm so that the forearm is perpendicular to the floor and the upper arm is perpendicular to your torso. Tip: The upper arm should be parallel to the floor and also creating a 90-degree angle with your torso. This will be your starting position.

As you breathe out, externally rotate your forearm so that the dumbbell is lifted forward as you maintain the 90 degree angle bend between the upper arms and the forearm. You will continue this external rotation until the forearm is parallel to the floor. At this point you will hold the contraction for a second.
As you breathe in, slowly go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Forearm supported, elbow still
Rotate slowly through the full range
Hold the dumbbell off-centre to make it harder
mistakes: Going too heavy and losing control
exercises.breathing: Breathe normally and steadily; do not hold your breath during the rotation.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lying Supination
exercises.description: Dumbbell Lying Supination is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the forearms.
setup: Lie sideways on a flat bench with one arm holding a dumbbell and the other hand on top of the bench folded so that you can rest your head on it.
steps: Bend the elbows of the arm holding the dumbbell so that it creates a 90-degree angle between the upper arm and the forearm.

Now raise the upper arm so that the forearm is parallel to the floor and perpendicular to your torso (Tip: So the forearm will be directly in front of you). The upper arm will be stationary by your torso and should be parallel to the floor (aligned with your torso at all times). This will be your starting position.

As you breathe out, externally rotate your forearm so that the dumbbell is lifted up in a semicircle motion as you maintain the 90 degree angle bend between the upper arms and the forearm. You will continue this external rotation until the forearm is perpendicular to the floor and the torso pointing towards the ceiling. At this point you will hold the contraction for a second.
As you breathe in, slowly go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then switch to the other arm.
cues: Forearm supported, elbow still
Rotate slowly through the full range
Hold the dumbbell off-centre to make it harder
mistakes: Going too heavy and losing control
exercises.breathing: Breathe normally and steadily; do not hold your breath during the rotation.

exercises.name: Wrist Rotations with Straight Bar
exercises.description: Wrist Rotations with Straight Bar is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the forearms.
setup: Hold a barbell with both hands and your palms facing down; hands spaced about shoulder width. This will be your starting position.
steps: Alternating between each of your hands, perform the movement by extending the wrist as though you were rolling up a newspaper. Continue alternating back and forth until failure.
Reverse the motion by flexing the wrist, rolling the opposite direction. Continue the alternating motion until failure.
cues: Forearm supported, elbow still
Rotate slowly through the full range
Hold the dumbbell off-centre to make it harder
mistakes: Going too heavy and losing control
exercises.breathing: Breathe normally and steadily; do not hold your breath during the rotation.

exercises.name: Plate Pinch
exercises.description: Plate Pinch is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the forearms.
setup: Grab two wide-rimmed plates and put them together with the smooth sides facing outward
steps: Use your fingers to grip the outside part of the plate and your thumb for the other side thus holding both plates together. This is the starting position.
Squeeze the plate with your fingers and thumb. Hold this position for as long as you can.
Repeat for the recommended amount of sets prescribed in your program.
Switch arms and repeat the movements.
cues: Squeeze as hard as possible for the whole set
Smooth plates and a thumb-against-fingers pinch

exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.

exercises.name: Flutter Kicks
exercises.description: Flutter Kicks is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the glutes, with help from the hamstrings.
setup: On a flat bench lie facedown with the hips on the edge of the bench, the legs straight with toes high off the floor and with the arms on top of the bench holding on to the front edge.
steps: Squeeze your glutes and hamstrings and straighten the legs until they are level with the hips. This will be your starting position.
Start the movement by lifting the left leg higher than the right leg.
Then lower the left leg as you lift the right leg.

Continue alternating in this manner (as though you are doing a flutter kick in water) until you have done the recommended amount of repetitions for each leg. Make sure that you keep a controlled movement at all times. Tip: You will breathe normally as you perform this movement.
cues: Hips on the edge of the bench, legs level with the hips
Kick the legs up and down in small fast movements
Squeeze the glutes
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Piriformis-SMR
exercises.description: Piriformis-SMR is an intermediate-level self-massage (foam rolling) exercise that mainly targets the glutes.
steps: Sit with your buttocks on top of a foam roll. Bend your knees, and then cross one leg so that the ankle is over the knee. This will be your starting position.

Shift your weight to the side of the crossed leg, rolling over the buttocks until you feel tension in your upper glute. You may assist the stretch by using one hand to pull the bent knee towards your chest. Hold this position for 10-30 seconds, and then switch sides.
cues: Roll slowly, about 2–3 cm per second
Pause 20–30 seconds on tender spots
Support your weight with hands and feet to control the pressure
30–90 seconds per area
mistakes: Rolling directly over joints or bones
Pressing so hard you tense up
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and stay relaxed. On a tender spot, pause and take a few long exhales to let the muscle release.
safety: Avoid rolling the lower back and neck with full body weight; use a softer tool there.

exercises.name: Frog Pumps (Dumbbell)
exercises.description: A glute bridge with the soles of the feet pressed together and knees open, done for high reps.
setup: Lie on your back with the soles of your feet together and knees falling out.
Rest a dumbbell on your hips.
steps: Drive your hips up by squeezing the glutes.
Lower and repeat quickly but controlled.
cues: Squeeze hard at the top
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you drive the hips up, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.description: Lying on your back and lifting your hips. A simple glute exercise and a good warm-up.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
steps: Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a line from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze the glutes.
Lower slowly.
cues: Push through the heels
Squeeze the glutes at the top
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you drive the hips up, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge (Barbell)
exercises.description: Lying on your back and lifting your hips. A simple glute exercise and a good warm-up.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
steps: Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a line from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze the glutes.
Lower slowly.
cues: Push through the heels
Squeeze the glutes at the top
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you drive the hips up, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Roll a padded barbell over your hips while lying on the floor.

exercises.name: Hip Lift with Band
exercises.description: Hip Lift with Band is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the glutes, with help from the calves and hamstrings. A variation of the glute bridge: a band across the hips, anchored on each side, adds resistance at the top.
setup: After choosing a suitable band, lay down in the middle of the rack, after securing the band on either side of you. If your rack doesn't have pegs, the band can be secured using heavy dumbbells or similar objects, just ensure they won't move.
steps: Adjust your position so that the band is directly over your hips. Bend your knees and place your feet flat on the floor. Your hands can be on the floor or holding the band in position.
Keeping your shoulders on the ground, drive through your heels to raise your hips, pushing into the band as high as you can.
Pause at the top of the motion, and return to the starting position.
cues: Push through the heels
Squeeze the glutes at the top
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you drive the hips up, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: A band across the hips, anchored on each side, adds resistance at the top.

exercises.name: Partial Glute Bridge (Barbell)
exercises.description: Lying on your back and lifting your hips. A simple glute exercise and a good warm-up.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
steps: Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a line from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze the glutes.
Lower slowly.
cues: Push through the heels
Squeeze the glutes at the top
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you drive the hips up, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Only the top part of the range, keeping constant tension on the glutes.

exercises.name: Physioball Hip Bridge
exercises.description: Physioball Hip Bridge is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the glutes, with help from the hamstrings. A variation of the glute bridge: upper back on a ball; the hips lower and lift.
setup: Lay on a ball so that your upper back is on the ball with your hips unsupported. Both feet should be flat on the floor, hip width apart or wider. This will be your starting position.
steps: Begin by extending the hips using your glutes and hamstrings, raising your hips upward as you bridge.
Pause at the top of the motion and return to the starting position.
cues: Push through the heels
Squeeze the glutes at the top
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you drive the hips up, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Upper back on a ball; the hips lower and lift.

exercises.name: Single Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.description: Lying on your back and lifting your hips. A simple glute exercise and a good warm-up.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
steps: Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a line from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze the glutes.
Lower slowly.
cues: Push through the heels
Squeeze the glutes at the top
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you drive the hips up, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Extend one leg and drive through the other heel.

exercises.name: Glute Kickback (Machine)
exercises.description: Kicking one leg straight back to squeeze the glute.
setup: Set the machine so the pad sits behind your working foot or knee.
Hold the handles and brace on the chest pad or support.
steps: Kick the working leg straight back by squeezing the glute.
Pause, then return slowly.
cues: Move from the hip, not the lower back
Hips stay square
mistakes: Arching the back to kick higher
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you drive the hips up, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Glute Kickback on Floor
exercises.description: Kicking one leg straight back to squeeze the glute.
setup: Start on hands and knees.
steps: Kick the working leg straight back by squeezing the glute.
Pause, then return slowly.
cues: Move from the hip, not the lower back
Hips stay square
mistakes: Arching the back to kick higher
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you drive the hips up, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Kick one leg back and up with the knee bent or straight.

exercises.name: Hip Extension with Bands
exercises.description: Hip Extension with Bands is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the glutes, with help from the hamstrings. A variation of the glute kickback: standing, a band at the ankle; drive the leg straight back.
setup: Secure one end of the band to the lower portion of a post and attach the other to one ankle.
steps: Facing the attachment point of the band, hold on to the column to stabilize yourself.
Keeping your head and your chest up, move the resisted leg back as far as you can while keeping the knee straight.
Return the leg to the starting position.
cues: Move from the hip, not the lower back
Hips stay square
mistakes: Arching the back to kick higher
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you drive the hips up, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Standing, a band at the ankle; drive the leg straight back.

exercises.name: Leg Lift
exercises.description: Leg Lift is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the glutes, with help from the hamstrings. A variation of the glute kickback: standing, holding a support; lift one leg back, optionally with an ankle weight.
setup: While standing up straight with both feet next to each other at around shoulder width, grab a sturdy surface such as the sides of a squat rack or the top of a chair to brace yourself and keep balance.
steps: With or without an ankle weight, lift one leg behind you as if performing a leg curl but standing up while keeping the other leg straight. Breathe out as you perform this movement.
Slowly bring the raised leg back to the floor as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Repeat the movement with the opposite leg.
cues: Move from the hip, not the lower back
Hips stay square
mistakes: Arching the back to kick higher
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you drive the hips up, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Standing, holding a support; lift one leg back, optionally with an ankle weight.

exercises.name: Rear Kick (Machine)
exercises.description: Kicking one leg straight back to squeeze the glute.
setup: Set the machine so the pad sits behind your working foot or knee.
Hold the handles and brace on the chest pad or support.
steps: Kick the working leg straight back by squeezing the glute.
Pause, then return slowly.
cues: Move from the hip, not the lower back
Hips stay square
mistakes: Arching the back to kick higher
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you drive the hips up, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Hevy lists this separately from the glute kickback machine; it is the same movement.

exercises.name: Standing Cable Glute Kickbacks
exercises.description: Kicking one leg straight back to squeeze the glute.
setup: Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley.
Face the machine and hold on for support.
steps: Kick the working leg straight back by squeezing the glute.
Pause, then return slowly.
cues: Move from the hip, not the lower back
Hips stay square
mistakes: Arching the back to kick higher
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you drive the hips up, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Ankle On The Knee
exercises.description: Ankle On The Knee is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the glutes.
setup: From a lying position, bend your knees and keep your feet on the floor.
steps: Place your ankle of one foot on your opposite knee.
Grasp the thigh or knee of the bottom leg and pull both of your legs into the chest. Relax your neck and shoulders. Hold for 10-20 seconds and then switch sides.
cues: Keep the hips square and the lower back flat on the floor where lying
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Twisting the pelvis to fake the range
Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Knee Across The Body
exercises.description: Knee Across The Body is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the glutes, with help from the abductors and lower back.
steps: Lie down on the floor with your right leg straight. Bend your left leg and lower it across your body, holding the knee down toward the floor with your right hand. (The knee doesn't need to touch the floor if you're tight.)

Place your left arm comfortably beside you and turn your head to the left. Imagine you have a weight tied to your tailbone. let your tailbone fall back toward the floor as your chest reaches in the opposite direction to stretch your lower back. Switch sides.
cues: Keep the hips square and the lower back flat on the floor where lying
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Twisting the pelvis to fake the range
Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Lying Glute
exercises.description: Lying Glute is an advanced-level stretch that mainly targets the glutes, with help from the abductors.
setup: Lie on your back with your partner kneeling beside you.
steps: Flex the hip of one leg, raising it off of the floor. Rotate the leg so the foot is over the opposite hip, the lower leg perpendicular to your body. Your partner should hold the knee and ankle in place. This will be your starting position.
Attempt to push your leg towards your partner, who should be preventing any actual movement of the leg.

After 10-20 seconds, completely relax as your partner gently pushes the ankle and knee towards your chest. Be sure to inform your helper when the stretch is adequate to prevent injury or overstretching.
cues: Keep the hips square and the lower back flat on the floor where lying
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Twisting the pelvis to fake the range
Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: One Knee To Chest
exercises.description: One Knee To Chest is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the glutes, with help from the hamstrings and lower back.
setup: Start off by lying on the floor.
steps: Extend one leg straight and pull the other knee to your chest. Hold under the knee joint to protect the kneecap.
Gently tug that knee toward your nose.
Switch sides. This stretches the buttocks and lower back of the bent leg and the hip flexor of the straight leg.
cues: Keep the hips square and the lower back flat on the floor where lying
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Twisting the pelvis to fake the range
Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Seated Glute
exercises.description: Seated Glute is an advanced-level stretch that mainly targets the glutes, with help from the adductors.
setup: In a seated position with your knees bent, cross one ankle over the opposite knee. Your partner will stand behind you. Now, lean forward as your partner braces your shoulders with their hands. This will be your starting position.
steps: Attempt to push your torso back for 10-20 seconds, as your partner prevents any actual movement of your torso.
Now relax your muscles as your partner increases the stretch by gently pushing your torso forward for 10-20 seconds.
cues: Keep the hips square and the lower back flat on the floor where lying
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Twisting the pelvis to fake the range
Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.description: Driving the hips up with your upper back on a bench. One of the most direct glute exercises.
setup: Sit on the floor with your upper back (just below the shoulder blades) against a bench.
Feet flat, hip-width apart, close enough that your shins are vertical at the top.
steps: Tuck your chin slightly and drive through your heels to lift the hips.
Lock out with hips fully extended and ribs down.
Squeeze the glutes for a second.
Lower with control.
cues: Shins vertical at the top
Ribs down; finish with the glutes, not the lower back
Eyes forward, chin tucked
mistakes: Arching the lower back to finish
Feet too far forward (hamstrings take over)
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you drive the hips up, breathe in as you lower.
safety: Use a bar pad or folded mat to protect your hips.

setup: Sit on the floor with your upper back (just below the shoulder blades) against a bench.
Place the weight across your hips: roll a padded barbell over them or hold a dumbbell in place.
Feet flat, hip-width apart, close enough that your shins are vertical at the top.

exercises.name: Kneeling Jump Squat
exercises.description: Kneeling Jump Squat is an advanced-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the glutes, with help from the calves, hamstrings and quadriceps. A variation of the jump squat: from kneeling, jump to the feet with a bar on the back.
setup: Begin kneeling on the floor with a barbell racked across the back of your shoulders, or you can use your body weight for this exercise. This can be done inside of a power rack to make unracking easier.
steps: Sit back with your hips until your glutes touch your feet, keeping your head and chest up.
Explode up with your hips, generating enough power to land with your feet flat on the floor.
Continue with the squat by driving through your heels and extending the knees to come to a standing position.
cues: Soft landings
exercises.breathing: Breathe in before the jump, breathe out sharply as you take off or land.
safety: Land softly with knees bent and in line with the toes.
Stop the set when jumps become slow or landings get sloppy.
variation_notes: From kneeling, jump to the feet with a bar on the back.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Clean
exercises.description: Swinging the kettlebell up into the rack position on the front of the shoulder in one movement.
setup: Set up as for a single-arm swing.
steps: Hike the bell back.
Drive the hips forward and guide the bell close to your body.
Rotate your hand around the handle to catch the bell softly in the rack.
cues: Keep the bell close; zip up the jacket
Do not let it flip onto the forearm
mistakes: Swinging it wide and letting it bang the wrist
exercises.breathing: Breathe out sharply as the hips snap.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Snatch
exercises.description: Swinging the kettlebell from between the legs to locked out overhead in one movement.
setup: Set up as for a single-arm swing.
steps: Hike the bell back and drive the hips.
Keep it close as it rises and punch your hand through at the top.
Lock out overhead, then let it drop back into the next swing.
cues: Punch through so the bell does not crash on the forearm
exercises.breathing: Breathe out sharply as the hips drive.
safety: Learn the swing and clean first.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Swing
exercises.description: An explosive hip hinge that swings a kettlebell to chest height. Builds power in the glutes and hamstrings.
setup: Stand with feet slightly wider than hips, kettlebell on the floor about 30 cm in front.
Hinge and grip the handle with both hands.
steps: Hike the bell back between your legs.
Snap your hips forward to stand tall, letting the bell float to chest height.
Let it fall back and hinge to receive it between your legs.
cues: It is a hinge, not a squat
Snap the hips; arms just hold on
Stand tall and squeeze the glutes at the top
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as the bell travels back, breathe out sharply as you snap the hips forward.
safety: Keep the bell close on the backswing and your back flat.

exercises.name: Kneeling Squat
exercises.description: Kneeling Squat is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the glutes, with help from the abs & core, hamstrings and lower back.
setup: Set the bar to the proper height in a power rack. Kneel behind the bar; it may be beneficial to put a mat down to pad your knees. Slide under the bar, racking it across the back of your shoulders. Your shoulder blades should be retracted and the bar tight across your back. Unrack the weight.
steps: With your head looking forward, sit back with your butt until you touch your calves.
Reverse the motion, returning the torso to an upright position.
cues: Kneel behind the bar on a mat
Sit back onto the heels
Drive the hips forward to kneel tall
exercises.breathing: Inhale and brace at the top, keep the brace on the way down and through the bottom, and exhale as you finish standing.

exercises.name: Reverse Hyperextension
exercises.description: Lying face down with your legs hanging off the end of a bench or machine, lifting the legs up behind you.
setup: Lie face down on the reverse hyper (or a high bench) with hips at the edge.
Hold the handles; legs hang down.
steps: Lift your legs up behind you until they are in line with your body.
Lower with control.
cues: Squeeze the glutes to lift
Do not swing
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you drive the hips up, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Reverse Plank
exercises.description: Holding a straight body facing up, supported on your hands (or forearms) and heels.
setup: Sit with legs straight and hands on the floor behind your hips, fingers toward your feet.
steps: Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to heels.
Hold.
cues: Squeeze the glutes
Chest open
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and steadily through the hold; do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Hang Snatch
exercises.description: Lifting the bar from the floor to locked arms overhead in one movement, catching it in an overhead squat.
setup: Take a wide (snatch) grip so the bar sits in your hip crease when standing.
Set up with the bar over mid-foot, back flat, hips lower than for a deadlift.
steps: Start standing with the bar at your hips, then lower it to just above the knees.
Extend explosively and pull yourself under the bar.
Catch it with locked arms in an overhead squat.
Stand up.
cues: Bar close to the body
Punch the arms up to lock out
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
safety: Olympic lifts are technical; learn them with a coach and an empty bar or PVC pipe first.
Use bumper plates and a platform so the bar can be dropped safely.
variation_notes: Starts from the hang position above the knees.

exercises.name: Power Snatch
