setup: Take a wide (snatch) grip so the bar sits in your hip crease when standing.
Set up with the bar over mid-foot, back flat, hips lower than for a deadlift.
steps: Lift the bar to the hips keeping it close.
Extend explosively and pull yourself under the bar.
Catch it with locked arms in an overhead squat.
Stand up.
cues: Bar close to the body
Punch the arms up to lock out
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
safety: Olympic lifts are technical; learn them with a coach and an empty bar or PVC pipe first.
Use bumper plates and a platform so the bar can be dropped safely.
variation_notes: Caught with a partial squat (thighs above parallel).

exercises.name: Snatch
exercises.description: Lifting the bar from the floor to locked arms overhead in one movement, catching it in an overhead squat.
setup: Take a wide (snatch) grip so the bar sits in your hip crease when standing.
Set up with the bar over mid-foot, back flat, hips lower than for a deadlift.
steps: Lift the bar to the hips keeping it close.
Extend explosively and pull yourself under the bar.
Catch it with locked arms in an overhead squat.
Stand up.
cues: Bar close to the body
Punch the arms up to lock out
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
safety: Olympic lifts are technical; learn them with a coach and an empty bar or PVC pipe first.
Use bumper plates and a platform so the bar can be dropped safely.

exercises.name: Step-up with Knee Raise
exercises.description: Step-up with Knee Raise is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the glutes, with help from the hamstrings and quadriceps. A variation of the step up: drive the other knee up at the top.
setup: Stand facing a box or bench of an appropriate height with your feet together. This will be your starting position.
steps: Begin the movement by stepping up, putting your left foot on the top of the bench. Extend through the hip and knee of your front leg to stand up on the box. As you stand on the box with your left leg, flex your right knee and hip, bringing your knee as high as you can.
Reverse this motion to step down off the box, and then repeat the sequence on the opposite leg.
cues: Push through the top leg, not the bottom foot
Stand fully tall on top
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back up.
safety: Use a stable box that will not slide.
variation_notes: Drive the other knee up at the top.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift
exercises.description: A deadlift with a very wide stance and hands inside the legs. The torso stays more upright and the hips and inner thighs work harder.
setup: Stand with feet well wider than shoulders, toes turned out, shins close to the bar.
Grip the bar inside your legs, arms hanging straight down.
Push your knees out and lift your chest.
steps: Brace and push the floor apart with your feet.
Keep the bar close as you stand up.
Lock out by squeezing the glutes.
Lower with control.
cues: Knees out over the toes
Chest up, hips close to the bar
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace hard before each rep. Hold it as you lift, and breathe out at the top or once the weight is back down.
safety: Needs good hip mobility; find a stance width you can get into with a flat back.

exercises.name: Box Jump (Multiple Response)
exercises.description: Box Jump (Multiple Response) is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the abductors, adductors, calves, glutes and quadriceps. A variation of the box jump: several jumps in a row without resetting.
setup: Assume a relaxed stance facing the box or platform approximately an arm's length away. Arms should be down at the sides and legs slightly bent.
steps: Using the arms to aid in the initial burst, jump upward and forward, landing with feet simultaneously on top of the box or platform.
Immediately drop or jump back down to the original starting place; then repeat the sequence.
cues: Land quietly
Knees in line with the toes
mistakes: Choosing a box so high that you land in a deep squat
exercises.breathing: Breathe in before the jump, breathe out sharply as you take off or land.
safety: Land softly with knees bent and in line with the toes.
Stop the set when jumps become slow or landings get sloppy.
Step down rather than jumping down to protect your Achilles tendons.
variation_notes: Several jumps in a row without resetting.

exercises.name: Box Skip
exercises.description: Box Skip is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the abductors, adductors, calves, glutes and quadriceps. A variation of the box jump: skipping onto a box, alternating legs.
setup: You will need several boxes lined up about 8 feet apart.
steps: Begin facing the first box with one leg slightly behind the other.
Drive off the back leg, attempting to gain as much height with the hips as possible.

Immediately upon landing on the box, drive the other leg forward and upward to gain height and distance, leaping from the box. Land between the first two boxes with the same leg that landed on the first box.
Then, step to the next box and repeat.
cues: Land quietly
Knees in line with the toes
mistakes: Choosing a box so high that you land in a deep squat
exercises.breathing: Breathe in before the jump, breathe out sharply as you take off or land.
safety: Land softly with knees bent and in line with the toes.
Stop the set when jumps become slow or landings get sloppy.
Step down rather than jumping down to protect your Achilles tendons.
variation_notes: Skipping onto a box, alternating legs.

exercises.name: Band Good Morning (Pull Through)
exercises.description: Band Good Morning (Pull Through) is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the glutes and lower back. A variation of the cable pull through: a band anchored low behind you replaces the cable.
setup: Loop the band around a post. Standing a little ways away, loop the opposite end around the neck. Your hands can help hold the band in position.
steps: Begin by bending at the hips, getting your butt back as far as possible. Keep your back flat and bend forward to about 90 degrees. Your knees should be only slightly bent.
Return to the starting position be driving through with the hips to come back to a standing position.
cues: It is a hinge, not a squat
Arms just hold the band
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you drive the hips up, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: A band anchored low behind you replaces the cable.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Clean
exercises.description: Dumbbell Clean is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the calves, forearms, glutes, lower back, quadriceps and traps. A variation of the clean: two dumbbells pulled and caught at the shoulders.
setup: Begin standing with a dumbbell in each hand with your feet shoulder width apart.
steps: Lower the weights to the floor by flexing at the hips and knees, pushing your hips back until the dumbbells reach the floor. This will be your starting position.

To initiate the movement, violently jump upward by extending the hips, knees, and ankles to acclerate the weights upward. Maintaining a neutral grip on the dumbbells, keep the arms straight until full extension is reached.
After full extension, rebend the hips and knees to receive the weight in a squat position. Allow the arms to bend, guiding the dumbbells to your shoulders.
Upon receiving the weight in the squat position, extend the hips and knees to finish in a standing position with the weights on your shoulders.
cues: Dumbbells stay close to the body
Explosive hip drive, then pull yourself under
Catch on the shoulders with the elbows forward
mistakes: Curling the dumbbells up with the arms
Dumbbells swinging away from the body
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
safety: Learn the movement with light dumbbells first.
variation_notes: Two dumbbells pulled and caught at the shoulders.

exercises.name: Power Clean from Blocks
exercises.description: Power Clean from Blocks is an intermediate-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the quadriceps. A variation of the clean: bar starts on blocks; caught above parallel.
setup: With a barbell on boxes of the desired height, take a grip just outside the legs. Lower your hips with the weight focused on the heels, back straight, head facing forward, chest up, with your shoulders just in front of the bar. This will be your starting position.
steps: Begin the first pull by driving through the heels, extending your knees. Your back angle should stay the same, and your arms should remain straight. As the bar approaches the mid-thigh position, begin extending through the hips.

In a jumping motion, accelerate by extending the hips, knees, and ankles, using speed to move the bar upward. There should be no need to actively pull through the arms to accelerate the weight. At the end of the second pull, the body should be fully extended, leaning slightly back, with the arms still extended.

As full extension is achieved, transition into the third pull by aggressively shrugging and flexing the arms with the elbows up and out. At peak extension, pull yourself under the bar far enough that it can be racked onto the shoulders, rotating your elbows under the bar as you do so. The bar should be racked onto the protracted shoulders, lightly touching the throat with the hands relaxed.

Immediately recover by driving through the heels, keeping the torso upright and elbows up. Continue until you have risen to a standing position, and complete the repetition by returning the weight to the boxes.
cues: Bar stays close to the body
Patient off the floor, explosive at the hips
Fast elbows in the catch
mistakes: Bar swinging away from the body
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
safety: Olympic lifts are technical; learn them with a coach and an empty bar or PVC pipe first.
Use bumper plates and a platform so the bar can be dropped safely.
variation_notes: Bar starts on blocks; caught above parallel.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Hang Power Clean
exercises.description: Smith Machine Hang Power Clean is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the glutes, lower back, quadriceps and traps. A variation of the clean: smith machine; teaches the bar path.
setup: Position the bar at knee height and load it to an appropriate weight.
steps: Take a pronated grip on the bar outside of shoulder width and unhook the bar from the machine. Your arms should be fully extended with your head and chest up. Your elbows should be pointed out with your shoulders back and down. Your hips should be back, loading the tension into the hamstrings. This will be your starting position.
Initate the movement by forcefully extending the hips and knees, accelerating into the bar. Ensure that you keep your arms straight during this part of the motion.
Upon full extension, rebend the hips and knees to lower your receiving position.
Allow the arms to flex at this point, rotating the elbows around the bar to receive it on your shoulders.
Extend through the hips and knees to come to a standing position with the bar racked on your shoulders to complete the movement.
cues: Bar stays close to the body
Patient off the floor, explosive at the hips
Fast elbows in the catch
mistakes: Bar swinging away from the body
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
safety: Olympic lifts are technical; learn them with a coach and an empty bar or PVC pipe first.
Use bumper plates and a platform so the bar can be dropped safely.
variation_notes: Smith machine; teaches the bar path.

exercises.name: Clean Deadlift
exercises.description: Clean Deadlift is a beginner-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the forearms, glutes, lower back, upper back, quadriceps and traps. A variation of the clean pull: lift to standing with clean positions, no jump.
setup: Begin standing with a barbell close to your shins. Your feet should be directly under your hips with your feet turned out slightly. Grip the bar with a double overhand grip or hook grip, about shoulder width apart. Squat down to the bar. Your spine should be in full extension, with a back angle that places your shoulders in front of the bar and your back as vertical as possible.
steps: Begin by driving through the floor through the front of your heels. As the bar travels upward, maintain a constant back angle. Flare your knees out to the side to help keep them out of the bar's path.
After the bar crosses the knees, complete the lift by driving the hips into the bar until your hips and knees are extended.
cues: Full extension of hips, knees and ankles
Arms stay straight
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
variation_notes: Lift to standing with clean positions, no jump.

exercises.name: Snatch Deadlift
exercises.description: Snatch Deadlift is an intermediate-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the forearms, glutes, lower back, quadriceps and traps. A variation of the clean pull: wide snatch grip, lift to standing.
setup: The snatch deadlift strengthens the first pull of the snatch. Begin with a wide snatch grip with the barbell placed on the platform. The feet should be directly under the hips, with the feet turned out. Squat down to the bar, keeping the back in absolute extension with the head facing forward.
steps: Initiate the movement by driving through the heels, raising the hips. The back angle should remain the same until the bar passes the knees.
At that point, drive your hips through the bar as you lay back. Return the bar to the platform by reversing the motion.
cues: Full extension of hips, knees and ankles
Arms stay straight
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
variation_notes: Wide snatch grip, lift to standing.

exercises.name: Snatch Pull
exercises.description: Snatch Pull is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the calves, glutes, lower back, quadriceps and traps. A variation of the clean pull: wide snatch grip, full extension and shrug.
setup: With a barbell on the floor close to the shins, take a wide snatch grip. Lower your hips with the weight focused on the heels, back straight, head facing forward, chest up, with your shoulders just in front of the bar. This will be your starting position.
steps: Begin the first pull by driving through the heels, extending your knees. Your back angle should stay the same, and your arms should remain straight. Move the weight with control as you continue to above the knees.

Next comes the second pull, the main source of acceleration for the pull. As the bar approaches the mid-thigh position, begin extending through the hips. In a jumping motion, accelerate by extending the hips, knees, and ankles, using speed to move the bar upward.

There should be no need to actively pull through the arms to accelerate the weight; at the end of the second pull, the body should be fully extended, leaning slightly back. Full extension should be violent and abrupt, and ensure that you do not prolong the extension for longer than necessary.
cues: Full extension of hips, knees and ankles
Arms stay straight
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
variation_notes: Wide snatch grip, full extension and shrug.

exercises.name: Downward Dog
exercises.description: A yoga pose forming an upside-down V, stretching the hamstrings, calves and shoulders.
steps: From hands and knees, lift your hips up and back.
Straighten your legs as far as comfortable and press your heels toward the floor.
Hold, then lower your knees.
cues: Long spine; bend the knees if needed
Push the floor away
mistakes: Rounding the back to straighten the legs
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly through the nose while holding the position.
safety: Warm up for 5–10 minutes before hard efforts.
Build duration and intensity gradually from week to week.

exercises.name: Front Leg Raises
exercises.description: Front Leg Raises is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the hamstrings.
steps: Stand next to a chair or other support, holding on with one hand.
Swing your leg forward, keeping the leg straight. Continue with a downward swing, bringing the leg as far back as your flexibility allows. Repeat 5-10 times, and then switch legs.
cues: Start small and slow, then grow the range
Smooth, controlled movement, no flinging
About 8–12 reps per side as a warm-up
mistakes: Swinging into end range with momentum
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Inchworm
exercises.description: Inchworm is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the hamstrings.
setup: Stand with your feet close together. Keeping your legs straight, stretch down and put your hands on the floor directly in front of you. This will be your starting position.
steps: Begin by walking your hands forward slowly, alternating your left and your right. As you do so, bend only at the hip, keeping your legs straight.
Keep going until your body is parallel to the ground in a pushup position.
Now, keep your hands in place and slowly take short steps with your feet, moving only a few inches at a time.
Continue walking until your feet are by hour hands, keeping your legs straight as you do so.
cues: Start small and slow, then grow the range
Smooth, controlled movement, no flinging
About 8–12 reps per side as a warm-up
mistakes: Swinging into end range with momentum
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch
exercises.description: World's Greatest Stretch is an intermediate-level stretch that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the calves, glutes and quadriceps.
setup: This is a three-part stretch. Begin by lunging forward, with your front foot flat on the ground and on the toes of your back foot. With your knees bent, squat down until your knee is almost touching the ground. Keep your torso erect, and hold this position for 10-20 seconds.
steps: Now, place the arm on the same side as your front leg on the ground, with the elbow next to the foot. Your other hand should be placed on the ground, parallel to your lead leg, to help support you during this portion of the stretch.

After 10-20 seconds, place your hands on either side of your front foot. Raise the toes of the front foot off of the ground, and straighten your leg. You may need to reposition your rear leg to do so. Hold for 10-20 seconds, and then repeat the entire sequence for the other side.
cues: Start small and slow, then grow the range
Smooth, controlled movement, no flinging
About 8–12 reps per side as a warm-up
mistakes: Swinging into end range with momentum
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Hamstring-SMR
exercises.description: Hamstring-SMR is a beginner-level self-massage (foam rolling) exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings.
setup: In a seated position, extend your legs over a foam roll so that it is position on the back of the upper legs. Place your hands to the side or behind you to help support your weight. This will be your starting position.
steps: Using your hands, lift your hips off of the floor and shift your weight on the foam roll to one leg. Relax the hamstrings of the leg you are stretching.
Roll over the foam from below the hip to above the back of the knee, pausing at points of tension for 10-30 seconds. Repeat for the other leg.
cues: Roll slowly, about 2–3 cm per second
Pause 20–30 seconds on tender spots
Support your weight with hands and feet to control the pressure
30–90 seconds per area
mistakes: Rolling directly over joints or bones
Pressing so hard you tense up
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and stay relaxed. On a tender spot, pause and take a few long exhales to let the muscle release.
safety: Avoid rolling the lower back and neck with full body weight; use a softer tool there.

exercises.name: Glute Ham Raise
exercises.description: On a glute-ham developer, you lower your torso and pull yourself back up using the hamstrings and glutes.
setup: Lock your feet in the foot plate with knees just behind the pad.
steps: Start upright, then lower your torso forward until it is parallel to the floor.
Pull yourself back up by curling your heels into the plate.
cues: Hips stay straight
Pull with the hamstrings
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back up.

exercises.name: Band Good Morning
exercises.description: Band Good Morning is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the glutes and lower back. A variation of the good morning: standing on a band looped behind the neck.
setup: Using a 41 inch band, stand on one end, spreading your feet a small amount. Bend at the hips to loop the end of the band behind your neck. This will be your starting position.
steps: Keeping your legs straight, extend through the hips to come to a near vertical position.
Ensure that you do not round your back as you go down back to the starting position.
cues: Flat back throughout
Hips back, not down
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace hard before each rep. Hold it as you lift, and breathe out at the top or once the weight is back down.
safety: Start very light; the lever arm makes this heavy on the lower back.
variation_notes: Standing on a band looped behind the neck.

exercises.name: Good Morning (Barbell)
exercises.description: With a bar on your upper back, you hinge forward at the hips and stand back up. Trains the hamstrings and lower back.
setup: Rest a light barbell on your upper back as for a squat.
Feet hip-width apart, knees soft.
steps: Push your hips back and lower your torso until it is near parallel or you feel a strong hamstring stretch.
Drive the hips forward to stand up.
cues: Flat back throughout
Hips back, not down
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace hard before each rep. Hold it as you lift, and breathe out at the top or once the weight is back down.
safety: Start very light; the lever arm makes this heavy on the lower back.

exercises.name: Good Morning off Pins
exercises.description: Good Morning off Pins is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the abs & core, glutes and lower back. A variation of the good morning: starts from the bottom with the bar on safety pins.
steps: Begin with a bar on a rack at about the same height as your stomach. Bend over underneath the bar and rack the bar across the rear of your shoulders as you would a power squat, not on top of your shoulders. At the proper height, you should be near parallel to the floor when bent over. Keep your back tight, shoulder blades pinched together, and your knees slightly bent. Keep your back arched and your cervical spine in proper alignment.
Begin the motion by extending through the hips with your glutes and hamstrings, and you are standing with the weight. Slowly lower the weight back to the pins returning to the starting position.
cues: Flat back throughout
Hips back, not down
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace hard before each rep. Hold it as you lift, and breathe out at the top or once the weight is back down.
safety: Start very light; the lever arm makes this heavy on the lower back.
variation_notes: Starts from the bottom with the bar on safety pins.

exercises.name: Hanging Bar Good Morning
exercises.description: Hanging Bar Good Morning is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the abs & core, glutes and lower back. A variation of the good morning: bar hangs from chains or bands at the bottom position.
setup: Begin with a bar on a rack at about the same height as your stomach. Suspend the bar using chains or suspension straps.
steps: Bend over underneath the bar and rack the bar across the rear of your shoulders as you would a power squat, not on top of your traps. At the proper height, you should be near parallel to the floor when bent over. Keep your back tight, shoulder blades pinched together, and your knees slightly bent. Keep your back arched and your cervical spine in proper alignment.
Begin the motion by extending through the hips with your glutes and hamstrings, and you are standing with the weight.
Slowly lower the weight back to the starting position, where it is supported by the chains.
cues: Flat back throughout
Hips back, not down
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace hard before each rep. Hold it as you lift, and breathe out at the top or once the weight is back down.
safety: Start very light; the lever arm makes this heavy on the lower back.
variation_notes: Bar hangs from chains or bands at the bottom position.

exercises.name: Intermediate Groin Stretch
exercises.description: Intermediate Groin Stretch is an intermediate-level stretch that mainly targets the hamstrings.
steps: Lie on your back with your legs extended. Loop a belt, rope, or band around one of your feet, and swing that leg as far to the side as you can. This will be your starting position.
Pull gently on the belt to create tension in your groin and hamstring muscles. Hold for 10-20 seconds, and repeat on the other side.
cues: Let the knees fall out under their own weight before pressing gently
Sit tall with a long spine
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: The Straddle
exercises.description: The Straddle is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the adductors and calves.
steps: Begin in a seated, upright position. Start by extending your legs in front of you in a V.
With your hands on the floor, lean forward as far as possible. Hold for 10 to 20 seconds.
cues: Let the knees fall out under their own weight before pressing gently
Sit tall with a long spine
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: 90/90 Hamstring
exercises.description: 90/90 Hamstring is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the calves.
setup: Lie on your back, with one leg extended straight out.
steps: With the other leg, bend the hip and knee to 90 degrees. You may brace your leg with your hands if necessary. This will be your starting position.
Extend your leg straight into the air, pausing briefly at the top. Return the leg to the starting position.
Repeat for 10-20 repetitions, and then switch to the other leg.
cues: Hinge from the hips with a long back instead of rounding to reach
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
A slight knee bend is fine
mistakes: Rounding the lower back to reach further
Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Chair Leg Extended Stretch
exercises.description: Chair Leg Extended Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the adductors.
setup: Sit upright in a chair and grip the seat on the sides.
steps: Raise one leg, extending the knee, flexing the ankle as you do so.
Slowly move that leg outward as far as you can, and then back to the center and down.
Repeat for your other leg.
cues: Hinge from the hips with a long back instead of rounding to reach
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
A slight knee bend is fine
mistakes: Rounding the lower back to reach further
Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Hamstring Stretch
exercises.description: Hamstring Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the hamstrings.
setup: Lie on your back with one leg extended above you, with the hip at ninety degrees. Keep the other leg flat on the floor.
steps: Loop a belt, band, or rope over the ball of your foot. This will be your starting position.
Pull on the belt to create tension in the calves and hamstrings. Hold this stretch for 10-30 seconds, and repeat with the other leg.
cues: Hinge from the hips with a long back instead of rounding to reach
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
A slight knee bend is fine
mistakes: Rounding the lower back to reach further
Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Leg-Up Hamstring Stretch
exercises.description: Leg-Up Hamstring Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the hamstrings.
setup: Lie flat on your back, bend one knee, and put that foot flat on the floor to stabilize your spine.
steps: Extend the other leg in the air. If you're tight, you wont be able to straighten it. That's okay. Extend the knee so that the sole of the lifted foot faces the ceiling (or as close as you can get it).
Slowly straighten the legs as much as possible and then pull the leg toward your nose. Switch sides.
cues: Hinge from the hips with a long back instead of rounding to reach
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
A slight knee bend is fine
mistakes: Rounding the lower back to reach further
Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Lying Hamstring
exercises.description: Lying Hamstring is an advanced-level stretch that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the calves.
setup: Lie on your back with your legs extended. Your partner should be kneeling beside you. Raise one leg up towards the ceiling and have your partner hold the ankle. Your partner can use their shoulder to brace your leg if necessary. This will be your starting position.
steps: With your partner holding your leg in place, attempt to flex the knee, contracting the hamstrings for 10-20 seconds.

Then relax your leg, allowing your partner to gently push the leg towards your head. Be sure to inform your helper when the stretch is adequate to prevent injury or overstretching. Switch sides once complete.
cues: Hinge from the hips with a long back instead of rounding to reach
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
A slight knee bend is fine
mistakes: Rounding the lower back to reach further
Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Runner's Stretch
exercises.description: Runner's Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the calves.
setup: It's easiest to get into this stretch if you start standing up, put one leg behind you, and slowly lower your torso down to the floor.
steps: Keep the front heel on the floor (if it lifts up, scoot your other leg further back).

Place your hands on either side of your front leg. To get more out of this stretch, push your butt up toward the ceiling, and then gradually lower it back toward the floor. You'll Stretch the hip flexor of the back leg and the hamstring and buttocks of the front.
cues: Hinge from the hips with a long back instead of rounding to reach
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
A slight knee bend is fine
mistakes: Rounding the lower back to reach further
Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.description: Seated Floor Hamstring Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the calves.
steps: Sit on a mat with your right leg extended in front of you and your left leg bent with your foot against your right inner thigh.
Lean forward from your hips and reach for your ankle until you feel a stretch in your hamstring. Hold for 15 seconds, then repeat for your other side.

setup: In a seated position with your legs extended, have your partner stand behind you. Now, lean forward as your partner braces your shoulders with their hands. This will be your starting position.
steps: Attempt to push your torso back for 10-20 seconds, as your partner prevents any actual movement of your torso.
Now relax your muscles as your partner increases the stretch by gently pushing your torso forward for 10-20 seconds.

steps: Loop a belt, rope, or band around one foot. Sit down with both legs extended . This will be your starting position.
Leaning forward slightly, pull on the belt to draw the toes of your foot back. Hold this position for 10-20 seconds and then repeat with the other leg.

setup: Being by looping a belt, band, or rope around one foot. While standing, place that foot forward.
steps: Bend your back leg, while keeping the front one straight. Now raise the toes of your front foot off of the ground and lean forward.
Using the belt, pull on the top of the foot to increase the stretch in the calf. Hold for 10-20 seconds and repeat with the other foot.

steps: Stand with some space in front and behind you.
Bend at the waist, keeping your legs straight, until you can relax and let your upper body hang down in front of you. Let your arms and hands hang down naturally. Hold for 10 to 20 seconds.

exercises.name: Upper Back-Leg Grab
exercises.description: Upper Back-Leg Grab is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the lower back and upper back.
steps: While seated, bend forward to hug your thighs from underneath with both arms.
Keep your knees together and your legs extended out as you bring your chest down to your knees. You can also stretch your middle back by pulling your back away from your knees as your hugging them.
cues: Hinge from the hips with a long back instead of rounding to reach

exercises.name: Hurdle Hops
exercises.description: Hurdle Hops is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the abductors, adductors, calves and glutes.
setup: Set up a row of hurdles or other small barriers, placing them a few feet apart.
steps: Stand in front of the first hurdle with your feet shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.
Begin by jumping with both feet over the first hurdle, swinging both arms as you jump.
Absorb the impact of landing by bending the knees, rebounding out of the first leap by jumping over the next hurdle. Continue until you have jumped over all of the hurdles.
cues: Land softly on the balls of the feet
Spend as little time on the ground as possible
Knees track over the toes
Arms drive each jump
mistakes: Landing on the heels or stiff-legged
Doing too many reps when tired
exercises.breathing: Take a quick breath before each effort and exhale sharply as you take off. Reset your breathing between reps.
safety: Use a forgiving surface and stop the set when landings get sloppy.

exercises.name: Knee Tuck Jump
exercises.description: Knee Tuck Jump is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the abductors, adductors, calves, glutes and quadriceps.
setup: Begin in a comfortable standing position with your knees slightly bent. Hold your hands in front of you, palms down with your fingertips together at chest height. This will be your starting position.
steps: Rapidly dip down into a quarter squat and immediately explode upward. Drive the knees towards the chest, attempting to touch them to the palms of the hands.
Jump as high as you can, raising your knees up, and then ensure a good land be re-extending your legs, absorbing impact through be allowing the knees to rebend.
cues: Jump straight up and land where you started
Land softly with bent knees
Keep the chest up
exercises.breathing: Take a quick breath before each effort and exhale sharply as you take off. Reset your breathing between reps.

exercises.name: Alternating Hang Clean
exercises.description: Alternating Hang Clean is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the biceps, calves, forearms, glutes, lower back and traps. A variation of the kettlebell clean: two kettlebells, cleaned one at a time.
setup: Place two kettlebells between your feet. To get in the starting position, push your butt back and look straight ahead.
steps: Clean one kettlebell to your shoulder and hold on to the other kettlebell in a hanging position. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrist as you do so.
Lower the cleaned kettlebell to a hanging position and clean the alternate kettlebell. Repeat.
cues: Keep the bell close; zip up the jacket
Do not let it flip onto the forearm
mistakes: Swinging it wide and letting it bang the wrist
exercises.breathing: Breathe out sharply as the hips snap.
variation_notes: Two kettlebells, cleaned one at a time.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Alternating Hang Clean
exercises.description: Double Kettlebell Alternating Hang Clean is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the biceps, calves, forearms, glutes, lower back, quadriceps and traps. A variation of the kettlebell clean: two kettlebells, alternating sides from the hang.
setup: Place two kettlebells between your feet. To get in the starting position, push your butt back and look straight ahead.
steps: Clean one kettlebell to your shoulder and hold on to the other kettlebell.
With a fluid motion, lower the top kettlebell while driving the bottom kettlebell up.
cues: Keep the bell close; zip up the jacket
Do not let it flip onto the forearm
mistakes: Swinging it wide and letting it bang the wrist
exercises.breathing: Breathe out sharply as the hips snap.
variation_notes: Two kettlebells, alternating sides from the hang.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Dead Clean
exercises.description: Kettlebell Dead Clean is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the calves, glutes, lower back, quadriceps and traps. A variation of the kettlebell clean: each rep starts from the floor.
setup: Place kettlebell between your feet. To get in the starting position, push your butt back and look straight ahead.
steps: Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you raise the kettlebell towards your shoulder. The wrist should rotate as you do so.
Lower the kettlebell, keeping the hamstrings loaded by keeping your back straight and your butt out.
cues: Keep the bell close; zip up the jacket
Do not let it flip onto the forearm
mistakes: Swinging it wide and letting it bang the wrist
exercises.breathing: Breathe out sharply as the hips snap.
variation_notes: Each rep starts from the floor.

exercises.name: One-Arm Open Palm Kettlebell Clean
exercises.description: One-Arm Open Palm Kettlebell Clean is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the forearms, glutes, lower back and quadriceps. A variation of the kettlebell clean: released and caught with an open hand.
setup: Place one kettlebell between your feet.
steps: Grab the handle with one hand and raise the kettlebell rapidly, let it flip so that the ball of the kettlebell lands in the palm of your hand.
Throw the kettlebell out in front of you and catch the handle with one hand.
Take the kettlebell to the floor and repeat. Make sure to work both arms.
cues: Keep the bell close; zip up the jacket
Do not let it flip onto the forearm
mistakes: Swinging it wide and letting it bang the wrist
exercises.breathing: Breathe out sharply as the hips snap.
variation_notes: Released and caught with an open hand.

exercises.name: Open Palm Kettlebell Clean
exercises.description: Open Palm Kettlebell Clean is an advanced-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the glutes, lower back and quadriceps. A variation of the kettlebell clean: released and caught with an open hand.
setup: Place one kettlebell between your feet. Clean the kettlebell by extending through the legs and hips as you raise the kettlebell towards your shoulders.
steps: Release the kettlebell as it comes up, and let it flip so that the ball of the kettlebell lands in the palms of your hands.
Release the kettlebell out in front of you and catch the handle with both hands. Lower the kettlebell to the starting position and repeat.
cues: Keep the bell close; zip up the jacket
Do not let it flip onto the forearm
mistakes: Swinging it wide and letting it bang the wrist
exercises.breathing: Breathe out sharply as the hips snap.
variation_notes: Released and caught with an open hand.

exercises.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Swings
exercises.description: One-Arm Kettlebell Swings is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the calves, glutes and lower back. A variation of the kettlebell swing: one hand; the core resists twisting.
setup: Stand with feet a little wider than shoulder width and a kettlebell on the floor just in front of you. Hinge at the hips and grip the handle with one hand.
steps: Hike the kettlebell back between your legs, keeping the back flat and the free arm out to the side for balance.
Drive the hips forward forcefully to stand tall, letting the momentum swing the kettlebell up to about chest height. The arm guides the bell; the hips lift it.
Let the bell fall back down, hinge at the hips as it passes between your legs, and go straight into the next swing.
Complete the set, then switch hands.
cues: It is a hinge, not a squat
Snap the hips; arms just hold on
Stand tall and squeeze the glutes at the top
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as the bell travels back, breathe out sharply as you snap the hips forward.
safety: Keep the bell close on the backswing and your back flat.
variation_notes: One hand; the core resists twisting.

exercises.name: Vertical Swing
exercises.description: Vertical Swing is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the glutes and quadriceps. A variation of the kettlebell swing: one dumbbell held by the end with both hands, swung up overhead.
setup: Allow the dumbbell to hang at arms length between your legs, holding it with both hands. Keep your back straight and your head up.
steps: Swing the dumbbell between your legs, flexing at the hips and bending the knees slightly.
Powerfully reverse the motion by extending at the hips, knees, and ankles to propel yourself upward, swinging the dumbell over your head.
As you land, absorb the impact through your legs and draw the dumbbell to your torso before the next repetition.
cues: It is a hinge, not a squat
Snap the hips; arms just hold on
Stand tall and squeeze the glutes at the top
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as the bell travels back, breathe out sharply as you snap the hips forward.
safety: Keep the bell close on the backswing and your back flat.
variation_notes: One dumbbell held by the end with both hands, swung up overhead.

exercises.name: Ball Leg Curl
exercises.description: Ball Leg Curl is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the calves and glutes. A variation of the leg curl: lying on the back, heels on a ball, hips lifted; curl the ball in.
setup: Begin on the floor laying on your back with your feet on top of the ball.
steps: Position the ball so that when your legs are extended your ankles are on top of the ball. This will be your starting position.
Raise your hips off of the ground, keeping your weight on the shoulder blades and your feet.
Flex the knees, pulling the ball as close to you as you can, contracting the hamstrings.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
cues: Hips stay down
Control the return
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl, breathe in as you return.
variation_notes: Lying on the back, heels on a ball, hips lifted; curl the ball in.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl (Machine)
exercises.description: Bending the knees against a pad to isolate the hamstrings.
setup: Lie face down with your knees just past the bench edge.
Place the pad just above your heels.
steps: Curl your heels toward your glutes.
Squeeze the hamstrings.
Return slowly to straight legs.
cues: Hips stay down
Control the return
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl, breathe in as you return.

exercises.name: Platform Hamstring Slides
exercises.description: Platform Hamstring Slides is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the glutes. A variation of the leg curl: heels on sliders or a towel with the hips lifted; slide the heels in.
setup: For this movement a wooden floor or similar is needed. Lay on your back with your legs extended. Place a gym towel or a light weight underneath your heel. This will be your starting position.
steps: Begin the movement by flexing the knee, keeping your other leg straight.
Continue bringing the heel closer to you, sliding it on the floor.
At full knee flexion, reverse the movement to return to the starting position.
cues: Hips stay down
Control the return
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl, breathe in as you return.
variation_notes: Heels on sliders or a towel with the hips lifted; slide the heels in.

exercises.name: Prone Manual Hamstring
exercises.description: Prone Manual Hamstring is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings. A variation of the leg curl: lying face down; a partner resists the curl by hand.
setup: You will need a partner for this exercise. Lay face down with your legs straight. Your assistant will place their hand on your heel.
steps: To begin, flex the knee to curl your leg up. Your partner should provide resistance, starting light and increasing the pressure as the movement is completed. Communicate with your partner to monitor appropriate resistance levels.
Pause at the top, returning the leg to the starting position as your partner provides resistance going the other direction.
cues: Hips stay down
Control the return
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl, breathe in as you return.
variation_notes: Lying face down; a partner resists the curl by hand.

exercises.name: Seated Band Hamstring Curl
exercises.description: Seated Band Hamstring Curl is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings. A variation of the leg curl: seated, a band anchored in front of you.
setup: Secure a band close to the ground and place a bench a couple feet away from it.
steps: Seat yourself on the bench and secure the band behind your ankles, beginning with your legs straight. This will be your starting position.
Flex the knees, bringing your feet towards the bench. You may need to lean back slightly to keep your feet from striking the floor.
Pause at the completion of the movement, and then slowly return to the starting position.

Control the return
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl, breathe in as you return.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl (Machine)

Place the lower pad behind your ankles.
steps: Curl your heels toward your glutes.
Squeeze the hamstrings.
Return slowly to straight legs.

Control the return
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl, breathe in as you return.

exercises.name: Standing Leg Curls

setup: Adjust the machine so your knees line up with the pivot.

steps: Curl your heels toward your glutes.

Return slowly to straight legs.

exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl, breathe in as you return.

exercises.name: Lunge Pass Through
exercises.description: Lunge Pass Through is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the calves, glutes and quadriceps. A variation of the lunge: pass a kettlebell under the front leg on each lunge.
setup: Stand with your torso upright holding a kettlebell in your right hand. This will be your starting position.
steps: Step forward with your left foot and lower your upper body down by flexing the hip and the knee, keeping the torso upright. Lower your back knee until it nearly touches the ground.
As you lunge, pass the kettlebell under your front leg to your opposite hand.
Pressing through the heel of your foot, return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the recommended amount of repetitions, alternating legs.
cues: Torso upright
Front knee in line with the toes
Push through the front heel
mistakes: Step too short so the heel lifts
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back up.
variation_notes: Pass a kettlebell under the front leg on each lunge.

exercises.name: Floor Glute-Ham Raise
exercises.description: Floor Glute-Ham Raise is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the calves and glutes. A variation of the nordic hamstring curl: kneeling with the ankles held down by a partner or bar.
setup: You can use a partner for this exercise or brace your feet under something stable.
steps: Begin on your knees with your upper legs and torso upright. If using a partner, they will firmly hold your feet to keep you in position. This will be your starting position.
Lower yourself by extending at the knee, taking care to NOT flex the hips as you go forward.

Place your hands in front of you as you reach the floor. This movement is very difficult and you may be unable to do it unaided. Use your arms to lightly push off the floor to aid your return to the starting position.
cues: Straight line from knees to head
Fight the fall
exercises.breathing: Breathe out slowly as you lower.
safety: Very intense; start with only a few reps.
variation_notes: Kneeling with the ankles held down by a partner or bar.

exercises.name: Nordic Hamstrings Curls
exercises.description: Kneeling with your ankles anchored, you lower your body forward as slowly as possible using the hamstrings.
setup: Kneel on a pad with your ankles secured under something solid or held by a partner.
steps: Keeping hips straight, lean forward and lower your body as slowly as you can.
Catch yourself with your hands.
Push off lightly and pull back up with the hamstrings.
cues: Straight line from knees to head
Fight the fall
exercises.breathing: Breathe out slowly as you lower.
safety: Very intense; start with only a few reps.

exercises.name: Pilates
exercises.description: Low-impact exercise focused on core control, posture and flexibility.
steps: Follow a mat or reformer session suited to your level.
cues: Move slowly and with control
Keep the core engaged
exercises.breathing: Breathe out on the effort and in on the return, as cued in the session.
safety: Warm up for 5–10 minutes before hard efforts.
Build duration and intensity gradually from week to week.

exercises.name: Split Squats
exercises.description: Split Squats is an intermediate-level stretch that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the calves, glutes and quadriceps.
steps: Being in a standing position. Jump into a split leg position, with one leg forward and one leg back, flexing the knees and lowering your hips slightly as you do so.
As you descend, immediately reverse direction, standing back up and jumping, reversing the position of your legs. Repeat 5-10 times on each leg.
cues: Tuck the pelvis under and squeeze the glute on the stretching side
Keep the knees close together for the quad stretch
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Arching the lower back instead of tucking the pelvis
Pulling the knee out to the side
Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift (Barbell)
exercises.description: A deadlift that starts standing and lowers only until the hamstrings are stretched, with soft knees. One of the best hamstring exercises.
setup: Stand tall holding the weight in front of your thighs, feet hip-width apart.
Unlock your knees slightly.
steps: Push your hips back and let the weight slide down the front of your legs.
Keep your back flat and knees soft (they barely move).
Stop when you feel a strong stretch in the hamstrings, usually just below the knee.
Drive the hips forward to stand up.
cues: Hips go back, not down
Weight stays close to the legs
Flat back from head to hips
mistakes: Rounding the back to reach lower
Bending the knees into a squat
exercises.breathing: Breathe in and brace at the top, hold as you lower, breathe out as you stand back up.
safety: Depth is set by your hamstring flexibility, not by touching the floor.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift from Deficit
exercises.description: Romanian Deadlift from Deficit is an intermediate-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the forearms, glutes, lower back and traps. A variation of the romanian deadlift: standing on a platform for a longer stretch at the bottom.
setup: Begin standing while holding a bar at arm's length in front of you. You can stand on a raised platform to increase the range of motion.
steps: Begin by flexing the knees slightly, and then flex at the hip, moving your butt back as far as possible, lowering the torso as far as flexibility allows. The back should remain in absolute extension at all times, and the bar should remain in contact with the legs. If done properly, there should be heavy tension felt in the hamstrings.

exercises.name: Kettlebell One-Legged Deadlift
exercises.description: Kettlebell One-Legged Deadlift is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the glutes and lower back. A variation of the single leg romanian deadlift: kettlebell held in the hand opposite the standing leg.
setup: Hold a kettlebell by the handle in one hand. Stand on one leg, on the same side that you hold the kettlebell.
steps: Keeping that knee slightly bent, perform a stiff legged deadlift by bending at the hip, extending your free leg behind you for balance.
Continue lowering the kettlebell until you are parallel to the ground, and then return to the upright position.
cues: Hips stay square to the floor

mistakes: Opening the hip toward the ceiling
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you hinge down, breathe out as you stand up.
safety: Hold a support with the free hand if balance limits you.
variation_notes: Kettlebell held in the hand opposite the standing leg.

exercises.description: A Romanian deadlift on one leg with the other leg extending behind you. Builds hamstrings, glutes and balance.
setup: Stand on one leg holding the weight, standing knee slightly bent.
steps: Hinge forward at the hip while the free leg extends straight back.
Lower until your torso is close to parallel or you feel the stretch.
Return to standing by driving the hip forward.

Body moves like a seesaw
mistakes: Opening the hip toward the ceiling

exercises.name: Prowler Sprint
exercises.description: Prowler Sprint is a beginner-level cardio exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the cardio, calves, chest, glutes and quadriceps. A variation of the sled push: light sled, sprinting.
setup: Place your sled on an appropriate surface, loaded to a suitable weight. The sled should provide enough resistance to require effort, but not so heavy that you are significantly slowed down.
steps: You may use the upright or the low handles for this exercise. Place your hands on the handles with your arms extended, leaning into the implement.
With good posture, drive through the ground with alternating, short steps. Move as fast as you can for a short distance.
cues: Low body angle
Drive the knees forward
exercises.breathing: Breathe hard and rhythmically; do not hold your breath for long pushes.
variation_notes: Light sled, sprinting.

exercises.name: Hang Snatch - Below Knees
exercises.description: Hang Snatch - Below Knees is an advanced-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the abs & core, calves, forearms, glutes, lower back, quadriceps and traps. A variation of the snatch: starts from the hang just below the knees.
setup: Begin with a wide grip on the bar, with an overhand or hook grip. The feet should be directly below the hips with the feet turned out. Your knees should be slightly bent, and the torso inclined forward. The spine should be fully extended and the head facing forward. The bar should be just below the knees. This will be your starting position.
steps: Aggressively extend through the legs and hips. At peak extension, shrug the shoulders and allow the elbows to flex to the side.

As you move your feet into the receiving position, forcefully pull yourself below the bar as you elevate the bar overhead. Receive the bar with your body as low as possible and the arms fully extended overhead.
Return to a standing position with the weight overhead, and then return the weight to the floor under control.
cues: Bar close to the body
Punch the arms up to lock out
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
safety: Olympic lifts are technical; learn them with a coach and an empty bar or PVC pipe first.
Use bumper plates and a platform so the bar can be dropped safely.
variation_notes: Starts from the hang just below the knees.

exercises.name: Muscle Snatch
exercises.description: Muscle Snatch is an intermediate-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the glutes, lower back, quadriceps and triceps. A variation of the snatch: no re-bend of the knees; the arms finish the lift.
setup: Begin with a loaded barbell held at the mid thigh position with a wide grip. The feet should be directly below the hips, with the feet turned out as needed. Lower the hips, with the chest up and the head looking forward. The shoulders should be just in front of the bar. This will be the starting position.
steps: Begin the pull by driving through the front of the heels, raising the bar. Transition into the second pull by extending through the hips knees and ankles, driving the bar up as quickly as possible. The bar should be close to the body.
Continue raising the bar to the overhead position, without rebending the knees.
cues: Bar close to the body
Punch the arms up to lock out
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
safety: Olympic lifts are technical; learn them with a coach and an empty bar or PVC pipe first.
Use bumper plates and a platform so the bar can be dropped safely.
variation_notes: No re-bend of the knees; the arms finish the lift.

exercises.name: Split Snatch
exercises.description: Split Snatch is an advanced-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the calves, forearms, glutes, lower back, quadriceps, traps and triceps. A variation of the snatch: caught in a split stance.
setup: Begin with a loaded barbell on the floor. The bar should be close to or touching the shins, and a wide grip should be taken on the bar. The feet should be directly below the hips, with the feet turned out as needed. Lower the hips, with the chest up and the head looking forward. The shoulders should be just in front of the bar. This will be the starting position.
steps: Begin the first pull by driving through the front of the heels, raising the bar from the ground. The back angle should stay the same until the bar passes the knees.

Transition into the second pull by extending through the hips knees and ankles, driving the bar up as quickly as possible. The bar should be close to the body. At peak extension, shrug the shoulders and allow the elbows to flex to the side.

As you move your feet into the receiving position, forcefully pull yourself below the bar as you elevate the bar overhead. The feet should move forcefully to a split position, one foot forward one foot back. Receive the bar with your body as low as possible and the arms fully extended overhead.
Keeping the bar aligned over the front of the heels, your head and chest up, drive through heels of the feet to move to a standing position, bringing your feet together.
Carefully return the weight to floor.
cues: Bar close to the body
Punch the arms up to lock out
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
safety: Olympic lifts are technical; learn them with a coach and an empty bar or PVC pipe first.
Use bumper plates and a platform so the bar can be dropped safely.
variation_notes: Caught in a split stance.

exercises.name: Linear 3-Part Start Technique
exercises.description: Linear 3-Part Start Technique is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the calves and quadriceps.
setup: This drill helps you accelerate as quickly as possible into a sprint from a dead stop. It helps to use a line to start from. Begin with two feet on the line. Place your left foot with the toe next to your right ankle. Place your right foot 4-6 inches behind the left.
steps: Place your right hand onto the line, and thing bring your nose close to your left knee.
Squat down as you lean foward, your head being lower than your hips and your weight loaded onto the left leg. This will be your starting position.
Take your left hand up so that it is parallel to the ground, pointing behind you, and explode out when ready.
cues: Drive the knee up and the foot down under the hips
Arms swing from the shoulder, elbows about 90 degrees
Stay tall with a slight forward lean
mistakes: Reaching out with the foot in front of the body
Running the drill tired; quality comes first
exercises.breathing: Breathe rhythmically; recover fully between reps so every rep is fast.

exercises.name: Linear Acceleration Wall Drill
exercises.description: Linear Acceleration Wall Drill is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the calves, glutes and quadriceps.
setup: Lean at around 45 degrees against a wall. Your feet should be together, glutes contracted.
steps: Begin by lifting your right knee quickly, pausing, and then driving it straight down into the ground.
Switch legs, raising the opposite knee, and then attacking the ground straight down.
Repeat once more with your right leg, and as soon as the right foot strikes the ground hammer them out rapidly, alternating left and right as fast as you can.
cues: Drive the knee up and the foot down under the hips
Arms swing from the shoulder, elbows about 90 degrees
Stay tall with a slight forward lean
mistakes: Reaching out with the foot in front of the body
Running the drill tired; quality comes first
exercises.breathing: Breathe rhythmically; recover fully between reps so every rep is fast.

exercises.name: Moving Claw Series
exercises.description: Moving Claw Series is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the calves and quadriceps.
setup: This move helps prepare your running form to help you excel at sprinting. As you run, be sure to flex the knee, aiming to kick your glutes as the hip extends.
steps: Reload the quad as the leg moves back forward, attacking the ground on the next step.
Ensure that as you run, you block with the arms, punching through in a rapid 1-2 motion.
cues: Drive the knee up and the foot down under the hips
Arms swing from the shoulder, elbows about 90 degrees
Stay tall with a slight forward lean
mistakes: Reaching out with the foot in front of the body
Running the drill tired; quality comes first
exercises.breathing: Breathe rhythmically; recover fully between reps so every rep is fast.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Stiff-Legged Deadlift
exercises.description: Smith Machine Stiff-Legged Deadlift is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the glutes and lower back. A variation of the straight leg deadlift: smith machine bar.
setup: To begin, set the bar on the smith machine to a height that is around the middle of your thighs. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, grasp the bar using a pronated (palms forward) grip that is shoulder width apart. You may need some wrist wraps if using a significant amount of weight.
steps: Lift the bar up by fully extending your arms while keeping your back straight. Stand with your torso straight and your legs spaced using a shoulder width or narrower stance. The knees should be slightly bent. This is your starting position.

Keeping the knees stationary, lower the barbell to over the top of your feet by bending at the waist while keeping your back straight. Keep moving forward as if you were going to pick something from the floor until you feel a stretch on the hamstrings. Exhale as you perform this movement

Start bringing your torso up straight again as soon as you feel the hamstrings stretch by extending your hips and waist until you are back at the starting position. Inhale as you perform this movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Flat back is more important than depth
Bar close to the legs
mistakes: Rounding the back to reach the floor
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace hard before each rep. Hold it as you lift, and breathe out at the top or once the weight is back down.
safety: If you cannot reach the floor with a flat back, use blocks or do Romanian deadlifts instead.
variation_notes: Smith machine bar.

exercises.name: Stiff-Legged Dumbbell Deadlift
exercises.description: Stiff-Legged Dumbbell Deadlift is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the glutes and lower back. A variation of the straight leg deadlift: dumbbells.
setup: Grasp a couple of dumbbells holding them by your side at arm's length.
steps: Stand with your torso straight and your legs spaced using a shoulder width or narrower stance. The knees should be slightly bent. This is your starting position.

Keeping the knees stationary, lower the dumbbells to over the top of your feet by bending at the waist while keeping your back straight. Keep moving forward as if you were going to pick something from the floor until you feel a stretch on the hamstrings. Exhale as you perform this movement
Start bringing your torso up straight again by extending your hips and waist until you are back at the starting position. Inhale as you perform this movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Flat back is more important than depth
Dumbbells close to the legs
mistakes: Rounding the back to reach the floor
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace hard before each rep. Hold it as you lift, and breathe out at the top or once the weight is back down.
safety: If you cannot reach the floor with a flat back, use blocks or do Romanian deadlifts instead.
variation_notes: Dumbbells.

exercises.name: Straight Leg Deadlift
exercises.description: A deadlift with nearly straight legs, starting from the floor each rep. Places a large stretch on the hamstrings.
setup: Stand with the bar over mid-foot, knees only slightly bent.
Hinge to grip the bar with a flat back.
steps: Lift the bar by driving the hips forward, keeping the legs nearly straight.
Lower by pushing the hips back until the bar reaches the floor or your flexibility limit.
cues: Flat back is more important than depth
Bar close to the legs
mistakes: Rounding the back to reach the floor
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace hard before each rep. Hold it as you lift, and breathe out at the top or once the weight is back down.
safety: If you cannot reach the floor with a flat back, use blocks or do Romanian deadlifts instead.

exercises.name: Wide Stance Stiff Legs
exercises.description: Wide Stance Stiff Legs is an intermediate-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the adductors, glutes and lower back. A variation of the straight leg deadlift: a wide stance adds the inner thighs.
steps: Begin with a barbell loaded on the floor. Adopt a wide stance, and then bend at the hips to grab the bar. Your hips should be as far back as possible, and your legs nearly straight. Keep your back straight, and your head and chest up. This will be your starting position.

Begin the movement be engaging the hips, driving them forward as you allow the arms to hang straight. Continue until you are standing straight up, and then slowly return the weight to the starting position. For successive reps, the weight need not touch the floor.
cues: Flat back is more important than depth
Bar close to the legs
mistakes: Rounding the back to reach the floor
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace hard before each rep. Hold it as you lift, and breathe out at the top or once the weight is back down.
safety: If you cannot reach the floor with a flat back, use blocks or do Romanian deadlifts instead.
variation_notes: A wide stance adds the inner thighs.

exercises.name: Stretching
exercises.description: Static or dynamic stretching to improve flexibility and recovery.
steps: Warm up the muscles first.
Hold each static stretch for 20–60 seconds without bouncing.
cues: Mild tension, never pain
Relax into the stretch
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and deeply; breathing out helps the muscle relax into the stretch.
safety: Warm up for 5–10 minutes before hard efforts.
Build duration and intensity gradually from week to week.

exercises.name: Power Stairs
exercises.description: Power Stairs is an intermediate-level strongman exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the adductors, calves, glutes, lower back, quadriceps and traps.
setup: In the power stairs, implements are moved up a staircase. For training purposes, these can be performed with a tire or box.
steps: Begin by taking the implement with both hands. Set your feet wide, with your head and chest up. Drive through the ground with your heels, extending your knees and hips to raise the weight from the ground.
As you lean back, attempt to swing the weight onto the stairs, which are usually around 16-18" high. You can use your legs to help push the weight onto the stair.
Repeat for 3-5 repetitions, and continue with a heavier weight, moving as fast as possible.
cues: Straddle the implement and wrap it tight to the body
Lap it first if needed, then drive the hips forward to load
Keep it close the whole way
mistakes: Letting it drift away from the body
exercises.breathing: Big breath and brace before the lift; exhale once the implement is loaded.
safety: Some back rounding is normal on stones; build up gradually and use tacky or sleeves for grip.

exercises.name: Reverse Band Sumo Deadlift
exercises.description: Reverse Band Sumo Deadlift is an advanced-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the abductors, adductors, calves, forearms, glutes, lower back, quadriceps and traps. A variation of the sumo deadlift: bands from above help off the floor.
setup: Begin with a bar loaded on the floor inside of a power rack. Attach bands to the top of the rack, using either pegs or the frame itself. Attach the other end to the barbell.
steps: Approach the bar so that the bar intersects the middle of the feet. The feet should be set very wide, near the collars. Bend at the hips to grip the bar. The arms should be directly below the shoulders, inside the legs, and you can use a pronated grip, a mixed grip, or hook grip. Relax the shoulders, which in effect lengthens your arms.

Take a breath, and then lower your hips, looking forward with your head with your chest up. Drive through the floor, spreading your feet apart, with your weight on the back half of your feet. Extend through the hips and knees.
As the bar passes through the knees, lean back and drive the hips into the bar, pulling your shoulder blades together.
Return the weight to the ground by bending at the hips and controlling the weight on the way down.
cues: Knees out over the toes
Chest up, hips close to the bar
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace hard before each rep. Hold it as you lift, and breathe out at the top or once the weight is back down.
safety: Needs good hip mobility; find a stance width you can get into with a flat back.
variation_notes: Bands from above help off the floor.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift with Bands
exercises.description: Sumo Deadlift with Bands is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the adductors, forearms, glutes, lower back, upper back, quadriceps and traps. A variation of the sumo deadlift: bands add load toward lockout.
setup: To deadlift with short bands, simply loop them over the bar before you start, and step into them to set up. Ensure that they under the back half of your foot, directly where you are driving into the floor.
steps: Begin with a bar loaded on the ground. Approach the bar so that the bar intersects the middle of the feet. The feet should be set very wide, near the collars. Bend at the hips to grip the bar. The arms should be directly below the shoulders, inside the legs, and you can use a pronated grip, a mixed grip, or hook grip.

Take a breath, and then lower your hips, looking forward with your head with your chest up. Drive through the floor, spreading your feet apart, with your weight on the back half of your feet. Extend through the hips and knees.
As the bar passes through the knees, lean back and drive the hips into the bar, pulling your shoulder blades together.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift with Chains
exercises.description: Sumo Deadlift with Chains is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the hamstrings, with help from the abductors, adductors, forearms, glutes, lower back, upper back, quadriceps and traps. A variation of the sumo deadlift: chains add load toward lockout.
setup: You can attach the chains to the sleeves of the bar, or just drape the middle over the bar so there is a greater weight increase as you lift. Attempt to keep the ends of the chains away from the plates so you don't hit them when you lower the weight.
