exercises.name: Yoga
exercises.description: A practice of postures, breathing and movement for flexibility, strength and relaxation.
steps: Follow a class or sequence suited to your level.
Move into each pose only as far as is comfortable.
cues: Breathe slowly through the nose
Never force a stretch
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly through the nose; let the breath set the pace of the movements.
safety: Warm up for 5–10 minutes before hard efforts.
Build duration and intensity gradually from week to week.

exercises.name: Chair Lower Back Stretch
exercises.description: Chair Lower Back Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the lats, with help from the lower back.
setup: Sit upright on a chair.
steps: Bend to one side with your arm over your head. You can hold onto the chair with your free hand.
Hold for 10 seconds, and repeat for your other side.
cues: Move slowly through the spine, one segment at a time
Stay in a comfortable range; this should feel easy
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.
safety: Stop if you feel pain shooting down a leg, and see a professional.

exercises.name: Ball Slams
exercises.description: Lifting a slam ball overhead and throwing it into the floor as hard as you can.
setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width holding a slam ball (one that does not bounce).
steps: Lift the ball overhead, rising onto your toes.
Slam it down hard in front of your feet, hinging with it.
Pick it up and repeat.
cues: Use the whole body
Hinge to pick it up
mistakes: Rounding the back to pick up the ball
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lift, breathe out hard as you slam.
safety: Use a dead-bounce slam ball.

exercises.name: Bent Over Row (Band)
exercises.description: A standing row with the torso hinged forward. It builds the whole upper back and lats and trains you to hold a strong hip hinge.
setup: Stand on the middle of the band with feet hip-width apart.
Hinge forward with a flat back and hold the band ends with arms straight.
steps: Pull the weight toward your lower ribs or upper stomach.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower under control until your arms are straight again, keeping the torso still.
cues: Pull with the elbows, not the hands
Keep the back flat and the torso angle fixed
Chest proud
mistakes: Standing up as you pull, turning it into a shrug
exercises.breathing: Brace your core before each rep. Breathe out as you pull, breathe in as you lower the weight.
safety: If your lower back tires before your upper back, use a chest-supported row instead.

exercises.name: Bent Over Row (Barbell)
exercises.description: A standing row with the torso hinged forward. It builds the whole upper back and lats and trains you to hold a strong hip hinge.
setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding the weight with an overhand grip just wider than your knees.
Push your hips back and bend the knees slightly until your torso is at about 30–45° above horizontal.
Let your arms hang straight down, back flat, neck in line with the spine.
steps: Pull the weight toward your lower ribs or upper stomach.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower under control until your arms are straight again, keeping the torso still.

exercises.name: One Arm Against Wall
exercises.description: One Arm Against Wall is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the lats.
steps: From a standing position, place a bent arm against a wall or doorway.
Slowly lean toward your arm until you feel a stretch in your lats.
cues: Keep the shoulders down away from the ears
Keep the ribs down; do not arch the back to fake the range
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Overhead Lat
exercises.description: Overhead Lat is an advanced-level stretch that mainly targets the lats, with help from the triceps.
setup: Sit upright on the floor with your partner behind you. Raise one arm straight up, and flex the elbow, attempting to touch your hand to your back. Your parner should hold your tricep and wrist. This will be your starting position.
steps: Attempt to pull your upper arm to your side as your partner prevents you from doing actually doing so.
After 10-20 seconds, relax the arm and allow your partner to further stretch the lat by applying gentle pressure to the tricep. Hold for 10-20 seconds, and then switch sides.
cues: Keep the shoulders down away from the ears
Keep the ribs down; do not arch the back to fake the range
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Floor Stretch
exercises.description: Side-Lying Floor Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the lats.
steps: First lie on your left side, bending your left knee in front of you to stabilize your torso (use your abdominal muscles as well to hold you upright).

Straighten your right leg and rest the right foot on the floor behind your left. Straighten your right arm over your head and gently pull on your right wrist to stretch the entire right side of the body. Switch sides.
cues: Keep the shoulders down away from the ears
Keep the ribs down; do not arch the back to fake the range
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Chin Up
exercises.description: A pull up with an underhand, shoulder-width grip. It uses more biceps and is usually a little easier than a pull up.
setup: Grip the bar underhand with hands about shoulder-width apart.
Hang with straight arms and a tight core.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades down to start.
Pull until your chin is over the bar.
Lower slowly to a full hang.
cues: Chest to the bar
Elbows close in front of the body
Full hang at the bottom
mistakes: Stopping short of a full hang
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.

Hang with straight arms and a tight core.

exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.
variation_notes: The counterweight lifts part of your body weight; more assistance makes it easier.

Hang with straight arms and a tight core.

exercises.name: Climbing
exercises.description: Indoor or outdoor rock climbing or bouldering.
steps: Warm up on easy routes.
Climb with straight arms where possible and push with the legs.
cues: Push with the legs
Keep hips close to the wall
exercises.breathing: Match your breathing to the effort. At an easy pace you should be able to talk in full sentences; at hard efforts breathe deeply and rhythmically through the mouth.
safety: Check knots, harness and belay every time, and learn safe falling for bouldering.

exercises.name: One Handed Hang
exercises.description: One Handed Hang is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the lats, with help from the biceps. A variation of the dead hang: hang from one hand.
steps: Grab onto a chinup bar with one hand, using a pronated grip. Keep your feet on the floor or a step. Allow the majority of your weight to hang from that hand, while keeping your feet on the ground. Hold for 10-20 seconds and switch sides.
cues: Relax the legs
Breathe steadily
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and steadily throughout the hold.
safety: Use a box to step down safely.
variation_notes: Hang from one hand.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row
exercises.description: A one-arm row with your other hand and knee on a bench for support. A very effective lat exercise that is easy on the lower back.
setup: Place one knee and the same-side hand on a flat bench.
Put the other foot on the floor, back flat and roughly parallel to the floor.
Hold the dumbbell with the free arm hanging straight down.
steps: Pull the dumbbell toward your hip, keeping the elbow close to your body.
Pause when the elbow is just past your torso.
Lower slowly until the arm is straight and you feel a stretch in the lat.
cues: Pull toward the hip, not the shoulder
Keep the shoulders square to the floor
mistakes: Twisting the torso to lift the weight
Shrugging the shoulder up to the ear
exercises.breathing: Brace your core before each rep. Breathe out as you pull, breathe in as you lower the weight.

exercises.name: Dynamic Back Stretch
exercises.description: Dynamic Back Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the lats.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your arms straight, swing them straight up in front of you 5-10 times, increasing the range of motion each time until your arms are above your head.
cues: Start small and slow, then grow the range
Smooth, controlled movement, no flinging
About 8–12 reps per side as a warm-up
mistakes: Swinging into end range with momentum
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Latissimus Dorsi-SMR
exercises.description: Latissimus Dorsi-SMR is a beginner-level self-massage (foam rolling) exercise that mainly targets the lats.
steps: While lying on the floor, place a foam roll under your back and to one side, just behind your arm pit. This will be your starting position.
Keep the arm of the side being stretched behind and to the side of you as you shift your weight onto your lats, keeping your upper body off of the ground. Hold for 10-30 seconds, and switch sides.
cues: Roll slowly, about 2–3 cm per second
Pause 20–30 seconds on tender spots
Support your weight with hands and feet to control the pressure
30–90 seconds per area
mistakes: Rolling directly over joints or bones
Pressing so hard you tense up
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and stay relaxed. On a tender spot, pause and take a few long exhales to let the muscle release.
safety: Avoid rolling the lower back and neck with full body weight; use a softer tool there.

exercises.name: Front Lever Hold
exercises.description: A gymnastic hold where you hang from a bar with your body horizontal and face up.
setup: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip and straight arms.
steps: Pull the bar down with straight arms while lifting your body to horizontal.
Hold the straight position.
cues: Straight arms, push the bar toward your hips
Body rigid
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and steadily through the hold; do not hold your breath.
safety: Progress with tuck and single-leg versions first.

exercises.name: Front Lever Raise
exercises.description: A gymnastic hold where you hang from a bar with your body horizontal and face up.
setup: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip and straight arms.
steps: From a hang, raise your straight body up to the front lever (or higher) with straight arms.
Lower slowly back to the hang.
cues: Straight arms, push the bar toward your hips
Body rigid
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise, breathe in as you lower.
safety: Progress with tuck and single-leg versions first.

exercises.name: Gorilla Row (Kettlebell)
exercises.description: Alternating kettlebell rows from a wide, deep hinge position with the kettlebells on the floor between your feet.
setup: Stand with feet wider than shoulders and two kettlebells between your feet.
Hinge forward with a flat back and grip both handles.
steps: Row one kettlebell to your hip while pushing the other into the floor.
Lower it back down and row the other side.
Keep alternating.
cues: Push the down kettlebell into the floor
Hips stay level
exercises.breathing: Breathe out with each pull, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Inverted Row
exercises.description: A bodyweight row hanging under a bar with your heels on the floor. Great for building up to pull ups.
setup: Set a bar at about hip height in a rack or Smith machine.
Lie under it and grip it slightly wider than shoulder width.
Straighten your body so it forms a line from head to heels.
steps: Pull your chest up to the bar.
Pause, then lower until your arms are straight.
cues: Body stays a straight plank
Lead with the chest
mistakes: Reaching with the chin instead of the chest
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.
variation_notes: Raise the bar or bend your knees to make it easier.

exercises.name: Landmine Row
exercises.description: A row using a barbell anchored in a landmine, pulled with both hands close together or one hand at a time.
setup: Stand beside or over the loaded end of the landmine bar.
Hinge forward with a flat back and grip the bar near the plates.
steps: Row the bar toward your torso.
Pause, then lower until your arms are straight.
cues: Flat back, fixed torso angle
Elbows drive back
mistakes: Using the legs to heave the bar
exercises.breathing: Brace your core before each rep. Breathe out as you pull, breathe in as you lower the weight.

exercises.name: Full Range-Of-Motion Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: Full Range-Of-Motion Lat Pulldown is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the lats, with help from the biceps and upper back. A variation of the lat pulldown: leaning back slightly with a full stretch at the top.
steps: Either standing or seated on a high bench, grasp two stirrup cables that are attached to the high pulleys. Grab with the opposing hand so your arms are crisscrossed about you and your palms are facing forward.

Keeping your chest up and maintaining a slight arch in your lower back, pull the handles down as if you were doing a regular pulldown. The range of motion will be more of an arc. During the movement, rotate your hands so that in the bottom position your palms face each other rather than forward. Return slowly to the starting position and repeat.
cues: Drive the elbows down toward your back pockets
Chest up to meet the bar
Full stretch at the top
mistakes: Leaning far back and rowing the weight
Pulling the bar behind the neck
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.
variation_notes: Leaning back slightly with a full stretch at the top.

exercises.name: Kneeling High Pulley Row
exercises.description: Kneeling High Pulley Row is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the lats, with help from the biceps and upper back. A variation of the lat pulldown: kneeling at a high pulley, pulling to the chest.
setup: Select the appropriate weight using a pulley that is above your head. Attach a rope to the cable and kneel a couple of feet away, holding the rope out in front of you with both arms extended. This will be your starting position.
steps: Initiate the movement by flexing the elbows and fully retracting your shoulders, pulling the rope toward your upper chest with your elbows out.
After pausing briefly, slowly return to the starting position.
cues: Drive the elbows down toward your back pockets
Chest up to meet the bar
Full stretch at the top
mistakes: Leaning far back and rowing the weight
Pulling the bar behind the neck
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.
variation_notes: Kneeling at a high pulley, pulling to the chest.

exercises.name: Kneeling Pulldown (Band)
exercises.description: A pulldown done kneeling, pulling a band anchored overhead. Good for training at home or warming up.
setup: Anchor the band high above you and kneel facing it.
Hold the band with arms straight overhead.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades down first, then pull your hands down beside your shoulders.
Keep your chest up and elbows pointing down.
Let the band pull your arms back up slowly until they are straight.
cues: Drive the elbows down toward your back pockets
Chest up
Full stretch at the top
mistakes: Letting the band snap the arms back up
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.

exercises.name: Kneeling Single-Arm High Pulley Row
exercises.description: Kneeling Single-Arm High Pulley Row is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the lats, with help from the biceps and upper back. A variation of the lat pulldown: kneeling at a high pulley, one arm at a time.
setup: Attach a single handle to a high pulley and make your weight selection.
steps: Kneel in front of the cable tower, taking the cable with one hand with your arm extended. This will be your starting position.

Starting with your palm facing forward, pull the weight down to your torso by flexing the elbow and retract the shoulder blade. As you do so, rotate the wrist so that at the completion of the movement, your palm is now facing you.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
cues: Drive the elbows down toward your back pockets
Chest up to meet the bar
Full stretch at the top
mistakes: Leaning far back and rowing the weight
Pulling the bar behind the neck
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.
variation_notes: Kneeling at a high pulley, one arm at a time.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Band)
exercises.description: A pulldown with a resistance band anchored overhead, done sitting or kneeling.
setup: Anchor the band high above you.
Kneel or sit facing the anchor, holding the band with straight arms.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades down first, then pull your hands down beside your shoulders.
Keep your chest up and elbows pointing down.
Let the band pull your arms back up slowly until they are straight.
cues: Drive the elbows down toward your back pockets
Chest up
Full stretch at the top
mistakes: Letting the band snap the arms back up
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Cable)
exercises.description: A seated vertical pull that trains the lats. It works like a pull up but lets you choose the load.
setup: Adjust the thigh pad so your legs are locked in.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width with an overhand grip.
Sit down with arms straight and lean back slightly.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades down first, then pull the bar to your upper chest.
Keep your chest up and elbows pointing down.
Let the bar rise slowly until your arms are straight and the lats are stretched.
cues: Drive the elbows down toward your back pockets
Chest up to meet the bar
Full stretch at the top
mistakes: Leaning far back and rowing the weight
Pulling the bar behind the neck
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Pulldown Behind The Neck
exercises.description: Wide-Grip Pulldown Behind The Neck is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the lats, with help from the biceps and upper back. A variation of the lat pulldown: bar pulled behind the head. Needs good shoulder mobility; most people should pull to the chest.
setup: Sit down on a pull-down machine with a wide bar attached to the top pulley. Make sure that you adjust the knee pad of the machine to fit your height. These pads will prevent your body from being raised by the resistance attached to the bar.
steps: Grab the bar with the palms facing forward using the prescribed grip. Note on grips: For a wide grip, your hands need to be spaced out at a distance wider than your shoulder width. For a medium grip, your hands need to be spaced out at a distance equal to your shoulder width and for a close grip at a distance smaller than your shoulder width.

As you have both arms extended in front of you holding the bar at the chosen grip width, bring your torso and head forward. Think of an imaginary line from the center of the bar down to the back of your neck. This is your starting position.

As you breathe out, bring the bar down until it touches the back of your neck by drawing the shoulders and the upper arms down and back. Tip: Concentrate on squeezing the back muscles once you reach the full contracted position. The upper torso should remain stationary and only the arms should move. The forearms should do no other work except for holding the bar; therefore do not try to pull down the bar using the forearms.

After a second on the contracted position squeezing your shoulder blades together, slowly raise the bar back to the starting position when your arms are fully extended and the lats are fully stretched. Inhale during this portion of the movement.
Repeat this motion for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
cues: Drive the elbows down toward your back pockets
Chest up to meet the bar
Full stretch at the top
mistakes: Leaning far back and rowing the weight
Pulling the bar behind the neck
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.
variation_notes: Bar pulled behind the head. Needs good shoulder mobility; most people should pull to the chest.

exercises.name: London Bridges
exercises.description: London Bridges is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the lats, with help from the biceps, forearms and upper back.
setup: Attach a climbing rope to a high beam or cross member. Below it, ensure that the smith machine bar is locked in place with the safeties and cannot move. Alternatively, a secure box could also be utilized.
steps: Stand on the bar, using the rope to balance yourself. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your body straight, lean back and lower your body by slowly going hand over hand with the rope. Continue until you are perpendicular to the ground.
Keeping your body straight, reverse the motion, going hand over hand back to the starting position.
cues: Lean back with a straight body
Pull hand over hand up the rope
Lower with control
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Low Row (Suspension)
exercises.description: A bodyweight row on suspension straps. Walking your feet closer to the anchor makes it harder.
setup: Face the anchor holding both handles with arms straight.
Lean back with your body straight, heels on the floor.
steps: Pull your chest toward the handles, elbows close to your sides.
Lower back to straight arms with control.
cues: Body stays rigid
Squeeze the shoulder blades at the top
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.

exercises.name: Meadows Rows (Barbell)
exercises.description: A one-arm landmine row done side-on to the bar, gripping the end of the bar with an overhand grip.
setup: Stand side-on to the end of a landmine bar in a staggered stance.
Rest your free forearm on your front knee and hinge forward.
Grip the thick end of the bar overhand.
steps: Row the bar up and back toward your hip.
Lower under control until the arm is straight.
cues: Elbow travels high and back
Keep the hips square
exercises.breathing: Brace your core before each rep. Breathe out as you pull, breathe in as you lower the weight.

exercises.name: Catch and Overhead Throw
exercises.description: Catch and Overhead Throw is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the lats, with help from the abs & core and chest.
setup: Begin standing while facing a wall or a partner.
steps: Using both hands, position the ball behind your head, stretching as much as possible, and forcefully throw the ball forward.

Ensure that you follow your throw through, being prepared to receive your rebound from your throw. If you are throwing against the wall, make sure that you stand close enough to the wall to receive the rebound, and aim a little higher than you would with a partner.
cues: Use the legs and hips first, the arms last
Throw as hard as you can; every rep is maximal
Use a light ball (2–5 kg) you can move fast
Reset fully between throws
mistakes: Using a ball too heavy to move quickly
Rounding the back when picking up or catching
exercises.breathing: Inhale as you load, exhale forcefully as you release the ball.
safety: Throw against a solid wall or into open space, never toward people.

exercises.name: Kipping Muscle Up
exercises.description: Kipping Muscle Up is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the lats, with help from the abs & core, biceps, forearms, upper back, traps and triceps. A variation of the muscle up: a hip swing helps the pull. Learn the strict version first.
setup: Grip the rings using a false grip, with the base of your palms on top of the rings.
steps: Begin with a movement swinging your legs backward slightly.

Counter that movement by swinging your legs forward and up, jerking your chin and chest back, pulling yourself up with both arms as you do so. As you reach the top position of the pull-up, pull the rings to your armpits as you roll your shoulders forward, allowing your elbows to move straight back behind you. This puts you into the proper position to continue into the dip portion of the movement.
Maintaining control and stability, extend through the elbow to complete the motion.
Use care when lowering yourself to the ground.
cues: Pull high and close to the bar
Fast transition
mistakes: Pulling straight up instead of toward the hips
One arm crossing over before the other ("chicken wing")
exercises.breathing: Breathe in at the hang, breathe out sharply through the pull and transition.
safety: Build 10+ strict pull ups and dips before learning this.
variation_notes: A hip swing helps the pull. Learn the strict version first.

exercises.name: Muscle Up
exercises.description: A gymnastic skill that combines an explosive pull up with a transition over the bar into a dip.
setup: Hang from the bar (or rings) with a false grip or a firm overhand grip.
Engage your shoulders and core.
steps: Pull explosively toward your lower chest, pulling the bar toward your hips.
As the bar reaches your chest, lean forward and rotate your wrists over the bar.
Press up to straight arms above the bar.
Lower back down under control.
cues: Pull high and close to the bar
Fast transition
mistakes: Pulling straight up instead of toward the hips
One arm crossing over before the other ("chicken wing")
exercises.breathing: Breathe in at the hang, breathe out sharply through the pull and transition.
safety: Build 10+ strict pull ups and dips before learning this.

exercises.name: Pendlay Row (Barbell)
exercises.description: A strict, explosive barbell row where each rep starts from a dead stop on the floor with the torso near horizontal.
setup: Set up like a deadlift with the bar over mid-foot.
Hinge until your torso is almost parallel to the floor, back flat.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width.
steps: Pull the bar explosively from the floor to your lower chest.
Lower it back to the floor and let it settle for a moment.
Reset your brace before the next rep.
cues: Torso stays parallel; only the arms move
Explode up, control down
mistakes: Lifting the torso to help the bar up
Bouncing the bar off the floor
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace while the bar is on the floor, pull, then breathe out at the top or as you set the bar down.
safety: Needs good hamstring flexibility to keep the back flat; raise the bar on blocks if you cannot.

exercises.name: Kipping Pull Up
exercises.description: Pulling your body up to a bar with an overhand grip. One of the best exercises for back and arm strength.
setup: Grip the bar overhand, slightly wider than shoulder width.
Hang with straight arms and legs together, core tight.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades down and back to start the pull.
Pull until your chin clears the bar, leading with the chest.
Lower under control to a full hang.
cues: Elbows drive down to your ribs
Body stays still; no swinging
Full hang at the bottom
mistakes: Kicking or swinging to get up
Half reps without a full hang
Craning the neck to reach the bar
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.
safety: If you cannot do full reps yet, use the assisted or negative versions instead of jerking.
Build strict pull-up strength first; kipping puts high stress on the shoulders.
variation_notes: Uses a rhythmic hip swing to help you up, common in CrossFit. It is a skill, not a strength builder.

exercises.name: Negative Pull Up
exercises.description: Pulling your body up to a bar with an overhand grip. One of the best exercises for back and arm strength.
setup: Grip the bar overhand, slightly wider than shoulder width.
Hang with straight arms and legs together, core tight.
steps: Step or jump up so your chin is over the bar.
Lower yourself as slowly as you can, ideally 3–5 seconds, to a full hang.
Step back up and repeat.
cues: Elbows drive down to your ribs
Body stays still; no swinging
Full hang at the bottom
mistakes: Kicking or swinging to get up
Half reps without a full hang
Craning the neck to reach the bar
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.
safety: If you cannot do full reps yet, use the assisted or negative versions instead of jerking.
variation_notes: Building strength in the lowering phase is a reliable path to your first full pull up.

exercises.name: Ring Pull Up
exercises.description: A pull up on gymnastic rings. The rings move freely, which lets the wrists and shoulders find a natural path.
setup: Set the rings high enough to hang with straight arms.
Grip the rings with palms facing forward or each other.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades down to start.
Pull until your chin is above your hands, letting the palms turn in.
Lower under control to a full hang.
cues: Elbows drive down to your ribs
Body stays still; no swinging
Full hang at the bottom
mistakes: Kicking or swinging to get up
Half reps without a full hang
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.
safety: If you cannot do full reps yet, use the assisted or negative versions instead of jerking.
variation_notes: The rings let the wrists rotate naturally, which many people find easier on the elbows and shoulders.

exercises.name: Rocky Pull-Ups/Pulldowns
exercises.description: Rocky Pull-Ups/Pulldowns is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the lats, with help from the biceps and upper back. A variation of the pull up: alternates pulling to the front and behind the neck.
setup: Grab the pull-up bar with the palms facing forward using a wide grip.
steps: As you have both arms extended in front of you holding the bar at the chosen grip width, bring your torso back around 30 degrees or so while creating a curvature on your lower back and sticking your chest out. This is your starting position.

Pull your torso up until the bar touches your upper chest by drawing the shoulders and the upper arms down and back. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: Concentrate on squeezing the back muscles once you reach the full contracted position. The upper torso should remain stationary as it moves through space and only the arms should move. The forearms should do no other work other than hold the bar.
After a second on the contracted position, start to inhale and slowly lower your torso back to the starting position when your arms are fully extended and the lats are fully stretched.

Now repeat the same movements as described above except this time your torso will remain straight as you go up and the bar will touch the back of the neck instead of the upper chest. Tip: Use the head to lean forward slightly as it will help you properly execute this portion of the exercise.
Once you have lowered yourself back down to the starting position, repeat the exercise for the prescribed amount of repetitions in your program.
cues: Elbows drive down to your ribs
Body stays still; no swinging
Full hang at the bottom
mistakes: Kicking or swinging to get up
Half reps without a full hang
Craning the neck to reach the bar
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.
safety: If you cannot do full reps yet, use the assisted or negative versions instead of jerking.
variation_notes: Alternates pulling to the front and behind the neck.

exercises.name: Side To Side Chins
exercises.description: Side To Side Chins is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the lats, with help from the biceps, forearms and upper back. A variation of the pull up: pull up toward one hand, then the other.
setup: Grab the pull-up bar with the palms facing forward using a wide grip.
steps: As you have both arms extended in front of you holding the bar at a wide grip, bring your torso back around 30 degrees or so while creating a curvature on your lower back and sticking your chest out. This is your starting position.

Pull your torso up while leaning to the left hand side until the bar almost touches your upper chest by drawing the shoulders and the upper arms down and back. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: Concentrate on squeezing the back muscles once you reach the full contracted position. The upper torso should remain stationary as it moves through space (no swinging) and only the arms should move. The forearms should do no other work other than hold the bar.
After a second of contraction, inhale as you go back to the starting position.

Now, pull your torso up while leaning to the right hand side until the bar almost touches your upper chest by drawing the shoulders and the upper arms down and back. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: Concentrate on squeezing the back muscles once you reach the full contracted position. The upper torso should remain stationary as it moves through space and only the arms should move. The forearms should do no other work other than hold the bar.
After a second of contraction, inhale as you go back to the starting position.
Repeat steps 3-6 until you have performed the prescribed amount of repetitions for each side.
cues: Elbows drive down to your ribs
Body stays still; no swinging
Full hang at the bottom
mistakes: Kicking or swinging to get up
Half reps without a full hang
Craning the neck to reach the bar
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.
safety: If you cannot do full reps yet, use the assisted or negative versions instead of jerking.
variation_notes: Pull up toward one hand, then the other.

exercises.name: Sternum Pull up (Gironda)
exercises.description: Pulling your body up to a bar with an overhand grip. One of the best exercises for back and arm strength.
setup: Grip the bar overhand, slightly wider than shoulder width.
Hang with straight arms and legs together, core tight.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades down and back to start the pull.
Pull until your chin clears the bar, leading with the chest.
Lower under control to a full hang.
cues: Elbows drive down to your ribs
Body stays still; no swinging
Full hang at the bottom
mistakes: Kicking or swinging to get up
Half reps without a full hang
Craning the neck to reach the bar
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.
safety: If you cannot do full reps yet, use the assisted or negative versions instead of jerking.
variation_notes: Lean back and pull until your lower chest touches the bar, finishing with the shoulder blades fully together.

exercises.name: V-Bar Pullup
exercises.description: V-Bar Pullup is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the lats, with help from the biceps and upper back. A variation of the pull up: a V handle over the bar; close neutral grip.
setup: Start by placing the middle of the V-bar in the middle of the pull-up bar (assuming that the pull-up station you are using does not have neutral grip handles). The V-Bar handles will be facing down so that you can hang from the pull-up bar through the use of the handles.
steps: Once you securely place the V-bar, take a hold of the bar from each side and hang from it. Stick your chest out and lean yourself back slightly in order to better engage the lats. This will be your starting position.

Using your lats, pull your torso up while leaning your head back slightly so that you do not hit yourself with the chin-up bar. Continue until your chest nearly touches the V-bar. Exhale as you execute this motion.
After a second hold on the contracted position, slowly lower your body back to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.
cues: Elbows drive down to your ribs
Body stays still; no swinging
Full hang at the bottom
mistakes: Kicking or swinging to get up
Half reps without a full hang
Craning the neck to reach the bar
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.
safety: If you cannot do full reps yet, use the assisted or negative versions instead of jerking.
variation_notes: A V handle over the bar; close neutral grip.

exercises.name: Wide Pull Up
exercises.description: Pulling your body up to a bar with an overhand grip. One of the best exercises for back and arm strength.
setup: Grip the bar overhand, slightly wider than shoulder width.
Hang with straight arms and legs together, core tight.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades down and back to start the pull.
Pull until your chin clears the bar, leading with the chest.
Lower under control to a full hang.
cues: Elbows drive down to your ribs
Body stays still; no swinging
Full hang at the bottom
mistakes: Kicking or swinging to get up
Half reps without a full hang
Craning the neck to reach the bar
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.
safety: If you cannot do full reps yet, use the assisted or negative versions instead of jerking.
Avoid very wide grips if they bother your shoulders.
variation_notes: Hands well outside shoulder width; shorter range and harder on the lats and shoulders.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Rear Pull-Up
exercises.description: Wide-Grip Rear Pull-Up is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the lats, with help from the biceps and upper back. A variation of the pull up: wide grip, head forward of the bar. Needs good shoulder mobility.
setup: Grab the pull-up bar with the palms facing forward using a wide grip.
steps: As you have both arms extended in front of you holding the bar, bring your torso forward and head so that there is an imaginary line from the pull-up bar to the back of your neck. This is your starting position.

Pull your torso up until the bar is near the back of your neck. To do this, draw the shoulders and upper arms down and back while slightly leaning your head forward. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: Concentrate on squeezing the back muscles once you reach the full contracted position. The upper torso should remain stationary as it moves through space and only the arms should move. The forearms should do no other work other than hold the bar.
After a second on the contracted position, start to inhale and slowly lower your torso back to the starting position when your arms are fully extended and the lats are fully stretched.
Repeat this motion for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
cues: Elbows drive down to your ribs
Body stays still; no swinging
Full hang at the bottom
mistakes: Kicking or swinging to get up
Half reps without a full hang
Craning the neck to reach the bar
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.
safety: If you cannot do full reps yet, use the assisted or negative versions instead of jerking.
variation_notes: Wide grip, head forward of the bar. Needs good shoulder mobility.

exercises.name: Bent-Arm Barbell Pullover
exercises.description: Bent-Arm Barbell Pullover is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the lats, with help from the chest and triceps. A variation of the pullover: barbell with bent elbows, lying across or along a bench.
setup: Lie on a flat bench with a barbell using a shoulder grip width.
steps: Hold the bar straight over your chest with a bend in your arms. This will be your starting position.
While keeping your arms in the bent arm position, lower the weight slowly in an arc behind your head while breathing in until you feel a stretch on the chest.
At that point, bring the barbell back to the starting position using the arc through which the weight was lowered and exhale as you perform this movement.
Hold the weight on the initial position for a second and repeat the motion for the prescribed number of repetitions.
cues: Ribs down; do not arch to get more range
Elbows stay slightly bent
mistakes: Going deeper than your shoulders allow
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as the weight goes back, breathe out as you pull it over.
safety: Skip or shorten the range if you have shoulder pain overhead.
variation_notes: Barbell with bent elbows, lying across or along a bench.

exercises.name: Pullover (Dumbbell)
exercises.description: An arcing movement from over the chest to behind the head and back, stretching and working the lats and chest.
setup: Lie on a flat bench holding one dumbbell with both hands above your chest.
Keep a slight bend in the elbows.
steps: Lower the dumbbell in an arc behind your head until you feel a stretch in the lats and chest.
Pull it back over your chest along the same arc.
cues: Ribs down; do not arch to get more range
Elbows stay slightly bent
mistakes: Going deeper than your shoulders allow
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as the weight goes back, breathe out as you pull it over.
safety: Skip or shorten the range if you have shoulder pain overhead.

exercises.name: Pullover (Machine)
exercises.description: An arcing movement from over the chest to behind the head and back, stretching and working the lats and chest.
setup: Adjust the seat so your shoulders line up with the machine pivot.
Place your elbows or forearms on the pads.
steps: Pull the pads down and forward in an arc until your arms reach your sides.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch in the lats.
cues: Ribs down; do not arch to get more range
Elbows stay slightly bent
mistakes: Going deeper than your shoulders allow
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as the weight goes back, breathe out as you pull it over.
safety: Skip or shorten the range if you have shoulder pain overhead.

exercises.name: Renegade Row (Dumbbell)
exercises.description: A row from a high plank on two dumbbells. It trains the back and challenges the core to resist rotation.
setup: Get into a high plank with hands on two dumbbells under your shoulders.
Set your feet wider than hip width for balance.
steps: Row one dumbbell to your hip while pushing the other into the floor.
Lower it under control.
Repeat on the other side.
cues: Hips stay square to the floor
Brace like a plank
mistakes: Twisting the hips up as you row
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you row, breathe in as you set the dumbbell down.
safety: Use hex dumbbells so they do not roll.

exercises.name: Rope Climb
exercises.description: Rope Climb is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the lats, with help from the biceps, forearms and upper back.
setup: Grab the rope with both hands above your head. Pull down on the rope as you take a small jump.
steps: Wrap the rope around one leg, using your feet to pinch the rope. Reach up as high as possible with your arms, gripping the rope tightly.
Release the rope from your feet as you pull yourself up with your arms, bringing your knees towards your chest.
Resecure your feet on the rope, and then stand up to take another high hold on the rope. Continue until you reach the top of the rope.
To lower yourself, loosen the grip of your feet on the rope as you slide down using a hand over hand motion.
cues: Pull with the arms and lock the rope with the feet
Stand up on the feet, then reach higher
Climb down hand over hand
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.
safety: Only climb as high as you can safely come back down.

exercises.name: Elevated Cable Rows
exercises.description: Elevated Cable Rows is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the lats, with help from the upper back and traps. A variation of the seated cable row: seated on a box for a lower angle of pull.
setup: Get a platform of some sort (it can be an aerobics or calf raise platform) that is around 4-6 inches in height.
steps: Place it on the seat of the cable row machine.
Sit down on the machine and place your feet on the front platform or crossbar provided making sure that your knees are slightly bent and not locked.
Lean over as you keep the natural alignment of your back and grab the V-bar handles.

With your arms extended pull back until your torso is at a 90-degree angle from your legs. Your back should be slightly arched and your chest should be sticking out. You should be feeling a nice stretch on your lats as you hold the bar in front of you. This is the starting position of the exercise.

Keeping the torso stationary, pull the handles back towards your torso while keeping the arms close to it until you touch the abdominals. Breathe out as you perform that movement. At that point you should be squeezing your back muscles hard. Hold that contraction for a second and slowly go back to the original position while breathing in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Sit tall; small forward lean at the stretch is fine
Elbows drive back past the body
Shoulders down, not shrugged
mistakes: Rocking the torso back and forth
Rounding the back at the front
exercises.breathing: Brace your core before each rep. Breathe out as you pull, breathe in as you lower the weight.
variation_notes: Seated on a box for a lower angle of pull.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row - Bar Grip
exercises.description: A seated row on a low cable station. A controlled way to train the mid back and lats with constant tension.
setup: Sit on the bench with feet on the footplate and knees slightly bent.
Grab the handle and sit upright with your arms straight in front of you.
steps: Pull the handle toward your lower ribs while keeping your torso upright.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together.
Let the arms extend forward slowly until you feel a stretch between the shoulder blades.
cues: Sit tall; small forward lean at the stretch is fine
Elbows drive back past the body
Shoulders down, not shrugged
mistakes: Rocking the torso back and forth
Rounding the back at the front
exercises.breathing: Brace your core before each rep. Breathe out as you pull, breathe in as you lower the weight.
variation_notes: A straight bar at about shoulder width; overhand or underhand grip.

exercises.breathing: Brace your core before each rep. Breathe out as you pull, breathe in as you lower the weight.
variation_notes: The close neutral grip lets the elbows travel close to the body and emphasises the lats.

exercises.name: Shotgun Row
exercises.description: Shotgun Row is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the lats, with help from the biceps and upper back. A variation of the seated cable row: one arm, with the palm turning up as you pull.
setup: Attach a single handle to a low cable.
steps: After selecting the correct weight, stand a couple feet back with a wide-split stance. Your arm should be extended and your shoulder forward. This will be your starting position.
Perform the movement by retracting the shoulder and flexing the elbow. As you pull, supinate the wrist, turning the palm upward as you go.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
cues: Sit tall; small forward lean at the stretch is fine
Elbows drive back past the body
Shoulders down, not shrugged
mistakes: Rocking the torso back and forth
Rounding the back at the front
exercises.breathing: Brace your core before each rep. Breathe out as you pull, breathe in as you lower the weight.
variation_notes: One arm, with the palm turning up as you pull.

exercises.name: Single Arm Cable Row
exercises.description: A seated row on a low cable station. A controlled way to train the mid back and lats with constant tension.
setup: Sit on the bench with feet on the footplate and knees slightly bent.
Grab the handle and sit upright with your arms straight in front of you.
steps: Pull the handle toward your lower ribs while keeping your torso upright.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together.
Let the arms extend forward slowly until you feel a stretch between the shoulder blades.
cues: Sit tall; small forward lean at the stretch is fine
Elbows drive back past the body
Shoulders down, not shrugged
Do not twist to finish the rep
mistakes: Rocking the torso back and forth
Rounding the back at the front
exercises.breathing: Brace your core before each rep. Breathe out as you pull, breathe in as you lower the weight.
variation_notes: Use a single handle; let the shoulder reach forward at the stretch, then pull to the hip.

exercises.name: Iso-Lateral High Row (Machine)
exercises.description: A plate-loaded or selectorised row machine, usually with a chest pad, for training the back without loading the spine.
setup: Adjust the seat so the handles are at about chest height.
Sit with your chest against the pad and grab the handles with straight arms.
steps: Pull the handles back until your elbows pass your torso.
Squeeze the shoulder blades.
Return slowly.
cues: Chest stays on the pad
Pull with the elbows
mistakes: Letting the stack slam between reps
exercises.breathing: Brace your core before each rep. Breathe out as you pull, breathe in as you lower the weight.
variation_notes: The handles start high in front and pull down and back, between a row and a pulldown.

exercises.name: Iso-Lateral Low Row

exercises.breathing: Brace your core before each rep. Breathe out as you pull, breathe in as you lower the weight.
variation_notes: The handles start low and pull back toward the hips, which favours the lats.

exercises.name: Cable Incline Pushdown
exercises.description: Cable Incline Pushdown is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the lats. A variation of the straight arm pulldown: lying back on an incline bench below a high pulley.
setup: Lie on incline an bench facing away from a high pulley machine that has a straight bar attachment on it.
steps: Grasp the straight bar attachment overhead with a pronated (overhand; palms down) shoulder width grip and extend your arms in front of you. The bar should be around 2 inches away from your upper thighs. This will be your starting position.
Keeping the upper arms stationary, lift your arms back in a semi circle until the bar is straight over your head. Breathe in during this portion of the movement.
Slowly go back to the starting position using your lats and hold the contraction once you reach the starting position. Breathe out during the execution of this movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Arms stay long with soft elbows
Move only at the shoulders
mistakes: Bending the elbows into a pushdown
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you sweep down, breathe in as the arms rise.
variation_notes: Lying back on an incline bench below a high pulley.

exercises.name: Rope Straight Arm Pulldown
exercises.description: A lat isolation exercise. Standing at a high cable, you sweep a bar or rope down to your thighs with straight arms.
setup: Attach a straight bar or rope to a high pulley.
Step back, hinge forward slightly and hold it with straight arms at about head height.
steps: Keeping the arms straight, sweep the handle down in an arc to your thighs.
Squeeze the lats at the bottom.
Let the arms rise slowly back to the start.
cues: Arms stay long with soft elbows
Move only at the shoulders
mistakes: Bending the elbows into a pushdown
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you sweep down, breathe in as the arms rise.
variation_notes: A rope lets your hands finish a little behind your hips for a stronger contraction.

exercises.name: Straight Arm Lat Pulldown (Cable)
exercises.description: A lat isolation exercise. Standing at a high cable, you sweep a bar or rope down to your thighs with straight arms.
setup: Attach a straight bar or rope to a high pulley.
Step back, hinge forward slightly and hold it with straight arms at about head height.
steps: Keeping the arms straight, sweep the handle down in an arc to your thighs.
Squeeze the lats at the bottom.
Let the arms rise slowly back to the start.
cues: Arms stay long with soft elbows
Move only at the shoulders
mistakes: Bending the elbows into a pushdown
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you sweep down, breathe in as the arms rise.

exercises.name: T Bar Row
exercises.description: A row with one end of a barbell anchored to the floor and a handle under the loaded end. It allows heavy loading of the mid back.
setup: Straddle the bar facing the loaded end and attach a close-grip handle under the plates.
Hinge forward with a flat back and knees slightly bent.
steps: Pull the handle toward your chest.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower until your arms are straight.
cues: Keep the chest up and back flat
Drive the elbows back past the body
exercises.breathing: Brace your core before each rep. Breathe out as you pull, breathe in as you lower the weight.
safety: If your back rounds, use a chest-supported version.

exercises.name: Back Extension (Hyperextension)
exercises.description: Bending forward over a hip pad and lifting your torso back up. Trains the lower back, glutes and hamstrings.
setup: Set the pad so the top sits just below your hip bones.
Lock your heels under the foot pads.
Cross your arms over your chest or hold a weight.
steps: Lower your torso by hinging at the hips until you feel a stretch in the hamstrings.
Raise your torso back until your body forms a straight line.
cues: Stop at a straight line; do not over-arch
Squeeze the glutes at the top
mistakes: Hyperextending the lower back at the top
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you rise.
safety: Keep the movement smooth; stop if you feel sharp back pain.

exercises.name: Back Extension (Machine)
exercises.description: Bending forward over a hip pad and lifting your torso back up. Trains the lower back, glutes and hamstrings.
setup: Sit in the machine with the back pad across your upper back and feet on the platform.
steps: Push back against the pad by extending your spine and hips.
Return slowly to the start.
cues: Stop at a straight line; do not over-arch
Squeeze the glutes at the top
mistakes: Hyperextending the lower back at the top
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you rise.
safety: Keep the movement smooth; stop if you feel sharp back pain.

Lock your heels under the foot pads.
Cross your arms over your chest or hold a weight.
steps: Lower your torso by hinging at the hips until you feel a stretch in the hamstrings.

Squeeze the glutes at the top

safety: Keep the movement smooth; stop if you feel sharp back pain.
variation_notes: Hug a plate to your chest or hold a dumbbell; add weight in small steps.

exercises.name: Hyperextensions With No Hyperextension Bench
exercises.description: Hyperextensions With No Hyperextension Bench is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the lower back, with help from the glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the back extension: a partner holds the legs on a flat bench.
setup: With someone holding down your legs, slide yourself down to the edge a flat bench until your hips hang off the end of the bench. Tip: Your entire upper body should be hanging down towards the floor. Also, you will be in the same position as if you were on a hyperextension bench but the range of motion will be shorter due to the height of the flat bench vs. that of the hyperextension bench.
steps: With your body straight, cross your arms in front of you (my preference) or behind your head. This will be your starting position. Tip: You can also hold a weight plate for extra resistance in front of you under your crossed arms.

Start bending forward slowly at the waist as far as you can while keeping your back flat. Inhale as you perform this movement. Keep moving forward until you almost touch the floor or you feel a nice stretch on the hamstrings (whichever comes first). Tip: Never round the back as you perform this exercise.

Slowly raise your torso back to the initial position as you exhale. Tip: Avoid the temptation to arch your back past a straight line. Also, do not swing the torso at any time in order to protect the back from injury.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Stop at a straight line; do not over-arch
Squeeze the glutes at the top
mistakes: Hyperextending the lower back at the top
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you rise.
safety: Keep the movement smooth; stop if you feel sharp back pain.
variation_notes: A partner holds the legs on a flat bench.

exercises.name: Weighted Ball Hyperextension
exercises.description: Weighted Ball Hyperextension is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the lower back, with help from the glutes, hamstrings and upper back. A variation of the back extension: lying face down over a ball, holding a weight.
setup: To begin, lie down on an exercise ball with your torso pressing against the ball and parallel to the floor. The ball of your feet should be pressed against the floor to help keep you balanced. Place a weighted plate under your chin or behind your neck. This is the starting position.
steps: Slowly raise your torso up by bending at the waist and lower back. Remember to exhale during this movement.
Hold the contraction on your lower back for a second and lower your torso back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions prescribed in your program.
cues: Stop at a straight line; do not over-arch
Squeeze the glutes at the top
mistakes: Hyperextending the lower back at the top
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you rise.
safety: Keep the movement smooth; stop if you feel sharp back pain.
variation_notes: Lying face down over a ball, holding a weight.

exercises.name: Cat Stretch
exercises.description: Cat Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the lower back, with help from the upper back and traps.
setup: Position yourself on the floor on your hands and knees.
steps: Pull your belly in and round your spine, lower back, shoulders, and neck, letting your head drop.
Hold for 15 seconds.
cues: Move slowly through the spine, one segment at a time
Stay in a comfortable range; this should feel easy
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.
safety: Stop if you feel pain shooting down a leg, and see a professional.

exercises.name: Child's Pose
exercises.description: Child's Pose is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the lower back, with help from the glutes and upper back.
setup: Get on your hands and knees, walk your hands in front of you.
steps: Lower your buttocks down to sit on your heels. Let your arms drag along the floor as you sit back to stretch your entire spine.
Once you settle onto your heels, bring your hands next to your feet and relax. "breathe" into your back. Rest your forehead on the floor. Avoid this position if you have knee problems.
cues: Move slowly through the spine, one segment at a time
Stay in a comfortable range; this should feel easy
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Dancer's Stretch
exercises.description: Dancer's Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the lower back, with help from the abductors and glutes.
setup: Sit up on the floor.
steps: Cross your right leg over your left, keeping the knee bent. Your left leg is straight and down on the floor.
Place your left arm on your right leg and your right hand on the floor.
Rotate your upper body to the right, and hold for 10-20 seconds. Switch sides.
cues: Move slowly through the spine, one segment at a time
Stay in a comfortable range; this should feel easy
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.
safety: Stop if you feel pain shooting down a leg, and see a professional.

exercises.name: Hug A Ball
exercises.description: Hug A Ball is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the lower back, with help from the calves and glutes.
setup: Seat yourself on the floor.
steps: Straddle an exercise ball between both legs and lower your hips down toward the floor.

Hug your arms around the ball to support your body. Adjust your legs so that your feet are flat on the floor and your knees line up over your ankles. Keep a good grip on the ball so it doesn't roll away from you and send you back onto your buttocks.
cues: Move slowly through the spine, one segment at a time
Stay in a comfortable range; this should feel easy
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed

exercises.name: Hug Knees To Chest
exercises.description: Hug Knees To Chest is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the lower back, with help from the glutes.
setup: Lie down on your back and pull both knees up to your chest.
steps: Hold your arms under the knees, not over (that would put to much pressure on your knee joints).
Slowly pull the knees toward your shoulders. This also stretches your buttocks muscles.
cues: Move slowly through the spine, one segment at a time
Stay in a comfortable range; this should feel easy

exercises.name: Pelvic Tilt Into Bridge
exercises.description: Pelvic Tilt Into Bridge is an intermediate-level stretch that mainly targets the lower back.
setup: Lie down with your feet on the floor, heels directly under your knees.
steps: Lift only your tailbone to the ceiling to stretch your lower back. (Don't lift the entire spine yet.) Pull in your stomach.
To go into a bridge, lift the entire spine except the neck.
cues: Move slowly through the spine, one segment at a time

exercises.name: Pyramid
exercises.description: Pyramid is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the lower back.
steps: Start off by rolling your torso forward onto the ball so your hips rest on top of the ball and become the highest point of your body.

Rest your hands and feet on the floor. Your arms and legs can be slightly bent or straight, depending on the size of the ball, your flexibility, and the length of your limbs. This also helps develop stabilizing strength in your torso and shoulders.
cues: Move slowly through the spine, one segment at a time
Stay in a comfortable range; this should feel easy
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side

exercises.name: Standing Pelvic Tilt
exercises.description: Standing Pelvic Tilt is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the lower back, with help from the glutes.
setup: Start off with your feet hip-distance apart.
steps: Bend your knees slightly to keep them soft and springy.
You may want to move your pelvis forward and backward and back few times before holding the tailbone forward in this stretch.
cues: Move slowly through the spine, one segment at a time
Stay in a comfortable range; this should feel easy

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.description: On hands and knees, extending the opposite arm and leg while keeping the back still.
setup: Start on hands and knees, hands under shoulders, knees under hips, back flat.
steps: Extend one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with your body.
Pause, return, and switch sides.
cues: Hips stay level
Reach long, not high
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you extend, breathe in as you return.

exercises.name: Axle Deadlift
exercises.description: Axle Deadlift is an intermediate-level strongman exercise that mainly targets the lower back, with help from the forearms, glutes, hamstrings, upper back, quadriceps and traps. A variation of the deadlift: a thick, non-rotating bar that is much harder to grip.
setup: Approach the bar so that it is centered over your feet. You feet should be about hip width apart. Bend at the hip to grip the bar at shoulder width, allowing your shoulder blades to protract. Typically, you would use an over/under grip.
steps: With your feet and your grip set, take a big breath and then lower your hips and flex the knees until your shins contact the bar. Look forward with your head, keep your chest up and your back arched, and begin driving through the heels to move the weight upward.
After the bar passes the knees, aggressively pull the bar back, pulling your shoulder blades together as you drive your hips forward into the bar.
Lower the bar by bending at the hips and guiding it to the floor.
cues: Weight stays close to the legs
Push the floor away
Hips and shoulders rise together
Stand tall at the top; do not lean back
mistakes: Weight drifting away from the body
Hips shooting up first so it becomes a stiff-leg pull
Jerking the weight off the floor
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace hard before each rep. Hold it as you lift, and breathe out at the top or once the weight is back down.
safety: Reset your position and brace before every rep.
Stop the set when you can no longer keep a flat back.
variation_notes: A thick, non-rotating bar that is much harder to grip.

setup: To deadlift with short bands, simply loop them over the bar before you start, and step into them to set up. For long bands, they will need to be anchored to a secure base, such as heavy dumbbells or a rack.

setup: Begin by having a platform or weight plates that you can stand on, usually 1-3 inches in height. Approach the bar so that it is centered over your feet. You feet should be about hip width apart. Bend at the hip to grip the bar at shoulder width, allowing your shoulder blades to protract. Typically, you would use an overhand grip or an over/under grip on heavier sets.

exercises.name: Reverse Band Deadlift
exercises.description: Reverse Band Deadlift is an advanced-level strength exercise that mainly targets the lower back, with help from the abductors, adductors, calves, glutes, hamstrings and quadriceps. A variation of the deadlift: bands from above help off the floor, so the lockout is heaviest.
setup: Set the bar up in a power rack. Attach bands to the top of the rack, using either bands pegs or the frame itself. Attach the other end of the bands to the bar.

exercises.name: Crossover Reverse Lunge
exercises.description: Crossover Reverse Lunge is an intermediate-level stretch that mainly targets the lower back, with help from the abs & core, abductors, glutes, hamstrings and quadriceps.
setup: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.
steps: Perform a rear lunge by stepping back with one foot and flexing the hips and front knee. As you do so, rotate your torso across the front leg.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position and repeat on the other side, continuing in an alternating fashion.
cues: Start small and slow, then grow the range
Smooth, controlled movement, no flinging
About 8–12 reps per side as a warm-up
mistakes: Swinging into end range with momentum
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Lower Back-SMR
exercises.description: Lower Back-SMR is a beginner-level self-massage (foam rolling) exercise that mainly targets the lower back.
steps: In a seated position, place a foam roll under your lower back. Cross your arms in front of you and protract your shoulders. This will be your starting position.

Raise your hips off of the floor and lean back, keeping your weight on your lower back. Now shift your weight slightly to one side, keeping your weight off of the spine and on the muscles to the side of it. Roll over your lower back, holding points of tension for 10-30 seconds. Repeat on the other side.
cues: Roll slowly, about 2–3 cm per second
Pause 20–30 seconds on tender spots
Support your weight with hands and feet to control the pressure
30–90 seconds per area
mistakes: Rolling directly over joints or bones
Pressing so hard you tense up
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and stay relaxed. On a tender spot, pause and take a few long exhales to let the muscle release.
safety: Avoid rolling the lower back and neck with full body weight; use a softer tool there.

exercises.name: Seated Good Mornings
exercises.description: Seated Good Mornings is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the lower back, with help from the glutes. A variation of the good morning: seated on a bench; hinge forward from the hips.
setup: Set up a box in a power rack. The pins should be set at an appropriate height. Begin by stepping under the bar and placing it across the back of the shoulders, not on top of your traps. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and rotate your elbows forward, attempting to bend the bar across your shoulders.
steps: Remove the bar from the rack, creating a tight arch in your lower back. Keep your head facing forward. With your back, shoulders, and core tight, push your knees and butt out and you begin your descent. Sit back with your hips until you are seated on the box. This will be your starting position.
Keeping the bar tight, bend forward at the hips as much as possible. If you set the pins to what would be parallel, you not only have a safety if you fail, but know when to stop.
Pause just above the pins and reverse the motion until your torso it upright.
cues: Flat back throughout
Hips back, not down
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace hard before each rep. Hold it as you lift, and breathe out at the top or once the weight is back down.
safety: Start very light; the lever arm makes this heavy on the lower back.
variation_notes: Seated on a bench; hinge forward from the hips.

exercises.name: Stiff Leg Barbell Good Morning
exercises.description: Stiff Leg Barbell Good Morning is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the lower back, with help from the glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the good morning: knees nearly straight, for more hamstring stretch.
setup: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
steps: Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance. Keep your head up at all times as looking down will get you off balance and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your legs stationary, move your torso forward by bending at the hips while inhaling. Lower your torso until it is parallel with the floor.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by elevating your torso back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Flat back throughout
Hips back, not down
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace hard before each rep. Hold it as you lift, and breathe out at the top or once the weight is back down.

variation_notes: Knees nearly straight, for more hamstring stretch.

exercises.name: Rack Pull
exercises.description: A partial deadlift from pins set around knee height. It overloads the top of the lift and the upper back.
setup: Set the safety pins so the bar sits just below or at the knees.
Set up as for a deadlift with a flat back.
steps: Drive the hips forward to stand up with the bar.
Lock out tall with shoulders back.
Lower back to the pins with control.
cues: Flat back
Squeeze the glutes to lock out
mistakes: Leaning back excessively at the top
Slamming the bar onto the pins
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace hard before each rep. Hold it as you lift, and breathe out at the top or once the weight is back down.

exercises.name: Rack Pull with Bands
exercises.description: Rack Pull with Bands is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the lower back, with help from the forearms, glutes, hamstrings, quadriceps and traps. A variation of the rack pull: bands add load toward lockout.
setup: Set up in a power rack with the bar on the pins. The pins should be set to the desired point; just below the knees, just above, or in the mid thigh position. Attach bands to the base of the rack, or secure them with dumbbells. Attach the other end to the bar. You may need to choke the bands to provide tension.
steps: Position yourself against the bar in proper deadlifting position. Your feet should be under your hips, your grip shoulder width, back arched, and hips back to engage the hamstrings. Since the weight is typically heavy, you may use a mixed grip, a hook grip, or use straps to aid in holding the weight.

With your head looking forward, extend through the hips and knees, pulling the weight up and back until lockout. Be sure to pull your shoulders back as you complete the movement. Return the weight to the pins and repeat.
cues: Flat back
Squeeze the glutes to lock out
mistakes: Leaning back excessively at the top
Slamming the bar onto the pins

variation_notes: Bands add load toward lockout.

exercises.name: Atlas Stone Trainer
exercises.description: Atlas Stone Trainer is an intermediate-level strongman exercise that mainly targets the lower back, with help from the biceps, forearms, glutes, hamstrings and quadriceps.
setup: This trainer is effective for developing Atlas Stone strength for those who don't have access to stones, and are typically made from bar ends or heavy pipe.
steps: Begin by loading the desired weight onto the bar. Straddle the weight, wrapping your arms around the implement, bending at the hips.

Begin by pulling the weight up past the knees, extending through the hips. As the weight clears the knees, it can be lapped by resting it on your thighs and sitting back, hugging it tightly to your chest.
Finish the movement by extending through your hips and knees to raise the weight as high as possible. The weight can be returned to the lap or to the ground for successive repetitions.
cues: Straddle the implement and wrap it tight to the body
Lap it first if needed, then drive the hips forward to load
Keep it close the whole way
mistakes: Letting it drift away from the body
exercises.breathing: Big breath and brace before the lift; exhale once the implement is loaded.
safety: Some back rounding is normal on stones; build up gradually and use tacky or sleeves for grip.

exercises.name: Atlas Stones
exercises.description: Atlas Stones is an advanced-level strongman exercise that mainly targets the lower back, with help from the abs & core, adductors, biceps, calves, forearms, glutes, hamstrings, upper back, quadriceps and traps.
setup: Begin with the atlas stone between your feet. Bend at the hips to wrap your arms vertically around the Atlas Stone, attempting to get your fingers underneath the stone. Many stones will have a small flat portion on the bottom, which will make the stone easier to hold.
steps: Pulling the stone into your torso, drive through the back half of your feet to pull the stone from the ground.
As the stone passes the knees, lap it by sitting backward, pulling the stone on top of your thighs.

Sit low, getting the stone high onto your chest as you change your grip to reach over the stone. Stand, driving through with your hips. Close distance to the loading platform, and lean back, extending the hips to get the stone as high as possible.

Lap it first if needed, then drive the hips forward to load
Keep it close the whole way
mistakes: Letting it drift away from the body
exercises.breathing: Big breath and brace before the lift; exhale once the implement is loaded.

exercises.name: Keg Load
exercises.description: Keg Load is an intermediate-level strongman exercise that mainly targets the lower back, with help from the abs & core, biceps, calves, forearms, glutes, hamstrings, upper back, quadriceps and traps.
setup: To load kegs, place the desired number a distance from the loading platform, typically 30-50 feet.
steps: Begin by grabbing the close handle of the first keg, tilting it onto its side to grab the opposite edge of the bottom of the keg. Lift the keg up to your chest.

The higher you can place the keg, the faster you should be able to move to the platform. Shouldering is usually not allowed. Be sure to keep a firm hold on the keg. Move as quickly as possible to the platform, and load it, extending through your hips, knees, and ankles to get it as high as possible.
Return to the starting position to retrieve the next keg, and repeat until the event is completed.

Keep it close the whole way
