exercises.name: Superman
exercises.description: Lying face down and lifting your arms and legs off the floor to strengthen the back of the body.
setup: Lie face down with arms extended overhead and legs straight.
steps: Lift your arms, chest and legs a few centimetres off the floor at the same time.
Hold for 1–2 seconds.
Lower slowly.
cues: Look at the floor to keep the neck neutral
Lift long, not high
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you lift, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Neck-SMR
exercises.description: Neck-SMR is an intermediate-level self-massage (foam rolling) exercise that mainly targets the neck.
steps: Using a muscle roller or a rolling pin, place the roller behind your head and against your neck. Make sure that you do not place the roller directly against the spine, but turned slightly so that the roller is pressed against the muscles to either side of the spine. This will be your starting position.
Starting at the top of your neck, slowly roll down the muscles of your neck, pausing at points of tension for 10-30 seconds.
cues: Roll slowly, about 2–3 cm per second
Pause 20–30 seconds on tender spots
Support your weight with hands and feet to control the pressure
30–90 seconds per area
mistakes: Rolling directly over joints or bones
Pressing so hard you tense up

exercises.name: Lying Face Up Plate Neck Resistance
exercises.description: Lying Face Up Plate Neck Resistance is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the neck. A variation of the lying neck curls: lying face up on a bench, a plate on the forehead.
setup: Lie face up with your whole body straight on a flat bench while holding a weight plate on top of your forehead. Tip: You will need to position yourself so that your shoulders are slightly above the end of a flat bench in order for the traps, neck and head to be off the bench. This will be your starting position.
steps: While keeping the plate secure on your forehead slowly lower your head back in a semi-circular motion as you breathe in.
Raise your head back up to the starting position in a semi-circular motion as you breathe out. Hold the contraction for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Slow and controlled
Small range is fine
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you curl, breathe in as you lower.
safety: Start with no weight and high reps. Stop if you feel pain, tingling or dizziness.
variation_notes: Lying face up on a bench, a plate on the forehead.

steps: Let your head lower gently backward.
Curl your chin toward your chest.
Lower slowly.

exercises.name: Lying Face Down Plate Neck Resistance
exercises.description: Lying Face Down Plate Neck Resistance is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the neck. A variation of the lying neck extension: lying face down on a bench, a plate on the back of the head.
setup: Lie face down with your whole body straight on a flat bench while holding a weight plate behind your head. Tip: You will need to position yourself so that your shoulders are slightly above the end of a flat bench in order for the upper chest, neck and face to be off the bench. This will be your starting position.
steps: While keeping the plate secure on the back of your head slowly lower your head (as in saying "yes") as you breathe in.
Raise your head back up to the starting position in a semi-circular motion as you breathe out. Hold the contraction for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Slow and controlled
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you lift, breathe in as you lower.
safety: Start with no weight and high reps. Stop if you feel pain, tingling or dizziness.
variation_notes: Lying face down on a bench, a plate on the back of the head.

exercises.name: Lying Neck Extension
exercises.description: Lying face down with your head off the end of a bench, lifting your head up and back.
setup: Lie face down on a bench with your head and neck past the edge.
steps: Let your head lower toward the floor.
Lift it up until it is level with your body or slightly higher.
Lower slowly.
cues: Slow and controlled
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you lift, breathe in as you lower.
safety: Start with no weight and high reps. Stop if you feel pain, tingling or dizziness.

exercises.name: Lying Neck Extension (Weighted)
exercises.description: Lying face down with your head off the end of a bench, lifting your head up and back.
setup: Lie face down on a bench with your head and neck past the edge.
steps: Let your head lower toward the floor.
Lift it up until it is level with your body or slightly higher.

exercises.name: Seated Head Harness Neck Resistance
exercises.description: Seated Head Harness Neck Resistance is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the neck. A variation of the lying neck extension: seated, bent forward, a weight hanging from a head harness.
setup: Place a neck strap on the floor at the end of a flat bench. Once you have selected the weights, sit at the end of the flat bench with your feet wider than shoulder width apart from each other. Your toes should be pointed out.
steps: Slowly move your torso forward until it is almost parallel with the floor. Using both hands, securely position the neck strap around your head. Tip: Make sure the weights are still lying on the floor to prevent any strain on the neck. Now grab the weight with both hands while elevating your torso back until it is almost perpendicular to the floor. Note: Your head and torso needs to be slightly tilted forward to perform this exercise.
Now place both hands on top of your knees. This is the starting position.
Slowly lower your neck down until your chin touches the upper part of your chest while breathing in.
While exhaling, bring your neck back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Slow and controlled
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you lift, breathe in as you lower.
safety: Start with no weight and high reps. Stop if you feel pain, tingling or dizziness.
variation_notes: Seated, bent forward, a weight hanging from a head harness.

exercises.name: Isometric Neck Exercise - Front And Back
exercises.description: Isometric Neck Exercise - Front And Back is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the neck.
setup: With your head and neck in a neutral position (normal position with head erect facing forward), place both of your hands on the front side of your head.
steps: Now gently push forward as you contract the neck muscles but resisting any movement of your head. Start with slow tension and increase slowly. Keep breathing normally as you execute this contraction.
Hold for the recommended number of seconds.
Now release the tension slowly.
Rest for the recommended amount of time and repeat with your hands placed on the back side of your head.
cues: Press the hand against the head while the head does not move
Build up to a moderate effort over 2 seconds
Hold 5–10 seconds
exercises.breathing: Breathe normally throughout; never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Isometric Neck Exercise - Sides
exercises.description: Isometric Neck Exercise - Sides is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the neck.
setup: With your head and neck in a neutral position (normal position with head erect facing forward), place your left hand on the left side of your head.
steps: Now gently push towards the left as you contract the left neck muscles but resisting any movement of your head. Start with slow tension and increase slowly. Keep breathing normally as you execute this contraction.
Hold for the recommended number of seconds.
Now release the tension slowly.
Rest for the recommended amount of time and repeat with your right hand placed on the right side of your head.
cues: Press the hand against the head while the head does not move
Build up to a moderate effort over 2 seconds
Hold 5–10 seconds
exercises.breathing: Breathe normally throughout; never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Chin To Chest Stretch
exercises.description: Chin To Chest Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the neck, with help from the traps.
steps: Get into a seated position on the floor.
Place both hands at the rear of your head, fingers interlocked, thumbs pointing down and elbows pointing straight ahead. Slowly pull your head down to your chest. Hold for 20-30 seconds.
cues: Move the head slowly and gently
Keep the shoulders down and relaxed
Hold 15–30 seconds
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.
safety: Stop if you feel dizziness, tingling or pain in the arms.

exercises.name: Side Neck Stretch
exercises.description: Side Neck Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the neck.
steps: Start with your shoulders relaxed, gently tilt your head towards your shoulder.
Assist stretch with a gentle pull on the side of the head.
cues: Move the head slowly and gently
Keep the shoulders down and relaxed
Hold 15–30 seconds
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.
safety: Stop if you feel dizziness, tingling or pain in the arms.

exercises.name: Belt Squat (Machine)
exercises.description: A squat with the load hanging from a belt around your hips, so nothing loads the spine.
setup: Attach the belt around your hips and stand on the platform.
Hold the handles lightly for balance.
steps: Squat down as deep as you can with good form.
Stand back up.
cues: Sit straight down
Knees out
mistakes: Pulling on the handles to help
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back up.

exercises.name: Weighted Squat
exercises.description: Weighted Squat is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the belt squat: a dipping belt holds the weight at the hips.
setup: Start by positioning two flat benches shoulder width apart from each other. Stand on top of them and wrap the weighted belt around your waist with the amount of weight you feel comfortable with. Make sure your toes are facing out.
steps: Once you are standing straight up with the weight hanging in between your legs, position your arms so that they are fully extended to the side of your body. This is the starting position.

Begin by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calves becomes slightly less than 90-degrees (which is the point in which the upper legs are below parallel to the floor). Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: If you performed the exercise correctly, the front of the knees should make an imaginary straight line with the toes that are perpendicular to the front. If your knees are past that imaginary line (if they are past your toes) then you are placing undue stress on the knee and the exercise has been performed incorrectly.

Begin to move the body back up by pushing the floor of the flat bench with the ball of your foot mainly as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position. Exhale as you perform this portion of the exercise.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Sit straight down
Knees out
mistakes: Pulling on the handles to help
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back up.
variation_notes: A dipping belt holds the weight at the hips.

exercises.name: Alternate Leg Diagonal Bound
exercises.description: Alternate Leg Diagonal Bound is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the abductors, adductors, calves, glutes and hamstrings.
setup: Assume a comfortable stance with one foot slightly in front of the other.
steps: Begin by pushing off with the front leg, driving the opposite knee forward and as high as possible before landing. Attempt to cover as much distance to each side with each bound.
It may help to use a line on the ground to guage distance from side to side.
Repeat the sequence with the other leg.
cues: Load the hips and swing the arms back before each jump
Drive through the whole foot and extend the hips fully
Stick the landing with bent knees before the next rep
exercises.breathing: Take a quick breath before each effort and exhale sharply as you take off. Reset your breathing between reps.

exercises.name: Side Standing Long Jump
exercises.description: Side Standing Long Jump is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes and hamstrings.
setup: Begin standing with your feet hip width apart in an athletic stance. Your head and chest should be up, knees and hips slightly bent. This will be your starting position.
steps: Leaning to your right, extend through your hips, knees, and ankles to jump into the air. Block with the arms to lead the movement, jumping as far to your right as you can.
Land facing the same direction with your feet hip width apart, absorbing the impact through your lower body.
cues: Load the hips and swing the arms back before each jump
Drive through the whole foot and extend the hips fully
Stick the landing with bent knees before the next rep
exercises.breathing: Take a quick breath before each effort and exhale sharply as you take off. Reset your breathing between reps.

exercises.name: Single Leg Push-off
exercises.description: Single Leg Push-off is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves and hamstrings.
setup: Stand on the ground with one foot resting on the box, heel close to the edge.
steps: Push off with your foot on top of the box, trying to gain as much height as possible by extending through the hip and knee.
Land with the same foot on top of the box, returning your other foot back to the start position.
cues: Load the hips and swing the arms back before each jump
Drive through the whole foot and extend the hips fully
Stick the landing with bent knees before the next rep
exercises.breathing: Take a quick breath before each effort and exhale sharply as you take off. Reset your breathing between reps.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Stride Jump
exercises.description: Single-Leg Stride Jump is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the abductors, adductors, calves and hamstrings.
setup: Stand to the side of a box with your inside foot on top of it, close to the edge.
steps: Begin by swinging the arms upward as you push through the top leg, jumping upward as high as possible. Attempt to drive the opposite knee upward.
Land in the same position that you started, using your inside leg to decelerate the impact.
cues: Load the hips and swing the arms back before each jump
Drive through the whole foot and extend the hips fully
Stick the landing with bent knees before the next rep
exercises.breathing: Take a quick breath before each effort and exhale sharply as you take off. Reset your breathing between reps.

exercises.name: Standing Long Jump
exercises.description: Standing Long Jump is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes and hamstrings.
setup: This drill is best done in sand or other soft landing surface. Ensure that you are able to measure distance. Stand in a partial squat stance with feet shoulder width apart.
steps: Utilizing a big arm swing and a countermovement of the legs, jump forward as far as you can.
Attempt to land with your feet out in front you, reaching as far as possible with your legs.
Measure the distance from your landing point to the starting point and track results.
cues: Load the hips and swing the arms back before each jump
Drive through the whole foot and extend the hips fully
Stick the landing with bent knees before the next rep
exercises.breathing: Take a quick breath before each effort and exhale sharply as you take off. Reset your breathing between reps.

exercises.name: Stride Jump Crossover
exercises.description: Stride Jump Crossover is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the abductors, adductors, calves and hamstrings.
setup: Stand to the side of a box with your inside foot on top of it, close to the edge.
steps: Begin by swinging the arms upward as you push through the top leg, jumping upward as high as possible. Attempt to drive the opposite knee upward.
Land in the opposite position that you started, on the opposite side of the box. The foot that was initially on the box will now be on the ground, with the opposite foot now on the box.
Repeat the movement, crossing back over to the other side.
cues: Load the hips and swing the arms back before each jump
Drive through the whole foot and extend the hips fully
Stick the landing with bent knees before the next rep
exercises.breathing: Take a quick breath before each effort and exhale sharply as you take off. Reset your breathing between reps.

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.description: Jumping from the floor onto a box and landing softly. Builds explosive leg power.
setup: Stand about a foot-length from a sturdy box, feet hip-width.
steps: Swing your arms back and dip into a quarter squat.
Jump explosively onto the box.
Land softly with both feet in a half squat.
Stand up, then step down (do not jump down).
cues: Land quietly
Knees in line with the toes
mistakes: Choosing a box so high that you land in a deep squat
exercises.breathing: Breathe in before the jump, breathe out sharply as you take off or land.
safety: Land softly with knees bent and in line with the toes.
Stop the set when jumps become slow or landings get sloppy.
Step down rather than jumping down to protect your Achilles tendons.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Seated Box Jump
exercises.description: Dumbbell Seated Box Jump is an intermediate-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the box jump: jump from a seated start, holding light dumbbells.
setup: Position a box a couple feet to the side of a bench. Hold a dumbbell to your chest with both hands and seat yourself on the bench facing the box. This will be your starting position.
steps: Plant your feet firmly on the ground as you lean forward, extending through the hips and knees to jump up and forward.
Land on the box with both feet, absorbing the impact by allowing the hips and knees to bend.
Step down and return to the starting position.
cues: Land quietly
Knees in line with the toes
mistakes: Choosing a box so high that you land in a deep squat
exercises.breathing: Breathe in before the jump, breathe out sharply as you take off or land.
safety: Land softly with knees bent and in line with the toes.
Stop the set when jumps become slow or landings get sloppy.
Step down rather than jumping down to protect your Achilles tendons.
variation_notes: Jump from a seated start, holding light dumbbells.

exercises.name: Lateral Box Jump
exercises.description: Jumping from the floor onto a box and landing softly. Builds explosive leg power.
setup: Stand about a foot-length from a sturdy box, feet hip-width.
steps: Swing your arms back and dip into a quarter squat.
Jump explosively onto the box.
Land softly with both feet in a half squat.
Stand up, then step down (do not jump down).
cues: Land quietly
Knees in line with the toes
mistakes: Choosing a box so high that you land in a deep squat
exercises.breathing: Breathe in before the jump, breathe out sharply as you take off or land.
safety: Land softly with knees bent and in line with the toes.
Stop the set when jumps become slow or landings get sloppy.
Step down rather than jumping down to protect your Achilles tendons.
variation_notes: Stand side-on to the box and jump sideways onto it.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat (Barbell)
exercises.description: A split squat with the back foot raised on a bench. A very effective single-leg exercise for quads and glutes.
setup: Stand about a long stride in front of a bench.
Place the top of your back foot on the bench.
steps: Lower until the front thigh is about parallel and the back knee is near the floor.
Drive up through the front foot.
Finish all reps, then switch legs.
cues: Front foot far enough forward that the heel stays down
Lean slightly forward for more glutes, stay upright for more quads
mistakes: Front foot too close to the bench
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back up.
safety: Start with bodyweight to find a stable foot position.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat (Dumbbell)
exercises.description: A split squat with the back foot raised on a bench. A very effective single-leg exercise for quads and glutes.

steps: Lower until the front thigh is about parallel and the back knee is near the floor.

exercises.name: One Leg Barbell Squat
exercises.description: One Leg Barbell Squat is an advanced-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the bulgarian split squat: rear foot on a bench, bar on the back.
setup: Start by standing about 2 to 3 feet in front of a flat bench with your back facing the bench. Have a barbell in front of you on the floor. Tip: Your feet should be shoulder width apart from each other.
steps: Bend the knees and use a pronated grip with your hands being wider than shoulder width apart from each other to lift the barbell up until you can rest it on your chest.

Then lift the barbell over your head and rest it on the base of your neck. Move one foot back so that your toe is resting on the flat bench. Your other foot should be stationary in front of you. Keep your head up at all times as looking down will get you off balance and also maintain a straight back. Tip: Make sure your back is straight and chest is out while performing this exercise.
As you inhale, slowly lower your leg until your thigh is parallel to the floor. At this point, your knee should be over your toes. Your chest should be directly above the middle of your thigh.
Leading with the chest and hips and contracting the quadriceps, elevate your leg back to the starting position as you exhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Switch legs and repeat the movement.
cues: Front foot far enough forward that the heel stays down
Lean slightly forward for more glutes, stay upright for more quads
mistakes: Front foot too close to the bench
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back up.
safety: Start with bodyweight to find a stable foot position.
variation_notes: Rear foot on a bench, bar on the back.

exercises.name: Suspended Split Squat
exercises.description: Suspended Split Squat is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the abductors, adductors, calves, glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the bulgarian split squat: rear foot in a suspension strap.
setup: Suspend your straps so the handles are 18-30 inches from the floor.
steps: Facing away from the setup, place your rear foot into the handle behind you. Keep your head looking forward and your chest up, with your knee slightly bent. This will be your starting position.
Descend by flexing the knee and hips, lowering yourself to the ground. Keep your weight on the heel of your foot and maintain your posture throughout the exercise.
At the bottom of the movement, reverse the motion, extending through the hip and knee to return to the starting position.
cues: Front foot far enough forward that the heel stays down
Lean slightly forward for more glutes, stay upright for more quads
mistakes: Front foot too close to the anchor
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back up.
safety: Start with bodyweight to find a stable foot position.
variation_notes: Rear foot in a suspension strap.

exercises.name: Burpee
exercises.description: A squat, a jump back to a plank, a push up, a jump forward and a jump up, all in one flowing movement.
setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
steps: Squat down and place your hands on the floor.
Jump your feet back to a plank and lower your chest to the floor.
Push up, jump your feet back toward your hands.
Jump up and clap overhead.
cues: Keep a steady rhythm
Land softly
exercises.breathing: Breathe out on the push up and on the jump; find a steady rhythm.

exercises.name: Burpee Broad Jumps

steps: Squat down and place your hands on the floor.
Jump your feet back to a plank and lower your chest to the floor.
Push up, jump your feet back toward your hands.
Jump up and clap overhead.

Land softly

variation_notes: Replace the vertical jump with a long forward jump, then continue from where you land.

exercises.name: Clean from Blocks
exercises.description: Clean from Blocks is an intermediate-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes, hamstrings and traps. A variation of the clean: bar starts on blocks at knee height.
setup: With a barbell on boxes or stands of the desired height, take an overhand or hook grip just outside the legs. Lower your hips with the weight focused on the heels, back straight, head facing forward, chest up, with your shoulders just in front of the bar. This will be your starting position.
steps: Begin the first pull by driving through the heels, extending your knees. Your back angle should stay the same, and your arms should remain straight with the elbows pointed out.

As full extension is achieved, transition into the receiving position by aggressively shrugging and flexing the arms with the elbows up and out. Aggressively pull yourself down, rotating your elbows under the bar as you do so. Receive the bar in a front squat position, the depth of which is dependent upon the height of the bar at the end of the third pull. The bar should be racked onto the protracted shoulders, lightly touching the throat with the hands relaxed. Continue to descend to the bottom squat position, which will help in the recovery.
Immediately recover by driving through the heels, keeping the torso upright and elbows up. Continue until you have risen to a standing position. Return the weight to the boxes for the next rep.
cues: Bar stays close to the body
Patient off the floor, explosive at the hips
Fast elbows in the catch
mistakes: Bar swinging away from the body
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
safety: Olympic lifts are technical; learn them with a coach and an empty bar or PVC pipe first.
Use bumper plates and a platform so the bar can be dropped safely.
variation_notes: Bar starts on blocks at knee height.

exercises.name: Hang Clean - Below the Knees
exercises.description: Hang Clean - Below the Knees is an intermediate-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, forearms, glutes, hamstrings, lower back and traps. A variation of the clean: starts from the hang just below the knees.
setup: Begin with a shoulder width, double overhand or hook grip, with the bar hanging just below the knees. Your back should be straight and inclined slightly forward.
steps: Begin by aggressively extending through the hips, knees and ankles, driving the weight upward. As you do so, shrug your shoulders towards your ears. As full extension is achieved, transition into the third pull by aggressively shrugging and flexing the arms with the elbows up and out.

At peak extension, aggressively pull yourself down, rotating your elbows under the bar as you do so. Receive the bar in a front squat position, the depth of which is dependent upon the height of the bar at the end of the third pull. The bar should be racked onto the protracted shoulders, lightly touching the throat with the hands relaxed. Continue to descend to the bottom squat position, which will help in the recovery.
Immediately recover by driving through the heels, keeping the torso upright and elbows up. Continue until you have risen to a standing position.
cues: Bar stays close to the body
Patient off the floor, explosive at the hips
Fast elbows in the catch
mistakes: Bar swinging away from the body
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
safety: Olympic lifts are technical; learn them with a coach and an empty bar or PVC pipe first.
Use bumper plates and a platform so the bar can be dropped safely.
variation_notes: Starts from the hang just below the knees.

exercises.name: Split Clean
exercises.description: Split Clean is an intermediate-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, forearms, glutes, hamstrings, lower back and traps. A variation of the clean: caught in a split stance instead of a squat.
setup: With a barbell on the floor close to the shins, take an overhand grip just outside the legs. Lower your hips with the weight focused on the heels, back straight, head facing forward, chest up, with your shoulders just in front of the bar. This will be your starting position.
steps: Begin the first pull by driving through the heels, extending your knees. Your back angle should stay the same, and your arms should remain straight. Move the weight with control as you continue to above the knees.

Next comes the second pull, the main source of acceleration for the clean. As the bar approaches the mid-thigh position, begin extending through the hips. In a jumping motion, accelerate by extending the hips, knees, and ankles, using speed to move the bar upward. There should be no need to actively pull through the arms to accelerate the weight; at the end of the second pull, the body should be fully extended, leaning slightly back, with the arms still extended.

As full extension is achieved, transition into the third pull by aggressively shrugging and flexing the arms with the elbows up and out. At peak extension, aggressively pull yourself down, rotating your elbows under the bar as you do so.

Receive the bar with the feet split, aggressively moving one foot forward and one foot back. The bar should be racked onto the protracted shoulders, lightly touching the throat with the hands relaxed. Continue to descend to the bottom position, which will help in the recovery.
Immediately recover by driving through the heels, keeping the torso upright and elbows up. Bring the feet together as you stand up.
cues: Bar stays close to the body
Patient off the floor, explosive at the hips
Fast elbows in the catch
mistakes: Bar swinging away from the body
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
safety: Olympic lifts are technical; learn them with a coach and an empty bar or PVC pipe first.
Use bumper plates and a platform so the bar can be dropped safely.
variation_notes: Caught in a split stance instead of a squat.

exercises.name: Conan's Wheel
exercises.description: Conan's Wheel is an intermediate-level strongman exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the abs & core, biceps, calves, forearms, lower back and traps.
steps: With the weight loaded, take a zurcher hold on the end of the implement. Place the bar in the crook of the elbow and hold onto your wrist. Try to keep the weight off of the forearms.

Begin by lifting the weight from the ground. Keep a tight, upright posture as you being to walk, taking short, fast steps. Look up and away as you turn in a circle. Do not hold your breath during the event. Continue walking until you complete one or more complete turns.
cues: Bar held in the crook of the elbows
Brace and walk in a circle
Short steps
exercises.breathing: Keep the core braced and breathe in short, steady breaths behind the brace. Do not hold your breath for the whole set.

exercises.name: Cable Deadlifts
exercises.description: Cable Deadlifts is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the forearms, glutes, hamstrings and lower back. A variation of the deadlift: low pulley with a bar, facing the stack.
setup: Move the cables to the bottom of the towers and select an appropriate weight. Stand directly in between the uprights.
steps: To begin, squat down be flexing your hips and knees until you can reach the handles.
After grasping them, begin your ascent. Driving through your heels extend your hips and knees keeping your hands hanging at your side. Keep your head and chest up throughout the movement.
After reaching a full standing position, Return to the starting position and repeat.
cues: Weight stays close to the legs
Push the floor away
Hips and shoulders rise together
Stand tall at the top; do not lean back
mistakes: Weight drifting away from the body
Hips shooting up first so it becomes a stiff-leg pull
Jerking the weight off the floor
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace hard before each rep. Hold it as you lift, and breathe out at the top or once the weight is back down.
safety: Reset your position and brace before every rep.
Stop the set when you can no longer keep a flat back.

exercises.name: Car Deadlift
exercises.description: Car Deadlift is an intermediate-level strongman exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the forearms, glutes, hamstrings, lower back and traps. A variation of the deadlift: strongman frame or handles beside the body.
setup: This event apparatus typically has neutral grip handles, however some have a straight bar that you can approach like a normal deadlift. The apparatus can be loaded with a vehicle or other heavy objects such as tractor tires or kegs.
steps: Center yourself between the handles if you are a strong squatter, or back a couple inches if you are a strong deadlifter. You feet should be about hip width apart. Bend at the hip to grip the handles. With your feet and your grip set, take a big breath and then lower your hips and flex the knees.

Look forward with your head, keep your chest up and your back arched, and begin driving through the heels to move the weight upward. As the weight comes up, pull your shoulder blades together as you drive your hips forward.
Lower the weight by bending at the hips and guiding it to the floor.

Push the floor away
Hips and shoulders rise together
Stand tall at the top; do not lean back

variation_notes: Strongman frame or handles beside the body.

exercises.name: Deadlift (Trap Bar)
exercises.description: Lifting a weight from the floor to standing by driving with the legs and hips. Trains nearly the whole back of the body.
setup: Stand in the centre of the trap bar.
Hinge and bend the knees to grip the handles at your sides.
Flat back, chest up.
steps: Brace, then push the floor away with your legs.
Keep the weight close to your legs as it rises.
Once the weight passes your knees, drive the hips forward to stand tall.
Lower by pushing the hips back first, then bending the knees once the weight passes them.

Hips and shoulders rise together
Stand tall at the top; do not lean back

variation_notes: The load sits at your sides, so the back stays more upright. Easier to learn and gentler on the lower back.

exercises.name: Leverage Deadlift
exercises.description: Leverage Deadlift is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the deadlift: a plate-loaded lever deadlift machine.
steps: Load the pins to an appropriate weight. Position yourself directly between the handles. Grasp the bottom handles with a comfortable grip, and then lower your hips as you take a breath. Look forward with your head and keep your chest up. This will be your starting position.
Return the weight to the starting position.

exercises.name: One-Arm Side Deadlift
exercises.description: One-Arm Side Deadlift is an advanced-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the abs & core, calves, glutes, hamstrings, lower back and traps. A variation of the deadlift: one hand in the middle of the bar beside you; the core stops you leaning.
setup: Stand to the side of a barbell next to its center. Bend your knees and lower your body until you are able to reach the barbell.
steps: Grasp the bar as if you were grabbing a briefcase (palms facing you since the bar is sideways). You may need a wrist wrap if you are using a significant amount of weight. This is your starting position.
Use your legs to help lift the barbell up while exhaling. Your arms should extend fully as bring the barbell up until you are in a standing position.
Slowly bring the barbell back down while inhaling. Tip: Make sure to bend your knees while lowering the weight to avoid any injury from occurring.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Switch arms and repeat the movement.

exercises.name: Rickshaw Deadlift
exercises.description: Rickshaw Deadlift is an intermediate-level strongman exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the forearms, glutes, hamstrings, lower back and traps. A variation of the deadlift: handles of a rickshaw frame beside the body.
setup: Load the frame with the desired weight. Center yourself between the handles. You feet should be about hip width apart. Bend at the hips to grip the handles, allowing your shoulder blades to protract.
steps: With your feet and your grip set, take a big breath and then lower your hips and flex the knees. Look forward with your head, keep your chest up and your back arched, and begin driving through the heels to move the weight upward. As the weight comes up, pull your shoulder blades together as you drive your hips forward.
Lower the weight by bending at the hips and guiding it to the ground.

exercises.name: Depth Jump Leap
exercises.description: Depth Jump Leap is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the abductors, adductors, calves, glutes and hamstrings.
setup: For this drill you will need two boxes or benches, one 12 to 16 inches high and the other 22 to 26 inches high.
steps: Stand on one of the two boxes with arms at the sides; feet should be together and slightly off the edge as in the depth jump. Place the other box approximately two or three feet in front of and facing the performer.
Begin by dropping off the initial box, landing and simultaneously taking off with both feet.
Rebound by driving upward and outward as intensely as possible, using the arms and full extension of the body to jump onto the higher box. Again, allow the legs to absorb the impact.
cues: Step off the box; do not jump off it
Land on both feet and leave the ground again as fast as possible
Knees track over the toes on landing
Start with a low box (30 cm)
mistakes: A box that is too high, causing a slow, deep landing
exercises.breathing: Take a quick breath before each effort and exhale sharply as you take off. Reset your breathing between reps.
safety: An advanced plyometric: build up with box jumps and hops first, and keep sets short.

exercises.name: Linear Depth Jump
exercises.description: Linear Depth Jump is an intermediate-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes and hamstrings.
setup: You will need two boxes or benches spaced a few feet away from each other. Begin by standing on one box facing towards the other platform.
steps: To initiate the movement, gently drop down to the ground between your platforms, allowing the knees and hips to flex.
Reverse the motion by exploding, extending through the hips, knees, and ankles to jump onto the other platform.
Land softly, asborbing the impact through the legs.
cues: Step off the box; do not jump off it
Land on both feet and leave the ground again as fast as possible
Knees track over the toes on landing
Start with a low box (30 cm)
mistakes: A box that is too high, causing a slow, deep landing
exercises.breathing: Take a quick breath before each effort and exhale sharply as you take off. Reset your breathing between reps.
safety: An advanced plyometric: build up with box jumps and hops first, and keep sets short.

exercises.name: Frog Hops
exercises.description: Frog Hops is an intermediate-level stretch that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes and hamstrings.
steps: Stand with your hands behind your head, and squat down keeping your torso upright and your head up. This will be your starting position.
Jump forward several feet, avoiding jumping unnecessarily high. As your feet contact the ground, absorb the impact through your legs, and jump again. Repeat this action 5-10 times.
cues: Start small and slow, then grow the range
Smooth, controlled movement, no flinging
About 8–12 reps per side as a warm-up
mistakes: Swinging into end range with momentum
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Iron Crosses (stretch)
exercises.description: Iron Crosses (stretch) is an intermediate-level stretch that mainly targets the quadriceps.
setup: Lie face down on the floor, with your arms extended out to your side, palms pressed to the floor. This will be your starting position.
steps: To begin, flex one knee and bring that leg across the back of your body, attempting to touch it to the ground near the opposite hand.
Promptly return the leg to the starting postion, and quickly repeat with the other leg. Continue alternating for 10-20 repetitions.
cues: Start small and slow, then grow the range
Smooth, controlled movement, no flinging
About 8–12 reps per side as a warm-up
mistakes: Swinging into end range with momentum
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Rear Leg Raises
exercises.description: Rear Leg Raises is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the quadriceps.
steps: Place yourself on your hands knees on an exercise mat. Your head should be looking forward and the bend of the knees should create a 90-degree angle between the hamstrings and the calves. This will be your starting position.
Extend one leg up and behind you. The knee and hip should both extend. Repeat for 5-10 repetitions, and then switch sides.
cues: Start small and slow, then grow the range
Smooth, controlled movement, no flinging
About 8–12 reps per side as a warm-up
mistakes: Swinging into end range with momentum
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Quadriceps-SMR
exercises.description: Quadriceps-SMR is an intermediate-level self-massage (foam rolling) exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps.
steps: Lay facedown on the floor with your weight supported by your hands or forearms. Place a foam roll underneath one leg on the quadriceps, and keep the foot off of the ground. Make sure to relax the leg as much as possible. This will be your starting position.
Shifting as much weight onto the leg to be stretched as is tolerable, roll over the foam from above the knee to below the hip, holding points of tension for 10-30 seconds. Switch sides.
cues: Roll slowly, about 2–3 cm per second
Pause 20–30 seconds on tender spots
Support your weight with hands and feet to control the pressure
30–90 seconds per area
mistakes: Rolling directly over joints or bones
Pressing so hard you tense up
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and stay relaxed. On a tender spot, pause and take a few long exhales to let the muscle release.
safety: Avoid rolling the lower back and neck with full body weight; use a softer tool there.

exercises.name: Frog Jumps
exercises.description: Jumping forward from a deep, wide squat and landing back in the same squat.
setup: Stand with feet wide, toes turned out.
Squat down and touch the floor between your feet.
steps: Jump forward explosively.
Land softly back into the deep squat.
Repeat.
cues: Land soft and deep
exercises.breathing: Breathe in before the jump, breathe out sharply as you take off or land.
safety: Land softly with knees bent and in line with the toes.
Stop the set when jumps become slow or landings get sloppy.

exercises.name: Frankenstein Squat
exercises.description: Frankenstein Squat is an intermediate-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the abs & core, calves, glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the front squat: arms straight out in front with the bar balanced on the shoulders, to teach an upright torso.
setup: This drill teaches you the proper positioning of both the bar and your body during the clean and front squat.
steps: Place the barbell on the front of the shoulders, releasing your grip and extending your arms out in front of you. The shoulders should be pushed forward to create a shelf, and the bar should be in contact with the throat. Ensure that you only move your shoulder blades forward; don't round the thoracic spine.

Squat by flexing the knees and hips, sitting in between your legs. Keep the torso upright, the arms up, and the shoulders forward, and the bar should stay in place. Go to the bottom of the squat, until your hamstrings contact your calves.
Return to the upright position by driving through the front of the heel and extending the knees and hips.
cues: Elbows up the whole time
Torso tall
Knees forward and out
mistakes: Elbows dropping so the bar rolls forward
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace before you descend. Hold it through the bottom, and breathe out as you pass the hardest part on the way up (or at the top).
safety: If you lose the bar forward, push it away and step back.
variation_notes: Arms straight out in front with the bar balanced on the shoulders, to teach an upright torso.

exercises.name: Front Barbell Squat To A Bench
exercises.description: Front Barbell Squat To A Bench is an advanced-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the front squat: front squat until you lightly touch a bench.
setup: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set a flat bench behind you and set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, bring your arms up under the bar while keeping the elbows high and the upper arm slightly above parallel to the floor. Rest the bar on top of the deltoids and cross your arms while grasping the bar for total control.
steps: Lift the bar off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times as looking down will get you off balance and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position. (Note: For the purposes of this discussion we will use the medium stance described above which targets overall development; however you can choose any of the three stances described in the foot positioning section).

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until you touch the bench with your glutes. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: If you performed the exercise correctly, the front of the knees should make an imaginary straight line with the toes that is perpendicular to the front. If your knees are past that imaginary line (if they are past your toes) then you are placing undue stress on the knee and the exercise has been performed incorrectly.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor mainly with the heel of your foot as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Elbows up the whole time
Torso tall
Knees forward and out
mistakes: Elbows dropping so the bar rolls forward
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace before you descend. Hold it through the bottom, and breathe out as you pass the hardest part on the way up (or at the top).
safety: If you lose the bar forward, push it away and step back.
variation_notes: Front squat until you lightly touch a bench.

exercises.name: Front Squat
exercises.description: A squat with the bar held on the front of the shoulders. It keeps the torso more upright and works the quads and upper back harder.
setup: Set the bar in a rack at upper-chest height.
Step under it so it rests on the front of your shoulders, close to your throat.
Hold it with fingertips under the bar and elbows high (or arms crossed).
steps: Brace and squat straight down, keeping the elbows high.
Go as deep as you can with an upright torso.
Drive up, leading with the elbows.
cues: Elbows up the whole time
Torso tall
Knees forward and out
mistakes: Elbows dropping so the bar rolls forward
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace before you descend. Hold it through the bottom, and breathe out as you pass the hardest part on the way up (or at the top).
safety: If you lose the bar forward, push it away and step back.

exercises.name: Front Squats With Two Kettlebells
exercises.description: Front Squats With Two Kettlebells is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves and glutes. A variation of the front squat: two kettlebells held in the rack position.
setup: Clean two kettlebells to your shoulders. Clean the kettlebells to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebells towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrists as you do so.
steps: Looking straight ahead at all times, squat as low as you can and pause at the bottom. As you squat down, push your knees out. You should squat between your legs, keeping an upright torso, with your head and chest up.
Rise back up by driving through your heels and repeat.
cues: Elbows up the whole time
Torso tall
Knees forward and out
mistakes: Elbows dropping so the kettlebells pull you forward
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace before you descend. Hold it through the bottom, and breathe out as you pass the hardest part on the way up (or at the top).
variation_notes: Two kettlebells held in the rack position.

exercises.name: Sit Squats
exercises.description: Sit Squats is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the abductors, glutes and hamstrings.
setup: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.
steps: Begin the movement by flexing your knees and hips, sitting back with your hips.
Continue until you have squatted a portion of the way down, but are above parallel, and quickly reverse the motion until you return to the starting position. Repeat for 5-10 repetitions.
cues: Keep the hips square and the lower back flat on the floor where lying
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Twisting the pelvis to fake the range
Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.description: A squat holding one weight against your chest. The front load makes good squat form easy to learn.
setup: Hold one dumbbell vertically by the top end (or a kettlebell by the horns) against your chest.
Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out.
steps: Squat down between your heels, elbows travelling inside your knees.
Go as deep as you can with a neutral back.
Stand up tall.
cues: Weight stays against your chest
Elbows push the knees out at the bottom
mistakes: Letting the weight drift away from the body
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace before you descend. Hold it through the bottom, and breathe out as you pass the hardest part on the way up (or at the top).

exercises.name: Kettlebell Goblet Squat
exercises.description: A squat holding one weight against your chest. The front load makes good squat form easy to learn.
setup: Hold a kettlebell by the horns (the sides of the handle) against your chest.
Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out.
steps: Squat down between your heels, elbows travelling inside your knees.
Go as deep as you can with a neutral back.
Stand up tall.
cues: Weight stays against your chest

mistakes: Letting the weight drift away from the body
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace before you descend. Hold it through the bottom, and breathe out as you pass the hardest part on the way up (or at the top).

exercises.name: Hack Squat
exercises.description: A barbell lift where you stand up holding the bar behind your legs. It works the quads hard with an upright torso.
setup: Stand in front of a barbell on the floor and grip it behind your legs.
steps: Stand up holding the bar behind your thighs, like a deadlift behind the body.
Lower it back down by bending at the knees.
cues: Back stays against the pad
Knees track over the toes
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back up.
safety: Re-engage the safety handles before stepping out.
variation_notes: The barbell version holds the bar behind your legs; it is quite different from the machine.

exercises.name: Hack Squat (Machine)
exercises.description: A squat on an angled sled machine with your back against a pad. It lets you train the quads hard with little stress on the back.
setup: Stand on the platform with your back and shoulders against the pads.
Feet shoulder-width, in the middle of the platform.
steps: Release the safety handles.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the platform.
Push back up through the whole foot.
cues: Back stays against the pad
Knees track over the toes
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back up.
safety: Re-engage the safety handles before stepping out.

exercises.name: Lying Machine Squat
exercises.description: Lying Machine Squat is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the hack squat: a lying squat machine, back on the pad.
setup: Adjust the leg machine to a height that will allow you to get inside it with your knees bent and the thighs slightly below parallel.
steps: Once you select the weight, position yourself inside the machine face up with the knees bent and thighs slightly below parallel to the platform. Make sure that the knees do not go past the toes. The angle created between the hamstrings and the calves should be one that is slightly less than 90 degrees (since your starting position requires you to start slightly below parallel). Your back and your head should be resting on the machine while your shoulders are pressed under the shoulder pads.
Place your hands by the handles and position your feet slightly pointing out at a shoulder width position. This will be your starting position.

While pressing with the balls of the feet as you breathe out, make your whole body erect as you squeeze the quads. Hold the contracted position for a second. Tip: Since you are starting below parallel, you can opt to use your hands to help you up by pressing on your thighs only on the first repetition.

Slowly squat down as you inhale but instead of going all the way down to the starting position, just stop once your thighs are parallel to the platform. The angle between your hamstrings and calves should be a 90-degree angle.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Back stays against the pad
Knees track over the toes
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back up.
safety: Re-engage the safety handles before stepping out.
variation_notes: A lying squat machine, back on the pad.

exercises.name: Narrow Stance Hack Squats
exercises.description: Narrow Stance Hack Squats is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the hack squat: feet close together, more quads.
setup: Place the back of your torso against the back pad of the machine and hook your shoulders under the shoulder pads provided.
steps: Position your legs in the platform using a less than shoulder width narrow stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Your feet should be around 3 inches or less apart. Tip: Keep your head up at all times and also maintain the back on the pad at all times.
Place your arms on the side handles of the machine and disengage the safety bars (which on most designs is done by moving the side handles from a facing front position to a diagonal position).
Now straighten your legs without locking the knees. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the unit by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up (back on the pad at all times). Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calves becomes slightly less than 90-degrees (which is the point in which the upper legs are below parallel to the floor). Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Begin to raise the unit as you exhale by pushing the floor with mainly with the heels of your feet as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Back stays against the pad
Knees track over the toes
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back up.
safety: Re-engage the safety handles before stepping out.
variation_notes: Feet close together, more quads.

exercises.name: Fast Skipping
exercises.description: Fast Skipping is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the abductors, adductors, calves, glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the high knees: quick, low skips.
setup: Start in a relaxed position with one leg slightly forward. This will be your starting position.
steps: Skip by executing a step-hop pattern of right-right-step to left-left-step, and so on, alternating back and forth.
Perform fast skips by maintaining close contact with the ground and reduce air time, moving as quickly as possible.
cues: Stay on the balls of the feet
Tall posture
exercises.breathing: Breathe rhythmically.
variation_notes: Quick, low skips.

exercises.name: Trail Running/Walking
exercises.description: Trail Running/Walking is a beginner-level cardio exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the cardio, calves, glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the hiking: on trails.
steps: Running or hiking on trails will get the blood pumping and heart beating almost immediately. Make sure you have good shoes. While you use the muscles in your calves and buttocks to pull yourself up a hill, the knees, joints and ankles absorb the bulk of the pounding coming back down. Take smaller steps as you walk downhill, keep your knees bent to reduce the impact and slow down to avoid falling.
A 150 lb person can burn over 200 calories for 30 minutes walking uphill, compared to 175 on a flat surface. If running the trail, a 150 lb person can burn well over 500 calories in 30 minutes.
cues: Short steps uphill
Soft knees downhill
exercises.breathing: Match your breathing to the effort. At an easy pace you should be able to talk in full sentences; at hard efforts breathe deeply and rhythmically through the mouth.
safety: Warm up for 5–10 minutes before hard efforts.
Build duration and intensity gradually from week to week.
variation_notes: On trails.

exercises.name: Hip Flexion with Band
exercises.description: Hip Flexion with Band is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps.
setup: Secure one end of the band to the lower portion of a post and attach the other to one ankle.
steps: Face away from the attachment point of the band.
Keeping your head and your chest up, raise your knee up to 90 degrees and pause.
Return the leg to the starting position.
cues: Stand tall facing away from the anchor
Drive the knee up to hip height
Lower slowly
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Bench Jump
exercises.description: Bench Jump is an intermediate-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes and hamstrings.
setup: Begin with a box or bench 1-2 feet in front of you. Stand with your feet shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.
steps: Perform a short squat in preparation for the jump; swing your arms behind you.
Rebound out of this position, extending through the hips, knees, and ankles to jump as high as possible. Swing your arms forward and up.
Jump over the bench, landing with the knees bent, absorbing the impact through the legs.
Turn around and face the opposite direction, then jump back over the bench.
cues: Land softly on the balls of the feet
Spend as little time on the ground as possible
Knees track over the toes
Arms drive each jump
mistakes: Landing on the heels or stiff-legged
Doing too many reps when tired
exercises.breathing: Take a quick breath before each effort and exhale sharply as you take off. Reset your breathing between reps.
safety: Use a forgiving surface and stop the set when landings get sloppy.

exercises.name: Front Cone Hops (or hurdle hops)
exercises.description: Front Cone Hops (or hurdle hops) is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the abductors, adductors, calves, glutes and hamstrings.
setup: Set up a row of cones or other small barriers, placing them a few feet apart.
steps: Stand in front of the first cone with your feet shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.
Begin by jumping with both feet over the first cone, swinging both arms as you jump.
Absorb the impact of landing by bending the knees, rebounding out of the first leap by jumping over the next cone.
Continue until you have jumped over all of the cones.
cues: Land softly on the balls of the feet
Spend as little time on the ground as possible
Knees track over the toes
Arms drive each jump
mistakes: Landing on the heels or stiff-legged
Doing too many reps when tired

setup: You will need a box for this exerise.
steps: Begin facing the box standing 1-2 feet from its edge.
By utilizing your hips, hop onto the box, landing on both legs. Ensure that you land with your legs bent and your feet flat.
Immediately upon landing, fully extend through the entire body and swing your arms overhead to explode off of the box. Use your legs to absorb the impact of landing.

setup: Stand to the side of a cone or hurdle.

Hop for a prescribed number or repetitions as quickly as possible, and finish this drill by sprinting a short distance upon landing the last hop.

steps: To begin, jump up and over to the other side of the box, landing with your right foot on top of the box and your left foot on the floor. Swing your arms to aid your movement.
Continue shuffling back and forth across the box.

setup: Stand to the side of a cone or hurdle. To get into the start position, stand on one leg with your knee slightly bent.
steps: To begin, execute a counterjump to hop sideways over the cone.

Continue hopping back and forth.

exercises.name: Jefferson Squats
exercises.description: Jefferson Squats is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes, hamstrings, lower back and traps.
setup: Place a barbell on the floor.
steps: Stand in the middle of the bar length wise.
Bend down by bending at the knees and keeping your back straight and grasp the front of the bar with your right hand. Your palm should be in (neutral grip) facing the left side.

Grasp the rear of the bar with your left hand. The palm of your hand should be in neutral grip alignment (palms facing the right side). Tip: Ensure that your grip is even on the bar. Your torso should be positioned right in the middle of the bar and the distance between your torso and your right hand (which should be at the front) should be the same as the distance between your torso and your left hand (which should be to your back).
Now stand straight up with the weight. Tip: Your feet should be shoulder width apart and your toes slightly pointed out.

Squat down by bending at the knees and keeping your back straight until your upper thighs are parallel with the floor. Tip: Keep your back as vertical as possible with the floor and your head up. Also remember to not let your knees go past your toes. Inhale during this portion of the movement.

Now drive yourself back up to the starting position by pushing with the feet . Tip: Keep the bar hanging at arm's length and your elbows locked with a slight bend. The arms only serve as hooks. Avoid doing any lifting with them. Do the lifting with your thighs; not your arms.
cues: Straddle the bar, one hand in front and one behind
Squat down with an upright torso
Alternate the leg in front each set
exercises.breathing: Inhale and brace at the top, keep the brace on the way down and through the bottom, and exhale as you finish standing.
safety: Uneven loading; start light.

exercises.name: Jump Squat
exercises.description: A bodyweight squat finished with an explosive jump.
setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
steps: Squat down to about parallel.
Jump as high as you can.
Land softly and go straight into the next squat.
cues: Soft landings
exercises.breathing: Breathe in before the jump, breathe out sharply as you take off or land.
safety: Land softly with knees bent and in line with the toes.
Stop the set when jumps become slow or landings get sloppy.

exercises.name: Weighted Jump Squat
exercises.description: Weighted Jump Squat is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes, hamstrings and lower back. A variation of the jump squat: light bar on the back.
setup: Position a lightly loaded barbell across the back of your shoulders. You could also use a weighted vest, sandbag, or other type of resistance for this exercise.
steps: The weight should be light enough that it doesn't slow you down significantly. Your feet should be just outside of shoulder width with your head and chest up. This will be your starting position.

Using a countermovement, squat partially down and immediately reverse your direction to explode off of the ground, extending through your hips, knees, and ankles. Maintain good posture throughout the jump.
As you return to the ground, absorb the impact through your legs.
cues: Soft landings
exercises.breathing: Breathe in before the jump, breathe out sharply as you take off or land.
safety: Land softly with knees bent and in line with the toes.
Stop the set when jumps become slow or landings get sloppy.
variation_notes: Light bar on the back.

exercises.name: Jumping Lunge
exercises.description: Jumping from one lunge position and switching legs in the air to land in the opposite lunge.
setup: Start in a lunge with one foot forward.
steps: Jump up explosively.
Switch legs in the air.
Land softly in a lunge with the other foot forward.
cues: Land softly and balanced

exercises.breathing: Breathe in before the jump, breathe out sharply as you take off or land.
safety: Land softly with knees bent and in line with the toes.

exercises.name: Scissors Jump
exercises.description: Scissors Jump is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the jumping lunge: switch legs in the air from a lunge.
setup: Assume a lunge stance position with one foot forward with the knee bent, and the rear knee nearly touching the ground.
steps: Ensure that the front knee is over the midline of the foot. Extending through both legs, jump as high as possible, swinging your arms to gain lift.
As you jump as high as you can, switch the position of your legs, moving your front leg to the back and the rear leg to the front.
As you land, absorb the impact through the legs by adopting the lunge position, and repeat.
cues: Land softly and balanced
mistakes: Front knee caving in on landing
exercises.breathing: Breathe in before the jump, breathe out sharply as you take off or land.
safety: Land softly with knees bent and in line with the toes.
Stop the set when jumps become slow or landings get sloppy.
variation_notes: Switch legs in the air from a lunge.

exercises.name: Double Leg Butt Kick
exercises.description: Double Leg Butt Kick is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the abductors, adductors, calves, glutes and hamstrings.
setup: Begin standing with your knees slightly bent.
steps: Quickly squat a short distance, flexing the hips and knees, and immediately extend to jump for maximum vertical height.
As you go up, tuck your heels by flexing the knees, attempting to touch the buttocks.
Finish the motion by landing with the knees only partially bent, using your legs to absorb the impact.

setup: Begin in a relaxed stance with your feet shoulder width apart and hold your arms close to the body.
steps: To initiate the move, squat down halfway and explode back up as high as possible.

exercises.name: Single Leg Butt Kick
exercises.description: Single Leg Butt Kick is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves and hamstrings.
setup: Begin by standing on one leg, with the bent knee raised. This will be your start position.
steps: Using a countermovement jump, take off upward by extending the hip, knee, and ankle of the grounded leg.
Immediately flex the knee and attempt to touch your butt with the heel of your jumping leg.
Return the leg to a partially bent position underneath the hips and land. Your opposite leg should stay in relatively the same position throughout the drill.

setup: Stand up straight while holding a barbell placed on the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck). Your feet should be placed wide apart with the foot of the lead leg angled out to the side. This will be your starting position.

exercises.description: Narrow Stance Leg Press is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the leg press: feet close together, more quads.
setup: Using a leg press machine, sit down on the machine and place your legs on the platform directly in front of you at a less-than-shoulder-width narrow stance with the toes slightly pointed out. steps: Lower the safety bars holding the weighted platform in place and press the platform all the way up until your legs are fully extended in front of you. Tip: Make sure that you do not lock your knees. Your torso and the legs should make a perfect 90-degree angle. This will be your starting position.
As you inhale, slowly lower the platform until your upper and lower legs make a 90-degree angle.
Pushing mainly with the heels of your feet and using the quadriceps go back to the starting position as you exhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and ensure to lock the safety pins properly once you are done. You do not want that platform falling on you fully loaded.

steps: Begin the movement by driving through your feet to move the bar upward, extending the hips and knees. Do not lock out your knees.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Pistol Squat
exercises.description: Smith Machine Pistol Squat is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the pistol squat: smith bar on the back for balance.
setup: To begin, first set the bar to a position that best matches your height. Step under it and position the bar across the back of your shoulders.
steps: Take the bar with your hands facing forward, unlock it and lift it off the rack by extending your legs. 3

Move one foot forward about 12 inches in front of the bar. Extend the other leg out in front of you, holding it off the ground. Look forward at all times and maintain a neutral or slightly arched spine. This will be your starting position.
Maintaining good posture, lower yourself by flexing the knee and hip, going down as far as flexibility allows.
Pause briefly at the bottom and then return to the starting position by driving through the heel of your foot, extending the knee and hip.
cues: Arms forward to counterbalance
Heel stays down
mistakes: Rounding the back to reach depth
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back up.
variation_notes: Smith bar on the back for balance.

exercises.name: All Fours Quad Stretch
exercises.description: All Fours Quad Stretch is an intermediate-level stretch that mainly targets the quadriceps.
setup: Start off on your hands and knees, then lift your leg off the floor and hold the foot with your hand.
steps: Use your hand to hold the foot or ankle, keeping the knee fully flexed, stretching the quadriceps and hip flexors.
Focus on extending your hips, thrusting them towards the floor. Hold for 10-20 seconds and then switch sides.
cues: Tuck the pelvis under and squeeze the glute on the stretching side
Keep the knees close together for the quad stretch
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Arching the lower back instead of tucking the pelvis
Pulling the knee out to the side
Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Looking At Ceiling
exercises.description: Looking At Ceiling is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the quadriceps.
steps: Kneel on the floor, holding your heels with both hands.
Lift your buttocks up and forward while bringing your head back to look up at the ceiling, to give an arch in your back.
cues: Tuck the pelvis under and squeeze the glute on the stretching side
Keep the knees close together for the quad stretch
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Arching the lower back instead of tucking the pelvis
Pulling the knee out to the side
Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Lying Prone Quadriceps
exercises.description: Lying Prone Quadriceps is an advanced-level stretch that mainly targets the quadriceps.
setup: Lay face down on the floor with your partner kneeling beside you. Flex one knee and raise that leg off the ground, attempting to touch your glutes with your foot. Your partner should hold the knee and ankle. This will be your starting position.
steps: Attempt to extend your knee while your partner prevents any actual movement.
After 10-20 seconds, relax your muscles as your partner gently pushes the foot towards your glutes, further stretching the quadriceps and hip flexors.
After 10-20 seconds, switch sides.
cues: Tuck the pelvis under and squeeze the glute on the stretching side
Keep the knees close together for the quad stretch
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed

exercises.name: On Your Side Quad Stretch
exercises.description: On Your Side Quad Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the quadriceps.
steps: Start off by lying on your right side, with your right knee bent at a 90-degree angle resting on the floor in front of you (this stabilizes the torso).
Bend your left knee behind you and hold your left foot with your left hand. To stretch your hip flexor, press your left hip forward as you push your left foot back into your hand. Switch sides.
cues: Tuck the pelvis under and squeeze the glute on the stretching side
Keep the knees close together for the quad stretch
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed

exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: On-Your-Back Quad Stretch
exercises.description: On-Your-Back Quad Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the quadriceps.
setup: Lie on a flat bench or step, and hang one leg and arm over the side.
steps: Bend the knee and hold the top of the foot. As you do this, be careful not to arch your lower back.
Pull the belly button to the spine to stay in neutral. Press your foot down and into your hand. To add the hip stretch, lift the hip of the leg you're holding up toward the ceiling.
Switch sides.
cues: Tuck the pelvis under and squeeze the glute on the stretching side
Keep the knees close together for the quad stretch
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed

exercises.name: One Half Locust
exercises.description: One Half Locust is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the abs & core, biceps and chest.
setup: Lie facedown on the floor.
steps: Put your left hand under your left hipbone to pad your hip and pubic bone.
Bend your right knee so you can hold the foot in your right hand.

Lift the foot in the air and simultaneously lift your shoulders off the floor. This also stretches the right hip flexor and the chest and shoulders. Switch sides. If it doesn't bother your back, you can try it with both arms and legs at the same time.
cues: Tuck the pelvis under and squeeze the glute on the stretching side
Keep the knees close together for the quad stretch
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed

exercises.name: Quad Stretch
exercises.description: Quad Stretch is an intermediate-level stretch that mainly targets the quadriceps.
steps: Lay on your side. Loop a belt, rope, or band around your top foot. Flex the knee and extend your hip, attempting to touch your glutes with your foot, and holding the belt with your hands. This will be your starting position.
With the belt being held over the shoulder or overhead, gently pull to increase the stretch in the quadriceps. Hold for 10-20 seconds, and then switch sides.
cues: Tuck the pelvis under and squeeze the glute on the stretching side
Keep the knees close together for the quad stretch
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
