exercises.name: Standing Elevated Quad Stretch
exercises.description: Standing Elevated Quad Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the quadriceps.
setup: Start by standing with your back about two to three feet away from a bench or step.
steps: Lift one leg behind you and rest your foot on the step,either on your instep or the ball of your foot, whichever you find most comfortable.
Keep your supporting knee slightly bent and avoid letting that knee extend out beyond your toes. Switch sides.
cues: Tuck the pelvis under and squeeze the glute on the stretching side
Keep the knees close together for the quad stretch
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Arching the lower back instead of tucking the pelvis
Pulling the knee out to the side

exercises.name: Elevated Back Lunge
exercises.description: Elevated Back Lunge is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the reverse lunge: standing on a platform for a deeper lunge.
setup: Position a bar onto a rack at shoulder height loaded to an appropriate weight. Place a short, raised platform behind you.
steps: Rack the bar onto your upper back, keeping your back arched and tight. Step onto your raised platform with both feet. This will be your starting position.
Begin by stepping backwards with one leg. Descend by flexing your hips and knees until your knee touches the floor.
Pause, and extend through the hips and knees to rise up, returning all the way to the starting position before alternating.
cues: Most weight on the front leg
Torso upright
mistakes: Stepping back too narrow (like a tightrope)
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back up.
variation_notes: Standing on a platform for a deeper lunge.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.description: Stepping backward into a lunge. Usually easier on the knees than a forward lunge.
setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
steps: Step one foot back and lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor.
Push through the front foot to stand back up.
Alternate legs.
cues: Most weight on the front leg
Torso upright
mistakes: Stepping back too narrow (like a tightrope)
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back up.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge (Barbell)
exercises.description: Stepping backward into a lunge. Usually easier on the knees than a forward lunge.
setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
steps: Step one foot back and lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor.
Push through the front foot to stand back up.
Alternate legs.
cues: Most weight on the front leg
Torso upright
mistakes: Stepping back too narrow (like a tightrope)
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back up.

exercises.name: Sissy Squat (Weighted)
exercises.description: Leaning back while bending the knees forward so the quads take nearly all the work.
setup: Stand holding something for balance (or use a sissy squat bench), weight held to the chest if loaded.
steps: Rise onto the balls of your feet and push your knees forward while leaning back, keeping hips straight.
Lower until your knees are well bent.
Return to standing using the quads.
cues: Straight line from knees to shoulders
Go only as low as you control
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back up.
safety: Very demanding on the knees; build up gradually.

exercises.name: Weighted Sissy Squat
exercises.description: Weighted Sissy Squat is an advanced-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the sissy squat: holding a plate at the chest.
setup: Standing upright, with feet at shoulder width and toes raised, use one hand to hold onto the beams of a squat rack and the opposite arm to hold a plate on top of your chest. This is your starting position.
steps: As you use one arm to hold yourself, bend at the knees and slowly lower your torso toward the ground by bringing your pelvis and knees forward. Inhale as you go down and stop when your upper and lower legs almost create a 90-degree angle. Hold the stretch position for a second.
After your one second hold, use your thigh muscles to bring your torso back up to the starting position. Exhale as you move up.
Repeat for the recommended amount of times.
cues: Straight line from knees to shoulders
Go only as low as you control
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back up.
safety: Very demanding on the knees; build up gradually.
variation_notes: Holding a plate at the chest.

exercises.name: Backward Drag
exercises.description: Backward Drag is a beginner-level strongman exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, forearms, glutes, hamstrings and lower back. A variation of the sled pull: walking backward, pulling the sled with straps or handles.
steps: Load a sled with the desired weight, attaching a rope or straps to the sled that you can hold onto.
Begin the exercise by moving backwards for a given distance. Leaning back, extend through the legs for short steps to move as quickly as possible.
cues: Stay low and drive through the legs
exercises.breathing: Breathe hard and rhythmically.
variation_notes: Walking backward, pulling the sled with straps or handles.

exercises.name: Bear Crawl Sled Drags
exercises.description: Bear Crawl Sled Drags is a beginner-level strongman exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the sled pull: crawling on hands and feet with the sled attached to a belt.
steps: Wearing either a harness or a loose weight belt, attach the chain to the back so that you will be facing away from the sled. Bend down so that your hands are on the ground. Your back should be flat and knees bent. This is your starting position.
Begin by driving with legs, alternating left and right. Use your hands to maintain balance and to help pull. Try to keep your back flat as you move over a given distance.
cues: Stay low and drive through the legs
exercises.breathing: Breathe hard and rhythmically.
variation_notes: Crawling on hands and feet with the sled attached to a belt.

exercises.name: Sled Drag - Harness
exercises.description: Sled Drag - Harness is a beginner-level strongman exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the sled pull: harness on the shoulders, walking or running forward.
steps: To begin, load the sled with the desired weight and attach the pulling strap. You can pull with handles, use a harness, or attach the pulling strap to a weight belt.
Whether pulling forwards or backwards, lean in the direction of travel and progress by extending through the hips and knees.
cues: Stay low and drive through the legs
exercises.breathing: Breathe hard and rhythmically.
variation_notes: Harness on the shoulders, walking or running forward.

exercises.name: Sled Pull
exercises.description: Dragging a weighted sled with a rope or harness, walking backward or forward.
setup: Attach a rope or harness to the sled.
Face the sled holding the rope (or face away wearing the harness).
steps: Walk backward hand over hand pulling the rope, or walk forward leaning into the harness.
Continue for the set distance.
cues: Stay low and drive through the legs
exercises.breathing: Breathe hard and rhythmically.

exercises.name: Sled Push
exercises.description: Pushing a weighted sled across the floor. Builds leg drive and conditioning with little stress on the joints.
setup: Grip the sled poles with arms extended or bent, body leaning forward at about 45°.
steps: Drive through the balls of your feet with short, powerful steps.
Keep pushing for the set distance.
cues: Low body angle
Drive the knees forward
exercises.breathing: Breathe hard and rhythmically; do not hold your breath for long pushes.

exercises.name: Power Snatch from Blocks
exercises.description: Power Snatch from Blocks is an intermediate-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, forearms, glutes, hamstrings, lower back, traps and triceps. A variation of the snatch: bar starts on blocks; caught above parallel.
setup: Begin with a loaded barbell on boxes or stands of the desired height. A wide grip should be taken on the bar. The feet should be directly below the hips, with the feet turned out as needed. Lower the hips, with the chest up and the head looking forward. The shoulders should be just in front of the bar, with the elbows pointed out. This will be the starting position.
steps: Begin the first pull by driving through the front of the heels, raising the bar from the boxes.

Transition into the second pull by extending through the hips knees and ankles, driving the bar up as quickly as possible. The bar should be close to the body. At peak extension, shrug the shoulders and allow the elbows to flex to the side.

As you move your feet into the receiving position, forcefully pull yourself below the bar as you elevate the bar overhead. The feet should move to just outside the hips, turned out as necessary. Receive the bar above a full squat and with the arms fully extended overhead.
Keeping the bar aligned over the front of the heels, your head and chest up, drive through heels of the feet to move to a standing position. Carefully return the weight to the boxes.
cues: Bar close to the body
Punch the arms up to lock out
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
safety: Olympic lifts are technical; learn them with a coach and an empty bar or PVC pipe first.
Use bumper plates and a platform so the bar can be dropped safely.
variation_notes: Bar starts on blocks; caught above parallel.

exercises.name: Snatch from Blocks
exercises.description: Snatch from Blocks is an advanced-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, forearms, glutes, hamstrings, lower back, traps and triceps. A variation of the snatch: bar starts on blocks.
setup: Begin with a loaded barbell on boxes or stands of the desired height. A wide grip should be taken on the bar. The feet should be directly below the hips, with the feet turned out as needed. Lower the hips, with the chest up and the head looking forward. The shoulders should be just in front of the bar, with the elbows pointed out. This will be the starting position.
steps: Begin the first pull by driving through the front of the heels, raising the bar from the boxes.

Transition into the second pull by extending through the hips knees and ankles, driving the bar up as quickly as possible. The bar should be close to the body. At peak extension, shrug the shoulders and allow the elbows to flex to the side.

As you move your feet into the receiving position, forcefully pull yourself below the bar as you elevate the bar overhead. The feet should move to just outside the hips, turned out as necessary. Receive the bar with your body as low as possible and the arms fully extended overhead.
Keeping the bar aligned over the front of the heels, your head and chest up, drive through heels of the feet to move to a standing position. Carefully return the weight to the boxes.
cues: Bar close to the body
Punch the arms up to lock out
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
safety: Olympic lifts are technical; learn them with a coach and an empty bar or PVC pipe first.
Use bumper plates and a platform so the bar can be dropped safely.
variation_notes: Bar starts on blocks.

exercises.name: Heaving Snatch Balance
exercises.description: Heaving Snatch Balance is an intermediate-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the abs & core, forearms, glutes, hamstrings and triceps.
setup: This drill helps you learn the snatch. Begin by holding a light weight across the back of the shoulders. Your feet should be slightly wider than hip width apart with the feet turned out, the same position that you would perform a squat with.
steps: Begin by dipping with the knees slightly, and popping back up to briefly unload the bar. Drive yourself underneath the bar, elevating it overhead as you descend into a full squat.
Return to a standing position.
cues: Bar on the back with a snatch grip
Drive yourself down under the bar, not the bar up
Catch in a full overhead squat with locked arms
exercises.breathing: Breathe in and brace before the dip; hold it through the catch and stand up.
safety: Use a rack and bumper plates; learn to bail forward or backward safely.

exercises.name: Snatch Balance
exercises.description: Snatch Balance is an intermediate-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes, hamstrings and triceps.
setup: Begin with the feet in the pulling position, the bar racked across the back of the shoulders, and the hands placed in a wide snatch grip.
steps: Pop the bar with an abrupt dip and drive of the knees, and aggressively drive under the bar, transitioning the feet into the receiving position.
Receive the bar locked out overhead near the bottom of the squat. The torso should remain vertical, lowering the hips between the legs.
Continue to descend to full depth, and return to a standing position. Carefully lower the weight.
cues: Bar on the back with a snatch grip
Drive yourself down under the bar, not the bar up
Catch in a full overhead squat with locked arms
exercises.breathing: Breathe in and brace before the dip; hold it through the catch and stand up.
safety: Use a rack and bumper plates; learn to bail forward or backward safely.

exercises.name: Jerk Dip Squat
exercises.description: Jerk Dip Squat is an intermediate-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the abs & core and calves. A variation of the split jerk: drill: the dip and drive only, bar in the front rack.
steps: This movement strengthens the dip portion of the jerk. Begin with the bar racked in the jerk position, with the shoulders forward to create a shelf and the bar lightly contacting the throat. The feet should be directly under the hips, with the feet turned out as is comfortable.

Keeping the torso vertical, dip by flexing the knees, allowing them to travel forward and without moving the hips to the rear. The dip should not be excessive. Return the weight to the starting position by driving forcefully though the feet.
cues: Vertical dip
Punch under the bar
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
safety: Olympic lifts are technical; learn them with a coach and an empty bar or PVC pipe first.
Use bumper plates and a platform so the bar can be dropped safely.
variation_notes: Drill: the dip and drive only, bar in the front rack.

exercises.name: Power Jerk
exercises.description: Power Jerk is an advanced-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the abs & core, calves, glutes, hamstrings and triceps. A variation of the split jerk: feet land in a quarter squat instead of a split.
setup: Standing with the weight racked on the front of the shoulders, begin with the dip. With your feet directly under your hips, flex the knees without moving the hips backward. Go down only slightly, and reverse direction as powerfully as possible.
steps: Drive through the heels create as much speed and force as possible, and be sure to move your head out of the way as the bar leaves the shoulders.

At this moment as the feet leave the floor, the feet must be placed into the receiving position as quickly as possible. In the brief moment the feet are not actively driving against the platform, the athletes effort to push the bar up will drive them down. The feet should be moved to a slightly wider stance, with the knees partially bent.
Receive the bar with the arms locked out overhead.
Return to a standing position.
cues: Vertical dip
Punch under the bar
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
safety: Olympic lifts are technical; learn them with a coach and an empty bar or PVC pipe first.
Use bumper plates and a platform so the bar can be dropped safely.
variation_notes: Feet land in a quarter squat instead of a split.

exercises.name: Squat Jerk
exercises.description: Squat Jerk is an advanced-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes, hamstrings and triceps. A variation of the split jerk: caught in a full overhead squat.
setup: Standing with the weight racked on the front of the shoulders, begin with the dip. With your feet directly under your hips, flex the knees without moving the hips backward. Go down only slightly, and reverse direction as powerfully as possible. Drive through the heels create as much speed and force as possible, and be sure to move your head out of the way as the bar leaves the shoulders.
steps: At this moment as the feet leave the floor, the feet must be placed into the receiving position as quickly as possible. In the brief moment the feet are not actively driving against the platform, the athlete's effort to push the bar up will drive them down. The feet should move forcefully to just outside the hips, turned out as necessary. Receive the bar with your body in a full squat and the arms fully extended overhead.
Keeping the bar aligned over the front of the heels, your head and chest up, drive throught heels of the feet to move to a standing position. Carefully return the weight to floor.
cues: Vertical dip
Punch under the bar
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
safety: Olympic lifts are technical; learn them with a coach and an empty bar or PVC pipe first.
Use bumper plates and a platform so the bar can be dropped safely.
variation_notes: Caught in a full overhead squat.

exercises.name: Lunge Sprint
exercises.description: Lunge Sprint is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the split squat: smith machine split squat, driving up as fast as possible.
setup: Adjust a bar in a Smith machine to an appropriate height. Position yourself under the bar, racking it across the back of your shoulders. Unrack the bar, and then split your feet, moving one foot forward and one foot back. This will be your starting position.
steps: Lower your back knee nearly to the ground, flexing the knees and lowering your hips as you do so.

At the bottom of the descent, immediately reverse direction. Explosively drive through the heel of your front foot with light pressure from your back foot. Jump up and reverse the position of your legs.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Straight down, straight up
Front heel stays planted
mistakes: Leaning forward over the front knee
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back up.
variation_notes: Smith machine split squat, driving up as fast as possible.

exercises.name: Smith Single-Leg Split Squat
exercises.description: Smith Single-Leg Split Squat is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the split squat: smith machine bar.
setup: To begin, place a flat bench 2-3 feet behind the smith machine. Then, set the bar on the height that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
steps: Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side (palms facing forward), unlock it and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.
Position your legs by placing one foot slightly forward under the bar and extending your other leg back and place the top of your foot on the bench. This will be your starting position

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knee as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calf becomes slightly less than 90-degrees (which is the point in which the upper legs are below parallel to the floor). Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: If you performed the exercise correctly, the front of the knee should make an imaginary straight line with the toes that is perpendicular to the front. If your knee is past that imaginary line (if it is past your toes) then you are placing undue stress on the knee and the exercise has been performed incorrectly.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot mainly as you straighten your leg again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Switch legs and repeat the movement.
cues: Straight down, straight up
Front heel stays planted
mistakes: Leaning forward over the front knee
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back up.
variation_notes: Smith machine bar.

exercises.name: Split Squat (Dumbbell)
exercises.description: A lunge without stepping: you stay in a split stance and lower straight down and up.
setup: Stand in a long split stance, holding dumbbells at your sides.
Back heel lifted.
steps: Lower straight down until the back knee nearly touches the floor.
Push up through the front foot.
Finish all reps, then switch legs.
cues: Straight down, straight up
Front heel stays planted
mistakes: Leaning forward over the front knee
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back up.

exercises.name: Bench Sprint
exercises.description: Bench Sprint is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes and hamstrings.
setup: Stand on the ground with one foot resting on a bench or box with your heel close to the edge.
steps: Push off with your foot on top of the bench, extending through the hip and knee.
Land with the opposite foot on top of the box, returning your other foot back to the start position.
Continue alternating from one foot to another to complete the set.
cues: Drive the knee up and the foot down under the hips
Arms swing from the shoulder, elbows about 90 degrees
Stay tall with a slight forward lean
mistakes: Reaching out with the foot in front of the body
Running the drill tired; quality comes first
exercises.breathing: Breathe rhythmically; recover fully between reps so every rep is fast.

exercises.name: Single-Cone Sprint Drill

setup: This drill teaches quick foot action. You need a single cone. Begin standing next to the cone with one arm back and one arm forward.
steps: Chop the feet as quickly as possible, blocking with the arms. Circle the cone, keep your knees up, with violent foot action.
Rest after three trips around the cone.

Arms swing from the shoulder, elbows about 90 degrees
Stay tall with a slight forward lean

exercises.name: Barbell Squat To A Bench
exercises.description: Barbell Squat To A Bench is an advanced-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes, hamstrings and lower back. A variation of the squat: squat until you lightly touch a bench, then stand.
setup: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first place a flat bench or a box behind you. The flat bench is used to teach you to set your hips back and to hit depth.
steps: Then, set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times as looking down will get you off balance and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position. (Note: For the purposes of this discussion we will use the medium stance described above which targets overall development; however you can choose any of the three stances discussed in the foot stances section).

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees and sitting your hips back as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until you slightly touch the bench behind you. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: If you performed the exercise correctly, the front of the knees should make an imaginary straight line with the toes that is perpendicular to the front. If your knees are past that imaginary line (if they are past your toes) then you are placing undue stress on the knee and the exercise has been performed incorrectly.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot as you straighten the legs and extend the hips to go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Chest up, back neutral
Whole foot on the floor, heels down
Stand up as fast as you can control
mistakes: Rounding the lower back at the bottom ("butt wink")
Hips rising faster than the chest
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace before you descend. Hold it through the bottom, and breathe out as you pass the hardest part on the way up (or at the top).

exercises.name: Box Squat (Barbell)

setup: Set the bar in a rack at about upper-chest height.
Step under it and rest it on your upper back (on the traps, not the neck), hands just outside your shoulders.
Stand up to lift it off, take two or three steps back, feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly.
steps: Brace your core, then break at the hips and knees at the same time.
Sit down between your heels, knees tracking in line with your toes.
Go down until your hips are at least level with your knees, or as deep as you can with a neutral back.

exercises.name: Box Squat with Bands
exercises.description: Box Squat with Bands is an advanced-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the abductors, adductors, calves, glutes, hamstrings and lower back. A variation of the squat: box squat with bands adding load near the top.
setup: Begin in a power rack with a box at the appropriate height behind you. Set up the bands on the sleeves, secured to either band pegs, the rack, or dumbbells so that there is appropriate tension. If dumbbells are used, secure them so that they don't move. Also, ensure that the dumbbells you are using are heavy enough for the bands that you are using. Additional plates can be used to hold the dumbbells down. If more tension is needed, you can either widen the base on the floor or choke the bands. Typically, you would aim for a box height that brings you to a parallel squat, but you can train higher or lower if desired.
steps: Begin by stepping under the bar and placing it across the back of the shoulders. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and rotate your elbows forward, attempting to bend the bar across your shoulders. Remove the bar from the rack, creating a tight arch in your lower back, and step back into position. Place your feet wider for more emphasis on the back, glutes, adductors, and hamstrings, or closer together for more quad development. Keep your head facing forward.

With your back, shoulders, and core tight, push your knees and butt out and you begin your descent. Sit back with your hips until you are seated on the box. Ideally, your shins should be perpendicular to the ground. Pause when you reach the box, and relax the hip flexors. Never bounce off of a box.

Keeping the weight on your heels and pushing your feet and knees out, drive upward off of the box as you lead the movement with your head. Continue upward, maintaining tightness head to toe. Use care to return the barbell to the rack.

exercises.name: Squat with Bands
exercises.description: Squat with Bands is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the adductors, calves, glutes, hamstrings and lower back. A variation of the squat: bands add load near the top.
setup: Set up the bands on the sleeves, secured to either band pegs, the rack, or dumbbells so that there is appropriate tension.
steps: Begin by stepping under the bar and placing it across the back of the shoulders. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and rotate your elbows forward, attempting to bend the bar across your shoulders. Remove the bar from the rack, creating a tight arch in your lower back, and step back into position. Place your feet wide for more emphasis on the back, glutes, adductors, and hamstrings. Keep your head facing forward.

With your back, shoulders, and core tight, push your knees and butt out and you begin your descent. Sit back with your hips as much as possible. Ideally, your shins should be perpendicular to the ground. Lower bar position necessitates a greater torso lean to keep the bar over the heels. Continue until you break parallel, which is defined as the crease of the hip being in line with the top of the knee.

Keeping the weight on your heels and pushing your feet and knees out, drive upward as you lead the movement with your head. Continue upward, maintaining tightness head to toe, until you have returned to the starting position.

Chest up, back neutral
Whole foot on the floor, heels down
Stand up as fast as you can control
mistakes: Rounding the lower back at the bottom ("butt wink")
Hips rising faster than the chest

setup: To set up the chains, begin by looping the leader chain over the sleeves of the bar. The heavy chain should be attached using a snap hook. Adjust the length of the lead chain so that a few links are still on the floor at the top of the movement.
steps: Begin by stepping under the bar and placing it across the back of the shoulders. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and rotate your elbows forward, attempting to bend the bar across your shoulders. Remove the bar from the rack, creating a tight arch in your lower back, and step back into position. Place your feet wide for more emphasis on the back, glutes, adductors, and hamstrings. Keep your head facing forward.

With your back, shoulders, and core tight, push your knees and butt out and you begin your descent. Sit back with your hips as much as possible. Ideally, your shins should be perpendicular to the ground. Lower bar position necessitates a greater torso lean to keep the bar over the heels. Continue until you break parallel, which is defined as the crease of the hip being in line with the top of the knee.

Keeping the weight on your heels and pushing your feet and knees out, drive upward as you lead the movement with your head. Continue upward, maintaining tightness head to toe, until you have returned to the starting position.

exercises.name: Squat with Plate Movers
exercises.description: Squat with Plate Movers is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the abductors, adductors, calves, glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the squat: a plate is moved with the feet between sets to build footwork.
setup: To begin, first set the bar on a rack to just below shoulder level. Position a weight plate on the ground a couple feet back from the rack. Once the bar is loaded, step under it and place the back of your shoulders across it.
steps: Hold on to the bar with both hands and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straighten your torso.
Step away from the rack and adopt a wide stance with the toes slightly pointed out, with one foot on the weight plate. Keep your head up at all times. This will be your starting position.
Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees and hips. Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calves becomes slightly less than 90-degrees.
Raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heels of your feet as you extend the hips and knees.
At the top of the movement, side step, bringing your feet together on the opposite side of the plate.
Using your inside foot, push the weight plate, sliding it across the floor to where you were just standing.
Place your inside foot on the weight plate, adopting a wide stance for the next repetition.

Chest up, back neutral

Stand up as fast as you can control
mistakes: Rounding the lower back at the bottom ("butt wink")

exercises.breathing: Take a big breath into your stomach and brace before you descend. Hold it through the bottom, and breathe out as you pass the hardest part on the way up (or at the top).

exercises.name: Wide Stance Barbell Squat
exercises.description: Wide Stance Barbell Squat is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes, hamstrings and lower back. A variation of the squat: feet wider, more hips and inner thighs.
setup: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
steps: Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a wider-than-shoulder-width stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times as looking down will get you off balance, and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calves becomes slightly less than 90-degrees (which is the point in which the upper legs are below parallel to the floor). Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: If you performed the exercise correctly, the front of the knees should make an imaginary straight line with the toes that is perpendicular to the front. If your knees are past that imaginary line (if they are past your toes) then you are placing undue stress on the knee and the exercise has been performed incorrectly.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Chest up, back neutral

Stand up as fast as you can control

exercises.name: Barbell Step Ups
exercises.description: Barbell Step Ups is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the step up: bar on the back.
setup: Stand up straight while holding a barbell placed on the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) and stand upright behind an elevated platform (such as the one used for spotting behind a flat bench). This is your starting position.

Step down with the left leg by flexing the hip and knee of the right leg as you inhale. Return to the original standing position by placing the right foot of to next to the left foot on the initial position.
Repeat with the right leg for the recommended amount of repetitions and then perform with the left leg.

exercises.name: Yoke Walk
exercises.description: Yoke Walk is an intermediate-level strongman exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the abs & core, abductors, adductors, calves, glutes, hamstrings and lower back.
setup: The yoke is usually done with a yoke apparatus, but is sometimes seen with refrigerators or other heavy objects.
steps: Begin by racking the apparatus across the back of the shoulders. With your head looking forward and back arched, lift the yoke by driving through the heels.

Begin walking as quickly as possible using short, quick steps. You may hold the side posts of the yoke to help steady it and hold it in position. Continue for the given distance as fast as possible, usually 75-100 feet.

Short, quick steps

exercises.name: Sandbag Load
exercises.description: Sandbag Load is a beginner-level strongman exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the abs & core, biceps, calves, forearms, glutes, hamstrings, lower back, upper back and traps.
setup: To load sandbags or other objects, begin with the implements placed a distance from the loading platform, typically 50 feet.
steps: Begin by lifting the sandbag. Sandbags are extremely awkward, and the manner of lifting them can vary depending on the particular sandbag used. Reach as far around it as possible, extending through the hips and knees to pull it up high. Shouldering is usually not allowed.
Move as quickly as possible to the platform, and load it, extending through your hips, knees, and ankles to get it as high as possible. Place it onto the platform, ensuring it doesn't fall off.
Return to the starting position to retrieve the next sandbag, and repeat until the event is completed.

safety: Some back rounding is normal on stones; build up gradually and use tacky or sleeves for grip.

exercises.name: Plie Dumbbell Squat

setup: Hold a dumbbell at the base with both hands and stand straight up. Move your legs so that they are wider than shoulder width apart from each other with your knees slightly bent.
steps: Your toes should be facing out. Note: Your arms should be stationary while performing the exercise. This is the starting position.
Slowly bend the knees and lower your legs until your thighs are parallel to the floor. Make sure to inhale as this is the eccentric part of the exercise.
Press mainly with the heel of the foot to bring the body back to the starting position while exhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

exercises.description: Tire Flip is an intermediate-level strongman exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the calves, chest, forearms, glutes, hamstrings, lower back, traps and triceps.
setup: Begin by gripping the bottom of the tire on the tread, and position your feet back a bit. Your chest should be driving into the tire.
steps: To lift the tire, extend through the hips, knees, and ankles, driving into the tire and up.

As the tire reaches a 45 degree angle, step forward and drive a knee into the tire. As you do so adjust your grip to the upper portion of the tire and push it forward as hard as possible to complete the turn. Repeat as necessary.

exercises.name: Walking, Treadmill
exercises.description: Walking, Treadmill is a beginner-level cardio exercise that mainly targets the quadriceps, with help from the cardio, calves, glutes and hamstrings. A variation of the treadmill: walking pace.
steps: To begin, step onto the treadmill and select the desired option from the menu. Most treadmills have a manual setting, or you can select a program to run. Typically, you can enter your age and weight to estimate the amount of calories burned during exercise. Elevation can be adjusted to change the intensity of the workout.

Treadmills offer convenience, cardiovascular benefits, and usually have less impact than walking outside. When walking, you should move at a moderate to fast pace, not a leisurely one. Being an activity of lower intensity, walking doesn't burn as many calories as some other activities, but still provides great benefit. A 150 lb person will burn about 175 calories walking 4 miles per hour for 30 minutes, compared to 450 calories running twice as fast. Maintain proper posture as you walk, and only hold onto the handles when necessary, such as when dismounting or checking your heart rate.

exercises.breathing: Match your breathing to the effort. At an easy pace you should be able to talk in full sentences; at hard efforts breathe deeply and rhythmically through the mouth.

Drive through the heel of your lead foot and extend both knees to raise yourself back up.

exercises.description: Anti-Gravity Press is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the upper back, traps and triceps.
setup: Place a bar on the ground behind the head of an incline bench.
steps: Lay on the bench face down. With a pronated grip, pick the barbell up from the floor. Flex the elbows, performing a reverse curl to bring the bar near your chest. This will be your starting position.
To begin, press the barbell out in front of your head by extending your elbows. Keep your arms parallel to the ground throughout the movement.
Return to the starting position and repeat to complete the set.
cues: Lie face down on an incline bench
Press the bar forward and slightly up with straight arms
Keep the chest on the pad
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Side Wrist Pull
exercises.description: Side Wrist Pull is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the forearms and lats.
steps: This stretch works best standing. Cross your left arm over the midline of your body and hold the left wrist in your right hand down at the level of your hips. Start the stretch with a bent left arm.
Slowly straighten, pull, and lift it up to shoulder height, as pictured. Feel this stretch originate in your back, not your shoulders, and don't pull too hard on the shoulders joint. Switch sides.
cues: Keep the shoulder relaxed and down
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Arnold Press (Dumbbell)
exercises.description: A dumbbell shoulder press that starts with palms facing you and rotates to palms forward as you press.
setup: Sit on an upright bench holding dumbbells in front of your shoulders, palms facing you, elbows in front.
steps: As you press up, open your elbows out to the sides and rotate the palms to face forward.
Finish with arms straight overhead.
Reverse the rotation as you lower back to the start.
cues: Smooth rotation through the whole press
Keep the ribs down
mistakes: Using weights too heavy to control the rotation
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you press and rotate, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Arnold Press
exercises.description: Kettlebell Arnold Press is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the triceps. A variation of the arnold press: kettlebells instead of dumbbells.
setup: Clean a kettlebell to your shoulder. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you raise the kettlebell towards your shoulder. The palm should be facing inward.
steps: Looking straight ahead, press the kettlebell out and overhead, rotating your wrist so that your palm faces forward at the top of the motion.
Return the kettlebell to the starting position, with the palm facing in.
cues: Smooth rotation through the whole press
Keep the ribs down
mistakes: Using weights too heavy to control the rotation
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you press and rotate, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Kettlebells instead of dumbbells.

exercises.name: Band Pullaparts
exercises.description: Pulling a band apart in front of your chest. A simple warm-up and shoulder-health exercise.
setup: Hold a light band in front of your chest with straight arms, hands shoulder-width apart.
steps: Pull the band apart until it touches your chest.
Return slowly to the start.
cues: Arms stay straight
Shoulders down
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.

exercises.name: Bear Crawl
exercises.description: Crawling on hands and feet with the knees hovering just above the floor.
setup: Start on hands and knees, then lift the knees a few centimetres.
steps: Move the opposite hand and foot forward together.
Keep crawling for the set distance.
cues: Back flat, hips low
Small steps
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily through the nose and mouth; do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Barbell Rear Delt Row
exercises.description: Barbell Rear Delt Row is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the biceps, lats and upper back. A variation of the bent over row: wide grip, bar to the upper chest, elbows out, for the rear delts.
setup: Stand up straight while holding a barbell using a wide (higher than shoulder width) and overhand (palms facing your body) grip.
steps: Bend knees slightly and bend over as you keep the natural arch of your back. Let the arms hang in front of you as they hold the bar. Once your torso is parallel to the floor, flare the elbows out and away from your body. Tip: Your torso and your arms should resemble the letter "T". Now you are ready to begin the exercise.

While keeping the upper arms perpendicular to the torso, pull the barbell up towards your upper chest as you squeeze the rear delts and you breathe out. Tip: When performed correctly, this exercise should resemble a bench press in reverse. Also, refrain from using your biceps to do the work. Focus on targeting the rear delts; the arms should only act as hooks.
Slowly go back to the initial position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Pull with the elbows, not the hands
Keep the back flat and the torso angle fixed
Chest proud
mistakes: Standing up as you pull, turning it into a shrug
exercises.breathing: Brace your core before each rep. Breathe out as you pull, breathe in as you lower the weight.
safety: If your lower back tires before your upper back, use a chest-supported row instead.
variation_notes: Wide grip, bar to the upper chest, elbows out, for the rear delts.

exercises.name: Car Drivers
exercises.description: Car Drivers is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the forearms.
setup: While standing upright, hold a barbell plate in both hands at the 3 and 9 o'clock positions. Your palms should be facing each other and your arms should be extended straight out in front of you. This will be your starting position.
steps: Initiate the movement by rotating the plate as far to one side as possible. Use the same type of movement you would use to turn a steering wheel to one side.
Reverse the motion, turning it all the way to the opposite side.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Hold a plate at arm's length in front at shoulder height
Turn it like a steering wheel
Arms stay straight and still
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Chair Upper Body Stretch
exercises.description: Chair Upper Body Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the biceps and chest.
steps: Sit on the edge of a chair, gripping the back of it.
Straighten your arms, keeping your back straight, and pull your upper body forward so you feel a stretch. Hold for 20-30 seconds.
cues: Keep the shoulders down away from the ears
Keep the ribs down; do not arch the back to fake the range
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Round The World Shoulder Stretch
exercises.description: Round The World Shoulder Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the biceps and chest.
setup: Stand up straight with your legs together, holding a bodybar or broomstick.
steps: Hold the pole behind your hips with a wider than shoulder width grip. Your palms should be down and your thumbs facing out.
Slowly lift your arms up behind your head. Don't force it if it gets hard to lift further.
cues: Keep the shoulders down away from the ears
Keep the ribs down; do not arch the back to fake the range
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Seated Front Deltoid
exercises.description: Seated Front Deltoid is an advanced-level stretch that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the chest.
setup: Sit upright on the floor with your legs bent, your partner standing behind you. Stick your arms straight out to your sides, with your palms facing the ground. Attempt to move them as far behind you as possible, as your assistant holds your wrists. This will be your starting position.
steps: Keeping your elbows straight, attempt to move your arms to the front, with your partner gently restraining you to prevent any actual movement for 10-20 seconds.
Now, relax your muscles and allow your partner to gently increase the stretch on the shoulders and chest. Hold for 10 to 20 seconds.
cues: Keep the shoulders down away from the ears
Keep the ribs down; do not arch the back to fake the range
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Shoulder Stretch
exercises.description: Shoulder Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the shoulders.
steps: Reach your left arm across your body and hold it straight.
cues: Keep the shoulders down away from the ears
Keep the ribs down; do not arch the back to fake the range
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed

exercises.name: Upward Stretch
exercises.description: Upward Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the chest and lats.
steps: Extend both hands straight above your head, palms touching.
Slowly push your hands up and back, keeping your back straight.
cues: Keep the shoulders down away from the ears
Keep the ribs down; do not arch the back to fake the range
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Crucifix
exercises.description: Crucifix is a beginner-level strongman exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the forearms.
steps: In the crucifix, you statically hold weights out to the side for time. While the event can be practiced using dumbbells, it is best to practice with one of the various implements used, such as axes and hammers, as it feels different.

Begin standing, and raise your arms out to the side holding the implements. Your arms should be parallel to the ground. In competition, judges or sensors are used to let you know when you break parallel. Hold for as long as you can. Typically, the weights should be heavy enough that you fail in 30-60 seconds.
cues: Arms straight out to the sides
Shoulders down, core braced
Hold for time
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Cuban Press
exercises.description: Cuban Press is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the traps.
setup: Take a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated grip in a standing position. Raise your upper arms so that they are parallel to the floor, allowing your lower arms to hang in the "scarecrow" position. This will be your starting position.
steps: To initiate the movement, externally rotate the shoulders to move the upper arm 180 degrees. Keep the upper arms in place, rotating the upper arms until the wrists are directly above the elbows, the forearms perpendicular to the floor.
Now press the dumbbells by extending at the elbows, straightening your arms overhead.
Return to the starting position as you breathe in by reversing the steps.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Upright row to elbows at shoulder height
Rotate the forearms up
Press overhead, then reverse the steps
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Arm Circles
exercises.description: Arm Circles is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the traps.
setup: Stand up and extend your arms straight out by the sides. The arms should be parallel to the floor and perpendicular (90-degree angle) to your torso. This will be your starting position.
steps: Slowly start to make circles of about 1 foot in diameter with each outstretched arm. Breathe normally as you perform the movement.
Continue the circular motion of the outstretched arms for about ten seconds. Then reverse the movement, going the opposite direction.
cues: Start small and slow, then grow the range
Smooth, controlled movement, no flinging
About 8–12 reps per side as a warm-up
mistakes: Swinging into end range with momentum
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Elbow Circles
exercises.description: Elbow Circles is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the traps.
setup: Sit or stand with your feet slightly apart.
steps: Place your hands on your shoulders with your elbows at shoulder level and pointing out.
Slowly make a circle with your elbows. Breathe out as you start the circle and breathe in as you complete the circle.
cues: Start small and slow, then grow the range
Smooth, controlled movement, no flinging
About 8–12 reps per side as a warm-up
mistakes: Swinging into end range with momentum
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Shoulder Circles
exercises.description: Shoulder Circles is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the traps.
steps: With shoulders relaxed and arms resting loosely at your sides (or in your lap if you're seated), gently roll your shoulders forward, up, back, and down.
Reverse direction. You can do this exercise alternating shoulders or both at the same time.
cues: Start small and slow, then grow the range
Smooth, controlled movement, no flinging
About 8–12 reps per side as a warm-up
mistakes: Swinging into end range with momentum
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Shoulder Raise
exercises.description: Shoulder Raise is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the lats.
steps: Relax your arms to your sides and raise your shoulders up toward your ears, then back down.
cues: Start small and slow, then grow the range
Smooth, controlled movement, no flinging
About 8–12 reps per side as a warm-up
mistakes: Swinging into end range with momentum
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily and rhythmically with the movement. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Cable Rope Rear-Delt Rows
exercises.description: Cable Rope Rear-Delt Rows is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the biceps and upper back. A variation of the face pull: seated, rope pulled to the neck with the elbows high.
setup: Sit in the same position on a low pulley row station as you would if you were doing seated cable rows for the back.
steps: Attach a rope to the pulley and grasp it with an overhand grip. Your arms should be extended and parallel to the floor with the elbows flared out.
Keep your lower back upright and slide your hips back so that your knees are slightly bent. This will be your starting position.

Pull the cable attachment towards your upper chest, just below the neck, as you keep your elbows up and out to the sides. Continue this motion as you exhale until the elbows travel slightly behind the back. Tip: Keep your upper arms horizontal, perpendicular to the torso and parallel to the floor throughout the motion.
Go back to the initial position where the arms are extended and the shoulders are stretched forward. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Elbows high and wide
Pull the ends apart
Finish like a "double biceps" pose
mistakes: Leaning back to pull heavy weight
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.
variation_notes: Seated, rope pulled to the neck with the elbows high.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.description: Pulling a rope toward your face with the elbows high. Trains the rear delts and rotator cuff and supports shoulder health.
setup: Set a pulley at upper-chest to face height with a rope attachment.
Grip the rope with palms facing each other or down and step back.
steps: Pull the rope toward your face, splitting the ends apart.
Finish with hands beside your ears and elbows high, rotating the forearms up.
Return slowly.
cues: Elbows high and wide
Pull the ends apart
Finish like a "double biceps" pose
mistakes: Leaning back to pull heavy weight
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.

exercises.name: Low Pulley Row To Neck
exercises.description: Low Pulley Row To Neck is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the biceps, upper back and traps. A variation of the face pull: seated at a low pulley, pulling to the neck with the elbows high.
setup: Sit on a low pulley row machine with a rope attachment.
steps: Grab the ends of the rope using a palms-down grip and sit with your back straight and your knees slightly bent. Tip: Keep your back almost completely vertical and your arms fully extended in front of you. This will be your starting position.

While keeping your torso stationary, lift your elbows and start bending them as you pull the rope towards your neck while exhaling. Throughout the movement your upper arms should remain parallel to the floor. Tip: Continue this motion until your hands are almost next to your ears (the forearms will not be parallel to the floor at the end of the movement as they will be angled a bit upwards) and your elbows are out away from your sides.
After holding for a second or so at the contracted position, come back slowly to the starting position as you inhale. Tip: Again, during no part of the movement should the torso move.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Elbows high and wide
Pull the ends apart
Finish like a "double biceps" pose
mistakes: Leaning back to pull heavy weight
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.
variation_notes: Seated at a low pulley, pulling to the neck with the elbows high.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Scaption
exercises.description: Dumbbell Scaption is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the traps. A variation of the front raise: raised at 30 degrees out from the front, thumbs up, in the shoulder blade plane.
setup: This corrective exercise strengthens the muscles that stabilize your shoulder blade. Hold a light weight in each hand, hanging at your sides. Your thumbs should pointing up.
steps: Begin the movement raising your arms out in front of you, about 30 degrees off center. Your arms should be fully extended as you perform the movement.
Continue until your arms are parallel to the ground, and then return to the starting position.
cues: Stop at shoulder height
Do not lean back
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.
variation_notes: Raised at 30 degrees out from the front, thumbs up, in the shoulder blade plane.

exercises.name: Front Incline Dumbbell Raise
exercises.description: Front Incline Dumbbell Raise is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders. A variation of the front raise: lying back on an incline bench, which starts the raise behind the body.
setup: Sit down on an incline bench with the incline set anywhere between 30 to 60 degrees while holding a dumbbell on each hand. Tip: You can change the angle to hit the muscle a little differently each time.
steps: Extend your arms straight in front of you and have your palms facing down with the dumbbells raised about 1 inch above your thighs. This will be your starting position.

Slowly raise the dumbbells straight up until they are slightly above your shoulders, while keeping your elbows locked. Squeeze at the top for a second and make sure you breathe out during this portion of the movement. Tip: Keep your head resting down against the bench and your legs on the floor at all times.
Lower the arms back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Stop at shoulder height
Do not lean back
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.
variation_notes: Lying back on an incline bench, which starts the raise behind the body.

exercises.name: Single Dumbbell Raise
exercises.description: Single Dumbbell Raise is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the forearms and traps. A variation of the front raise: one dumbbell held in both hands.
setup: With a wide stance, hold a dumbell with both hands, grasping the head of the dumbbell instead of the handle. Your arms should be extended and hanging at the waist. This will be your starting position.
steps: Raise the weight until it is above shoulder level, keeping your arms extended. Your torso and hips should remain stationary throughout the movement.
Return to the starting position and repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Stop at shoulder height
Do not lean back
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.
variation_notes: One dumbbell held in both hands.

exercises.name: Standing Dumbbell Straight-Arm Front Delt Raise Above Head
exercises.description: Standing Dumbbell Straight-Arm Front Delt Raise Above Head is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders. A variation of the front raise: raised all the way above the head.
setup: Hold the dumbbells in front of your thighs, palms facing your thighs.
steps: Keep your arms straight with a slight bend at the elbows but keep them locked. This will be your starting position.
Raise the dumbbells in a semicircular motion to arm's length overhead as you exhale.
Slowly return to the starting position using the same path as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Stop at shoulder height
Do not lean back
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.
variation_notes: Raised all the way above the head.

exercises.name: Standing Front Barbell Raise Over Head
exercises.description: Standing Front Barbell Raise Over Head is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders. A variation of the front raise: barbell raised all the way above the head.
setup: To begin, stand straight with a barbell in your hands. You should grip the bar with palms facing down and a closer than shoulder width grip apart from each other.
steps: Your feet should be shoulder width apart from each other. Your elbows should be slightly bent. This is the starting position.
Lift the barbell up until it is directly over your head while exhaling. Make sure to keep your elbows slightly bent when performing each repetition.
Once you feel the contraction, begin to lower the barbell back down to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Stop at shoulder height
Do not lean back
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.
