exercises.name: Handstand Hold
exercises.description: Holding a handstand, free-standing or against a wall, to build shoulder strength and balance.
setup: Warm up your wrists.
Place your hands shoulder-width apart on the floor, about a hand-length from a wall if using one.
steps: Kick up into a handstand.
Push the floor away and squeeze your legs together.
Hold for the target time, then come down with control.
cues: Push tall through the shoulders
Ribs in, body in one line
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and steadily; avoid holding your breath.
safety: Learn how to cartwheel or roll out safely before training free-standing.

exercises.name: Handstand Push Up
exercises.description: A vertical push up upside down, usually with your feet against a wall. It needs strong shoulders and good balance.
setup: Kick up into a handstand facing a wall, hands about shoulder-width and 10–20 cm from the wall.
Body straight, core tight.
steps: Lower your head slowly toward the floor until it lightly touches (use a pad).
Press back up to straight arms.
cues: Make a tripod: head slightly in front of the hands
Keep the core tight so the back does not arch
exercises.breathing: Breathe in on the way down, breathe out as you press up.
safety: Use a mat or folded towel under your head and learn to exit the handstand safely first.

exercises.name: Barbell Incline Shoulder Raise
exercises.description: Barbell Incline Shoulder Raise is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the chest.
setup: Lie back on an Incline Bench. Using a medium width grip (a grip that is slightly wider than shoulder width), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms straight. This will be your starting position.
steps: While keeping the arms straight, lift the bar by protracting your shoulder blades, raising the shoulders from the bench as you breathe out.
Bring back the bar to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Arms stay straight the whole time
Push the weight up by spreading the shoulder blades
Small, controlled range
exercises.breathing: Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Incline Shoulder Raise
exercises.description: Dumbbell Incline Shoulder Raise is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the triceps.
setup: Sit on an Incline Bench while holding a dumbbell on each hand on top of your thighs.
steps: Lift your legs up to kick the weights to your shoulders and lean back. Position the dumbbells above your shoulders with your arms extended. The arms should be perpendicular to the floor with your palms facing forward and knuckles pointing towards the ceiling. This will be your starting position.
While keeping the arms straight and locked, lift the dumbbells by raising the shoulders from the bench as you breathe out.
Bring back the dumbbells to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Arms stay straight the whole time
Push the weight up by spreading the shoulder blades
Small, controlled range
exercises.breathing: Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.

exercises.name: Smith Incline Shoulder Raise
exercises.description: Smith Incline Shoulder Raise is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the chest.
setup: Place an incline bench underneath the smith machine. Place the barbell at a height that you can reach when lying down and your arms are almost fully extended. Once the weight you need is selected, lie down on the incline bench and make sure your shoulders are aligned right under the barbell.
steps: Using a shoulder width pronated (palms forward) grip, lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with a slight bend at the elbows. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe out, lift the bar up until your arms are fully extended. Note: The contraction should be felt around the shoulders.
After a second pause, bring the bar back down to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the bar back in the rack.
cues: Arms stay straight the whole time
Push the weight up by spreading the shoulder blades
Small, controlled range
exercises.breathing: Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.

exercises.name: Iron Cross
exercises.description: Iron Cross is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the chest, glutes, hamstrings, lower back, quadriceps and traps.
setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a light dumbbell in each hand with arms straight out in front at shoulder height.
steps: Keeping the arms straight out in front, sit down into a squat until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Drive back up to standing and, as you rise, sweep the arms out to the sides until they form a T at shoulder height.
Bring the arms back to the front and repeat, keeping the elbows soft and the shoulders down.
cues: Arms stay straight at shoulder height
Squat with the dumbbells out in front
Stand and open the arms to the sides
mistakes: Rounding the back in the squat
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Two-Arm Kettlebell Clean
exercises.description: Two-Arm Kettlebell Clean is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the calves, glutes, hamstrings, lower back and traps. A variation of the kettlebell clean: one kettlebell held by both hands.
setup: Place two kettlebells between your feet. To get in the starting position, push your butt back and look straight ahead.
steps: Clean the kettlebells to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you raise the kettlebells towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrists as you do so.
Lower the kettlebells back to the starting position and repeat.
cues: Keep the bell close; zip up the jacket
Do not let it flip onto the forearm
mistakes: Swinging it wide and letting it bang the wrist
exercises.breathing: Breathe out sharply as the hips snap.
variation_notes: One kettlebell held by both hands.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Halo
exercises.description: Circling a kettlebell around your head. Warms up the shoulders and improves their range of motion.
setup: Stand tall holding a kettlebell upside down by the horns at chest height.
steps: Circle the kettlebell around your head, keeping it close.
Return to the front and reverse the direction.
cues: Keep it close to your head and neck
Ribs down; do not arch
mistakes: Moving the head instead of the bell
Using a bell that is too heavy
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily throughout.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Halo with Overhead Extension
exercises.description: Kettlebell Halo with Overhead Extension is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders and triceps, with help from the traps, upper back and abs & core. A variation of the kettlebell halo: adds a press overhead after each circle.
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart. Hold a kettlebell upside down by the horns, with the bell above your hands and close to your chest. Brace your abdominals and squeeze your glutes so your ribcage stays down. This is your starting position.
steps: Keeping your elbows close to your head, move the kettlebell up past one ear and around until it sits behind your head. Pause here.
From this position, extend your elbows to press the kettlebell up and overhead until your arms are straight, keeping your upper arms alongside your head.
Bend your elbows to lower the kettlebell back to the pause position behind your head, under control.
Continue the circle past the opposite ear and back down to the starting position in front of your chest to complete one repetition.

Alternate the direction of the circle on each repetition. Keep your head, hips and lower back still throughout; if your lower back arches or you cannot reach the overhead position without leaning back, use a lighter weight or perform the halo and the extension as separate exercises.
cues: Keep it close to your head and neck
Ribs down; do not arch
mistakes: Moving the head instead of the bell
Using a bell that is too heavy
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily throughout.
variation_notes: Adds a press overhead after each circle.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Jerk
exercises.description: Double Kettlebell Jerk is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the calves, quadriceps and triceps.
setup: Hold a kettlebell by the handle in each hand.
steps: Clean the kettlebells to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebells towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrists as you do so, so that the palms face forward. This will be your starting position.
Dip your body by bending the knees, keeping your torso upright.
Immediately reverse direction, driving through the heels, in essence jumping to create momentum.
As you do so, press the kettlebells overhead to lockout by extending the arms, using your body's momentum to move the weights.
Return your feet to the ground in a split fashion, with one foot forward and one foot back.
Keeping the weights overhead, return to a standing position, bringing your feet together. Lower the weights to perform the next repetition.
cues: Short, quick dip with the torso upright
Drive the bell up with the legs, then drop under it
Lock the arm out before standing up
mistakes: Pressing with the shoulder instead of using the legs
exercises.breathing: Exhale on the drive, inhale in the lockout, exhale as the bell drops back to the rack.

exercises.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Clean and Jerk
exercises.description: One-Arm Kettlebell Clean and Jerk is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders.
setup: Hold a kettlebell by the handle.
steps: Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulder. Rotate your wrist as you do so, so that the palm faces forward.
Dip your body by bending the knees, keeping your torso upright.

Immediately reverse direction, driving through the heels, in essence jumping to create momentum. As you do so, press the kettlebell overhead to lockout by extending the arms, using your body's momentum to move the weight.
Receive the weight overhead by returning to a squat position underneath the weight.
Keeping the weight overhead, return to a standing position. Lower the weight to the floor to perform the next repetition.
cues: Short, quick dip with the torso upright
Drive the bell up with the legs, then drop under it
Lock the arm out before standing up
mistakes: Pressing with the shoulder instead of using the legs
exercises.breathing: Exhale on the drive, inhale in the lockout, exhale as the bell drops back to the rack.

exercises.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Jerk
exercises.description: One-Arm Kettlebell Jerk is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the calves, quadriceps and triceps.
setup: Hold a kettlebell by the handle. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulder. Rotate your wrist as you do so, so that the palm faces forward. This will be your starting position.
steps: Dip your body by bending the knees, keeping your torso upright.

Immediately reverse direction, driving through the heels, in essence jumping to create momentum. As you do so, press the kettlebell overhead to lockout by extending the arms, using your body's momentum to move the weight. Receive the weight overhead by returning to a squat position underneath the weight. Keeping the weight overhead, return to a standing position.
Lower the weight to perform the next repetition.
cues: Short, quick dip with the torso upright
Drive the bell up with the legs, then drop under it
Lock the arm out before standing up
mistakes: Pressing with the shoulder instead of using the legs
exercises.breathing: Exhale on the drive, inhale in the lockout, exhale as the bell drops back to the rack.

exercises.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Split Jerk
exercises.description: One-Arm Kettlebell Split Jerk is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the glutes, hamstrings, quadriceps and triceps.
setup: Hold a kettlebell by the handle. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulder. Rotate your wrist as you do so, so that the palm faces forward. This will be your starting position.
steps: Dip your body by bending the knees, keeping your torso upright.

Immediately reverse direction, driving through the heels, in essence jumping to create momentum. As you do so, press the kettlebell overhead to lockout by extending the arms, using your body's momentum to move the weight.
Receive the weight overhead by returning to a squat position underneath the weight, positioning one leg in front of you and one leg behind you.
Keeping the weight overhead, return to a standing position and bring your feet together. Lower the weight to perform the next repetition.
cues: Short, quick dip with the torso upright
Drive the bell up with the legs, then drop under it
Lock the arm out before standing up
mistakes: Pressing with the shoulder instead of using the legs
exercises.breathing: Exhale on the drive, inhale in the lockout, exhale as the bell drops back to the rack.

exercises.name: Two-Arm Kettlebell Jerk
exercises.description: Two-Arm Kettlebell Jerk is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the calves, quadriceps and triceps.
steps: Clean two kettlebells to your shoulders. Clean the kettlebells to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you swing the kettlebells towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrists as you do so, so that the palms face forward. Squat down a few inches and reverse the motion rapidly driving both kettlebells overhead. Immediately after the initial push, squat down again and get under the kettlebells. Once the kettlebells are locked out, stand upright to complete the exercise.
cues: Short, quick dip with the torso upright
Drive the bell up with the legs, then drop under it
Lock the arm out before standing up
mistakes: Pressing with the shoulder instead of using the legs
exercises.breathing: Exhale on the drive, inhale in the lockout, exhale as the bell drops back to the rack.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Pirate Ships
exercises.description: Kettlebell Pirate Ships is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the abs & core.
setup: With a wide stance, hold a kettlebell with both hands. Allow it to hang at waist level with your arms extended. This will be your starting position.
steps: Initiate the movement by turning to one side, swinging the kettlebell to head height. Briefly pause at the top of the motion.
Allow the bell to drop as you rotate to the opposite side, again raising the kettlebell to head height.
Repeat for the desired amount of repetitions.
cues: Kettlebell held by the horns at arm's length
Swing it side to side in an arc overhead
Hips and legs stay still
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Snatch
exercises.description: Double Kettlebell Snatch is an advanced-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the glutes, hamstrings and quadriceps. A variation of the kettlebell snatch: two kettlebells.
setup: Place two kettlebells behind your feet. Bend your knees and sit back to pick up the kettlebells.
steps: Swing the kettlebells between your legs forcefully and reverse the direction.
Drive through with your hips and lock the ketttlebells overhead in one uninterrupted motion.
cues: Punch through so the bell does not crash on the forearm
exercises.breathing: Breathe out sharply as the hips drive.
safety: Learn the swing and clean first.
variation_notes: Two kettlebells.

exercises.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Split Snatch
exercises.description: One-Arm Kettlebell Split Snatch is an advanced-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the hamstrings and quadriceps. A variation of the kettlebell snatch: caught in a split stance.
setup: Hold a kettlebell in one hand by the handle.
steps: Squat towards the floor, and then reverse the motion, extending the hips, knees, and finally the ankles, to raise the kettlebell overhead.

After fully extending the body, descend into a lunge position to receive the weights overhead, one leg forward and one leg back. Ensure you drive through with your hips and lock the ketttlebells overhead in one uninterrupted motion.
Return to a standing position, holding the weight overhead, and bring the feet together. Lower the weight to return to the starting position.
cues: Punch through so the bell does not crash on the forearm
exercises.breathing: Breathe out sharply as the hips drive.
safety: Learn the swing and clean first.
variation_notes: Caught in a split stance.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Turkish Get Up
exercises.description: Getting up from lying to standing while holding a kettlebell straight overhead, then reversing the steps.
setup: Lie on your back holding the kettlebell straight above your shoulder.
Bend the same-side knee with the foot flat.
steps: Roll to the opposite elbow, then hand.
Lift the hips into a bridge and sweep the straight leg back under you to a kneel.
Stand up from the lunge.
Reverse every step back to lying.
cues: Eyes on the bell
Arm stays vertical and locked
exercises.breathing: Breathe steadily; take a breath at each position.
safety: Learn it with a shoe balanced on your fist before using a kettlebell.

exercises.name: Alternating Deltoid Raise
exercises.description: Alternating Deltoid Raise is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders. A variation of the lateral raise: one arm raises to the front while the other raises to the side, then swap.
setup: In a standing position, hold a pair of dumbbells at your side.
steps: Keeping your elbows slightly bent, raise the weights directly in front of you to shoulder height, avoiding any swinging or cheating.
Return the weights to your side.
On the next repetition, raise the weights laterally, raising them out to your side to about shoulder height.
Return the weights to the starting position and continue alternating to the front and side.
cues: Think "push the weight out", not up
Shoulders stay down, away from the ears
Slow on the way down
mistakes: Swinging the body to lift the weight
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.
variation_notes: One arm raises to the front while the other raises to the side, then swap.

exercises.name: Cable Seated Lateral Raise
exercises.description: Cable Seated Lateral Raise is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the upper back and traps. A variation of the lateral raise: seated beside a low pulley.
setup: Stand in the middle of two low pulleys that are opposite to each other and place a flat bench right behind you (in perpendicular fashion to you; the narrow edge of the bench should be the one behind you). Select the weight to be used on each pulley.
steps: Now sit at the edge of the flat bench behind you with your feet placed in front of your knees.
Bend forward while keeping your back flat and rest your torso on the thighs.

Have someone give you the single handles attached to the pulleys. Grasp the left pulley with the right hand and the right pulley with the left after you select your weight. The pulleys should run under your knees and your arms will be extended with palms facing each other and a slight bend at the elbows. This will be the starting position.

While keeping the arms stationary, raise the upper arms to the sides until they are parallel to the floor and at shoulder height. Exhale during the execution of this movement and hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly lower your arms to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions. Tip: Maintain upper arms perpendicular to torso and a fixed elbow position (10 degree to 30 degree angle) throughout exercise.
cues: Think "push the weight out", not up
Shoulders stay down, away from the ears
Slow on the way down
mistakes: Swinging the body to lift the weight
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.
variation_notes: Seated beside a low pulley.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Raise
exercises.description: Dumbbell Raise is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the biceps. A variation of the lateral raise: starts with the dumbbells beside the thighs and palms facing back.
setup: Grab a dumbbell in each arm and stand up straight with your arms extended by your sides with a slight bend at the elbows and your back straight. This will be your starting position. Tip: The dumbbell should be next to your thighs with the palm of your hands facing back.
steps: Use your side shoulders to lift the dumbbells as you exhale. The dumbbells should be to the side of the body as you move them up. Continue to lift it until the dumbbells are nearly in line with your chin. Tip: Your elbows should drive the motion. As you lift the dumbbell, your elbow should always be higher than your forearm. Also, keep your torso stationary and pause for a second at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells back down slowly to the starting position. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Think "push the weight out", not up
Shoulders stay down, away from the ears
Slow on the way down
mistakes: Swinging the body to lift the weight
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.
variation_notes: Starts with the dumbbells beside the thighs and palms facing back.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise (Band)
exercises.description: Raising the arms out to the sides to shoulder height. The key exercise for wider-looking shoulders.
setup: Stand on the middle of the band and hold an end in each hand.
steps: Raise your arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Lead with the elbows, keeping the hands slightly lower than or level with the elbows.
Lower slowly back to your sides.
cues: Think "push the weight out", not up
Shoulders stay down, away from the ears
Slow on the way down
mistakes: Swinging the body to lift the weight
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise (Cable)
exercises.description: Raising the arms out to the sides to shoulder height. The key exercise for wider-looking shoulders.
setup: Set a pulley at the lowest position with a single handle.
Stand side-on and hold the handle with the far hand.
steps: Raise your arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Lead with the elbows, keeping the hands slightly lower than or level with the elbows.
Lower slowly back to your sides.
cues: Think "push the weight out", not up
Shoulders stay down, away from the ears
Slow on the way down
mistakes: Swinging the body to lift the weight
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.
variation_notes: The cable keeps tension at the bottom where dumbbells feel light.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise (Dumbbell)
exercises.description: Raising the arms out to the sides to shoulder height. The key exercise for wider-looking shoulders.
setup: Stand tall with the weights at your sides, palms facing in.
Bend the elbows slightly and lean forward a little.
steps: Raise your arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Lead with the elbows, keeping the hands slightly lower than or level with the elbows.
Lower slowly back to your sides.
cues: Think "push the weight out", not up
Shoulders stay down, away from the ears
Slow on the way down
mistakes: Swinging the body to lift the weight
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise (Machine)
exercises.description: Raising the arms out to the sides to shoulder height. The key exercise for wider-looking shoulders.
setup: Adjust the seat so your shoulders line up with the machine pivot.
Place your arms against the pads.
steps: Raise your arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Lead with the elbows, keeping the hands slightly lower than or level with the elbows.
Lower slowly back to your sides.
cues: Think "push the weight out", not up
Shoulders stay down, away from the ears
Slow on the way down
mistakes: Swinging the body to lift the weight
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.
variation_notes: The machine guides the arc so you can focus on the side delts.

exercises.name: Lying One-Arm Lateral Raise
exercises.description: Lying One-Arm Lateral Raise is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders. A variation of the lateral raise: lying on your side on a bench; tension is highest at the bottom.
setup: While holding a dumbbell in one hand, lay with your chest down on a flat bench. The other hand can be used to hold to the leg of the bench for stability.
steps: Position the palm of the hand that is holding the dumbbell in a neutral manner (palms facing your torso) as you keep the arm extended with the elbow slightly bent. This will be your starting position.

Now raise the arm with the dumbbell to the side until your elbow is at shoulder height and your arm is roughly parallel to the floor as you exhale. Tip: Maintain your arm perpendicular to the torso while keeping your arm extended throughout the movement. Also, keep the contraction at the top for a second.
Slowly lower the dumbbell to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Think "push the weight out", not up
Shoulders stay down, away from the ears
Slow on the way down
mistakes: Swinging the body to lift the weight
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.
variation_notes: Lying on your side on a bench; tension is highest at the bottom.

exercises.name: One-Arm Incline Lateral Raise
exercises.description: One-Arm Incline Lateral Raise is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders. A variation of the lateral raise: lying sideways on an incline bench.
setup: Lie down sideways on an incline bench press with a dumbbell in the hand. Make sure the shoulder is pressing against the incline bench and the arm is lying across your body with the palm around your navel.
steps: Hold a dumbbell in your uppermost arm while keeping it extended in front of you parallel to the floor. This is your starting position.

While keeping the dumbbell parallel to the floor at all times, perform a lateral raise. Your arm should travel straight up until it is pointing at the ceiling. Tip: Exhale as you perform this movement. Hold the dumbbell in the position and feel the contraction in the shoulders for a second.
While inhaling lower the weight across your body back into the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
Switch arms and repeat the movement.
cues: Think "push the weight out", not up
Shoulders stay down, away from the ears
Slow on the way down
mistakes: Swinging the body to lift the weight
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.
variation_notes: Lying sideways on an incline bench.

exercises.name: One-Arm Side Laterals
exercises.description: One-Arm Side Laterals is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders. A variation of the lateral raise: one arm at a time, holding a support with the other.
setup: Pick a dumbbell and place it in one of your hands. Your non lifting hand should be used to grab something steady such as an incline bench press. Lean towards your lifting arm and away from the hand that is gripping the incline bench as this will allow you to keep your balance.
steps: Stand with a straight torso and have the dumbbell by your side at arm's length with the palm of the hand facing you. This will be your starting position.

While maintaining the torso stationary (no swinging), lift the dumbbell to your side with a slight bend on the elbow and your hand slightly tilted forward as if pouring water in a glass. Continue to go up until you arm is parallel to the floor. Exhale as you execute this movement and pause for a second at the top.
Lower the dumbbell back down slowly to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Switch arms and repeat the exercise.
cues: Think "push the weight out", not up
Shoulders stay down, away from the ears
Slow on the way down
mistakes: Swinging the body to lift the weight
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.
variation_notes: One arm at a time, holding a support with the other.

exercises.name: Power Partials
exercises.description: Power Partials is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders. A variation of the lateral raise: short, fast lateral raises from the bottom of the range.
setup: Stand up with your torso upright and a dumbbell on each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso.
steps: The palms of the hands should be facing your torso. Your feet should be about shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your arms straight and the torso stationary, lift the weights out to your sides until they are about shoulder level height while exhaling.

Feel the contraction for a second and begin to lower the weights back down to the starting position while inhaling. Tip: Keep the palms facing down with the little finger slightly higher while lifting and lowering the weights as it will concentrate the stress on your shoulders mainly.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Think "push the weight out", not up
Shoulders stay down, away from the ears
Slow on the way down
mistakes: Swinging the body to lift the weight
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.
variation_notes: Short, fast lateral raises from the bottom of the range.

exercises.name: Seated Lateral Raise (Dumbbell)
exercises.description: Raising the arms out to the sides to shoulder height. The key exercise for wider-looking shoulders.
setup: Stand tall with the weights at your sides, palms facing in.
Bend the elbows slightly and lean forward a little.
steps: Raise your arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Lead with the elbows, keeping the hands slightly lower than or level with the elbows.
Lower slowly back to your sides.

Shoulders stay down, away from the ears

exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.

exercises.name: Side Laterals to Front Raise
exercises.description: Side Laterals to Front Raise is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the traps. A variation of the lateral raise: raise to the side, bring the arms to the front at shoulder height, then lower.
setup: In a standing position, hold a pair of dumbbells at your side. This will be your starting position.
steps: Keeping your elbows slightly bent, raise the weights directly in front of you to shoulder height, avoiding any swinging or cheating.
At the top of the exercise move the weights out in front of you, keeping your arms extended.
Lower the weights with a controlled motion.
On the next repetition, raise the weights in front of you to shoulder height before moving the weights laterally to your sides.
Lower the weights to the starting position.

Shoulders stay down, away from the ears
Slow on the way down
mistakes: Swinging the body to lift the weight
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.
variation_notes: Raise to the side, bring the arms to the front at shoulder height, then lower.

exercises.name: Single Arm Lateral Raise (Cable)
exercises.description: Raising the arms out to the sides to shoulder height. The key exercise for wider-looking shoulders.
setup: Stand tall with the weights at your sides, palms facing in.
Bend the elbows slightly and lean forward a little.
steps: Raise your arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Lead with the elbows, keeping the hands slightly lower than or level with the elbows.
Lower slowly back to your sides.

Shoulders stay down, away from the ears

exercises.name: Backward Medicine Ball Throw
exercises.description: Backward Medicine Ball Throw is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the shoulders.
setup: This exercise is best done with a partner. If you lack a partner, the ball can be thrown and retrieved or thrown against a wall.
steps: Begin standing a few meters in front of your partner, both facing the same direction. Begin holding the ball between your legs.
Squat down and then forcefully reverse direction, coming to full extension and you toss the ball over your head to your partner.
Your partner can then roll the ball back to you. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
cues: Use the legs and hips first, the arms last
Throw as hard as you can; every rep is maximal
Use a light ball (2–5 kg) you can move fast
Reset fully between throws
mistakes: Using a ball too heavy to move quickly
Rounding the back when picking up or catching
exercises.breathing: Inhale as you load, exhale forcefully as you release the ball.
safety: Throw against a solid wall or into open space, never toward people.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Scoop Throw
exercises.description: Medicine Ball Scoop Throw is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the abs & core, hamstrings and quadriceps.
setup: Assume a semisquat stance with a medicine ball in your hands. Your arms should hang so the ball is near your feet.
steps: Begin by thrusting the hips forward as you extend through the legs, jumping up.
As you do, swing your arms up and over your head, keeping them extended, releasing the ball at the peak of your movement. The goal is to throw the ball the greatest distance behind you.
cues: Use the legs and hips first, the arms last
Throw as hard as you can; every rep is maximal
Use a light ball (2–5 kg) you can move fast
Reset fully between throws
mistakes: Using a ball too heavy to move quickly
Rounding the back when picking up or catching
exercises.breathing: Inhale as you load, exhale forcefully as you release the ball.

exercises.name: Return Push from Stance
exercises.description: Return Push from Stance is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the chest and triceps.
setup: You will need a partner for this drill.
steps: Begin in an athletic 2 or 3 point stance.
At the signal, move into a position to receive the pass from your partner.
Catch the medicine ball with both hands and immediately throw it back to your partner.
You can modify this drill by running different routes.
cues: Use the legs and hips first, the arms last
Throw as hard as you can; every rep is maximal
Use a light ball (2–5 kg) you can move fast
Reset fully between throws
mistakes: Using a ball too heavy to move quickly
Rounding the back when picking up or catching
exercises.breathing: Inhale as you load, exhale forcefully as you release the ball.
safety: Throw against a solid wall or into open space, never toward people.

setup: Grab a dumbbell with each hand and stand up erect.

exercises.name: Standing Military Press (Barbell)
exercises.description: Pressing a weight from your shoulders to straight arms overhead. The main strength exercise for the shoulders.
setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart and the weight at shoulder height.
Grip just outside shoulder width with wrists straight and elbows slightly in front of the bar.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your stomach so your ribs stay down.
steps: Press the weight straight up, moving your head back slightly to let it pass.
Once it passes your forehead, bring your head forward under the weight.
Finish with arms straight and the weight directly above your shoulders.
Lower under control back to your shoulders.

Push your head through at the top

exercises.name: Standing Palm-In One-Arm Dumbbell Press
exercises.description: Standing Palm-In One-Arm Dumbbell Press is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the triceps. A variation of the overhead press: one dumbbell, palm facing in.
setup: Start by having a dumbbell in one hand with your arm fully extended to the side using a neutral grip. Use your other arm to hold on to an incline bench to keep your balance.
steps: Your feet should be shoulder width apart from each other. Now slowly lift the dumbbell up until you create a 90 degree angle with your arm. Note: Your forearm should be perpendicular to the floor. Continue to maintain a neutral grip throughout the entire exercise.
Slowly lift the dumbbell up until your arm is fully extended. This the starting position.
While inhaling lower the weight down until your arm is at a 90 degree angle again.

Feel the contraction for a second and then lift the weight back up towards the starting position while exhaling. Remember to hold on to the incline bench and keep your feet positioned to keep balance during the exercise.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Switch arms and repeat the exercise.

Finish with the weight stacked over your shoulders

exercises.name: Pike Pushup

Stand up.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Push Press
exercises.description: Double Kettlebell Push Press is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the calves, quadriceps and triceps. A variation of the push press: two kettlebells from the rack position.
setup: Clean two kettlebells to your shoulders.
steps: Squat down a few inches and reverse the motion rapidly. Use the momentum from the legs to drive the kettlebells overhead.
Once the kettlebells are locked out, lower the kettlebells to your shoulders and repeat.
cues: Short, straight-down dip
Legs then arms, in one smooth motion
mistakes: Dipping too deep or letting the knees go forward
Pressing before the legs finish driving
exercises.breathing: Breathe in and brace before the dip, hold through the drive, breathe out at lockout.

exercises.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Push Press
exercises.description: One-Arm Kettlebell Push Press is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the calves, quadriceps and triceps. A variation of the push press: one kettlebell from the rack position.
setup: Hold a kettlebell by the handle. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulder. Rotate your wrist as you do so, so that the palm faces forward. This will be your starting position.
steps: Dip your body by bending the knees, keeping your torso upright.

Immediately reverse direction, driving through the heels, in essence jumping to create momentum. As you do so, press the kettlebell overhead to lockout by extending the arms, using your body's momentum to move the weight. Lower the weight to perform the next repetition.

exercises.name: Push Press
exercises.description: An overhead press driven by a short, explosive dip and drive of the legs. It lets you move more weight than a strict press.
setup: Stand with the bar in the front rack, resting on your shoulders, grip just outside shoulder width.
Feet hip-width apart, core braced.
steps: Dip a short distance by bending the knees, keeping the torso upright.
Drive up hard through the legs and use that momentum to press the bar overhead.
Lock out with arms straight and the bar over mid-foot.
Lower the bar back to your shoulders, absorbing it with the legs.
cues: Short, straight-down dip
Legs then arms, in one smooth motion
mistakes: Dipping too deep or letting the knees go forward
Pressing before the legs finish driving
exercises.breathing: Breathe in and brace before the dip, hold through the drive, breathe out at lockout.

exercises.name: Push Press - Behind the Neck
exercises.description: Push Press - Behind the Neck is an intermediate-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the calves, quadriceps and triceps. A variation of the push press: bar starts behind the head. Needs good shoulder mobility.
setup: Standing with the weight racked on the back of the shoulders, begin with the dip. With your feet directly under your hips, flex the knees without moving the hips backward. Go down only slightly, and reverse direction as powerfully as possible. Drive through the heels create as much speed and force as possible, moving the bar in a vertical path.
steps: Using the momentum generated, finish pressing the weight overhead be extending through the arms.
Return to the starting position, using your legs to absorb the impact.

Legs then arms, in one smooth motion

exercises.name: Back Flyes - With Bands
exercises.description: Back Flyes - With Bands is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the upper back and triceps. A variation of the rear delt reverse fly: pulling a band apart in front of the chest.
setup: Run a band around a stationary post like that of a squat rack.
steps: Grab the band by the handles and stand back so that the tension in the band rises.

Extend and lift the arms straight in front of you. Tip: Your arms should be straight and parallel to the floor while perpendicular to your torso. Your feet should be firmly planted on the floor spread at shoulder width. This will be your starting position.
As you exhale, move your arms to the sides and back. Keep your arms extended and parallel to the floor. Continue the movement until the arms are extended to your sides.
After a pause, go back to the original position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Lead with the back of the hands/elbows
Do not squeeze the shoulder blades hard; let the rear delts do it
mistakes: Turning it into a row by bending the elbows
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.
variation_notes: Pulling a band apart in front of the chest.

exercises.name: Bent Over Dumbbell Rear Delt Raise With Head On Bench
aliases: Rear Delt Reverse Fly (Head on Bench)
exercises.description: Bent Over Dumbbell Rear Delt Raise With Head On Bench is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders. A variation of the rear delt reverse fly: forehead rests on an incline bench to stop the body helping.
setup: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell in each hand and with an incline bench in front of you.
steps: While keeping your back straight and maintaining the natural arch of your back, lean forward until your forehead touches the bench in front of you. Let the arms hang in front of you perpendicular to the ground. The palms of your hands should be facing each other and your torso should be parallel to the floor. This will be your starting position.

Keeping your torso forward and stationary, and the arms straight with a slight bend at the elbows, lift the dumbbells straight to the side until both arms are parallel to the floor. Exhale as you lift the weights. Caution: avoid swinging the torso or bringing the arms back as opposed to the side.
After a one second contraction at the top, slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.

exercises.name: Reverse Flyes With External Rotation

exercises.description: Reverse Flyes With External Rotation is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders. A variation of the rear delt reverse fly: rotate the forearms up at the top to also work the rotator cuff.
setup: To begin, lie down on an incline bench set at a 30-degree angle with the chest and stomach pressing against the incline.
steps: Have the dumbbells in each hand with the palms facing down to the floor. Your arms should be in front of you so that they are perpendicular to the angle of the bench. Tip: Your elbows should have a slight bend. The legs should be stationary while applying pressure with the ball of your toes (your heels should not be touching the floor). This is the starting position.
Maintaining the slight bend of the elbows, move the weights out and away from each other in an arc motion while exhaling.

As you lift the weight, your wrist should externally rotate by 90-degrees so that you go from a palms down (pronated) grip to a palms facing each other (neutral) grip. Tip: Try to squeeze your shoulder blades together to get the best results from this exercise.
The arms should be elevated until they are level with the head.
Feel the contraction and slowly lower the weights back down to the starting position while inhaling.

exercises.name: Sled Reverse Flye
exercises.description: Sled Reverse Flye is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders. A variation of the rear delt reverse fly: walking backward pulling sled straps apart.
setup: Attach dual handles to a sled connected by a rope or chain. Load the sled to a light weight.
steps: Face the sled, backing up until there is some tension in the line. Take both handles at arms length at about waist level. Bend the knees slightly and keep your chest and head up. This will be your starting position.
Without flexing the elbow, pull the handles upward and apart, performing a reverse fly with some external rotation. Your palms should be facing forward as you do this.
Return to the starting position, taking a couple steps back to take the slack out of the line.

exercises.name: External Rotation
exercises.description: External Rotation is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders.
setup: Lie sideways on a flat bench with one arm holding a dumbbell and the other hand on top of the bench folded so that you can rest your head on it.
steps: Bend the elbows of the arm holding the dumbbell so that it creates a 90-degree angle between the upper arm and the forearm. Tip: Keep the arm parallel to your torso.

Now bend the elbow while keeping the upper arm stationary. In this manner, the forearm will be parallel to the floor and perpendicular to your torso (Tip: So the forearm will be directly in front of you). The upper arm will be stationary by your torso and should be parallel to the floor (aligned with your torso at all times). This will be your starting position.

As you breathe out, externally rotate your forearm so that the dumbbell is lifted up in a semicircle motion as you maintain the 90 degree angle bend between the upper arms and the forearm. You will continue this external rotation until the forearm is perpendicular to the floor and the torso pointing towards the ceiling. At this point you will hold the contraction for a second.
As you breathe in, slowly go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then switch to the other arm.
cues: Elbow pinned to the side at 90 degrees (a rolled towel helps)
Rotate the forearm out, keeping the wrist straight
Light weight and slow, controlled reps
mistakes: Elbow drifting away from the body
Using too much weight and twisting the torso
exercises.breathing: Exhale as you rotate out, inhale as you return.

exercises.name: External Rotation with Band
exercises.description: External Rotation with Band is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders.
setup: Choke the band around a post. The band should be at the same height as your elbow. Stand with your left side to the band a couple of feet away.
steps: Grasp the end of the band with your right hand, and keep your elbow pressed firmly to your side. We recommend you hold a pad or foam roll in place with your elbow to keep it firmly in position.
With your upper arm in position, your elbow should be flexed to 90 degrees with your hand reaching across the front of your torso. This will be your starting position.
Execute the movement by rotating your arm in a backhand motion, keeping your elbow in place.
Continue as far as you are able, pause, and then return to the starting position.

cues: Elbow pinned to the side at 90 degrees
Rotate the forearm in across the stomach
Light, slow and controlled

Twisting the torso instead of the shoulder

setup: Adjust the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height.
Sit with your back against the pad and feet flat.
steps: Press the handles up until your arms are almost straight.
Lower slowly until your hands are at shoulder height.
cues: Back stays against the pad
Do not shrug at the top
mistakes: Seat too low so the start is too deep
Arching away from the back pad

exercises.name: Landmine Linear Jammer
exercises.description: Landmine Linear Jammer is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the abs & core, calves, chest, hamstrings, quadriceps and triceps. A variation of the single arm landmine press: both hands, driven explosively from a quarter squat.
setup: Position a bar into landmine or, lacking one, securely anchor it in a corner. Load the bar to an appropriate weight and position the handle attachment on the bar.
steps: Raise the bar from the floor, taking the handles to your shoulders. This will be your starting position.
In an athletic stance, squat by flexing your hips and setting your hips back, keeping your arms flexed.

Reverse the motion by powerfully extending through the hips, knees, and ankles, while also extending the elbows to straighten the arms. This movement should be done explosively, coming out of the squat to full extension as powerfully as possible.
Return to the starting position.
cues: Ribs down, do not lean back
Reach at the top
mistakes: Leaning away from the working arm
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you press, breathe in as you lower.
variation_notes: Both hands, driven explosively from a quarter squat.

exercises.name: Single Arm Landmine Press (Barbell)
exercises.description: Pressing the end of a landmine bar up and forward with one arm. A shoulder-friendly alternative to overhead pressing.
setup: Stand or kneel facing the end of a landmine bar.
Hold the bar end in one hand at shoulder height, elbow tucked.
steps: Press the bar up and forward until your arm is straight.
Let your shoulder blade reach forward at the top.
Lower under control back to your shoulder.
cues: Ribs down, do not lean back
Reach at the top
mistakes: Leaning away from the working arm
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you press, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Sled Overhead Backward Walk
exercises.description: Sled Overhead Backward Walk is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the calves, upper back and quadriceps. A variation of the sled pull: straps held overhead, walking backward.
setup: Attach dual handles to a sled connected by a rope or chain. Load the sled to a light weight.
steps: Face the sled, backing up until there is some tension in the line. Hold your hands directly above your head with your elbows extended. This will be your starting position.
Walk backwards, keeping your arms raised above your head. Avoid jerky movements.
cues: Stay low and drive through the legs
exercises.breathing: Breathe hard and rhythmically.
variation_notes: Straps held overhead, walking backward.

exercises.name: Jerk Balance
exercises.description: Jerk Balance is an intermediate-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the glutes, hamstrings, quadriceps and triceps. A variation of the split jerk: drill: step into the split while pressing under the bar.
setup: This drill helps you learn to drive yourself low enough during the jerk and corrects those who move backward during the movement. Begin with the bar racked in the jerk position, with the shoulders forward, torso upright, and the feet split slightly apart.
steps: Initiate the movement as you would a normal jerk, dipping at the knees while keeping your torso vertical, and driving back up forcefully, using momentum and not your arms to elevate the weight.
Keep the rear foot in place, using it to drive your body forward into a full split as you jerk the weight. Recover by standing up with the weight overhead.
cues: Vertical dip
Punch under the bar
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
safety: Olympic lifts are technical; learn them with a coach and an empty bar or PVC pipe first.
Use bumper plates and a platform so the bar can be dropped safely.
variation_notes: Drill: step into the split while pressing under the bar.

exercises.name: Rack Delivery
exercises.description: Rack Delivery is an intermediate-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the forearms and traps. A variation of the split jerk: drill: practise catching the bar in the front rack.
setup: This drill teaches the delivery of the barbell to the rack position on the shoulders. Begin holding a bar in the scarecrow position, with the upper arms parallel to the floor, and the forearms hanging down. Use a hook grip, with your fingers wrapped over your thumbs.
steps: Begin by rotating the elbows around the bar, delivering the bar to the shoulders. As your elbows come forward, relax your grip. The shoulders should be protracted, providing a shelf for the bar, which should lightly contact the throat.

It is important that the bar stay close to the body at all times, as with a heavier load any distance will result in an unwanted collision. As the movement becomes smoother, speed and load can be increased before progressing further.
cues: Vertical dip
Punch under the bar
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.
safety: Olympic lifts are technical; learn them with a coach and an empty bar or PVC pipe first.
Use bumper plates and a platform so the bar can be dropped safely.
variation_notes: Drill: practise catching the bar in the front rack.

exercises.name: Split Jerk
exercises.description: Driving the bar up from the shoulders with the legs and dropping under it into a split stance with locked arms.
setup: Hold the bar in the front rack, feet hip-width.
steps: Dip a short distance straight down.
Drive up explosively and push yourself under the bar.
Land in a split stance with arms locked overhead.
Step the front foot back, then the back foot forward to finish.

Punch under the bar
exercises.breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift starts, hold it through the pull and catch, and breathe out once the bar is secure.

exercises.name: Kneeling Arm Drill
exercises.description: Kneeling Arm Drill is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the abs & core.
setup: This drill helps increase arm efficiency during the run. Begin kneeling, left foot in front, right knee down. Apply pressure through the front heel to keep your glutes and hamstrings activated.
steps: Begin by blocking the arms in long, pendulum like swings. Close the arm angle, blocking with the arms as you would when jogging, progressing to a run and finally a sprint.
As soon as your hands pass the hip, accelerate them forward during the sprinting motion to move them as quickly as possible.
Switch knees and repeat.
cues: Drive the knee up and the foot down under the hips
Arms swing from the shoulder, elbows about 90 degrees
Stay tall with a slight forward lean
mistakes: Reaching out with the foot in front of the body
Running the drill tired; quality comes first
exercises.breathing: Breathe rhythmically; recover fully between reps so every rep is fast.

exercises.name: Circus Bell
exercises.description: Circus Bell is an advanced-level strongman exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the forearms, glutes, hamstrings, lower back, traps and triceps.
setup: The circus bell is an oversized dumbbell with a thick handle. Begin with the dumbbell between your feet, and grip the handle with both hands.
steps: Clean the dumbbell by extending through your hips and knees to deliver the implement to the desired shoulder, letting go with the extra hand.

Ensure that you get one of the dumbbell heads behind the shoulder to keep from being thrown off balance. To raise it overhead, dip by flexing the knees, and the drive upwards as you extend the dumbbell overhead, leaning slightly away from it as you do so.
Carefully guide the bell back to the floor, keeping it under control as much as possible. It is best to perform this event on a thick rubber mat to prevent damage to the floor.
cues: Clean the implement to the chest or shoulder first
Dip and drive with the legs, then press
Lock out with the implement over the mid-foot
mistakes: Losing the brace during the clean
exercises.breathing: Big breath and brace before the clean; re-breathe at the shoulder, then brace again for the press.
safety: Learn with an empty log or light bell, ideally with a coach.

exercises.name: Log Lift
exercises.description: Log Lift is an intermediate-level strongman exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the abs & core, chest, glutes, hamstrings, lower back, upper back, quadriceps, traps and triceps.
setup: Begin standing with the log in front of you. Grasp the handles, and begin to clean the log. As you are bent over to start the clean, attempt to get the log as high as possible, pulling it into your chest. Extend through the hips and knees to bring it up to complete the clean.
steps: Push your head back and look up, creating a shelf on your chest to rest the log. Begin the press by dipping, flexing slightly through the knees and reversing the motion. This push press will generate momentum to start the log moving vertically. Continue by extending through the elbows to press the log above your head. There are no strict rules on form, so use whatever techniques you are most efficient with. As the log is pressed, ensure that you push your head through on each repetition, looking forward.
Repeat as many times as possible. Attempt to control the descent of the log as it is returned to the ground.
cues: Clean the implement to the chest or shoulder first
Dip and drive with the legs, then press
Lock out with the implement over the mid-foot
mistakes: Losing the brace during the clean
exercises.breathing: Big breath and brace before the clean; re-breathe at the shoulder, then brace again for the press.
safety: Learn with an empty log or light bell, ideally with a coach.

exercises.name: Dumbbell One-Arm Upright Row
exercises.description: Dumbbell One-Arm Upright Row is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the biceps and traps. A variation of the upright row: one dumbbell, other hand on the hip.
setup: Grab a dumbbell and stand up straight with your arm extended in front of you with a slight bend at the elbows and your back straight. This will be your starting position. Tip: The dumbbell should be resting on top of your thigh with the palm of your hands facing your thighs.
steps: Keep the other hand can be kept fully extended to the side, by the waist or grabbing a fixed surface. This will be your starting position.

Use your side shoulders to lift the dumbbell as you exhale. The dumbbell should be close to the body as you move it up. Continue to lift it until the dumbbell is nearly in line with your chin. Tip: Your elbows should drive the motion. As you lift the dumbbell, your elbow should always be higher than your forearm. Also, keep your torso stationary and pause for a second at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbell back down slowly to the starting position. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and switch arms.
cues: Elbows above the hands
Stop at shoulder height
mistakes: Narrow grip and pulling too high, which can pinch the shoulders
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you raise the weight, breathe in as you lower it.
safety: Use a grip at least shoulder-width and stop at shoulder height to reduce shoulder impingement risk.
variation_notes: One dumbbell, other hand on the hip.

exercises.name: Smith Machine One-Arm Upright Row
exercises.description: Smith Machine One-Arm Upright Row is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the biceps and traps. A variation of the upright row: one hand in the middle of a Smith bar.
setup: With the bar at thigh level, load an appropriate weight.
steps: Take a wide grip on the bar and unhook the weight, removing your off hand from the bar. Your arm should be extended as you stand up straight with your head and chest up. This will be your starting position.
Begin the movement by flexing the elbow, raising the upper arm with the elbow pointed out. Continue until your upper arm is parallel to the floor.
After a brief pause, return the weight to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before engaging the hooks to rack the weight.

exercises.description: Straight Raises on Incline Bench is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the shoulders, with help from the traps. A variation of the y raise: lying face down on an incline bench, raise a light bar straight out in front.

exercises.name: Clean Shrug
exercises.description: Clean Shrug is a beginner-level Olympic-lifting exercise that mainly targets the traps, with help from the forearms. A variation of the clean pull: from the hang, extend and shrug, no arm pull.
steps: Begin with a shoulder width, double overhand or hook grip, with the bar hanging at the mid thigh position. Your back should be straight and inclined slightly forward.

exercises.name: Barbell Shrug Behind The Back
exercises.description: Barbell Shrug Behind The Back is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the traps, with help from the forearms and upper back. A variation of the shrug: bar held behind the thighs, which hits the middle traps more.
setup: Stand up straight with your feet at shoulder width as you hold a barbell with both hands behind your back using a pronated grip (palms facing back). Tip: Your hands should be a little wider than shoulder width apart. You can use wrist wraps for this exercise for better grip. This will be your starting position.
steps: Raise your shoulders up as far as you can go as you breathe out and hold the contraction for a second. Tip: Refrain from trying to lift the barbell by using your biceps. The arms should remain stretched out at all times.
Slowly return to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Straight up and down; do not roll the shoulders
Arms stay straight
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you shrug up, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps
exercises.description: Overhead Triceps is an advanced-level stretch that mainly targets the triceps, with help from the lats.
setup: Sit upright on the floor with your partner behind you. Raise one arm straight up, and flex the elbow, attempting to touch your hand to your back. Your parner should hold your elbow and wrist. This will be your starting position.
steps: Attempt to extend the arm straight into the air as your partner prevents you from doing actually doing so.
