Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Tricep Side Stretch
exercises.description: Tricep Side Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the triceps.
steps: Bring right arm across your body and over your left shoulder, holding your elbow with your left hand, until you feel a stretch in your tricep. Then repeat for your other arm.
cues: Keep the shoulder relaxed and down
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Triceps Stretch
exercises.description: Triceps Stretch is a beginner-level stretch that mainly targets the triceps, with help from the lats.
steps: Reach your hand behind your head, grasp your elbow and gently pull. Hold for 10 to 20 seconds, then switch sides.
cues: Keep the shoulder relaxed and down
Ease into the stretch until you feel gentle tension, never pain
Hold 20–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side
Keep the rest of the body relaxed
mistakes: Forcing the stretch until it hurts
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose. Ease a little further into the stretch on each exhale, and never hold your breath.

exercises.name: Bench Dip
exercises.description: Dips with your hands on a bench behind you and feet on the floor.
setup: Sit on the edge of a bench, hands beside your hips, fingers forward.
Slide your hips off the bench, feet on the floor in front.
steps: Bend your elbows to lower your hips toward the floor.
Stop when your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Press back up.
cues: Keep your back close to the bench
Elbows point straight back
mistakes: Dropping too low and straining the shoulders
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you press up.
safety: This position stresses the front of the shoulder; keep the range moderate.

exercises.name: Weighted Bench Dip
exercises.description: Weighted Bench Dip is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps, with help from the chest. A variation of the bench dip: a plate on the thighs.
setup: For this exercise you will need to place a bench behind your back and another one in front of you. With the benches perpendicular to your body, hold on to one bench on its edge with the hands close to your body, separated at shoulder width. Your arms should be fully extended.
steps: The legs will be extended forward on top of the other bench. Your legs should be parallel to the floor while your torso is to be perpendicular to the floor. Have your partner place the dumbbell on your lap. Note: This exercise is best performed with a partner as placing the weight on your lap can be challenging and cause injury without assistance. This will be your starting position.

Slowly lower your body as you inhale by bending at the elbows until you lower yourself far enough to where there is an angle slightly smaller than 90 degrees between the upper arm and the forearm. Tip: Keep the elbows as close as possible throughout the movement. Forearms should always be pointing down.
Using your triceps to bring your torso up again, lift yourself back to the starting position while exhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Keep your back close to the bench
Elbows point straight back
mistakes: Dropping too low and straining the shoulders
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you press up.
safety: This position stresses the front of the shoulder; keep the range moderate.
variation_notes: A plate on the thighs.

exercises.name: Bench Press - Close Grip (Barbell)
exercises.description: A bench press with hands about shoulder-width apart, which shifts more of the work to the triceps.
setup: Lie on the bench with your eyes under the bar (or the handles/weights level with your chest).
Plant your feet flat on the floor, slightly wider than your hips.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down and keep them pinned to the bench; allow a small natural arch in your lower back.
Grip slightly wider than shoulder width with wrists stacked straight over your forearms.
steps: Unrack or lift the weight to straight arms over your shoulders.
Lower it under control to your lower chest, elbows about 45–70° from your torso.
Touch the chest lightly without bouncing.
Press back up and slightly toward your face so the weight finishes over your shoulders.
cues: Shoulder blades stay pinched the whole set
Forearms vertical at the bottom
Push your feet into the floor
Weight travels from lower chest to over the shoulders
Elbows tucked close to the ribs
mistakes: Flaring the elbows to 90°, which stresses the shoulders
Bouncing the weight off the chest
Lifting the hips off the bench
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath and brace before lowering. Hold it on the way down, then breathe out through pursed lips as you push past the hardest part of the press.
safety: Use safety bars or a spotter for heavy barbell sets.
Keep your head, upper back and hips on the bench.
variation_notes: Grip about shoulder-width, not narrower, to spare your wrists.
Keep the elbows closer to the body and touch slightly lower on the chest.

exercises.name: Bench Press with Chains
exercises.description: Bench Press with Chains is an advanced-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps, with help from the chest and lats. A variation of the bench press: chains add load as the bar rises, so the top of the press is heaviest.
setup: Adjust the leader chain, shortening it to the desired length. Place the chains on the sleeves of the bar.
steps: Lying on the bench, get your head beyond the bar if possible. Tuck your feet underneath you and arch your back. Using the bar to help support your weight, lift your shoulder off the bench and retract them, squeezing the shoulder blades together. Use your feet to drive your traps into the bench. Maintain this tight body position throughout the movement. However wide your grip, it should cover the ring on the bar.

Pull the bar out of the rack without protracting your shoulders. Focus on squeezing the bar and trying to pull it apart. Lower the bar to your lower chest or upper stomach. The bar, wrist, and elbow should stay in line at all times.
Pause when the barbell touches your torso, and then drive the bar up with as much force as possible. The elbows should be tucked in until lockout.
cues: Shoulder blades stay pinched the whole set
Forearms vertical at the bottom
Push your feet into the floor
Weight travels from lower chest to over the shoulders
mistakes: Flaring the elbows to 90°, which stresses the shoulders
Bouncing the weight off the chest
Lifting the hips off the bench
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath and brace before lowering. Hold it on the way down, then breathe out through pursed lips as you push past the hardest part of the press.
safety: Use safety bars or a spotter for heavy barbell sets.
Keep your head, upper back and hips on the bench.
variation_notes: Chains add load as the bar rises, so the top of the press is heaviest.

exercises.name: Board Press
exercises.description: Board Press is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps, with help from the chest, forearms and lats. A variation of the bench press: boards on the chest stop the bar short to overload the top half.
setup: Begin by lying on the bench, getting your head beyond the bar if possible. One to five boards, made out of 2x6's, can be screwed together and held in place by a training partner, bands, or just tucked under your shirt.
steps: Tuck your feet underneath you and arch your back. Using the bar to help support your weight, lift your shoulder off the bench and retract them, squeezing the shoulder blades together. Use your feet to drive your traps into the bench. Maintain this tight body position throughout the movement.

You can take a standard bench grip, or shoulder width to focus on the triceps. Pull the bar out of the rack without protracting your shoulders. The bar, wrist, and elbow should stay in line at all times. Focus on squeezing the bar and trying to pull it apart.
Lower the bar to the boards, and then drive the bar up with as much force as possible. The elbows should be tucked in until lockout.
cues: Shoulder blades stay pinched the whole set
Forearms vertical at the bottom
Push your feet into the floor
Weight travels from lower chest to over the shoulders
mistakes: Flaring the elbows to 90°, which stresses the shoulders
Bouncing the weight off the chest
Lifting the hips off the bench
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath and brace before lowering. Hold it on the way down, then breathe out through pursed lips as you push past the hardest part of the press.
safety: Use safety bars or a spotter for heavy barbell sets.
Keep your head, upper back and hips on the bench.
variation_notes: Boards on the chest stop the bar short to overload the top half.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Dumbbell Press
exercises.description: Close-Grip Dumbbell Press is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps, with help from the chest. A variation of the bench press: dumbbells pressed touching each other, which shifts work to the triceps.
setup: Place a dumbbell standing up on a flat bench.
steps: Ensuring that the dumbbell stays securely placed at the top of the bench, lie perpendicular to the bench with only your shoulders lying on the surface. Hips should be below the bench and your legs bent with your feet firmly on the floor.

Grasp the dumbbell with both hands and hold it straight over your chest at arm's length. Both palms should be pressing against the underside of the sides of the dumbbell. This will be your starting position.
Initiate the movement by lowering the dumbbell to your chest.
Return to the starting position by extending the elbows.
cues: Shoulder blades stay pinched the whole set
Forearms vertical at the bottom
Push your feet into the floor
Weight travels from lower chest to over the shoulders
mistakes: Flaring the elbows to 90°, which stresses the shoulders
Bouncing the weight off the chest
Lifting the hips off the bench
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath and brace before lowering. Hold it on the way down, then breathe out through pursed lips as you push past the hardest part of the press.
safety: Use safety bars or a spotter for heavy barbell sets.
Keep your head, upper back and hips on the bench.
variation_notes: Dumbbells pressed touching each other, which shifts work to the triceps.

exercises.name: Close-Grip EZ-Bar Press
exercises.description: Close-Grip EZ-Bar Press is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps, with help from the chest. A variation of the bench press: eZ bar with a narrow grip, which shifts work to the triceps.
setup: Lie on a flat bench with an EZ bar loaded to an appropriate weight.
steps: Using a narrow grip lift the bar and hold it straight over your torso with your elbows in. The arms should be perpendicular to the floor. This will be your starting position.
Now lower the bar down to your lower chest as you breathe in. Keep the elbows in as you perform this movement.
Using the triceps to push the bar back up, press it back to the starting position by extending the elbows as you exhale.
Repeat.
cues: Shoulder blades stay pinched the whole set
Forearms vertical at the bottom
Push your feet into the floor
Weight travels from lower chest to over the shoulders
mistakes: Flaring the elbows to 90°, which stresses the shoulders
Bouncing the weight off the chest
Lifting the hips off the bench
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath and brace before lowering. Hold it on the way down, then breathe out through pursed lips as you push past the hardest part of the press.
safety: Use safety bars or a spotter for heavy barbell sets.
Keep your head, upper back and hips on the bench.
variation_notes: EZ bar with a narrow grip, which shifts work to the triceps.

exercises.name: Pin Presses
exercises.description: Pin Presses is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps, with help from the chest, forearms, lats and upper back. A variation of the bench press: pressing from safety pins set just above the chest, starting from a dead stop.
setup: Pin presses remove the eccentric phase of the bench press, developing starting strength. They also allow you to train a desired range of motion.
steps: The bench should be set up in a power rack. Set the pins to the desired point in your range of motion, whether it just be lockout or an inch off of your chest. The bar should be moved to the pins and prepared for lifting.

Begin by lying on the bench, with the bar directly above the contact point during your regular bench. Tuck your feet underneath you and arch your back. Using the bar to help support your weight, lift your shoulder off the bench and retract them, squeezing the shoulder blades together. Use your feet to drive your traps into the bench. Maintain this tight body position throughout the movement.
You can take a standard bench grip, or shoulder width to focus on the triceps. The bar, wrist, and elbow should stay in line at all times. Focus on squeezing the bar and trying to pull it apart.
Drive the bar up with as much force as possible. The elbows should be tucked in until lockout.
Return the bar to the pins, pausing before beginning the next repetition.
cues: Shoulder blades stay pinched the whole set
Forearms vertical at the bottom
Push your feet into the floor
Weight travels from lower chest to over the shoulders
mistakes: Flaring the elbows to 90°, which stresses the shoulders
Bouncing the weight off the chest
Lifting the hips off the bench
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath and brace before lowering. Hold it on the way down, then breathe out through pursed lips as you push past the hardest part of the press.
safety: Use safety bars or a spotter for heavy barbell sets.
Keep your head, upper back and hips on the bench.
variation_notes: Pressing from safety pins set just above the chest, starting from a dead stop.

exercises.name: Reverse Band Bench Press
exercises.description: Reverse Band Bench Press is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps, with help from the chest, forearms, lats and upper back. A variation of the bench press: bands from the top of the rack help most at the chest and less at lockout.
setup: Position a bench inside a power rack, with the bar set to the correct height. Begin by anchoring bands either to band pegs or to the top of the rack. Ensure that you will be position properly under the bands. Attach the other end to the barbell.
steps: Lie on the bench, tuck your feet underneath you and arch your back. Using the bar to help support your weight, lift your shoulder off the bench and retract them, squeezing the shoulder blades together. Use your feet to drive your traps into the bench. Maintain this tight body position throughout the movement. However wide your grip, it should cover the ring on the bar.

Pull the bar out of the rack without protracting your shoulders. Focus on squeezing the bar and trying to pull it apart. Lower the bar to your lower chest or upper stomach. The bar, wrist, and elbow should stay in line at all times.
Pause when the barbell touches your torso, and then drive the bar up with as much force as possible. The elbows should be tucked in until lockout.
cues: Shoulder blades stay pinched the whole set
Forearms vertical at the bottom
Push your feet into the floor
Weight travels from lower chest to over the shoulders
mistakes: Flaring the elbows to 90°, which stresses the shoulders
Bouncing the weight off the chest
Lifting the hips off the bench
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath and brace before lowering. Hold it on the way down, then breathe out through pursed lips as you push past the hardest part of the press.
safety: Use safety bars or a spotter for heavy barbell sets.
Keep your head, upper back and hips on the bench.
variation_notes: Bands from the top of the rack help most at the chest and less at lockout.

exercises.name: Reverse Triceps Bench Press
exercises.description: Reverse Triceps Bench Press is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps, with help from the chest. A variation of the bench press: underhand grip; works the triceps and upper chest. Use a spotter.
setup: Lie back on a flat bench. Using a close, supinated grip (around shoulder width), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked extended in front of you and perpendicular to the floor. This will be your starting position.
steps: As you breathe in, come down slowly until you feel the bar on your middle chest. Tip: Make sure that as opposed to a regular bench press, you keep the elbows close to the torso at all times in order to maximize triceps involvement.

After a second pause, bring the bar back to the starting position as you breathe out and push the bar using your triceps muscles. Lock your arms in the contracted position, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly again. Tip: It should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the bar back in the rack.
cues: Shoulder blades stay pinched the whole set
Forearms vertical at the bottom
Push your feet into the floor
Weight travels from lower chest to over the shoulders
mistakes: Flaring the elbows to 90°, which stresses the shoulders
Bouncing the weight off the chest
Lifting the hips off the bench
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath and brace before lowering. Hold it on the way down, then breathe out through pursed lips as you push past the hardest part of the press.
safety: Use safety bars or a spotter for heavy barbell sets.
Keep your head, upper back and hips on the bench.
variation_notes: Underhand grip; works the triceps and upper chest. Use a spotter.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Close-Grip Bench Press
exercises.description: Smith Machine Close-Grip Bench Press is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps, with help from the chest. A variation of the bench press: smith machine with a narrow grip, for the triceps.
setup: Place a flat bench underneath the smith machine. Place the barbell at a height that you can reach when lying down and your arms are almost fully extended. Once the weight you need is selected, lie down on the flat bench. Using a close and pronated grip (palms facing forward) that is around shoulder width, unlock the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked. This will be your starting position.
steps: As you breathe in, come down slowly until you feel the bar on your middle chest. Tip: Make sure that as opposed to a regular bench press, you keep the elbows close to the torso at all times in order to maximize triceps involvement.

After a second pause, bring the bar back to the starting position as you breathe out and push the bar using your triceps muscles. Lock your arms in the contracted position, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly again. Tip: It should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, lock the bar back in the rack.
cues: Shoulder blades stay pinched the whole set
Forearms vertical at the bottom
Push your feet into the floor
Weight travels from lower chest to over the shoulders
mistakes: Flaring the elbows to 90°, which stresses the shoulders
Bouncing the weight off the chest
Lifting the hips off the bench
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath and brace before lowering. Hold it on the way down, then breathe out through pursed lips as you push past the hardest part of the press.
safety: Use safety bars or a spotter for heavy barbell sets.
Keep your head, upper back and hips on the bench.
variation_notes: Smith machine with a narrow grip, for the triceps.

exercises.name: Body Tricep Press
exercises.description: Body Tricep Press is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps.
setup: Position a bar in a rack at chest height.
steps: Standing, take a shoulder width grip on the bar and step a yard or two back, feet together and arms extended so that you are leaning on the bar. This will be your starting position.
Begin by flexing the elbow, lowering yourself towards the bar.
Pause, and then reverse the motion by extending the elbows.
Progress from bodyweight by adding chains over your shoulders.
cues: Body in one straight line like a plank
Only the elbows move
Lower until the forearms touch, then press back up
exercises.breathing: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press up.

exercises.name: Body-Up
exercises.description: Body-Up is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps, with help from the abs & core and forearms.
setup: Assume a plank position on the ground. You should be supporting your bodyweight on your toes and forearms, keeping your torso straight. Your forearms should be shoulder-width apart. This will be your starting position.
steps: Pressing your palms firmly into the ground, extend through the elbows to raise your body from the ground. Keep your torso rigid as you perform the movement.
Slowly lower your forearms back to the ground by allowing the elbows to flex.
Repeat.
cues: Body in one straight line like a plank
Only the elbows move
Lower until the forearms touch, then press back up
exercises.breathing: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press up.

exercises.name: Floor Press with Chains
exercises.description: Floor Press with Chains is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps, with help from the chest. A variation of the floor press: chains add load near lockout.
setup: Adjust the j-hooks so they are at the appropriate height to rack the bar. For this exercise, drape the chains directly over the end of the bar, trying to keep the ends away from the plates.
steps: Begin lying on the floor with your head near the end of a power rack. Keeping your shoulder blades pulled together, pull the bar off of the hooks.

Lower the bar towards the bottom of your chest or upper stomach, squeezing the bar and attempting to pull it apart as you do so. Ensure that you tuck your elbows throughout the movement. Lower the bar until your upper arm contacts the ground and pause, preventing any slamming or bouncing of the weight.
Press the bar back up as fast as you can, keeping the bar, your wrists, and elbows in line as you do so.
cues: Elbows about 45° from your body
Pause on the floor, do not bounce
mistakes: Slamming the elbows into the floor
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath and brace before lowering. Hold it on the way down, then breathe out through pursed lips as you push past the hardest part of the press.
safety: With a barbell, set it up in a rack at the right height or use pins; getting a heavy bar into position from the floor is hard.
variation_notes: Chains add load near lockout.

exercises.name: One Arm Floor Press
exercises.description: One Arm Floor Press is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps, with help from the chest. A variation of the floor press: one hand in the middle of the bar; needs control to keep it level.
setup: Lie down on a flat surface with your back pressing against the floor or an exercise mat. Make sure your knees are bent.
steps: Have a partner hand you the bar on one hand. When starting, your arm should be just about fully extended, similar to the starting position of a barbell bench press. However, this time your grip will be neutral (palms facing your torso).
Make sure the hand you are not using to lift the weight is placed by your side.
Begin the exercise by lowering the barbell until your elbow touches the ground. Make sure to breathe in as this is the eccentric (lowering part of the exercise).
Then start lifting the barbell back up to the original starting position. Remember to breathe out during the concentric (lifting part of the exercise).
Repeat until you have performed your recommended repetitions.
Switch arms and repeat the movement.
cues: Elbows about 45° from your body
Pause on the floor, do not bounce
mistakes: Slamming the elbows into the floor
exercises.breathing: Take a big breath and brace before lowering. Hold it on the way down, then breathe out through pursed lips as you push past the hardest part of the press.
safety: With a barbell, set it up in a rack at the right height or use pins; getting a heavy bar into position from the floor is hard.
variation_notes: One hand in the middle of the bar; needs control to keep it level.

exercises.name: Floor Triceps Dip
exercises.description: A small triceps dip sitting on the floor with hands behind you, lifting your hips by straightening your arms.
setup: Sit on the floor, knees bent, hands on the floor behind you with fingers forward.
Lift your hips slightly.
steps: Bend your elbows to lower toward the floor.
Straighten them to push back up.
cues: Elbows point back
Keep the hips lifted
exercises.breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push up.

exercises.name: JM Press (Barbell)
exercises.description: A hybrid of a close-grip bench press and a skullcrusher that lets you load the triceps heavily.
setup: Lie on a bench with a shoulder-width grip on the bar, arms straight over your shoulders.
steps: Lower the bar toward your chin/upper chest by bending the elbows and letting them travel slightly forward.
Stop when the forearms meet the upper arms.
Press back up to straight arms.
cues: Elbows stay tucked
Bar path to the upper chest/chin
mistakes: Going too heavy before learning the path
exercises.breathing: Breathe in and brace as you lower, breathe out as you press.
safety: Use safety bars; start light while learning the movement.

exercises.name: Supine Chest Throw
exercises.description: Supine Chest Throw is a beginner-level plyometric exercise that mainly targets the triceps, with help from the chest.
setup: This drill is great for chest passes when you lack a partner or a wall of sufficient strength. Lay on the ground on your back with your knees bent.
steps: Begin with the ball on your chest, held with both hands on the bottom.
Explode up, extending through the elbow to throw the ball directly above you as high as possible.
Catch the ball with both hands as it comes down.
cues: Use the legs and hips first, the arms last
Throw as hard as you can; every rep is maximal
Use a light ball (2–5 kg) you can move fast
Reset fully between throws
mistakes: Using a ball too heavy to move quickly
Rounding the back when picking up or catching
exercises.breathing: Inhale as you load, exhale forcefully as you release the ball.
safety: Throw against a solid wall or into open space, never toward people.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Overhead Triceps Extension
exercises.description: Kettlebell Overhead Triceps Extension is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps, with help from the abs & core. A variation of the overhead triceps extension: one kettlebell held by the horns.
setup: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a kettlebell by the horns with both hands. Press it overhead until your arms are extended, with the bell hanging behind your hands.
steps: Brace your abdominals and keep your upper arms vertical and close to your head. This is your starting position.
Bend at the elbows to lower the kettlebell behind your head, going as far as your shoulder mobility allows without your elbows flaring outward.
Extend your elbows to press the kettlebell back to the starting position, keeping your upper arms still throughout.
Keep your ribcage down and avoid arching your lower back as you extend.
cues: Elbows point forward, not out
Upper arms stay still
Ribs down
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you straighten your arms, breathe in as you bend them.
safety: Reduce the range if your elbows or shoulders feel strained.
variation_notes: One kettlebell held by the horns.

exercises.name: Kneeling Cable Triceps Extension
exercises.description: Kneeling Cable Triceps Extension is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps. A variation of the overhead triceps extension: kneeling with the upper arms on a bench, facing away from a high pulley.
setup: Place a bench sideways in front of a high pulley machine.
steps: Hold a straight bar attachment above your head with your hands about 6 inches apart with your palms facing down.
Face away from the machine and kneel.
Place your head and the back of your upper arms on the bench. Your elbows should be bent with the forearms pointing towards the high pulley. This will be your starting position.

While keeping your upper arms close to your head at all times with the elbows in, press the bar out in a semicircular motion until the elbows are locked and your arms are parallel to the floor. Contract the triceps hard and keep this position for a second. Exhale as you perform this movement.
Slowly return to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Elbows point forward, not out
Upper arms stay still
Ribs down
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you straighten your arms, breathe in as you bend them.
safety: Reduce the range if your elbows or shoulders feel strained.
variation_notes: Kneeling with the upper arms on a bench, facing away from a high pulley.

exercises.name: Low Cable Triceps Extension
exercises.description: Low Cable Triceps Extension is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps. A variation of the overhead triceps extension: facing away from a low pulley.
setup: Select the desired weight and lay down face up on the bench of a seated row machine that has a rope attached to it. Your head should be pointing towards the attachment.
steps: Grab the outside of the rope ends with your palms facing each other (neutral grip).

Position your elbows so that they are bent at a 90 degree angle and your upper arms are perpendicular (90 degree angle) to your torso. Tip: Keep the elbows in and make sure that the upper arms point to the ceiling while your forearms point towards the pulley above your head. This will be your starting position.

As you breathe out, extend your lower arms until they are straight and vertical. The upper arms and elbows remain stationary throughout the movement. Only the forearms should move. Contract the triceps hard for a second.
As you breathe in slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Elbows point forward, not out
Upper arms stay still
Ribs down
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you straighten your arms, breathe in as you bend them.
safety: Reduce the range if your elbows or shoulders feel strained.
variation_notes: Facing away from a low pulley.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Extension (Cable)
exercises.description: Straightening the arms overhead. With the arms up, the long head of the triceps is stretched and works hard.
setup: Attach a rope to a low or mid pulley.
Face away from the stack, step forward and hold the rope behind your head.
steps: Bend your elbows to lower the weight behind your head.
Go as low as is comfortable to feel a stretch in the triceps.
Straighten your arms back overhead.
cues: Elbows point forward, not out
Upper arms stay still
Ribs down
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you straighten your arms, breathe in as you bend them.
safety: Reduce the range if your elbows or shoulders feel strained.

exercises.name: Seated Triceps Press
exercises.description: Seated Triceps Press is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps. A variation of the overhead triceps extension: one dumbbell in both hands, seated.
setup: Sit down on a bench with back support and grasp a dumbbell with both hands and hold it overhead at arm's length. Tip: a better way is to have somebody hand it to you especially if it is very heavy. The resistance should be resting in the palms of your hands with your thumbs around it. The palm of the hand should be facing inward. This will be your starting position.
steps: Keeping your upper arms close to your head (elbows in) and perpendicular to the floor, lower the resistance in a semi-circular motion behind your head until your forearms touch your biceps. Tip: The upper arms should remain stationary and only the forearms should move. Breathe in as you perform this step.

setup: Lie on the floor and place your hands on an upright dumbbell. Supporting your weight on your toes and hands, keep your torso rigid and your elbows in with your arms straight. This will be your starting position.
steps: Lower your body, allowing the elbows to flex while you inhale. Keep your body straight, not allowing your hips to rise or sag.

setup: Place your hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulder width, under or just outside your shoulders.
Step your feet back so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.

Push the floor away until your arms are straight.

steps: Take hold of the band, raising your elbows so that the upper arm is perpendicular to the floor. With the elbow flexed, the band should be above your head. This will be your starting position.
Extend through the elbow to straighten your arm, keeping your upper arm in place. Pause at the top of the motion, and return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Cable Incline Triceps Extension
exercises.description: Cable Incline Triceps Extension is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps. A variation of the skullcrusher: lying on an incline bench facing away from a low pulley.
setup: Lie on incline an bench facing away from a high pulley machine that has a straight bar attachment on it.
steps: Grasp the straight bar attachment overhead with a pronated (overhand; palms down) narrow grip (less than shoulder width) and keep your elbows tucked in to your sides. Your upper arms should create around a 25 degree angle when measured from the floor.
Keeping the upper arms stationary, extend the arms as you flex the triceps. Breathe out during this portion of the movement and hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

exercises.name: Cable Lying Triceps Extension

setup: Lie on a flat bench and grasp the straight bar attachment of a low pulley with a narrow overhand grip. Tip: The easiest way to do this is to have someone hand you the bar as you lay down.

Lower the bar by bending at the elbow while keeping the upper arms stationary and elbows in. Go down until the bar lightly touches your forehead. Breathe in as you perform this portion of the movement.

steps: Begin by extending through the elbow, keeping your upper arm still, with your wrists pronated.

exercises.name: Decline Close-Grip Bench To Skull Crusher
exercises.description: Decline Close-Grip Bench To Skull Crusher is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps, with help from the chest. A variation of the skullcrusher: alternates close-grip presses and skull crushers on a decline bench.
setup: Secure your legs at the end of the decline bench and slowly lay down on the bench.
steps: Using a close grip (a grip that is slightly less than shoulder width), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked and elbows in. The arms should be perpendicular to the floor. This will be your starting position. Tip: In order to protect your rotator cuff, it is best if you have a spotter help you lift the barbell off the rack.
Now lower the bar down to your lower chest as you breathe in. Keep the elbows in as you perform this movement.
Using the triceps to push the bar back up, press it back to the starting position as you exhale.

As you breathe in and you keep the upper arms stationary, bring the bar down slowly by moving your forearms in a semicircular motion towards you until you feel the bar slightly touch your forehead. Breathe in as you perform this portion of the movement.
Lift the bar back to the starting position by contracting the triceps and exhaling.
Repeat steps 3-6 until the recommended amount of repetitions is performed.

Elbows point to the ceiling, not out
mistakes: Turning it into a press by moving the upper arms
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you straighten your arms, breathe in as you bend them.
safety: Use a spotter or a controlled weight; you are lowering it toward your face.
variation_notes: Alternates close-grip presses and skull crushers on a decline bench.

exercises.name: Lying Triceps Press
exercises.description: Lying Triceps Press is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps. A variation of the skullcrusher: eZ bar lowered to the forehead.
setup: Lie on a flat bench with either an e-z bar (my preference) or a straight bar placed on the floor behind your head and your feet on the floor.
steps: Grab the bar behind you, using a medium overhand (pronated) grip, and raise the bar in front of you at arms length. Tip: The arms should be perpendicular to the torso and the floor. The elbows should be tucked in. This is the starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the weight until the bar lightly touches your forehead while keeping the upper arms and elbows stationary.
At that point, use the triceps to bring the weight back up to the starting position as you breathe out.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Upper arms stay still, tilted slightly back
Elbows point to the ceiling, not out
mistakes: Turning it into a press by moving the upper arms
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you straighten your arms, breathe in as you bend them.
safety: Use a spotter or a controlled weight; you are lowering it toward your face.
variation_notes: EZ bar lowered to the forehead.

setup: Lie flat on a bench while holding a dumbbell at arms length. Your arm should be perpendicular to your body. The palm of your hand should be facing towards your feet as a pronated grip is required to perform this exercise.
steps: Place your non lifting hand on your bicep for support.

exercises.name: Tate Press
exercises.description: Tate Press is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps, with help from the chest.
setup: Lie down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand on top of your thighs. The palms of your hand will be facing each other.
steps: By using your thighs to help you get the dumbbells up, clean the dumbbells one arm at a time so that you can hold them in front of you at shoulder width. Note: when holding the dumbbells in front of you, make sure your arms are wider than shoulder width apart from each other using a pronated (palms forward) grip. Allow your elbows to point out. This is your starting position.

Keeping the upper arms stationary, slowly move the dumbbells in and down in a semi circular motion until they touch the upper chest while inhaling. Keep full control of the dumbbells at all times and do not move the upper arms nor rest the dumbbells on the chest.

As you breathe out, move the dumbbells up using your triceps and the same semi-circular motion but in reverse. Attempt to keep the dumbbells together as they move up. Lock your arms in the contracted position, hold for a second and then start coming down again slowly again. Tip: It should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions of your training program.
cues: Dumbbells touch over the chest, elbows out
Lower the dumbbells to the chest by bending the elbows outward
Press back up
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Seated Bent-Over One-Arm Dumbbell Triceps Extension
exercises.description: Seated Bent-Over One-Arm Dumbbell Triceps Extension is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps. A variation of the triceps kickback: seated and bent over, one arm.
setup: Sit down at the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell in one arm using a neutral grip (palms of the hand facing you).
steps: Bend your knees slightly and bring your torso forward, by bending at the waist, while keeping the back straight until it is almost parallel to the floor. Make sure that you keep the head up.

The upper arm with the dumbbell should be close to the torso and aligned with it (lifted up until it is parallel to the floor while the forearms are pointing towards the floor as the hands hold the weights). Tip: There should be a 90-degree angle between the forearms and the upper arm. This is your starting position.

Keeping the upper arm stationary, use the triceps to lift the weight as you exhale until the forearm is parallel to the floor and the whole arm is extended. Like many other arm exercises, only the forearm moves.
After a second contraction at the top, slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
Switch arms and repeat the exercise.
cues: Upper arm stays parallel to the floor
Only the forearm moves
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you straighten your arms, breathe in as you bend them.
variation_notes: Seated and bent over, one arm.

exercises.name: Cable One Arm Tricep Extension
exercises.description: Cable One Arm Tricep Extension is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the triceps. A variation of the triceps pushdown: one handle, palm up.
setup: With your right hand, grasp a single handle attached to the high-cable pulley using a supinated (underhand; palms facing up) grip. You should be standing directly in front of the weight stack.
steps: Now pull the handle down so that your upper arm and elbow are locked in to the side of your body. Your upper arm and forearm should form an acute angle (less than 90-degrees). You can keep the other arm by the waist and you can have one leg in front of you and the other one back for better balance. This will be your starting position.

As you contract the triceps, move the single handle attachment down to your side until your arm is straight. Breathe out as you perform this movement. Tip: Only the forearms should move. Your upper arms should remain stationary at all times.
Squeeze the triceps and hold for a second in this contracted position.
Slowly return the handle to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then perform the same movement with the other arm.

Only the forearms move
mistakes: Leaning over the weight and pushing with the body
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you straighten your arms, breathe in as you bend them.

exercises.name: Straight Bar Bench Mid Rows
exercises.description: Straight Bar Bench Mid Rows is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the upper back, with help from the biceps and lats. A variation of the bent over row: standing on a bench behind a bar resting on its end.
setup: Place a loaded barbell on the end of a bench. Standing on the bench behind the bar, take a medium, pronated grip. Stand with your hips back and chest up, maintaining a neutral spine. This will be your starting position.
steps: Row the bar to your torso by retracting the shoulder blades and flexing the elbows. Use a controlled movement with no jerking.
After a brief pause, slowly return the bar to the starting position, ensuring to go all the way down.
cues: Pull with the elbows, not the hands
Keep the back flat and the torso angle fixed
Chest proud

exercises.description: Two-Arm Kettlebell Row is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the upper back, with help from the biceps and lats. A variation of the bent over row: two kettlebells.
steps: Place two kettlebells in front of your feet. Bend your knees slightly and then push your butt out as much as possible as you bend over to get in the starting position.
Grab both kettlebells and pull them to your stomach, retracting your shoulder blades and flexing the elbows. Keep your back straight. Lower and repeat.

exercises.name: Chest Supported Incline Row (Dumbbell)
exercises.description: A row with your chest resting on a support, which takes the lower back out of the exercise.
setup: Set an incline bench to about 30–45° and lie face down with your chest on the pad.
Let your arms hang straight down holding the weight.
steps: Row the weight up until your elbows pass your torso.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
cues: Chest stays on the pad
Lead with the elbows
mistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad to cheat
exercises.breathing: Brace your core before each rep. Breathe out as you pull, breathe in as you lower the weight.

Squeeze the shoulder blades together.
Lower slowly to straight arms.

exercises.name: Incline Bench Pull
exercises.description: Incline Bench Pull is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the upper back, with help from the lats. A variation of the chest supported row: lying face down on an incline bench, rowing a barbell.
setup: Grab a dumbbell in each hand and lie face down on an incline bench that is set to an incline that is approximately 30 degrees.
steps: Let the arms hang to your sides fully extended as they point to the floor.
Turn the wrists until your hands have a pronated (palms down) grip.
Now flare the elbows out. This will be your starting position.

As you breathe out, start to pull the dumbbells up as if you are doing a reverse bench press. You will do this by bending at the elbows and bringing the upper arms up as you let the forearms hang. Continue this motion until the upper arms are at the same level as your back. Tip: The elbows will come out to the side and your upper arms and torso should make the letter "T" at the top of the movement. Hold the contraction at the top for a second.
Slowly go back down to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Chest stays on the pad
Lead with the elbows
mistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad to cheat
exercises.breathing: Brace your core before each rep. Breathe out as you pull, breathe in as you lower the weight.
variation_notes: Lying face down on an incline bench, rowing a barbell.

exercises.name: One Arm Chin-Up
exercises.description: One Arm Chin-Up is an advanced-level strength exercise that mainly targets the upper back, with help from the biceps, forearms and lats. A variation of the chin up: one hand on the bar; the other may hold the wrist for help. Very advanced.
setup: For this exercise, start out by placing a towel around a chin up bar.
steps: Grab the chin-up bar with your palm facing you. One hand will be grabbing the chin-up bar and the other will be grabbing the towel.
Bring your torso back around 30 degrees or so while creating a curvature on your lower back and sticking your chest out. This is your starting position.v

Pull your torso up until the bar touches your upper chest by drawing the shoulders and the upper arms down and back. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: Concentrate on squeezing the back muscles once you reach the full contracted position. The upper torso should remain stationary as it moves through space and only the arms should move. The forearms should do no other work other than hold the bar.
After a second on the contracted position, start to inhale and slowly lower your torso back to the starting position when your arms are fully extended and the lats are fully stretched.
Repeat this motion for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
Switch arms and repeat the movement.
cues: Chest to the bar
Elbows close in front of the body
Full hang at the bottom
mistakes: Stopping short of a full hang
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.
variation_notes: One hand on the bar; the other may hold the wrist for help. Very advanced.

exercises.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Row
exercises.description: One-Arm Kettlebell Row is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the upper back, with help from the biceps and lats. A variation of the dumbbell row: kettlebell instead of a dumbbell.
steps: Place a kettlebell in front of your feet. Bend your knees slightly and then push your butt out as much as possible as you bend over to get in the starting position. Grab the kettlebell and pull it to your stomach, retracting your shoulder blade and flexing the elbow. Keep your back straight. Lower and repeat.
cues: Pull toward the hip, not the shoulder
Keep the shoulders square to the floor

Shrugging the shoulder up to the ear

variation_notes: Kettlebell instead of a dumbbell.

exercises.name: Rhomboids-SMR
exercises.description: Rhomboids-SMR is an intermediate-level self-massage (foam rolling) exercise that mainly targets the upper back, with help from the traps.
steps: Lay down with your back on the floor. Place a foam roll underneath your upper back, and cross your arms in front of you, protracting your shoulders. This will be your starting position.

Raise your hips off of the ground, placing your weight onto the foam roll. Shift your weight to one side at a time, rolling over your middle and upper back. Pause at points of tension for 10-30 seconds.
cues: Roll slowly, about 2–3 cm per second
Pause 20–30 seconds on tender spots
Support your weight with hands and feet to control the pressure
30–90 seconds per area
mistakes: Rolling directly over joints or bones
Pressing so hard you tense up
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly and stay relaxed. On a tender spot, pause and take a few long exhales to let the muscle release.
safety: Avoid rolling the lower back and neck with full body weight; use a softer tool there.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Mid Row
exercises.description: Bodyweight Mid Row is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the upper back, with help from the biceps and lats. A variation of the inverted row: rowing the body up to a bar or handles.
setup: Begin by taking a medium to wide grip on a pull-up apparatus with your palms facing away from you. From a hanging position, tuck your knees to your chest, leaning back and getting your legs over your side of the pull-up apparatus. This will be your starting position.
steps: Beginning with your arms straight, flex the elbows and retract the shoulder blades to raise your body up until your legs contact the pull-up apparatus.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
cues: Body stays a straight plank
Lead with the chest
mistakes: Reaching with the chin instead of the chest
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.
variation_notes: Rowing the body up to a bar or handles.

exercises.name: Suspended Row
exercises.description: Suspended Row is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the upper back, with help from the biceps and lats. A variation of the low row (suspension): suspension straps.
setup: Suspend your straps at around chest height. Take a handle in each hand and lean back. Keep your body erect and your head and chest up. Your arms should be fully extended. This will be your starting position.
steps: Begin by flexing the elbow to initiate the movement. Protract your shoulder blades as you do so.
At the completion of the motion pause, and then return to the starting position.
cues: Body stays rigid
Squeeze the shoulder blades at the top
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.
variation_notes: Suspension straps.

exercises.name: Bent Over One-Arm Long Bar Row
exercises.description: Bent Over One-Arm Long Bar Row is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the upper back, with help from the biceps, lats, lower back and traps. A variation of the meadows row: one hand on the end of a barbell anchored in a corner.
setup: Put weight on one of the ends of an Olympic barbell. Make sure that you either place the other end of the barbell in the corner of two walls; or put a heavy object on the ground so the barbell cannot slide backward.
steps: Bend forward until your torso is as close to parallel with the floor as you can and keep your knees slightly bent.
Now grab the bar with one arm just behind the plates on the side where the weight was placed and put your other hand on your knee. This will be your starting position.

Pull the bar straight up with your elbow in (to maximize back stimulation) until the plates touch your lower chest. Squeeze the back muscles as you lift the weight up and hold for a second at the top of the movement. Breathe out as you lift the weight. Tip: Do not allow for any swinging of the torso. Only the arm should move.

Slowly lower the bar to the starting position getting a nice stretch on the lats. Tip: Do not let the plates touch the floor. To ensure the best range of motion, I recommend using small plates (25-lb ones) as opposed to larger plates (like 35-45lb ones).
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and switch arms.
cues: Elbow travels high and back
Keep the hips square
exercises.breathing: Brace your core before each rep. Breathe out as you pull, breathe in as you lower the weight.
variation_notes: One hand on the end of a barbell anchored in a corner.

exercises.name: One-Arm Long Bar Row
exercises.description: One-Arm Long Bar Row is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the upper back, with help from the biceps and lats. A variation of the meadows row: one hand on the end of a barbell anchored in a corner.
setup: Position a bar into a landmine or in a corner to keep it from moving. Load an appropriate weight onto your end.
steps: Stand next to the bar, and take a grip with one hand close to the collar. Using your hips and legs, rise to a standing position.
Assume a bent-knee stance with your hips back and your chest up. Your arm should be extended. This will be your starting position.
Pull the weight to your side by retracting the shoulder and flexing the elbow. Do not jerk the weight or cheat during the movement.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.

Keep the hips square

exercises.name: Middle Back Shrug
exercises.description: Middle Back Shrug is an intermediate-level strength exercise that mainly targets the upper back.
setup: Lie facedown on an incline bench while holding a dumbbell in each hand. Your arms should be fully extended hanging down and pointing towards the floor. The palms of your hands should be facing each other. This will be your starting position.
steps: As you exhale, squeeze your shoulder blades together and hold the contraction for a full second. Tip: This movement is just like the reverse action of a hug, or trying to perform rear laterals as if you had no arms.
As you inhale go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Lie face down on an incline bench
Squeeze the shoulder blades together, arms straight
Hold 1 second, lower slowly
exercises.breathing: Inhale during the easier (lowering) phase, exhale as you work through the hardest part of the rep. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Mixed Grip Chin
exercises.description: Mixed Grip Chin is an advanced-level strength exercise that mainly targets the upper back, with help from the biceps and lats. A variation of the pull up: one palm toward you, one away.
setup: Using a spacing that is just about 1 inch wider than shoulder width, grab a pull-up bar with the palms of one hand facing forward and the palms of the other hand facing towards you. This will be your starting position.
steps: Now start to pull yourself up as you exhale. Tip: With the arm that has the palms facing up concentrate on using the back muscles in order to perform the movement. The elbow of that arm should remain close to the torso. With the other arm that has the palms facing forward, the elbows will be away but in line with the torso. You will concentrate on using the lats to pull your body up.
After a second contraction at the top, start to slowly come down as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

On the following set, switch grips; so if you had the right hand with the palms facing you and the left one with the palms facing forward, on the next set you will have the palms facing forward for the right hand and facing you for the left.
cues: Elbows drive down to your ribs
Body stays still; no swinging
Full hang at the bottom
mistakes: Kicking or swinging to get up
Half reps without a full hang
Craning the neck to reach the bar
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull up or down, breathe in as you return to the stretched position.
safety: If you cannot do full reps yet, use the assisted or negative versions instead of jerking.
variation_notes: One palm toward you, one away.

exercises.name: Alternating Renegade Row
exercises.description: Alternating Renegade Row is an advanced-level strength exercise that mainly targets the upper back, with help from the abs & core, biceps, chest, lats and triceps. A variation of the renegade row: kettlebells instead of dumbbells.
setup: Place two kettlebells on the floor about shoulder width apart. Position yourself on your toes and your hands as though you were doing a pushup, with the body straight and extended. Use the handles of the kettlebells to support your upper body. You may need to position your feet wide for support.
steps: Push one kettlebell into the floor and row the other kettlebell, retracting the shoulder blade of the working side as you flex the elbow, pulling it to your side.
Then lower the kettlebell to the floor and begin the kettlebell in the opposite hand. Repeat for several reps.
cues: Hips stay square to the floor
Brace like a plank
mistakes: Twisting the hips up as you row
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you row, breathe in as you set the kettlebell down.
safety: Use kettlebells with flat bottoms so they do not roll.
variation_notes: Kettlebells instead of dumbbells.

exercises.name: Scapular Pull Ups
exercises.description: Small pull ups where only the shoulder blades move. They teach the first part of a pull up and strengthen the shoulders.
setup: Hang from a bar with straight arms and an overhand grip.
steps: Without bending your elbows, pull your shoulder blades down and together so your body rises a few centimetres.
Hold for a second.
Let your shoulders rise back to a relaxed hang.
cues: Arms stay straight
Think "shoulders away from ears"
exercises.breathing: Breathe out as you pull the shoulders down, breathe in as you relax.

exercises.name: Lying Cambered Barbell Row
exercises.description: Lying Cambered Barbell Row is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the upper back, with help from the biceps, lats and traps. A variation of the seal row: a cambered bar lets the hands travel past the bench.

steps: Lie face down on the exercise bench and grab the bar using a palms down (pronated grip) that is wider than shoulder width. This will be your starting position.
As you exhale row the bar up as you keep the elbows close to your body to either your chest, in order to target the upper mid back, or to your stomach if targeting the lats is your goal.
After a second hold at the top, lower back down to the starting position slowly as you inhale.
cues: Chest and hips stay on the bench
Squeeze the shoulder blades at the top
exercises.breathing: Brace your core before each rep. Breathe out as you pull, breathe in as you lower the weight.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row - Bar Wide Grip
exercises.description: A seated row on a low cable station. A controlled way to train the mid back and lats with constant tension.
setup: Sit on the bench with feet on the footplate and knees slightly bent.
Grab the handle and sit upright with your arms straight in front of you.
steps: Pull the handle toward your lower ribs while keeping your torso upright.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together.
Let the arms extend forward slowly until you feel a stretch between the shoulder blades.

Shoulders down, not shrugged

exercises.name: Sled Row
exercises.description: Sled Row is a beginner-level strength exercise that mainly targets the upper back, with help from the biceps and lats.
setup: Attach dual handles to a sled connected by a rope or chain. Load the sled to an appropriate weight. Face the sled, backing up until there is some tension in the line.
steps: With a handle in each hand, bend the knees slightly, keep your head and chest up, and begin with your arms extended.
To initiate the movement, flex the elbow as you retract your shoulder blades, pulling the sled towards you.
Take a step or two back to get tension in the line and repeat.

Pause at the top, then lower slowly.

Shoulders down, away from the ears
